chapters.title: Chapter 712 - 712: Future Planning
chapters.content:
(The DarkSky guild Headquarters)
While ChaosBringer and the rebel faction celebrated TheBoss's killing of the Emperor, Cervantez and the DarkSky guild entered a state of panic because of it.
"A 35% debuff? Is this a joke? Why must the entire righteous faction suffer because the Emperor is dead? How is that fair?" Lysa complained, as she simply could not accept over a third of her stats being locked.
"It wasn't fair on 'TheBoss' to have his location exposed every two hours. He managed to kill the Emperor, having surmounted impossible odds and outsmarting every righteous faction player along the way.
Although no-one from our guild participated in his hunt personally, none of us complained about it being unfair either.
Infact I remember you particularly following the hunt closely Lysa, even laughing gleefully when his back was against the wall.
However, now when the rules are against us, you immediately find things harder to accept…" Cervantez said, as he rejected Lysa's notion that it was unfair.
The entire righteous faction was coordinating to kill one man, if nobody protested for him when the odds were stacked against him, nobody had the right to protest now either, just because the situation did not favor them.
"But 30 days? 30 bloody days?" Lysa complained, banging her palm on the conference table as she seemed on the verge of popping a vein.
"The Uprising, being the opportunistic snakes that they are, will immediately try to make the most of this situation…. How are we to defend against them in this weakened state?" Lysa complained, as Cervantez and the other elders in the room let out a deep sigh.
What Lysa said wasn't untrue at all and a 35% debuff was definitely a big problem, however, complaining about it was going to solve nothing.
As bad as the situation seemed, they had no other option but to accept it and move forward, as just like Lysa feared, the uprising were definitely going to try and make the most of this situation.
"The main problem is that he did it too fast…. I did not expect the Emperor to be dead so soon. It will be harder to rally NPC support with the Emperor now dead, and I'm sure there will be many righteous faction players who will jump ship to the rebel side now that things don't seem so smooth on this end anymore" Tor said, as he voiced what everyone else on the table feared.
"Well, we can't afford to worry about the bigger picture right now. The North, South and center are sure to fall, so all we can worry about now is to protect the west.
We knew this day was coming, so even if it's a little early than what we anticipated, it's not like we are completely unprepared.
We will defend the west, even if it's the last thing we do" Cervantez declared eventually, as he ordered his men to not worry about the affairs of the rest of the Empire and solely focus all their attention on securing the west before the vast majority of enemies poured in.
*********
(Meanwhile the Whitesaber guild)
Whitesaber was The Uprising's partner guild in the Western Duchy region, who were promised a partnership with the uprising, as long as they managed to capture the western region.
After sending a notice to mobilize all the uprising guild members, the second message that ChaosBringer wrote was to the Uprising's partner guilds in the North and the West, of which there were three in the north and just one in the west.
The message read :-
[ As per our previous agreement, The Emperor is dead and the opportunity to strike and rebel has finally come.
The Uprising's forces will capture the South and Center as promised, however, we require you to honor your word as well.
The Uprising's victory is all but assured with 'TheBoss' as its leader, however, whether we partner with you or not, now depends on your performance.
With or without your help, 'The Uprising' will unite the Empire under one banner sooner or later, however, now is the chance for you to prove your competence and become partners and overlords of your own regions.
The North Duke is dead, and the Empire's NPC'S are weakened by 50%.
A better chance to strike will never come.
Your rewards will depend on your contribution and believe me when I say this, we will not be stingy with the spoils of war.
We at the uprising will be hoping to hear back news of your resounding victory in the coming days… Please feel free to connect with us in-case you need any supply or logistic assistance, or if you need urgent manpower.
-With regards,
Uprising Spokesman,
ChaosBringer]
As soon as the guildmaster of the Whitesaber guild received this message, he immediately began to mobilize his guild as even he could sense the change in tides.
Initially when the Whitesaber guild accepted the proposal to team up with 'TheBoss' and rebels, there were a few elders within the guild who remained doubtful about the rebels abilities to unify the east, center and south under their control, however, all those doubts were now dispelled.
With the Emperor dead and the NPC's demoralized, the current scales of war were tipped overwhelmingly in favor of the rebels and this was the last chance for guilds like them to partner up.
If they failed this chance, it was more than likely that 'The Uprising' would never partner with them again, and hence to maximize their own benefits, they had to win as much territory as possible.
"Prepare for war… we march tomorrow! Send orders to all guild members to prepare for war and recall all those who are away for levelling or adventure.
The entire guild will take part in this war for the sake of our future and by the grace of the gaming gods we shall prevail!
We will win this war, and we will become the next overlords of the west" The guildmaster said, instructing his vice guildmaster who immediately began typing the message as he prepared the men for war.

chapters.title: Chapter 713 - 713: Parental Worry
chapters.content:
(PinkLotus's POV)
PinkLotus frowned deeply when all her stats were reduced by 35%.
She too was tracking the development surrounding 'TheBoss' closely, and while she did not feel surprised that he succeeded in outsmarting everyone, she felt annoyed at receiving a penalty for his success.
"Why must I be penalized? I technically don't belong to any faction. Although I'm not a rebel, I'm not a righteous player either… gosh, this is so annoying" she cursed, as she did not feel content with the current state of affairs.
As far as she was concerned, her personal strength mattered more to her than the success or failure of the righteous faction, which was why she felt beyond livid at the unfair penalty.
"You know, if you think about it, you're more than likely to fight a war in this weakened state very soon…." Luke said calmly, as he stood beside her near the waterfall where she usually trained.
"Oh?" PinkLotus replied, sounding surprised as she waited for Luke to explain his statement.
"The righteous faction is weakened, the rebels are sure to make a move…. If Leo were to ever cash-in his bet and have you fight for the rebels, it's going to be pretty soon" Luke explained, as he reminded PinkLotus about the terms of their last spar.
"Right…" PinkLotus said grimly, her eyes widening as flashbacks of their previous battle flashed in her head.
In return for accepting her request to spar, Leo had put forward the condition that were she to lose, she was to join him in war whenever he called for it.
That day, he defeated her brutally and he was roughly 122 levels stronger now compared to that day after his recent rampage within the light faction.
The gap between them was widening at a rapid pace and whatever little hope she had to catch-up to Leo, seemed to be slipping away every passing day.
"Stupid…Stupid game developers, I hate them…" she cursed as she started to hack away at the waterfall in fury.
Beside her, Luke stood with a soft smile on his face as he began analyzing the future events with a calm head.
Even Though he was not a part of the DarkSky guild anymore, he could envision exactly what everyone in the guild must be discussing at this moment and how they would react to this news.
"*Sigh*, I wish I was back in a group again…. Solo play is kinda boring" Luke muttered to himself, sighing as he missed his leadership post within the DarkSky guild.
However, although he missed the whole experience, he did not feel keen on returning, as he knew that the DarkSky guild was not the right fit for him anymore.
If he were ever to join a guild again, Luke felt sure that it would either be his own new guild, or another organisation, however, he was not keen on joining the DarkSky guild anymore.
********
(Jacob and Elena's POV)
Elena and Jacob both found themselves sitting within Elena's restaurant, located inside a remote righteous faction tier1 town.
Jacob was on his way to disrupt some pursuers who planned to camp and kill Leo, however, once Leo changed his course and veered away from where Jacob was stationed, Jacob decided to give-up on the chase and instead decided to spend the rest of the day with his lovely wife at her own restaurant.
"Jacob, I talked to Rita today, she's saying that there are at least a 100 million players trying to kill our son's best friend 'TheBoss' and that he's the most dangerous man to ever live…. Is that true?" Elena asked, with concern evident in her eyes as Jacob failed to form a proper answer.
"T-that, right… no…" he said, lying through his teeth, as although it was indeed the truth, Jacob decided to not make Elena worry about it.
"Rita doesn't know anything Elena, Leo is only business friends with 'TheBoss', the two aren't really chummy, the actions of 'TheBoss' does not concern our son" Jacob said, as Elena nervously clutched her cooking apron around her neck.
"I don't like our son being friends with such a dangerous guy… but he's all grown up now, and I can't even scold him.
Jacob… Please talk to him when you can? He doesn't need to be friends with a KingSlayer.
Even if he earns a few less gold coins a month it's okay, but don't let him stay with a bad company" Elena said, as Jacob nodded his head in agreement.
"I'll talk to him, don't worry…." He said, as his reply made Elena instantly beam into a smile.
"Both our kids are kind-hearted and morally decent…. All this murder, carnage and this deplorable game world, it doesn't suit us…" Elena continued, as Jacob felt it hard to swallow the food she had cooked when she talked about the game this way.
Only Jacob knew that all three of them were dangerous murderers and killers, as all three of them were within the top 10,000 ranks of the game, being three of the strongest players all around.
However, in front of Elena all three of them were as straight as an arrow, not even daring to harm a fly, because they knew better than to upset her.
If not for her, Jacob had no doubt in his mind that the three of them were unhinged to their cores, however, any semblance of decency that they had was only because of Elena and the values she instilled in them over the years.
Jacob quite enjoyed watching his enemies squirm and die, and he enjoyed the thrill of the hunt as well and somehow, he knew that his children did too.
Usually, such individuals became prone to mental instability, however, because of Elena the three of them retained some modicum of decency.
She was the guiding light in their lives, however, with the boys not being around her anymore, slowly but surely that light was starting to drift away.
—------

chapters.title: Chapter 714 - 714: Improvement
chapters.content:
(Leo's POV)
Far removed from the intricate strategies devised by players like ChaosBringer and Cervantez, Leo kept his focus squarely on survival.
Navigating treacherous terrain, he pressed forward toward the safety of the rebel-controlled zone, his singular goal being to finally log out of the game after several hours of intense action.
[System Notification: Congratulations, player 'TheBoss,' for surviving yet another 2 hours within the Empire-controlled zone. You receive +2 levels.]
A glowing system notification appeared in Leo's view, briefly breaking the monotony of his trek.
Gazing at the system bar, he allowed himself a soft grin as he found a glimmer of joy amidst the relentless grind.
"The only redeeming part of my location being exposed every two hours is getting these +2 levels. At this rate, I'll hit level 1000 soon enough… and that will certainly be something to see." Leo mused, as he opened his stat panel to check on his progress.
**********
TheBoss/Leo Skyshard's Character Profile

Race: Human (Status: Restricted)
Title: [Fake It Till You Make It] (Equipped)

************
His stats reflected his current strength— where none dipped below the impressive 1500 mark.
This meant that even under a debilitating 30% strength debuff, every attribute of his would remain well above 1000 which was a testament to his monstrous progress as a player.
"Is this what compounding really feels like?" Leo mused, a smirk forming.
"Fake it till you make it sounded like a cruel joke back when I was stuck fighting for my life every day. But now? Now it's unstoppable. Those desperate times… maybe they were exactly what I needed to reach this point." Leo muttered to himself as his thoughts drifted to the past.
Back when he just started to play the game, survival had once hinged on staying a step ahead of Cervantez and the other rankers to maintain his ruse, forcing Leo to take insane risks that often pushed him beyond his limits.
However, what had started as a desperate scramble had snowballed into an unstoppable avalanche over the years, eventually bringing him to the point where he was today.
'I can't complain about my journey now… I have no regrets' Leo thought, as his eyes drifted from his stats to his inventory, where he noticed a key issue.
"Only 12 sets of daggers left," Leo muttered, running a hand over his chin. "I came into this mission with over 250. If this keeps up, I might run out of weapons entirely."
The toll of recent battles had been severe. Despite salvaging and reusing daggers when possible, his arsenal had dwindled to just 12 sets of daggers now or roughly 144 daggers in total which was a tiny tally for an assassin who had hundreds of opponents constantly on the hunt for him.
"If I have to use Amanda's gift…" His expression darkened. "That'll really piss me off." Leo mused, as just the thought of having to use the Nightblade Dagger set or the daggers of love set, completely pissed him off.
*Thump*
*Thump*
The clatter of hooves and distant voices broke through his thoughts, instantly setting him on edge.
"He's on this road! TheBoss's last known location places him here!"
"The footprints in the mud suggest a solo traveler passed through. He must be close!"
"We've got 200 men. Use our numbers—overwhelm him the moment we find him!"
The voices of righteous faction players carried through the air, their determination unmistakable.
"It seems like the righteous faction is finally catching up to my path change… trouble will follow me continuously from here till home then" Leo muttered, as he prepared for battle.
"It's him! It's the Boss!" Said one of the righteous faction players leading the vanguard, as with Leo not keen on escaping, he let the enemies approach him undeterred.
"Someone share the information on the forums that we have found 'TheBoss', share our live location. And the others fall into formation, we need to fight as one!" said the leader of the group, as many righteous faction players dismounted and quickly got into battle formation.
"Well you've found me…. Let's see what you can do with the 35% debuff!" Leo said, as he threw a couple of smoke bombs amidst the group and charged into battle with nothing but two daggers in hand.
"Aghh–"
"Where is he?"
"I can't see nothing–"
"Jake are you okay?"
"Agghhhh"
Once the smoke took hold, chaos unfolded as within seconds dozens of players died.
Eventually, a couple minutes later, as the smoke dispelled, Leo turned out to be the only player left alive as he wiped out the party of 200 in just under 2 minutes.
"Too easy" he mused, as with the 35% debuff the common players were no longer a credible challenge to his safety.
For him, killing a bunch of level 300-400 players was no different from fighting children and hence he stopped avoiding them and started slaughtering them whenever he came across one such group.

chapters.title: Chapter 715 - 715: True Chaos
chapters.content:
Over the next 12 hours Leo was relentlessly pursued by righteous faction players, their numbers and determination seemingly endless.
His survival was a combination of sharp instincts, clever tactics, and sheer grit.
He evaded some groups by using [Vanish] and smoke bombs, disoriented others with quick, calculated ambushes, and deftly circled around larger patrols to stay ahead of his pursuers.
However, despite his best efforts, fatigue had begun to take its toll on his body.
The castle fight had left him battered, and with his supply of health and stamina potions depleted, he was out of quick fixes for his degrading physical condition.
Towards the end of the gaming day, when the righteous faction players were to log out once more, the situation degraded for him to the point where every movement felt labored, his muscles screaming with each step as he pushed forward toward the safety of rebel-controlled territory.
But the rebel zone was still a day's journey away, and the weight of exhaustion was becoming impossible to ignore.
"I'll have to take a few hours of rest…. I can't continue like this anymore" Leo muttered to himself near the end, as although the night was the best time for him to cover lots of ground when he had no threats chasing him, tonight he was forced to take rest, atleast until a majority of his stamina bar recovered.
Leo calculated this to be a necessary sacrifice, as he understood that without resting today, he was sure to fall prey tomorrow.
Thankfully though, while Leo struggled, the righteous faction players fared no better.
The deaths of the Emperor and the North Duke spread like wildfire across the empire, throwing the entire righteous faction into disarray.
Soldiers and players alike were debilitated by the stat debuffs, their morale shattered as chaos engulfed the once-organized faction.
Even with their numbers, their ability to organize an effective pursuit seemed to be faltering as problems erose for them in every corner.
*********
The death of the Emperor and his entire bloodline sent shockwaves through the streets of StrongHaven City, the heart of the Unity Empire.
News spread faster than wildfire, whispered in hushed tones at first but soon shouted from rooftops as panic began to set in around the evening following the emperor's death.
"The Emperor is dead! The rebels sent their best—just one man—and he slaughtered them all!" cried a baker, abandoning his stall as customers fled without paying.
In the crowded streets, merchants hastily packed their wares, leaving goods and coins scattered on the cobblestones.
Children clung to their mothers, crying amidst the chaos, while nobles in gilded carriages shouted orders to their drivers, desperate to escape the chaotic city that could very well soon turn into a failed state.
All around, the once-proud capital devolved into a chaotic choir of despair, as rumors spread like poison, each more exaggerated than the last.
"I heard 'TheBoss' didn't just kill the Emperor—he killed the Duke of the North too!"
"They say he used magic to turn invisible and walk straight into the throne room!"
"Invisible? No, no. I heard he killed 5000 guards on his way in and walked out without a scratch!"
The city's heart, its bustling marketplace, lay in shambles. Stalls overturned, their goods spilling into the streets as the only sounds that could be heard were the shouts of a frightened populace.
Amidst this chaos, City guards patrolled the streets in disarray, their usual discipline broken.
Some argued over who should take command, while others shouted at panicking citizens to stay indoors.
"Calm yourselves! Order will be restored!" one guard shouted, his voice cracking under the weight of his own uncertainty.
But the citizens were far from calm. Rocks and debris were hurled at soldiers in misplaced anger.
While one group of townsfolk surrounded a patrol, shouting accusations of incompetence:
"You couldn't even protect the Emperor! How are we supposed to trust you with our lives?"
The guards raised their shields, unsure whether to retreat or respond as the tension escalated with every second, threatening to erupt into violence.
*******
(In the Noble Quarter)
Behind gilded gates of the noble community in StrongHaven, nobles huddled in their manors, whispering among themselves.
"This must be rebel propaganda," one baron muttered, pacing the length of his lavish hall.
"No one man could breach the palace walls, let alone kill the Emperor." he said, as he refused to beleive the rumors that were floating around, however, the others around him seemed less optimistic.
"He's dead… such rumours would be quelled by now if he wasn't…" said a viscount who looked like he had lost his soul.
"If the Emperor is truly dead, what stops the rebels from marching here next?" another noblewoman hissed, her knuckles white as she clutched her pearls.
In the end, a decision was made to send emissaries to the remaining loyal generals to prepare a convoy to escape the city, but the nobles argued over who should go, none willing to leave the safety of their manors.
The name 'TheBoss' was on every tongue, whispered in fear and awe alike.
"One man versus an empire… Is he even human?"
"The rebels will win now. With 'TheBoss' on their side, there's no stopping them."
*********
(Meanwhile in the slums)
As the city unraveled, banners bearing the Emperor's crest were torn down by angry citizens in the slims, replaced with crude symbols of rebellion and photos of 'TheBoss' that were once placed there during his time at the grand tournament.
The downtrodden, who were already discontent with the status quo, saw this as an opportunity for change and decided to support the rebel leader wholeheartedly as with the Emperor dead, they became the first to embrace the change.
The golden age of the Unity Empire seemed to crumble in real time, its foundation shaking beneath the weight of a single assassin's blade.
The chaos was far from over, but one truth echoed through the streets…. That StrongHaven would never be the same again, now that the Evanus bloodline was at an end.

chapters.title: Chapter 716 - 716: True Chaos (2)
chapters.content:
The chaos across the Empire did not affect the NPCs alone, as players also faced major difficulties.
For the righteous faction players, the aftermath of the Emperor's death was nothing short of catastrophic, as in just a single day's time with the news of the emperor's death spreading, the capital city came to a screeching halt.
StrongHaven City, which had once been an organized and thriving network of the games strongest guilds and the single location to obtain the games best NPC quests now seemed like a crumbling empire—both figuratively and literally.
The first and most immediate problem that the players encountered was the sudden refusal of NPC workers to cooperate.
Blacksmiths, who had loyally forged weapons and armor for guilds, closed their shops without explanation.
Miners tasked with collecting vital resources abandoned their work posts, leaving the service of guilds that employed them in a mass strike.
Couriers, who once ran across cities delivering important messages and goods for players, simply vanished without a trace as the collapse of critical infrastructure took place right before the players eyes.
However, as if the situation was not bad enough with the infrastructure collapse, the second blow came with the abrupt collapse of all government services.
The royal bounty boards, a vital source of income and rewards for players, stood bare.
A red notification hung over the boards declaring that the 'Service Is Temporarily Unavailable', as Quest-givers who once offered lucrative missions to players were nowhere to be found.
"What the hell! I had an ongoing quest to submit 7 archaic spider fangs… it was going to pay me 30 gold and lots of experience, however, the quest can no longer be submitted! I've been working on it for 15 fucking days…" one player complained, as suddenly he realized that he could not turn his quest in anymore.
Even the stables where one could hire horses to travel out of the city, a service that was almost never out of horses usually, now ran out of horses to rent as they too abruptly closed shop.
This turn of events, unfortunately left millions of players stranded in StrongHaven City, as there were many who had flocked to the city just to take part in the historic hunt of 'TheBoss', however, they now found themselves suddenly cut off from their guildmates and supplies, unable to travel to outposts where reinforcements were desperately needed.
"What the hell is this?" one player shouted in frustration, banging on the locked doors of the stable farm.
"I was supposed to report back to Ipswich town! How am I supposed to move now?"
Another player, equally exasperated, replied, "You think that's bad? My escort quest failed because the NPC just up and left! I didn't even get to turn it in!"
Finally, on top of everything else, the streets themselves turned extremely dangerous for the players.
NPC guards, already spread thin, were unable to maintain order amidst the chaos as groups of looters roamed freely, ambushing players and NPCs alike.
For righteous faction players, this added layer of danger made even the simplest tasks perilous.
Quests that required moving through city streets became an ordeal, with players having to fight off mobs of angry citizens or bandits.
However, perhaps the most surprising backlash came from the NPC commoners.
The righteous faction guilds' decision to loot flour and grain for their defense strategies had come back to haunt them in spectacular fashion, as the moment the Emperor died, so did the patience of the commoners.
In the slums, furious NPCs stormed guild outposts, demanding justice.
As at the Sunspire Vanguard guildhall, one of the stronger guilds within StrongHaven, whose members had partaken in the looting, a mob of farmers gathered, their anger palpable.
"You took our grain to scatter on the streets!" one old man shouted, shaking his fist. "You called it a strategy, but what about us? Our children go hungry while you play war!"
Rocks and debris rained down on the guildhall's windows, shattering the glass as players inside scrambled to figure out how to respond.
"Do we fight them?" one guild member asked nervously, clutching his weapon.
"No, you idiot!" another barked back. "If we attack the NPCs, the entire faction's morale will plummet further. Just stay inside!" his superior replied, as the guild members were forced to hole up within their headquarters, unable to come out.
******
(Meanwhile on the forums)
Across the forums, players from the righteous faction shared in the rising frustration and fear as the situation only seemed to go from bad to worse.
"What's happening to this game? I can't even complete basic quests anymore!"
"This is all because of TheBoss! If we don't stop him, the righteous faction is finished."
"We cannot hunt TheBoss when there's trouble at home… the unrest that started from the capital will soon spread to every corner of Empire controlled territories. If we don't contain it, all the guilds currently holding lands will find it hard to maintain control"
"If we kill 'TheBoss', all of this mess will probably solve itself…"
A heated discussion took place on the forums, with one faction suggesting that the only way out of this mess was to double down and hunt 'TheBoss' at any cost, however, not not everyone was convinced they could stop him.
"Kill him? He's already won. We're down 35% in stats. The NPCs hate us. What chance do we even have?"
The more rational side replied, as many rejected the notion of partaking in yet another grand hunt, after their past failures and decided to cut losses by managing the bad situation as best as they could.
As the chaos continued to unfold, one truth became increasingly clear, that the righteous faction was no longer just losing a war—it was falling apart from within.
A majority of the players struggled to keep their guilds afloat, as the rebels prepared to take advantage of the crumbling empire.
Yet, despite how bad the situation looked already, the fact of the matter was, that the righteous faction's real nightmare was actually only beginning.
—-------

chapters.title: Chapter 717 - 717: Almost Home
chapters.content:
( Leo's POV )
After resting for roughly 6 hours and rejuvenating his stamina bar back to maximum, Leo began to slowly make his way back towards the rebel controlled territory at a pace which did not deplete his stamina.
He enjoyed roughly 4 hours of nearly uninterrupted walking through the serene early morning scenery of the game, as he enjoyed the sunrise over the neighbouring farm fields and managed to cross a minor village before the players logged-in yet again.
Leo now had to cover roughly 20 hours of journey on foot to reach the safety of rebel controlled territory which meant that if he could survive the tide of players coming after him through the traditional gaming day, even if he was slow and made little progress, he could still definitely reach his destination by midnight, finally putting an end to his crazy adventure.
"One final push…" he muttered, steeling his resolve as he began to jog yet again, with the first notification of the day being the same one that exposed his location yet again.
**********
Aware of his ability to move through the night now, the righteous faction players quickly understood that if they failed to hunt him tonight, Leo was going to make it back to the safe-zone by tomorrow, which meant that it was a now or never for those who dreamed to hunt him.
However, for roughly 70% of the righteous players who were nowhere near his current location and could not reach in-time, the dream to hunt him down was already over, as only those who were tracking him from the start and were close-by, now stood a chance to finally mount a resistance.
"TheBoss still has to cross Redallion Town to reach the safe-zone. No matter what subroute he takes, all paths eventually converge at Redallion Town, and hence any meaningful ambush can only be set-up there" An analyst wrote on the forums as after analysing Leo's path thoroughly, he came to the conclusion that Leo was headed for Redallion Town.
According to him and a host of other experts, Leo was enroute to reach Redallion Town in 6 hours time, giving righteous faction players in the area ample time to assemble and set-up an ambush.
"Alone or in small parties of 100-400 people, we stand no chance against 'TheBoss'.
If 1400 top rankers failed to defeat him during the event, 2000 common players are most definitely not going to.
The only shot we have is to gather at Redallion and take down 'TheBoss' with a force of 10,000 men or more" A player wrote, as his post became upvoted and shared by thousands.
Slowly but surely, support for the ambush at Redallion grew, as a thousand…five thousand….. ten and soon twenty thousand men assembled at the place.
The news of the Emperor's death had sent the small town on its edge, however, surprisingly it remained one of the few places across the Empire where law and order did not collapse completely.
The local NPC authorities and local guard were successful in enforcing a curfew, managing the riot situation successfully, however, the situation still remained extremely volatile.
Hence, when thousands of armed players suddenly flooded to the town, tensions began to flare as the common NPC's did not take kindly to the foreign presence.
Hours passed by, and roughly around 40 minutes before 'TheBoss' was scheduled to arrive at the place, a small fight broke out between the righteous faction players and the NPC commoners, as a bunch of small kids pelted stones at a group of undisciplined players, who angrily retaliated by restraining and hurting the boys.
This small incident, when witnessed by the common populace, sparked an immediate unrest as riots broke out town wide.
Commoners began clashing with the players on the streets, as farmers and housewives armed with sickles and kitchen knives began demanding that the foreigners begone from their lands.
The towns mayor and local guards, also turned against the players, asking them to observe the curfew and not patrol the streets armed, which led to the players fighting back against the NPC's, making the situation turn from bad to worse.
For the players, this was their last shot at taking down 'TheBoss', and they could not observe a curfew under any circumstances, however, the local authorities were not willing to take 'No' for an answer.
Unfortunately, this led to a situation where by the time Leo reached the town, the players became too busy to even locate him, as he navigated the chaotic streets with ease and bypassed the town with his excellent hiding skills, managing to get around the last player holdout.
An hour later, as his location was revealed yet again and the players realized that he went past Redallion, all hope finally seemed lost, as apart from a few extremely determined and delusional people, all else lost hope to catch him.
"It's over…. We have lost–"
"In the end I guess it was just never meant to be"
"I guess it wasn't 'TheBoss' who won. It was 'We' who lost"
Sad messages like these flooded the forums, as the morale of the righteous faction players hit a rock bottom.
For Leo, the last day of his journey which he anticipated to be the most difficult, surprisingly turned out to be the most quiet as apart from killing a few hundred weak players, he encountered no major trouble at all!
In the end, by the time the normal gaming day ended, he was only a few dozen miles away from safety, as he could almost breathe the freedom from where he was.
"I've done it…. I've achieved the impossible!!!" He said to himself, clutching his fists, as only now did he let himself believe that he was going to make it…. That he was going to win against all odds.
—-----

chapters.title: Chapter 718 - 718: Mysterious Archer
chapters.content:
(A few minutes later, Leo's POV)
A few minutes later, as the official gaming hours ended, Leo let out a huge sigh of relief, thinking that he had finally made it!
"Wooo—, nothing can stop me now!" He muttered under his breath, walking happily towards the boundary, when suddenly he sensed danger.
There was an unmistakable whistling noise behind him, like the whirring of a weapon through the wind, causing his pupils to dilate.
'Incoming….' he thought, managing to turn his head ever so slightly out of reflex, as an arrow zoomed past his face, grazing just the tip of his ears.
-120.
A stream of blood streaked down his ear, as he turned to face the enemy, who to his surprise was nowhere in sight.
"The hell?" Leo muttered, becoming extremely alert, as he scanned his surroundings with extreme caution.
"Who's there? Who dares shoot at me?" He asked, however, there was no response.
The archer who shot the arrow at Leo had now expertly concealed themself, making it nearly impossible for Leo to pinpoint his/her location.
*Shot*
A stinging sensation arose in his shoulder, followed by a searing pain that spread rapidly through his arm.
Leo staggered backward, his breath hitching as the world momentarily blurred around him.
His left shoulder had been impaled completely by a foreign object and as he tried to remove it with his right palm, he realized that it felt like the smooth shaft of an arrow.
"Argh!" he gritted his teeth, feeling his knees weaken, as when he tried to pull the arrow out, the pain he felt was too excruciating to beat.
He had been impaled through his shoulders just a few hours ago today, however, this time, the pain wasn't just surface-deep; it radiated through his entire arm, sending sharp, nerve-wracking jolts into his shoulder and chest.
His left palm, which was clutching a dagger that he had pulled out for protection, trembled uncontrollably as he felt his grip falter.
The arrow hadn't just pierced him—it had struck a critical nerve cluster in his left arm, disrupting his ability to control his hand entirely.
The dagger slipped from his grasp, clattering uselessly to the ground as Leo felt his fingers going numb.
Panic swirled in his chest as he tried and failed to flex his palm, as even the slightest movement sent waves of excruciating pain shooting through his arm, making it nearly impossible to steady himself.
'This… isn't just an arrow,' Leo thought, a cold realization dawning on him, as the precision of the shot and the unrelenting agony it caused were unlike anything he had experienced before.
To make matters worse, the attack had come out of nowhere—completely silent and invisible, giving Leo no chance at defending himself.
'Where?' Leo thought, struggling back to his feet as he tried to detect the enemy desperately.
He strained his senses to the limit, trying to pinpoint the direction of the shot, but there was nothing to grasp on.
In the open surroundings around him, there was no rustle of movement, no glint of light reflecting off a weapon.
The arrow seemed to have materialized from thin air, bypassing every instinct and defense he had.
"How... how the hell did the enemy do that?" he whispered, his voice shaking with frustration and pain.
The invisibility and soundlessness of the attack made it all the more terrifying. It was as if his assailant were a phantom, striking from the shadows with supernatural precision.
"Fuck, fuck, fuck…. I'm so close to safety too–" Leo thought, as he felt his instincts screaming at him to move, to find cover and hide, but his body felt sluggish, as if it were weighed down by the injury.
"Can't die here…" He muttered eventually, as using all the tricks he had up his sleeve at once, he used [Vanish] followed by [Mirror World] to create countless clones of himself, that scattered away in all directions, while he himself ran towards safety in a separate direction, with two clones acting as a body shield for him, running in front and behind.
*Shot*
An arrow whizzed through the air, silent and swift, embedding itself into the neck of the clone trailing behind Leo.
The clone didn't even falter—it simply disintegrated into shimmering fragments, vanishing like smoke in the wind, as Leo stumbled on the path he ran.
'The enemy is behind me', he thought, as his heart raced.
Turning, he faced the direction where the enemy was at, and waited for any incoming attacks while still remaining invisible to the naked eye, as he tried to figure out how the enemy pin-pointed his exact location.
Out of all the clones scattered in every direction, the enemy had pinpointed him, the real him, with terrifying accuracy, and this baffled Leo.
The clones were meant to confuse, to scatter his enemy's focus and attacks, but somehow, the enemy had seen through his strategy with ease.
"How?" He muttered under his breath, until he noticed the faint crimson trail on the road leading up to his position.
Blood.
Leo's breath hitched as he realized the horrifying truth. His wound. The arrow in his shoulder had left him bleeding heavily, and the trail of blood was like a beacon, guiding his enemy directly to him.
"Damn it!" he hissed, feeling a wave of dread wash over him, as no amount of clones or misdirection could ever mask the glaring evidence he was leaving behind with every step.
"Fuck me…" he muttered, as he could feel his strength ebbing as blood loss began to take its toll, making his movements slightly sluggish and unsteady.
He clenched his jaw, forcing himself to think through the pain, but with the enemy still undetectable to him, he could not come up with many viable solutions.
'I need to find the enemy and somehow confront him… with the enemy being an Archer, unless I can close-in the range advantage, I'm going to be a dead man' Leo thought, as he understood that without locating the enemy and closing down, he had no chance for survival.

chapters.title: Chapter 719 - 719: The Silent Arrow
chapters.content:
Leo desperately tried to locate the Hidden Archer. However, unbeknownst to him, the opponent he faced today was a cautious man, who also happened to be a master.
Locating him was never going to be easy, as the man was an expert in camouflage and concealment.
The opponent that Leo faced today was none other than Arlen Dreadveil, a renowned demon slayer from the Northern War Front and one of Denver Willow's closest friends.
Known as "The Silent Arrow," Arlen's reputation was legendary, and it was well deserved.
Arlen's name was whispered with reverence across the Unity Empire as a man who thrived in chaos, holding the Northern Frontline against countless demonic invasions.
His skill with the bow was unmatched as every arrow he loosened found its mark without fail.
It was said that he once took down 6 High Demons with a single shot, earning him the nickname "Demonbane."
But to Arlen, his greatest achievements weren't in the number of demons he'd slain but in the bonds he'd forged over the years, with none being stronger than his friendship with Denver Willow.
Arlen and Denver had served side by side on the Northern Frontlines for years, their camaraderie forged in the crucible of relentless battle.
Denver called Arlen his "anchor in chaos," the one who always provided clarity and calm amidst the storm, which was why the news of Denver's death had shattered Arlen.
When Arlen learned that Denver's killer—a lone assassin named TheBoss—had infiltrated StrongHaven and slaughtered not only Denver but the Emperor as well, his rage knew no bounds.
Being only a few kilometres north of StrongHaven, in his birth village on a short vacation, Arlen was initially headed back to the North Wall once his vacation was over, however, he travelled south instead when he learned of his friend's death.
To him, nothing mattered more than avenging his fallen brother, as his own sense of justice demanded it.
For hours, Arlen had tracked Leo, methodically piecing together his movements.
Broken twigs, faint footprints, and the telltale trail of blood left by Leo slaying his pursuers along the way, gave Arlen the confidence that he was on the right path, until eventually, he caught up to Leo right near the edge of the Empire controlled zone.
Had it been anyone else, they would probably have confronted Leo that very second when they spotted him, however, Arlen did not.
Having near infinite patience and unmatched discipline, Arlen controlled his rage and searched for a vantage point before attacking Leo, ensuring that his camouflage was perfect before he did.
His first shot was supposed to blow his enemy's head out, however, to his absolute shock, the kid sensed the attack and dodged reflexively, taking only a minor hit to his ears.
'He's fast…' Arlen thought at that point, as knocking another arrow he prepared for his signature attack the [Silent Shot].
The silent shot was a move that was both invisible and impossible to perceive as it left no noise or disturbance in air currents as it moved.
It was the attack that earned him his nickname as 'The Silent Arrow' and he expected his shot to take the enemy out for sure when he released it.
He aimed his shot straight for the enemy's heart, however, a gust of wind at the very last second changed the shot's trajectory ever so slightly, making it hit the target's shoulder instead of his heart.
'Oh Snap!' Arlen thought, as he grit his teeth in anger.
He wasn't supposed to miss, however, through sheer dumb luck, his opponent survived once again.
To make matters even worse, Leo summoned a bunch of clones and began to run desperately for his life while being shielded by two clones, however, Arlen only focused on the trail of blood he left behind, to take out his protection first, before trying to take him out.
This time, his arrow found its mark precisely, piercing his targets head, however, much to his surprise yet again, his opponent seemed to figure out his location, as instead of continuing to run, the opponent stood frozen in one place, making Arlen question his intentions.
'What are you trying to achieve here assassin? Although I can't see you, I still know where you are' Arlen thought, as although he could not see Leo physically while he used [Vanish], he could still visualize him based on his blood trail.
However, being the cautious man that he was, Arlen did not shoot another arrow, as he felt worried that with his opponents fast reflexes, he would dodge the attack and also pinpoint his location, putting him at a severe disadvantage.
'You're bleeding profusely, I'm fine just the way I am…. And I have more patience than you….. you're not going to outsmart me' Arlen thought, as he steadied his breathing and took aim.
"Your move–" he muttered ever so slightly as he waited for Leo to make his move first before releasing the arrow that he had already notched.
For Leo, this was the worst situation possible, as with his opponent reacting to his movements after he made them, he was always going to be a step behind the enemy in the fight.
********
(60 seconds later, Leo's POV)
A full minute passed and no new shots came Leo's way, making him lose patience.
Unlike his opponent, Leo wasn't the most patient man and when the shots stopped coming, he slowly started to move back while still facing the side where he felt the threat was at.
At first his steps were slow but slowly he started to pick up pace as he backpedaled.
'I'm only a couple kilometers off the border, even if I die, I just need to cross the edge so that my gaming career doesn't end here…' Leo thought, as at this point, he gave up on the thought of taking his enemy down and instead decided to focus on somehow returning to the safe-zone first.
—----

chapters.title: Chapter 720 - 720: Trouble
chapters.content:
Leo's steps were hurried but deliberate as he ran backward, his sharp gaze locked in the direction he believed the Archer to be.
He was still invisible and the enemy could not perceive him directly, however, with the faint trail of blood that he left behind with every step, Leo knew that the enemy was still tracking him relentlessly.
The open road stretched endlessly before him, the sparse trees and open fields on either side offering little in terms of cover or safety, as Leo quickly rejected the idea of trying and misleading his opponents gaze by moving through various obstacles, as his current environment did not allow for such tricks.
Seconds passed, and his breaths began to come in short bursts, the burning sensation in his lungs a cruel reminder of his physical limits. Yet, he didn't dare turn his back entirely—not with a dangerous Master Archer stalking him.
'If I can't see him, I'll never stand a chance,' Leo realized, his eyes darting to every faint shimmer or shadow that might betray the Archer's location, but he had no luck.
Arlen was simply impossible to perceive when hidden, just as he himself was when using [Vanish] without the trail of blood.
All around him, the silence was deafening, save for the very soft rhythmic pounding of his boots on the dirt road and the faint rustling of wind through the fields.
It was a calm that made every hair on his body stand on end—a calm that could only mean death was near.
Every second he feared being impaled by an unseen arrow, his fear driving every muscle in his body to move faster.
******
Perched unseen a few hundred meters away, Arlen stretched the bowstring with the nocked arrow to its limit.
He admired his opponent's tenacity, even begrudgingly respected it, as under the circumstances, he recognised that running away was the best option.
The range and accuracy of his shots greatly diminished after 700 meters, and with the opponent retreating fast, Arlen knew that he had one good shot left in him, before having to abandon his current hiding spot and chase after him.
"I have to make this next shot count…" Arlen muttered, as he began channeling mana into the arrow to attempt yet another [Silent Shot].
On paper, the 'Silent Shot' had no weakness. It was truly an imperceivable attack that could kill any opponent, however, only Arlen knew that it had a major drawback.
The attack could only be used once every minute, as it had a 60 second cooldown time, making it impossible to use as a rapid shot.
This was the only reason behind why, after missing his first silent shot, he did not immediately follow it up with a second to finish the job, as he simply could not do it, even if he wanted to.
Thankfully, 60 seconds had already passed since the last time he used the move and hence, when Leo began to run again, Arlen decided to use it once more.
[Silent Shot]
The attack soared silently through the air, invisible and soundless, as it zeroed in on Leo's location with deadly accuracy.
For Arlen, he could not perceive Leo and his running movement since Leo was currently invisible and hence Arlen, based on his own observations of Leo's movements, made an educated guess of how he would be moving.
Observing the trail of blood, he could already imagine how Leo might be moving, however, while Arlen pictured Leo running with his back exposed, Leo in fact ran facing him, which caused Arlen's estimations to deviate by mere millimetres.
*Slash*
-650 HP
Imperceivable, the arrow slashed past Leo's left torso, piercing through his premium chainmail and plucking a few grams of his flesh.
If he wasn't running facing forwards, the shot was sure to pierce his heart, however, he survived because of his unusual running posture.
Nonetheless, the searing pain of the near-miss sent shockwaves through his torso, as he staggered but somehow managed to keep his footing, sheer adrenaline coursing through him as he continued to move.
"That was too close," Leo muttered, clutching his side, as blood trickled from his wound, joining the trail already marking his path.
From his hidden vantage point, Arlen's sharp eyes narrowed as he watched the assassin evade what should have been a fatal shot.
'He shouldn't have seen that coming. How the hell did he dodge it?' Arlen wondered, as seeing his enemy still moving, he felt furious.
Arlen's knuckles whitened as he gripped his bow tighter. He prided himself on precision, on certainty, and yet this boy had defied him twice now.
"You're just prolonging the inevitable," Arlen whispered, knocking another arrow, as he finally abandoned his hiding spot and began rushing after Leo.
Meanwhile, Leo's near-death experience only spurred him onward. With no time to dwell on the pain, he hastened his pace, forcing his legs to move faster despite the screaming protest from his body.
The plan was simple: force Arlen to move, to break his calculated stillness as Leo truly believed that if he could disrupt his enemy's rhythm, it could potentially buy him the precious seconds he needed to cross into rebel-controlled territory, as slowly but surely he inched closer.
Behind him, Arlen frowned, as he too picked up the pace, while still trying to move in a way where he wouldn't immediately catch Leo's eyes.
"Fine, boy," he muttered, "If you want the hunt… I'll give you the hunt" Arlen said, as he stretched the bowstring back, ready to unleash another shot.
—-------

chapters.title: Chapter 721 - 721: Reaching Safety
chapters.content:
1500 meters, that was all that seperated Leo from the safety of the rebel controlled territory.
From the corner of his eyes he could see the water bridge that demarcated the boundary between Empire controlled central lands and Rebel Controlled South and the faint glint of the Yakasa River Stream that flowed under it.
Yet, while the bridge was so close, it seemed so far with a mad Archer on his back.
"Oh fuck you Archer…. Once I reach the safety of the rebel zone and ain't afraid to die, then I'll show you who 'TheBoss' is!" Leo said, as he ran at top speed, pushing through the pain in his upper body.
Meanwhile, Arlen loosened another shot, this one not silent, as Leo with his heightened senses heard it coming from a 100 meters away.
"Oh no you don't!" Leo muttered, as at the last second, he moved his good right arm, slicing the incoming arrow in half, as it cluttered harmlessly by his side.
At this point, he deactivated [Vanish] as apart from draining his mana constantly, the move did not seem to do much else.
For a normal individual, slicing an arrow in half, mid-trajectory would be impossible, however, for Leo with his superior agility and reflexes, achieving this feat was nothing much.
However, for Arlen this was a big shock, as he peered towards Leo with his eyes wide open in shock.
"No wonder he killed Denver, this kid is a bit of a monster…" Arlen murmured, as his eyes finally met those of Leo.
Tracing the path of the incoming arrow, Leo finally spotted the enemy who was somehow matching him step for step while carrying a bow and a quiver full of arrows.
His mixed gray and brown bearded appearance and receding hairline told Leo that he was an old monster, most likely one of the game's legendary NPCs, however, Leo was not impressed.
Narrowing his eyes, Leo bared his teeth to show that he was not afraid of the opponent, although he seemed to be on the run.
In response, Arlen pulled out yet another arrow from his quiver and without missing a step notched it on, as he prepared to take aim while running.
"Oh no… no… no, now that I see you, you're fucked" Leo muttered, as he began to run haphazardly.
Sometimes he ran straight, sometimes he randomly veered to a side, before explosively changing direction and speed to make tracking him more difficult.
From a distance, Arlen frowned, as much to his surprise, he could not get a lock on Leo, his haphazard movements throwing his pursuer off.
"It seems I can't get a confident shot on this fast prey from this distance, first I'll have to close the gap–" Arlen muttered, as he picked up the pace and tried to close the gap between himself and Leo from over 700 meters to under 100.
This was of-course easier said than done, as while he was fast, so was Leo.
For every meter that he gained on Leo, they seemed to have ran four, as it did not take long before Arlen realized that at this rate it would take him a good hour or two of constant running before he could actually catch his opponent.
"Very well then, I'll catch you on the bridge…." Arlen muttered, as while Leo moved erratically on the road, he would not have so much freedom while on the bridge, giving Arlen the chance he needed to shoot Leo down.
Freezing, he hence nocked another arrow, and prepared to unleash yet another Silent Shot.
Meanwhile, observing the enemy's change in demeanor after he paused, Leo too got a read on what was going to happen next.
Picking up his pace, he turned his back towards the opponent and began running at his top speed in his natural posture, as suddenly, he began to widen the gap between himself and Arlen at an absurd pace.
The Archer shook, Realized only then that the only reason he was even keeping up with the young Assassin's speed was because he was running on his heels, but now that he assumed his natural posture, his true speed came out.
"What a beast!" Arlen commented, as he steadied his breathing and prepared for the shot, visualizing it's trajectory and exact distance.
828 meters, he thought, visualizing the point of contact at precisely the halfway point of the bridge, as he let go of yet another [Silent Shot].
********
Meanwhile, Leo ran like a madman when he approached the bridge, the smell of freedom filling his nostrils already.
"Just 20 more meters…." He muttered, as he dashed at full speed, covering half the length of the bridge in just under two breaths.
However, then the arrow hit!
-1700.
An arrow pierced through his back right through the middle and came out of his chest, as he felt his vision nearly black out from the pain.
His legs wobbled and for a second he felt like they could not support his weight anymore. However, crawling on all fours, he continued to move, pushing through those last 10 meters like a man possessed.
[System Notification:- Congratulations to 'TheBoss', for reaching the 'Rebel Zone'. The hunt has been called off! Your location will no longer be exposed during the next gaming day!]
Only when Leo saw this notification flash past his screen, did he finally breathe a sigh of relief.
Only 30% of his HP bar remained, however, he was no longer afraid of death.
Instead, he stood back to his feet and faced his chasing opponent defiantly, as he clenched a dagger with his one good arm hard and pointed it towards Arlen.
"Come…. I'm ready to face you now" Leo declared, as with the psychological pressure of reaching the safe-zone now gone, Leo once again returned to his ruthless best.
The opponent had dared make him run like a chicken for so long, it was finally his turn to make the enemy pay!

chapters.title: Chapter 722 - 722: Grim Reaper
chapters.content:
Arlen was confused on why Leo suddenly stopped running once he crossed the bridge?
If he wanted to fight, he could have done so anytime? However, stopping so abruptly made no sense to him…..
'Is he planning to cut the ropes of the bridge? Is he trying to pull some childish trick and drop me in the water?' Arlen wondered, as watching Leo stand so close to the bridge and the supporting ropes, Arlen wondered what his intentions were?
The current below the bridge was weak at best and the bridge was mostly for convenience and not necessity.
Even if he fell, it wasn't like coming ashore on the other side was particularly difficult, and hence Arlen felt even more confused by Leo's movements.
Cautious as he was, he slowed down his run and notched another arrow, as he cautiously approached Leo, one step at a time.
"I'm Master Arlen…" he shouted once he was within earshot range, "I thought it was best I introduce myself before I kill you" he clarified, as Leo's eyes darkened.
"I'm 'TheBoss', but you can call me Grim Reaper you weasly ass bitch, because I'll be reaping your soul today" Leo declared, not holding back at all, as he gestured for Arlen to cross the bridge if he dared.
For a moment, Arlen hesitated, feeling unsure of what his opponent planned, however, after seeing the arrow still sticking out of his opponent's midsection, he decided to approach nonetheless.
*Thud*
*Thud*
*Thud*
The wooden plans of the bridge creaked everytime Arlen took a step, as he pointed the arrow straight towards Leo's head.
With every step that he took, he felt more and more assured of hitting Leo straight in the head, as based on the speed of his shot, he knew it would be impossible to defend.
Finally, when he was a quarter way into the bridge and the distance between him and Leo was merely 15 meters, he finally loosened his shot, thinking that his opponent was as good as dead.
'Rest in hell…' he thought, observing the arrow fly with calm confidence, as he saw it zooming towards Leo in a flash.
*Zrrrr*
In a blur, Leo moved his head at the last possible microsecond, dodging the move completely, as he retaliated by throwing the dagger in his palm which surprisingly found its mark, precisely slashing the string on his opponents bow, before whistling past his neck, drawing a single drop of blood.
"What?" Arlen muttered in shock as it all happened in a blur.
He could not even notice his opponents movement, much less react to it, as by the time his brain processed that his opponent had dodged his attack, and that too from this close of a range, he already had his bowstring cut in half.
Bewildered, he looked at the now straight bow in his hand and then towards Leo in surprise, as the grin on Leo's face broadened.
"Aghhh… the scent of fear…. So refreshing" Leo said like a maniac, as he pulled out yet another dagger from his belt.
"How?" Arlen muttered in utter disbelief, as he had never seen a man like Leo ever before in his life.
His reflexes were beyond those of a normal human, as dodging his full power shot from a mere 15 meters range was supposed to be impossible!
However, what Arlen did not know was that his reflexes were actually Leo's strongest suit even before he ever started to play the game Terra Nova Online.
During his initial evaluation, reflex test was the one where he got a SSS evaluation, and his senses had only been sharpened since then.
As his agility and constitution improved so did his reflexes, as his muscles became better attuned to his neural signals and could execute the commands they gave faster.
However, the breaking point came from the marrow meditation manual method.
After achieving minor success, Leo's new cells helped increase his innate talent even more, which was why he could dodge Arlen's attack now with such ease.
"Hohoho. What happened now? Lost all your confidence you one trick pony? Don't have the balls to hunt me with your bow destroyed?" Leo taunted, as he took a step onto the bridge, prompting Arlen to take one back.
An Archer without a bow was like a mage without mana, and in this state Arlen knew he was no match for his opponent who was a freak and a killer.
"I don't know why you're hunting me, but I'll give you one chance to fuck off. Run and never show me your face again because next time I see you, I will kill you" Leo threatened, as he gave Arlen one last chance to run.
"Run? Never…. You killed my sworn brother Denver, I will kill you or be killed here today!" Arlen declared, as Leo shrugged his shoulders and pointed towards the sky.
"Very well…. Look there, your wish is about to be granted" Leo said pointing towards the sky, as somehow because of his casually attitude and confidence, Arlen really did end up looking towards the sky, becoming momentarily distracted.
However, this was a fatal mistake.
In a split second, Leo charged the full distance of 15 meters between them, pouncing upon Arlen with a [Kill Strike].
'Not good…' Arlen thought, noticing Leo's movement once he was already halfway, as he tried to block with the handle of his bow.
*Clink*
Metal clashed against metal and Arlen was pushed a couple steps back because of Leo's momentum, however, before he could ever recover, Leo sent a kick to his face, making him keel over, before following through with a dagger plunge straight into his brain.
"That's what it feels like to be impaled…." Leo pointed out, before impaling him a few more times at critical spots.
"Like I said…. I'm the Grim reaper" Leo said at the end, as he claimed yet another master warrior's life on the same crazy day.

chapters.title: Chapter 723 - 723: Psychological Effects
chapters.content:
[Congratulations to the player 'TheBoss', for successfully defeating Master Arlen (Lv734) who is one of the game's world bosses.
You have gained
+2 levels
+1 broken rangers bow (Semi-Legendary)
+1 Full heal potion
+1 Quiver of arrows (Unique) ]
Leo received a system message informing him of all the loot he had obtained from killing Arlen, however, he ignored all of the items mentioned on the list, emptying them from his inventory apart from the Full Heal potion.
Leo was not a hoarder, and having no use for a broken Bow and a quiver of arrows, he decided to leave it all behind for some lucky passerby to find, as although he understood that the bow and arrows had quite a lot of value attached to them, he simply did not care.
He did not lack funds at the slightest within the game and understood that a couple hundred thousand coins here or there were not going to change his life.
*Gulp*
Focusing instead on the arrow embedded in his chest, Leo decided to remove it while he gulped down the Full heal potion, to quickly get rid of the injuries ailing his battered body.
"What a fucking day…." he mumbled, after finishing the drink, as he wiped off the last drop from over his chin and smacked it onto the dry ground below.
Immediately, he began feeling the effects of the potion as his wounds began to heal up, and soon, the injury warning that flashed on his gaming screen, warning him that he was bleeding constantly, faded away, in-turn opening-up the option for him to log-out atlast.
"Level 992…. Not bad" Leo jested before he logged out, as he felt proud with the results of this last endeavor overall.
********
(Real World, the VIP sector)
As soon as Leo put aside the VR helmet, he felt a wave of mental fatigue instantly hit him, as his head felt much heavier than usual as if it were filled with lead.
"I've been playing this game non-stop for over 5 days now. This is without a doubt my longest gaming run yet" Leo observed, as immediately a wave of thirst and hunger hit him.
In the five days where he had been playing Terra Nova Online non-stop, his bodily functions had apparently taken a hit.
His clothes smelled disgusting, as his body was forced to eliminate waste buildups through the sweat pores, and his stomach felt rumbling and shrunken from its usual size from not receiving a single grain of food in five days.
Thankfully, he was a master level warrior now and not a weak human, for he could bear longer stints of hunger better than normal humans, who would look pale and weak after not eating for 5 days.
"Where's the damn water?" He wondered, as he walked into the kitchen and placed his mouth directly under the faucet that produced drinking water.
*Gulp*
*Gulp*
Drinking like a maniac, he drank at least a couple liters of water before finally being satiated, as only then did he pause to take in a deep breath.
*GASP*
Gasping loudly, Leo chuckled as he finally understood the downside of gaming for too long, as without nourishment pipes connected to the players bodies, continuing to play for days was not a feasible option.
"All the nutrients in my body must have been redirected to my brain for the past 5 days. However, once I ran out of those, my in-game performance was sure to dip.
I'd say my current limit is 7 days, if I'm to ever try going this long without a break again" Leo calculated, as he moved over to the fridge and began devouring the raw fruits and vegetables within, without a care in the world about the mess he left behind.
*Crunch*
*Crush*
Eating haphazardly, he swallowed anything edible he could get his hands at, as the hunger in his stomach only seemed to flare after he took the first bite of food.
As he devoured the contents of the fridge like a starved beast, Leo's mind began to clear. The fog of exhaustion from five days of non-stop gaming slowly lifted, replaced by a sharp, cold clarity that only came from pushing his body to the edge.
His hands trembled slightly—not from weakness, but from the bloodlust still coursing through his veins after his intense battle with Master Arlen, as despite the battle being over, Leo still felt unnaturally aggressive for no reason.
"What's wrong with me? I'm back home… Then why am I still craving blood? Why do I have the urge to pull out a dagger and start hacking away at a body….. I need to calm down…" Leo said, looking at his trembling hands, as he tried to get a grip on himself.
For a while, his hands did not stop trembling, however, after a lot of conscious effort, he returned back to normal, with the bloodlust leaving him, as he began to eat once more at a normal pace.
Having just engaged in a large-scale massacre, Leo found himself battling with the psychological aftermath of that event, as it seemed to have left a scar on his brain.
Surprisingly, he did not feel guilty about his actions, even though he did murder a child, as instead he felt proud of the fact that he went against so many men and still walked out alive in what he assessed to be a broken state of mind.
Instead of worrying over what he had done, he felt a sense of pride and satisfaction in his work that was morally wrong on many modern earth levels.
"I finally understand why historic gods and kings were such insufferable pricks…. Once you begin to feel invincible, it's really impossible to restrain your desires" Leo noted, as he opened and closed his palm while breathing deeply.
Today, he was feeling invincible, however, he did not wish to turn into a prick, and hence after introspecting he immediately began to backtrack.
It took a lot of mental tempering for him to return to his usual humble, family loving state of mind, however, thankfully he managed to do so before Amanda walked into the kitchen, as before her, he only presented his best self.
"Ohhh? What the hell love, you've made a complete mess here…. Hahaha" Amanda noted, walking into the kitchen, as she noticed Leo's crude way of eating food and could not contain her laughter.
Smiling back, Leo threw away the half eaten apple and rushed to embrace her, opening his wide arms.
---------

chapters.title: Chapter 724 - 724: Young Love
chapters.content:
"I'm back…" Leo declared wrapping his arms around Amanda, as she hugged him back warmly.
"Ewww…. You stink" she noted, pinching her nose, as Leo smiled even wider.
"And you smell like fresh flowers" Leo retorted, making a point to sniff her hair, which made Amanda's scalp tickle.
Giggling, she tried to pull away from Leo, however, Leo forced her to stay put.
"If I'm going to take a bath, you're definitely joining me–" he declared, as Amanda's eyes brightened up at that idea.
"Why not?" She replied, as she started to frisk his back.
"You'll need the extra pair of hands to reach spots you otherwise can't reach" she said in a sexy voice, stretching out each word, as she tried to arouse Leo.
Swallowing a mouthful of saliva, Leo excitedly followed her into the bathroom, his manhood already up and ready for yet another battle, as all the lingering traces of his bloodlust simply evaporated away without a trace.
By embracing Amanda, he felt grounded to reality once more, as all the mental problems he was facing seemed to fade away.
Over the next two hours, he had a thorough scrubbing session, where he sweated and cleaned in a recurring cycle and sometimes helped clean Amanda too.
In the end, it was Amanda who walked out of the shower with wobbly legs, as she could no longer walk straight anymore.
"T-that… mmm… that makes up for you not seeing me the last few days," Amanda murmured with a soft smile as Leo pulled her into a deep, lingering kiss.
With each passing day, his love for Amanda only seemed to grow stronger, as in every way, she felt like the perfect partner for him.
She was kind, understanding, and patient, and although he was not the easiest guy to be with, she never made him feel like he was anything but perfect.
Because of his gaming commitments, he failed to meet her for the last five days straight and even ignored her messages within the game asking his well being, because he was simply too overwhelmed to reply, however, despite these issues bothering her secretly, Amanda chose not to voice her frustrations immediately during their reunion.
Instead, she greeted him with warmth and affection, welcoming him home with her radiant smile, as it was only after they had spent quality time together, reconnecting and enjoying each other's company, that she gently brought up the issue in the most subtle way possible.
It was this subtle approach that Leo appreciated most about her, as he was acutely aware of his own shortcomings, however, often found himself becoming defensive when confronted about the same directly.
Hence, Amanda's calm and considerate way of addressing things, made it easier for him to reflect and take accountability, which was one of the many reasons he felt so deeply for her.
From him, Amanda never demanded perfection—only sincerity. And for Amanda, Leo was willing to try his best every single day.
"I'm sorry babe, this mission was important, but if I'm honest I could have found a moment to reply to your messages within the game…. I'll do better next time" Leo said, after pulling away from the kiss, as Amanda's lips automatically curved into a big smile.
She knew Leo was busy within the game world, as she tracked him live just like half the righteous faction server, however, she expected him to reply at night when he had some peace and quiet.
As his girlfriend, she could not help but worry for his well-being, and only wanted to know if he was doing okay.
However, not wanting to push the subject, she did not directly voice her concerns and only tried to subtly imply them.
Thankfully, Leo was not obnoxious and got the hint immediately and even apologized where he should.
This of-course put Amanda's heart to ease immediately, as just like how Leo appreciated her measured approach to confrontation, she appreciated his ability to take accountability, as for her, this quality of Leo only made him a more attractive man.
Hugging him tight, she did not respond to his words with words and only replied with actions as she showed her approval happily.
Just like Leo, she too found herself falling deeper and deeper in love with him everyday, and could not wait to start a family with him, once they landed on planet Radiance.
'Will he give me kids if I ask?' Amanda wondered once the thought popped in her head, as she suddenly blushed hard.
Traditionally kids were meant to be had between husband and wife after being bonded through marriage, however, Leo had yet to properly propose.
Amanda knew that they were going to marry sometime in the future, however, Leo did not seem to be as keen as her for the same.
'I hope once we reach planet Terra Nova, the dynamic between us doesn't change' Amanda hoped, as she clung onto Leo just a bit tighter.
Meanwhile, on the other side of the cuddling, Leo's thoughts veered to the half-eaten apple that he left in the kitchen before meeting Amanda, as he wondered if he could go back and finish it now?
'That apple was unexpectedly juicy… sucking on it was almost half as good as sucking on Amanda's tits' Leo thought, as he really admired the quality of the produce.
His eyes then veered towards Amanda's breasts, as his manhood suddenly popped up for round 4.
'Easy there big guy….. relax' Leo thought, desperately trying to control his manhood from poking Amanda's belly, however, it was to no avail.
"Seriously Leo? Again?" Amanda asked, chuckling, as Leo simply shrugged his shoulders helplessly in response.
"What can I do… I love you too much" Leo admitted, as Amanda crossed her legs and pushed him away.
"Absolutely not, my legs already feel jelly, there won't be a round four" She said, running away from Leo, who hopelessly chased after her while laughing heartily.
—------
