chapters.title: Chapter 725 - 725: Falling Apart
chapters.content:
(Next day, Terra Nova Online)
The next day, as players returned to the world of Terra Nova, they were surprised to see that there was no new notification exposing TheBoss's live location.
Apparently, 'TheBoss' had safely made it back to the safe-zone over the night, completely dashing all hopes that the righteous faction harbored to punish him.
"This is unfair…. This game is rigged… how can one man get away with so much slaughter? Is he really stronger than an entire faction?"
"As a righteous faction player, I'm ashamed to belong to this faction today…. If we cannot collectively bring down one man, we deserve to lose the faction war."
"What do you mean he killed yet another world boss? That's four of them now!"
The righteous faction players were greatly disheartened to find out that Leo escaped, their collective morale sinking to an all-time low.
But as they began to complain on the forums to try and blow off some steam, they quickly realized that his escape was the least of their current problems.
Reports began flooding in about rebel forces surging across the borders, with them attacking every major town and village along the line of control, which made the righteous faction players feel extremely concerned over their immediate future.
Stronghold after stronghold fell with unprecedented speed, as the righteous faction's debilitated forces failed to mount effective resistance.
"Another outpost lost at the Southern Front. The rebels are pushing directly toward MudStomp village!"
"They've taken Hempstead Keep too… How is this happening so fast? The fighting at Hempstead started only a couple hours ago!"
The death of the Emperor had thrown the righteous faction into utter chaos, and the rebels wasted no time exploiting the vacuum.
With the righteous faction NPCs debuffed 50% and the players 35%, the rebels managed to steamroll through their outposts with ease, as the first day of fighting seemed to be overwhelmingly in their favor.
With every outpost they conquered, the rebels gained resources, ground, and most importantly, momentum.
While the righteous faction players, weakened by the stat debuff and plagued by internal disorganization, found themselves scrambling to defend territory that was slipping away faster than they could react.
"Forget chasing TheBoss. If we don't regroup now, there won't be a faction left to defend!" one guild leader exclaimed in desperation, as he called on help from the righteous faction players to come help him defend the village he was an administrator for, however, his call for help remained unheard.
With the rebels marching along every major road, every major route. There were dozens of villages under siege under any given moment and helping just him out was not possible.
To make matters worse, righteous faction guilds began to backstab other righteous faction guilds in these times of unrest, as a massive civil war broke off in the northern and western duchies, with major guilds taking up arms against one another.
********
(In the North)
Leo's allies in the North were the three biggest guilds in the region, who already controlled over 20% of the lands, administering them under the authority of the North Duke.
However, with the North Duke dead, these guilds wasted no time turning against their former allies, as in a move that sent shockwaves through the region, they declared independence, citing the lack of leadership and protection from the central government as justification for their rebellion.
Then, riding out of their territories with thousands of guild members and well-armed NPC mercenaries under their control, they launched a coordinated series of attacks on neighboring regions.
Their strategy was ruthless and efficient: striking key supply depots, capturing strategic outposts, and overwhelming local defenses in a well-planned pincer hold.
The local defenders, already weakened by the 50% stat debuff and disheartened by the death of their leader, were caught completely off guard.
Dozens of outposts fell within hours, as the defenders found themselves betrayed by the very people they once considered allies.
"Traitors!" one commander yelled as his small garrison was overwhelmed. "The North will burn because of you!"
But the guild leaders showed no remorse. Their goal was clear—to seize as much land and power as possible before order could be restored, as they knew that in this chaos, whoever controlled the most territory would dictate the terms of the future.
What made the situation even more dire was that these guilds weren't the only ones betraying the righteous faction.
Across the Northern and Western Duchies, smaller guilds and independent NPC lords began to splinter off, either joining the rebels outright or carving out their own fiefdoms.
Villages that had once been under the protection of righteous faction guilds found themselves looted by the very forces meant to defend them, as the common farmers and merchants were left to fend for themselves, caught in the crossfire of a civil war that seemed to have no end in sight.
"How can we hold the line when our own people stab us in the back?" a righteous faction player vented in frustration on the forums, however, the guilt shaming stopped noone.
The righteous faction was a sinking ship and even the rats were ready to jump overboard now.
The backstabbing made it impossible for the remaining loyalist lords to mount any meaningful resistance, as every time they attempted to muster troops to push back against the rebels, they were blindsided by another betrayal from within.
In the end, what should have been a united defense quickly devolved into infighting, with guilds prioritizing personal gain over the survival of their faction.
Within a single day, Leo's three allied guilds in the north, who had been preparing for this fight for months, expanded their territory under control from 20% to 35%, making massive strides all around.
They were condemned for their greed, however, nobody knew yet that they planned to eventually bend the knee to Leo, as that piece of news were reserved for after StrongHaven fell.
—-------

chapters.title: Chapter 726 - 726: Returning Home
chapters.content:
(The next day, Briarhelm)
2 days after Leo killed the Emperor, the fighting across the Empire only grew more fierce, with the rebels making gains everywhere apart from the West.
Cervantez, and the DarkSky guild having prepared in advance for this eventual attack, did not allow the WhiteSaber guild members to run wild in the West, becoming a stubborn thorn in their side.
Having already dug-up defensive posts and stocked up on significant ammunition, the DarkSky guild was not afraid of a prolonged battle of arbitrage, and were prepared to face a long siege.
However, despite them holding the advantage in these early stages, for now, the war in the West was only starting and too soon to call, as the fall of a couple villages could easily turn the tide against them.
******
Sitting in his office, ChaosBringer glanced over all the new pieces of news coming about the war, when suddenly he heard a knock on his door.
*Knock*
*Knock*
"Come in" ChaosBringer said, as an informant wearing the Uprising's uniform walked in, appearing slightly out of breath as if having sprinted here with urgency.
"Lord ChaosBringer, it's confirmed, someone has spotted Ben Faulkner and Lord Boss's pet entering the gates…." An uprising member said, as he informed ChaosBringer of Dumpy and Ben's arrival.
"And what about the lord himself?" ChaosBringer inquired, as the informant shook his head in denial.
"Unfortunately, he doesn't seem to be with them, but with how stealthy he is, I'm not sure if we can rely on our eyes to detect him" he informed, as ChaosBringer dismissed him with a curt gesture.
"Our Lord is back home victorious! This is a cause for great celebration…. I must go at once!" ChaosBringer said excitedly, as he straightened his attire and began to fix every last loose strand in his hair.
"Perfect–" he declared after a while, as he exited his office and began making his way towards Leo's quarters where he stayed with Ben and Dumpy alone.
**********
(Outside Leo's residence in Briarhelm)
ChaosBringer arrived outside Leo's residence in Briarhelm, just before Ben and Dumpy made their way there, allowing him to greet the duo and congratulate them on their victorious return.
"Agh, this lowly one greets Master Ben Faulkner and the esteemed Lord Dumpy on their victorious return from a legendary adventure.
If it pleases you, this lowly one plans to hold a grand feast in your honor tonight in Briarhelm, you only have to give a command" ChaosBringer said, bowing politely, as Dumpy beamed listening to those words.
"I remember you… lowly human, you're one of the few sensible ones that greet my Lord Father correctly…. I will accept your congratulations" Dumpy said, as ChaosBringer bowed even deeply when being acknowledged by the mythical beast.
"Through my own visual device, I tracked your adventure, and I must say, it was quite the treat to watch, your strength and intelligence knows no bounds–" ChaosBringer said, as although he did not use terms like 'Livestream' before an NPC, he conveyed the fact that he had watched Dumpy in action, which quite pleased the narcissistic frog.
"My failures are mine, however, my achievements only belong to my Lord Father. It's because of him that I'm strong today, so all the credit must go to him" Dumpy said, while growing a few inches in size as he visibly puffed up from the compliments.
Ben however was more measured and did not seem too impressed by ChaosBringers flattery, as he simply dismissed ChaosBringer with a few short words.
"We are tired after a long journey, there's no need for elaborate banquets tonight, you can perhaps host one when my disciple returns" Ben said, as ChaosBringer bowed, getting the message.
It seemed like 'TheBoss' had not travelled with them back to Briarhelm and was going to take a few days more to return.
"I will not disturb you then, I have held you long enough" ChaosBringer said, backpedaling as he left, as he did not dare turn his back on Ben or Dumpy, as it would be a great sign of disrespect.
Only when the two of them were out of his field of vision, did ChaosBringer finally turn and let out a deep sigh, as he seemed slightly disappointed that 'TheBoss' did not return with his crew.
"I wanted to talk about strategy with God Boss… his immeasurable wisdom would be invaluable in such important times. However, I must make-do now with my own instincts.
He's already done enough, if I cannot topple the Empire even now, then I probably don't deserve the 'instigator' class" ChaosBringer murmured to himself, as he made his way back to his office.
*********
(Meanwhile Cervantez)
Only now did Cervantez feel the backlash of letting Luke walk out of his guild, as once the war officially began, Luke's absence started to be sorely felt within the guild.
Luke was the DarkSky guilds foremost strategist and with him overseeing missions, Cervantez used to be quite mentally free.
However, ever since Luke had left, he had to pick-up the workload of the vice guild master as well, making his usual work day extremely busy.
On the bright side, the light faction seemed to be imploding, with every region but the Western Duchy suffering massive losses, which was perfect for Cervantez and his vision to make the West the last holdout.
However, on the down side, it seemed as if the leadership skills of his core team were not as good as Luke's, as despite having better positioning to defend villages and frontier territories, the guild still faced massive daily losses in their fight against the WhiteSabers.
Hence, while the bigger picture that Cervantez had for the guild, which was to turn them into the last resistance against the rebels, was still intact.
The execution of those plans seemed to be not up to par, putting additional stress on him as their leader.
—-----

chapters.title: Chapter 727 - 727: Consequences
chapters.content:
(One Week Later, Briarhelm)
Nine days after Leo killed the Emperor, the rebels succeeded in fully unifying the Southern Duchy under their control.
With relentless progress each day, it took them just over a week to eliminate the final holdout—an NPC viscount—securing absolute dominance over the Duchy.
This victory had significant geographic implications, as now the rebels effectively cornered the Empire's forces from two fronts, cutting them off completely from the East and South.
However, while the rebel victory in the south was concerning for many who resided in central and western regions, it was even worse for the righteous faction players who were still stuck in the south, as they had been stripped away of all their rights and relegated to the status of prisoners of war.
Many among them began to regret their choice to remain in the South and resist the rebels, as in hindsight, they realized their beliefs had been naive at best and delusional at worst.
Raised on platitudes like "Wars are not won by the number of soldiers fighting them" and "Courage can overcome any adversity," they had clung to the hope that sheer determination and heart could halt the rebel advance. But the harsh reality proved them wrong.
The rebel advance was unstoppable, and with higher numbers and greater physical strength, the rebels sweeped any battlefield they entered cleanly, with the righteous faction players having no chance to effectively fight back.
Once captured and defeated, the righteous faction players in the South were presented with two stark choices by the system.
The first option allowed them to surrender and pledge their allegiance to the rebels, effectively jumping ship and changing sides, but to do this, one had to pay a steep cost.
Every player wanting to take this route had to forfeit 50% of the items in their inventory, which included their hard-earned weapons, armor, rare items, and even in-game currency or other assets that many had spent years acquiring.
The items were to drop randomly, with the victorious rebels who captured them being allowed to loot it freely.
However, if one felt unsatisfied with this choice, the second one was even worse.
The second option that the system offered was an outright 30 day gaming ban, which for many was too harsh of a penalty to accept.
The second penalty was essentially a forced exile, severing one from the game's progress and community, significantly reducing their chances for a promotion during the next evaluation.
Hence, stuck between a rock and a hard place, the majority chose to convert and endure the humiliation of surrender, rather than not playing the game at all.
This meant that the defenders became the predators, with the rebels gaining hundreds of thousands of new members, all of whom were deployed straight into battle into the central regions, while the winners of the South looted their dropped spoils.
Many of the rebels openly boasted about their newfound riches and mocked the righteous faction players' years of effort on the forums, and how their effort was now being reduced to nothing but loot.
However, the humiliation didn't stop at simply looting.
Former righteous faction players were paraded before their peers as symbols of the rebel victory, and public executions of NPCs loyal to the Empire were made before the common masses to serve as a grim warning against armed civil unrest.
The rebel victory was not just a conquest of land but a brutal dismantling of morale, leaving the righteous faction players broken, looted, and humiliated in its wake.
"Years of grinding gone in minutes. I can't believe this is how it ends," one defeated player muttered in despair on the forums, his post quickly gaining hundreds of likes from others who shared the sentiment.
"I had two unique grade items—both now gone! This system is a joke. What kind of choice is this? Either lose everything or get banned. How is that fair?" Another added, his case being similar to that of many.
"That's what you get for standing in our way. Thanks for the loot—I've never been this rich before." A rebel player gloated, as hundreds others joined in the mockery, sharing photos of their new loot on the forums with one even gleefully posting, "Southern gear firesale, courtesy of the righteous losers. Come and get it!"
Such gloating after months of online banter between the two sides only made the rivalry worse as the righteous faction players felt like they were being subjected to unprecedented social oppression.
"We need to hold strong in the central territories. The rebels are winning now, but they can't maintain this momentum forever." One righteous player wrote, trying to rally support, however, others weren't so optimistic.
"What's the point? They've got hundreds of thousands of our faction's players already switching sides. It's over."
"Honestly, they deserve it. The righteous faction has been the more privileged side for years now. But it looks like it's our turn to suffer."
"This isn't justice; it's cruelty. If the rebels win this way, they're no better than the Empire they're fighting against."
No longer did the righteous faction players have the same brashness and arrogance about their texts as they did a month ago, as slowly but surely, their voices seemed more humbled.
Among the chaos, a troll chimed in: "LMAO, righteous faction players crying? Just take the ban and touch grass for 30 days. Problem solved."
The forums buzzed with posts debating the ethics of the rebels' actions, the righteousness of their cause, and the hopelessness of those who had been caught in the crossfire.
Mixed reactions painted a vivid picture of a player base divided, each post revealing a different perspective, but Leo simply looked at all this mess unfolding with emotionless eyes.
Having logged into the game a full 9 days after his last adventure, Leo felt the online discussions ongoing on the forums to be utterly pointless, as to him, yapping and complaining when nothing positive was ever going to come from it seemed pointless.
"Fools…" he muttered, closing the chat, as he finally made his way through the gates of Briarhelm, to finally return safely to his temporary base of operations.

chapters.title: Chapter 728 - 728: The Anomaly
chapters.content:
(Meanwhile On The Arc Ship)
Raya monitored the increasing volatility within the game, especially within the forums with a concerned face.
"The system options for losing the war are very harsh, the players are not happy at all" She muttered, observing the situation, as sitting beside her, Raven raised an eyebrow.
"How bad is it? Let me take a look–" Raven said, as he moved away from his station and walked over to Raya's, peering over her shoulder to look at her monitor.
"Over 75% of the righteous faction players are worried that their faction will lose the war and that they will be forced to become prisoners of war, 17% are unsure on how they want to process this news and only 8% believe they can still win–" Raya pointed out, placing her finger on the screen where this information was displayed.
"Yeah and it looks like almost 99.8% righteous faction players are unhappy with the system penalties for losing the war, saying that it's excessive, while 0.2% feel excited at the prospect of defeating and looting the rebels" Raven read from the screen as frown lines appeared on his forehead.
These were some of the highest disapproval numbers they had ever seen since the game began, and it seemed like a cause for concern.
"They're brats…" a voice came from the control room's entrance, as in-came Captain Kid, with usual sharp uniform and practiced cadence.
"This game is designed to prepare them for life on planet Terra Nova, not to keep them entertained on their way there.
Once we land on planet Terra Nova, many of these players will be expected to take part in actual wars with actual consequences, where they can die fighting, be captured as prisoners, or cut open and sold for organs.
The new world they are headed to is no sunshine and rainbows and hence we will not alter the penalties.
Losing just 50% of your assets after losing a war is actually a merciful outcome. If they can't handle this, they won't survive on Terra Nova" Kid said ruthlessly as both Raya and Raven fell silent.
They knew captain kid was not wrong, it was a dog eat dog universe out there and their job as arc ship operators was to prepare the passengers for that exact world.
Hence even though the system penalties seemed like a bitter pill to swallow, in reality it was a watered down version of what many may have to endure going ahead.
"What's the status of the anomaly? Has he finally returned to the game?" Captain Kid asked, as Raven quickly returned to his work post and opened a report for Captain Kid to glance over.
It had been 9 days already since he killed the Emperor and surprisingly he had not logged into the game a single day since.
"Allowing him to choose his gaming hours was a mistake…. By letting him play non-stop for days, we have created a monster we can no longer control, 4 world bosses are dead, defeated in one on one battles and he is eyeing the dragon next…. Honestly, that boy has started to scare me to my core" Kid said, as he shuddered involuntarily thinking about Leo.
"The anomaly has not shown signs of dual-cerebral processing since logging back on, it seems like his secondary cortex has not fully activated. But heat signatures from his gaming helmet suggest that he has an increased blood flow to that region of his brain, compared to data recorded from a fortnight ago–" Raven reported, as captain kid let out a deep sigh.
[Parallel Processing] was an innate skill that only a handful of super talented geniuses in the universe were ever born with.
For most individuals, their subconscious cerebral reflex was only catered towards survival.
Hence, if they touched a super hot surface, their muscles knew how to pull away without their brain commanding them to do so, however, that was the limit of their abilities.
However, for the chosen few with an active subconscious cerebral cortex, they could train their muscle reflexes to do much more than just survive, and in his last battle with Arlen, Leo seemed to do just that.
In the final moments of their fight, where he evaded Arlen's arrow and countered by cutting off his bowstring, it was an action so fast that it exceeded the thinking and processing speed of a normal brain.
Instead, it was his subconscious reflexes that took over, not only helping him dodge, but also countering with an attack he did not actively plan for, as battle reflexes seemed to now be ingrained in his very being.
This movement was a sign that Leo had started to tap into his subconscious cerebral cortex and started to unlock the ability [Parallel Processing] which was going to make him a super anomaly in the future.
Even amongst [Master] and [Grandmaster] warriors capable of destroying armies on their own, fighters having [Parallel Processing] ability were deemed a cut above their peers, as they were considered heaven sent battle geniuses.
If Captain Kid thought that Leo was special enough before, he was absolutely stunned when he showed potential for this rare ability, as since that day he simply began referring to Leo as 'The Anomaly' instead of his name.
For now, it seemed like he had not mastered how to tap-into Parallel Processing at will and could only enter that state when completely immersed in a battle, however, with him meditating and producing new superior blood cells everyday, Kid had no doubt that he would learn to actively control it in a few months.
"I can't even begin to fathom what this kid's future holds as there's sure to be a frenzy to recruit him when we land on Terra Nova.
There has never been a genius quite like him before and he has not even unlocked the eight skill slot yet, which he most likely will in the future" Kid said, sighing nonstop after each sentence, as he could not see a ceiling to Leo's achievements.
"Don't forget…. He may even kill the dragon" Raven added, as at that point Kid simply gave up on thinking.
If Leo did manage to defeat the dragon and the demon king, he would become the only player ever to truly finish the tutorial game, completing all three of its most difficult quests.

chapters.title: Chapter 729 - 729: Changing Impact
chapters.content:
Leo's return to Briarhelm was nothing short of legendary.
From the second that the guards at the gates spotted him, the news of his return spread through the city like wildfire, with droves of rebels crowding the streets to watch him pass.
With his mask broken, Leo wore a thin black cloth over his face to cover some of his features, adorning a different look to his usual staple of a rigid mask and cold eyes.
He walked in a leisurely manner, with both his hands tucked behind his back, not trying to do anything special. However, to the onlookers, he seemed regal, his stride effortlessly captivating, as if he walked on the wind, his feet barely touching the ground.
The streets of Briarhelm were eerily silent despite the massive crowd that had gathered.
Every pair of eyes seemed to remain locked onto him as he walked, some filled with admiration, others with disbelief, but all bearing a reverence that words could not describe.
No one dared to obstruct his path as he walked, as they instinctively parted like the sea before him, creating a perfectly clear walkway for the man who had single-handedly toppled an empire's foundation.
Murmurs of awe rippled through the crowd as Leo passed by.
"It's him!… It's the King-Slayer."
"Did you see his walk? It's like he's floating!"
"I can't believe I'm this close to TheBoss. This is a moment I'll tell my grandchildren about."
But it wasn't just words. The crowd's reverence was visible in their actions.
As Leo walked by, his presence left an almost ethereal stillness in the air for the cult members of his church.
The dirt beneath his feet became sacred ground the moment he stepped past it, as church members scrambled to get some.
Once he had moved a few steps ahead, a frenzy erupted behind him as many scrambled to scoop up handfuls of the dirt he had walked on.
"It's the dirt where he walked! It has to bring good fortune in battles!" one player exclaimed, holding a fistful of soil as if it were a priceless treasure.
Another shouted, "Don't you dare sell it for money or trade it with others for puny monetary gains! That's not just dirt—that's a relic!"
Even the NPCs, though programmed to follow their routines, halted their activities, standing in rapt attention, captivated by Leo's presence, as the crowd and their reverence towards him made them curious about his stature.
Around him, some church members stood frozen, tears glistening in their eyes as they felt overwhelmed by the sheer gravity of being in his proximity, with the most devout believers showing the most exaggerated reactions.
However, while the cultists cried like babies, the moderate ones captured the moment in-game, as screenshots and recordings of his return to Briarhelm flooded the Terra Nova forums within seconds, each post glorifying the encounter.
"TheBoss is back in town! Suck on these nuts righteous faction–"
"All of you together couldn't stop him from returning where he belongs"
"Look at his eyes…. TheBoss doesn't even care for his own fame, he doesn't even acknowledge the crowd, he's… SO DAMN COOL"
Despite the grandeur of the moment, Leo paid no attention to the crowd. His gaze remained forward, his posture calm but unyielding, as though the chaos surrounding him was nothing more than a distant hum.
And yet, every movement, every slight tilt of his head, was analyzed and dissected by the crowd as if it held the secret to his power.
By the time he reached his apartment, the crowd had swelled to an overwhelming size, with players and NPCs alike craning their necks to get one last glimpse of him before he vanished into his abode.
With ChaosBringer having deployed guards to keep the crowd away from his house already, they could unfortunately not follow him as he walked into his quarters, however, while the crowd was barred entry, ChaosBringer himself waited patiently in TheBoss's garden, just outside the entrance to his home.
"Welcome back, my liege, your return to Briarhelm has been eagerly awaited by us lowly one's for weeks now, but now that you're here, we are truly humbled by your presence" ChaosBringer said, as he bowed almost 90° to greet Leo.
Up till now, Leo had a perfectly calm face on, however, the moment he saw ChaosBringer, the hands that were comfortably behind his back, suddenly came to the front as he covered his nether regions with them in a groin guard posture.
"Rise—" he said nervously, as although he knew that he could not avoid this meeting with ChaosBringer, Leo still wished to carry it out with as much distance between them as possible.
"Thank You my merciful lord for allowing this lowly one to stand. Your kindness truly knows no bounds…" ChaosBringer began, as he gazed towards Leo with the most loving of eyes, the passionate kind that was usually reserved only for lovers, making Leo immediately feel increasingly uncomfortable.
"Does the Lord wish to rest? This humble one has been learning the art of massaging and has recently acquired [Intermediate] proficiency for the same.
If the Lord gives me a chance, I can help you melt away all the stress of your journey and can even impart a temporary physical recovery boost to you–" ChaosBringer suggested, rubbing his hands that had long pointy nails eagerly.
"No, not tired… not at all" Leo replied, fumbling as his left eye began to twitch constantly.
"I see…. Then if the Lord does have stamina, may I suggest stepping into your quarters and conversing about the war? There are some urgent matters that I must bring to your attention—" ChaosBringer suggested, as Leo instantly shot down the idea.
"No need to be alone in my quarters, we are alone enough here. You may say whatever you want to say" Leo urged, as he absolutely refused to allow ChaosBringer to be alone with him in an enclosed room.
—------

The quarter-finals voting event for Lord Dumpy is now open, let's get it guys! The other three don't stand a chance, onto the semis we go! Vote! Vote! Vote! ///

chapters.title: Chapter 730 - 730: Luke
chapters.content:
"So how is the war developing?" Leo asked curiously, as once he got over his discomfort being around ChaosBringer, he went straight down to business.
"The war is developing decently, my liege, the South has already been unified under your banner and we are about 10 days of conquest away from laying a siege on StrongHaven.
If things stay the way they are currently, we should be able to conquer the city before the debuff period ends, however, our scouts report that the righteous faction players have started to reinforce the city defences and are stocking up on supplies in preparation for a long siege.
Under such circumstances, if they have the necessary numbers to defend, it's near impossible to conquer StrongHaven City with brute force alone, which is a source of great concern and shame for me" ChaosBringer said, as he gave a curt summary of the situation.
"What about the North and West?" Leo asked, scratching his chin, as he soaked in all the information that ChaosBringer provided.
"The north is as good as conquered. With the North Duke Denver Willow dead, the northern NPC nobles have no-one to rally around and have become easy pickings for the three major guilds that we have allied with.
Currently, over 50% of the northern Duchy is under the control of our partners and they are making rapid progress.
As things stand, they are expected to swear fealty to us once you officially take the throne" ChaosBringer said, as he led with the good news.
"The West however is more complicated…." He continued, as he balled a fist, his own nails digging into his flesh as his jaw tightened just a little.
"The WhiteSabers are struggling to make gains in the West, with the DarkSky guild and the West Duke's forces mounting a formidable challenge
As of now, only a few small villages have been annexed and they are facing intense struggles to even hold on to them.
Their guildmaster has requested manpower and logistic assistance from us and we have obliged what we could spare, however, things don't look so bright in the west.
For now, it seems unlikely that we will be able to annex it anytime soon" ChaosBringer reported, as Leo simply waved off his concerns.
"Let me worry about the West, I have a score to settle with a certain someone there… You just focus on the siege in StrongHaven and contact me if you need some specific assistance that no-one else can perform.
As long as it's assassination or creating an opening, I'll complete any mission that you give me" Leo replied, as ChaosBringer bowed deeply once more.
"You humble me with your faith in my abilities to lead–" he said, his voice cracking and his eyes tearing up as he genuinely seemed moved by Leo's words.
Initially he had come here only to seek advice on how to tackle the StrongHaven City problem, however, with Leo delegating that same problem back to him, he had circled back to point zero.
Nonetheless, he felt much more confident in being able to tackle this problem now that Leo had shown faith in him, with his brain suddenly feeling reinvigorated.
"I will not disappoint you my liege, even if the heavens open up and swallow me, I will find a way to deliver StrongHaven City to you and roll a red carpet for you all the way from the city gates till the throne room" ChaosBringer promised, as Leo gave him a thumbs up sign.
"I expect nothing less from the leader of the Uprising" he said, as he hand signed him to take his leave now.
Bowing, ChaosBringer took his leave with tears streaking down his eyes, as he began to feel enlightened.
'Lord Boss expects me to win this for him…. He believes in my competence! I must not let him down now–' ChaosBringer thought, as he rushed back to his office to come-up with a new plan to capture StrongHaven City.
*************
(Meanwhile Luke)
After weeks of practicing the mind meditation manual, Luke finally began noticing major improvements to his character build.
His two newly acquired [Legendary] ranked skills were now up-to (Intermediate) proficiency, while his Semi-Legendary skills were already on (Advanced).
He had already managed to clear the level threshold to become a (Master) level fighter and now, as long as he could bring his two (Legendary) ranked skills to (Advanced) mastery, he could finally step into the ranks of a master warrior just like his brother and PinkLotus.
"I made a lot of mistakes early into my gaming career by learning skills I should not have.
I had to re-do my foundation twice and get accustomed to new skills that have not yet become second nature to be in battle…" Luke mused, reflecting on his gaming journey, as he finally managed to single out the exact moments where he made mistakes.
"Leo's master, Ben Faulkner, played a huge role in him becoming who he is today…. Having a master warrior as a teacher helped him avoid many foundational mistakes and set him on the right path ahead.
I could have been the same…. After my stellar performance in the grand tournament, there were many master knights willing to take me under their tutelage and I should have taken them up on their offer.
However, just because of my commitments for the DarkSky guild, I could not join them, or the West Duke's forces, both of which could have changed my gaming career big time…" Luke mused as he let out a deep sigh.
While he did not regret his time at the DarkSky guild, as it was a productive learning experience in its own right, in hindsight he felt like he could have done better if he remained united and free like Leo, having dared to rely on his own strength rather than finding a reliable shoulder to lean on.
"Never again…. Once we land on planet Terra Nova, I'll never make this same mistake again. I won't be tied down unless there are significant benefits attached" Luke resolved, as he decided to learn from his mistakes and move on.

chapters.title: Chapter 731 - 731: Precarious situation
chapters.content:
( Meanwhile, the WhiteSaber guild, The Western Duchy)
The spacious command tent of the Whitesaber guild was a flurry of activity, but none of the commotion seemed to enter the guild master's ears who was lost studying the war map.
Seated at the center of the room, his piercing gaze was fixed on the massive paper map sprawled across the table, however, judging by his expression and how his lips were pressed into a thin line, one could easily establish that he did not appreciate what he saw before him.
Every red marker on the map—representing the guild's planned conquests—seemed to mock him, reminding him of the sharp divergence between ambition and reality.
'This is bad…. Everytime I send my men to fight, it bites me back spectacularly' The guildmaster thought, as he clicked his tongue in disgust.
Unlike NPC's, who stayed dead after being killed once players could respawn infinitely, giving them a massive advantage in NPC vs player wars in the long run.
However, when his men lost 3-5 levels each time after dying, the resentment within them was not easy to manage.
Gaining 3-5 levels in this current gaming environment was extremely tough and about a month's work for most and seeing it go down the drain for nothing made many feel furious.
It wasn't a problem as long as the WhiteSaber won the fight and territorial gains were made, however, when they charged and died pointlessly day after day, many began to feel discontent.
Thankfully, with the uprising members joining his war effort, the overall morale within the guild seemed to have been uplifted somewhat, however, the situation still remained precarious.
"Guildmaster….. Guildmaster" an urgent voice came from outside his tent, as a scout hurried in, while clutching a tattered report in his palms.
The scout was in a visibly pitiful condition with his armor being dirt-streaked, and his breathing labored from the urgency of his message.
"Another failure at Coventry Town, Guildmaster," the scout reported, barely able to meet the guildmaster's eyes.
"Our forces were driven back again…by both DarkSky operatives and the Duke's men, apparently they're working in tandem now, even cooperating on strategy" the scout reported, as the WhiteSaber guild master felt his blood boil listening to this report.
"How many?" the guildmaster asked, his voice sounding steady on the surface, but with a dangerous undertone hidden beneath.
"We lost eight thousand men—half of them ambushed by DarkSky's rogues before even reaching the gates. The rest fell to the Duke's forces, who…well let's just say that the enemy fought with a resilience we hadn't anticipated."
"What?" the WhiteSaber guildmaster said, slamming a fist onto the table, as the sound of the wooden table cracking spread across the tent.
"Coventry should've fallen days ago. It's just a tier3 town, damn it. What's stopping us? I want details."
The scout hesitated, then stepped forward, unfolding the report. "The DarkSky guild is using hit-and-run tactics, wearing down our forces before they can reach their targets. Meanwhile, the Duke's men, though weakened, have fortified key positions and are holding their ground far better than we estimated."
Listening to this report the guildmaster took a deep breath, his mind racing.
"Dismissed," he ordered, waving the scout away, as he needed time to think alone.
*********
After the scout left, the guildmaster leaned back in his chair, his eyes flicking to the calendar pinned to the tent wall.
Twelve days... It had been twelve days since they'd launched their grand offensive, a campaign meant to carve a path of dominance through the western territories.
However, so far, their conquests amounted to two villages and one town, and each victory had come at a staggering cost.
The guild's elite forces were stretched thin, morale was dwindling, and supplies were running dangerously low.
The failures weren't just frustrating—they were humiliating, as the Whitesabers, known as one of the most powerful guilds in the game world, were supposed to steamroll through these lands, however, instead, they were bogged down by a war effort that felt more like a slow bleed than a triumphant march.
'Everyone apart from us is thriving. The uprising rebels are steamrolling their way to the Capital, while the Northern guilds are also dominating their local regions.
The WhiteSabers are the only guild in this alliance without any merit to show for and if things don't change soon, we might not get a piece of the pie when everything is said and done…' He thought, as he dug his nails into his own skin.
This was supposed to be the WhiteSaber guilds moment to shine. This was their ticket out of mediocrity and into the stratosphere, however, they could not deliver on this heaven sent opportunity as expected.
The guild's fatal mistake so far was that they had underestimated their enemies—both the DarkSky guild and the Duke's forces, however, even worse, they had overestimated their own ability to wage war under the current debuff.
The 35% debuff was causing their chief mages to be able to only cast their best spells twice instead of thrice and their archers could no longer shoot as far as necessary.
These problems though seemingly simple affected the war mechanics big time, and the WhiteSabers were only finding this out now.
"Tell the generals to meet me in an hour," the guildmaster muttered to an aide. "If we don't change our strategy, this war will break us."
The aide nodded and rushed off, leaving the WhiteSabers guildmaster alone with his thoughts.
"Cervantez…Duke James…" he whispered, the names laced with frustration. "You won't hold me back forever."
But even as he spoke the words, doubt crept into his heart. Could they truly turn the tide, or was this the beginning of the Whitesabers' inevitable decline?
"Let me talk to my generals…. Including the one the uprising sent.
If I can solicit more supplies and support from the uprising, perhaps we can turn this war on its head" He concluded, as at the end he realized that he could not turn the tides of this war with his own strength and needed to rely on the uprising to win more land.
—--------

Only the top1 progresses! Let's do it guys! Lord Dumpy for the win! ///

chapters.title: Chapter 732 - 732: A crazy plan
chapters.content:
(At the general's meeting, WhiteSaber guild)
The war room inside the Whitesaber guild's headquarters was shrouded in a suffocating silence before the general's meeting officially began.
Around the massive, circular table sat the guild's war generals, their faces pale and drawn, as no-one was able to look the other in the eye, with every single one of them having faced one humiliating defeat or the other over the past few days.
No one spoke as they waited for the guildmaster to enter, as the only sound in the room came from the occasional tapping of shoes or adjusting of chairs, which left a slight screeching sound on the floor below.
Then, as the guildmaster entered, the silence broke, as all the war generals stood up at once, waiting for the guildmaster to take his seat before they were seated yet again.
"Let's begin." the guildmaster said, as he demanded the generals to one by one deliver the status of their war progress starting from the rightmost end of the table and circling all the way to the left.
As per his instructions, the generals began to get up one after another and delivered their grim pieces of news, until the table rotated to the only guest speaker on the table, General Floren Mayes of the Uprising.
"We entered the war and were directed to take down Camp Nou, which we did in just under 4 hours. It was a resounding success and still remains to be the only town we have captured in this war effort" Mayes gloated, as the silence in the room only seemed to deepen.
'You're only succeeding because you don't have to face the 35% stat debuff like we do…' thought many, however, nobody dared voice it aloud, lest they antagonise their only allies in this war.
The guildmaster's hands in particular were clasped tightly, his knuckles white, as for a long moment, he said nothing, letting the weight of their words settle.
Finally, he leaned forward, his voice low and sharp.
"Is this what the Whitesaber guild has become? A laughingstock? A guild that loses to rogue NPCs and a pack of glorified measly rankers?" he asked, his anger palpable as the generals flinched, but no one dared to respond.
The guildmaster's eyes narrowed. "Look at me," he ordered.
Slowly, reluctantly, the generals raised their eyes to meet his. The weight of their collective failure hung heavy in the room, unspoken but palpable.
"We're supposed to be the strongest guild in the west," the guildmaster continued, his voice growing colder with each word. "But here we are, twelve days into this campaign, and we've barely made progress. Two villages. One town. And that town, as rightly pointed out, was delivered through OUTSIDE assistance and not our own competence.
If it was the Uprising who wanted to win this war by their own strength then they don't need us as allies in the West now, do they?" The guildmaster asked as everyone lowered their eyes in shame once more.
"No more…. I say no more, we can't carry on like this and hope to win and hence I've come up with a strategy to change our fortunes" The guildmaster declared, as his words now had the entire audience listening in rapt attention.
"To kill a snake, you kill off the snake's head, and to kill an army, you kill their general.
If we take out West Duke James and capture the Western Capital City of Bernabeu, we will win the war in the west.
And hence, I propose that we regroup and redirect all our war efforts to taking down the West Duke" the guildmaster proposed, as his words caused quite the stir amongst the others.
The room erupted into murmurs as the guildmaster's proposal sank in. The idea of targeting West Duke James and the Western Capital City of Bernabeu was bold—perhaps even reckless, however, if successful it could really change the tide of war big-time.
General Markus, still reeling from the failure at Coventry Town, was the first to speak. "Guildmaster, with all due respect, attacking Bernabeu will be no small feat. The capital is heavily fortified and even with the Duke's forces weakened it won't be easy to capture. Also…if we fail, it could spell disaster for the entire campaign."
The guildmaster's gaze shifted sharply to Markus, silencing him with a single glare. "Do you have a better suggestion, Markus?" he asked coldly.
Markus hesitated, then shook his head. "No, Guildmaster."
The guildmaster straightened in his chair, his commanding presence filling the room. "Good. Then listen carefully."
He gestured to the map spread out on the table, pointing to key locations surrounding Bernabeu. "The Duke's forces are concentrated here, here, and here." His finger tapped on the city itself, the North Gate, and the nearby garrison. "We will deploy three separate units to simultaneously assault these positions. The main force will lay siege to the capital, while our elite teams infiltrate the city to take out the Duke. Once his head is removed, the remaining forces will crumble."
Another general, Lyra, raised her voice. "And what of the DarkSky guild? They've been shadowing our every move, and I doubt they'll sit idly by while we make such a bold play."
The guildmaster's lips curled into a grim smile. "Let them come. Their interference will only hasten their own demise. As our friends from the uprising will be waiting till they make a move to make their move.
We will become the mantis, the DarkSky guild will be the cicada while the uprising will be the oriole"
The room fell silent once more, the weight of the guildmaster's plan settling over the gathered generals. Despite the risks, his proposal carried an undeniable logic—and for the first time in days, a faint flicker of hope arose within the hearts of them all.
"Prepare your units," the guildmaster commanded, rising to his feet. "This war has dragged on long enough. It's time we remind the world why the Whitesaber guild is feared."
With those words, the guildmaster concluded the day's meeting, but as the generals filed out, a lingering unease hung in the air.
The plan was bold, yes—but many understood that boldness alone might not be enough to turn the tide of this war.
To execute it, they were all going to be at the top of their game and make no mistakes, as only then could something so crazy be pulled off.

chapters.title: Chapter 733 - 733: Blood Brothers
chapters.content:
After the meeting with the WhiteSaber guild concluded, General Floren Mayes immediately texted ChaosBringer about everything that went down in the meeting which was then passed onto 'TheBoss' by ChaosBringer, in one short message.
When ChaosBringer forwarded the message to Leo, he never expected Leo to do much about it, as although Leo had said that he would 'Handle' the West, ChaosBringer did not actually expect him to be involved personally, however, Leo decided to make a move anyways.
[ Hey, thankyou for the update on what's going on in the West, I'll head down there myself and see if I can make a difference to the war effort– ] was what Leo replied to ChaosBringer, with his message absolutely baffling the Uprising's leader.
"Why are you bothering with such a small time operation?" Was what ChaosBringer wanted to type and send, as according to him, even if the WhiteSabers failed to gain control of the west, the uprising could easily conquer it given enough time, however, 'The boss' did not seem keen on waiting.
In the end, ChaosBringer decided to not send that message out, as he did not wish to offend the big boss, but he was worried about the same nonetheless.
"Do you need me to send more men to support you? I can send a whole army…." He asked, over the text chat, to which 'TheBoss' simply replied "I am the army."
In the end, when ChaosBringer read that reply, a stupidly wide grin spread on his face as he realized that 'TheBoss' was probably the only player in the game who could say something so ridiculous and still make it sound legit.
***********
(Meanwhile PinkLotus)
PinkLotus was out training near the waterfall, when a private message popped up in her dms.
Since she only had two friends who could send her private messages within the game, with one of them training right beside her, she knew who the text was from and hence paused her training immediately to respond.
"Hey, as per your promise I need you to help me in a war, head over to the Western Duchy, I hope to see you in Shack-Shack village in 2 days time.
And if you can, please bring my brother alongside you, but do warn him it will be a war against DarkSky" Leo said in his text message, as PinkLotus read it solemnly.
"Hmmm…." She mused, glancing over to where Luke was practicing his skills as she wondered whether or not to pass on the message.
She had been friends with Luke for over half a year now and slowly but surely their bond had been progressively growing stronger.
She now understood more about who he was and what he wanted from life and hence she also understood how he was going to react to the news of potentially fighting his old guild.
'Should I not ask him? I think there's a reason behind why Leo asked me to pass the message on and did not text Luke directly…. He knows his brother's nature all too well….' PinkLotus thought, as she kept glancing absentmindedly in Luke's direction, making him acutely aware of her lingering stare while training.
"What?" Luke asked, pausing for a moment, as PinkLotus shook her head and jumped down from the rock she was on to look him in the eye.
"Your brother called in the favor I owe him…. So I guess I'm heading to war" PinkLotus began, as Luke nodded patiently to her words.
"Are you okay with the idea that I'm going to be fighting the DarkSky guild potentially? Or are you not happy about that?" She asked as Luke scratched his hair for a while.
"Umm…. I mean, I am not thrilled at the idea that either the DarkSky guild or you might come out of this war injured, but I guess that's how life works. They have chosen to be enemies with my brother and now they have to live with the consequences of it" Luke replied, as PinkLotus's eyes brightened up.
She knew how much that guild meant to Luke, however, listening to his opinion now, she could really feel just how much he had matured.
"That's right, it did not have to be this way–" PinkLotus said, shrugging her shoulders as she sheathed her sword and began to tie her hair into a pony, in preparation for the long journey ahead.
"So when do we leave?" Luke asked, as PinkLotus paused her action midway and looked towards Luke in an expression full of surprise.
"We?" She asked, as Luke raised an eyebrow of confusion.
"Of Course 'we', I'm not letting my brother and my good friend fight alone…. Or did Leo not ask for me?" Luke asked, sounding horrified, as he immediately assumed that maybe Leo did not consider him to be good enough to join this war effort.
"Of Course he asked for you, I just did not ask because I did not want to potentially upset you…. I know how much you love your guild members and how you see them as family" PinkLotus clarified, as Luke breathed a sigh of relief.
"They were like family to me… yeah, but Leo IS my family. The blood between us runs thick and he will always be my priority" Luke said, as PinkLotus's pupils dilated in response.
If there was one trait about Leo that she appreciated a lot, it was his unquestionable love for Amanda and how he was ready to fight the world for her.
In comparison, while Luke was a gentleman and a much more level headed guy to talk to, he was also a little people pleaser who could not make the tough decisions when he had to.
Hence, watching him now grow and become more practical, PinkLotus felt a renewed sense of attraction towards him, as finally, he was beginning to show signs of becoming the man she dreamed of.
—-----
/// A/N - Hey guys, Lord Dumpy was leading the character voting till the last 60 seconds, but then someone blindsided us and made the opponent win by a mere 2000 points.
It was a last second heist, a dirty loss, but it is what it is.
[ Dumpy :- The lowly mongrels used their tricks to beat me, but this majestic frog doesn't feel discouraged from petty losing! We will be stronger next time!] ///

chapters.title: Chapter 734 - 734: A Personal Grudge
chapters.content:
(Leo's POV)
Until now, Leo had never fought a war out of personal grudges. Terra Nova Online had always been a fresh start for him, a place free from the baggage of real-world rivalries or deep hatred.
However, that changed the day his brother, Luke, was disrespected and betrayed by his own guild, The DarkSky.
Cervantez had always been there, a constant rival since Leo's early gaming days. They weren't friends—Leo couldn't say he liked him much on a personal level—but he'd respected Cervantez for one thing: the way he'd helped Luke when no one else would. For that alone, Leo had held him in some regard.
But when it truly mattered, when a decisive guild vote could have changed everything, Cervantez turned his back. He didn't stand by Luke. He didn't even try.
That moment shattered whatever respect Leo had for him. It was the first time Leo felt a bitterness creeping into the game world, a resentment that sat heavy in his chest and refused to leave.
And hence for the first time ever…. It was personal.
By all means right now, after having killed the Emperor, he should have directed his energies towards capturing the throne of StrongHaven and to become the first ever player Emperor within the game, however, Leo decided not to do that.
Instead, he decided to go west and enter the only righteous faction zone still left within the game and risk his life once more just to prove a point.
This time, he wasn't going there to achieve a purpose, this time he was just going to war for the sake of war, as his only goal was to annihilate and humiliate the DarkSky forces.
He wanted to just show Cervantez that disrespecting his brother was the worst decision he ever made as a guildmaster, and that it would be a decision that Leo would never let him recover from.
It was a decision driven by pure hatred and an equally strong desire to humiliate and emancipate that drove Leo to the West, as this time he was just going to bully the weak, with the only intent of bullying them.
*********
(Meanwhile, in the West, the Whitesabers)
The Whitesabers were never informed about 'TheBoss' heading over personally to help them in the war effort, and hence they prepared like they were fighting without him.
The atmosphere in the guild when the guildmaster announced that the guild would be taking one decisive stand to hopefully win this war, was quite grim, as the tactic exclaimed a lack of confidence and desperation.
Throughout the various WhiteSaber camps and settlements, the news spread like a chilling wind. For many rank-and-file members, it was as if they could feel the weight of their failures pressing down on them, as whispers began floating through the ranks:
"This is it, huh? If we lose this fight, we're done…"
"Pulling back from every front just to hit one city? It's like we're cornered rats…"
Still, no one dared question the guildmaster's orders aloud. For all their doubts and fears, the Whitesabers were a disciplined force. Orders were orders, and every soldier understood that their next battle could define the guild's future.
Meanwhile, to maintain control over the guild's waning morale, the guildmaster ensured that no one lingered too long in thought.
Messengers and officers barked orders from dawn to dusk, their relentless pace leaving little room for doubts to fester.
"Pack up the forward camps immediately!" barked a squad leader as soldiers scrambled to tear down tents and gather supplies. "We will march for Bernabeu in two days!"
Another officer shouted to a group of mages. "You there! Reinforce the barricades as we pull out. We're not leaving these positions open for DarkSky to exploit!"
Weapons were sharpened. Supplies were rationed. Battle standards were dusted off and raised high, the white saber insignia fluttering defiantly in the wind. The guild's elite forces were pulled back from every other battlefield—Coventry, the villages on the outskirts, even minor sieges—leaving behind ghost towns and empty trenches. Every available soldier was marching toward a singular purpose: Bernabeu.
********
(2 days later)
When the day to march finally came, the scene that unfolded before one was both awe-inspiring and unsettling.
The WhiteSaber army marched as one, thousands of boots pounding in unison against the dirt roads. Unit after unit fell into line, banners flying high above their heads, as from infantry to cavalry, mages to siege engineers, every guild member joined the march.
As they passed through former strongholds and abandoned camps that the army once captured, the scale of the regrouping effort became clear.
Entire battlefields lay eerily empty, with only the smoldering remnants of fires and broken barricades left behind, to show that there used to be a massive army camp here once.
However, apart from the boot marks and ash scorched Earth, there was nothing else left to show that there might have been a massive army stationed here just a day ago.
"The whole WhiteSaber has assembled…," a DarkSky scout reported to his Cervantez as he observed the piling army.
"No stragglers. They're leaving nothing behind."
At the head of the army, the guildmaster rode silently, his expression set in stone as he scanned the horizon.
Bernabeu loomed far to the west, a city that now represented both their greatest challenge and their last hope for victory.
For the Whitesabers, there was no turning back now, the march to Bernabeu had begun, and with it came the weight of every failure, every loss, and every bitter lesson learned over the past fourteen days.
Victory or annihilation awaited them, and none could say which outcome was going to unfold.
—-----
///A/N - Hey guys! So today was the WSA award ceremony, and Terra Nova Online won the bronze prize thanks to all of your love and support.
It's truly been a humbling experience, and to see this work receive such recognition on a global stage was heartwarming.
I'll drop a photo of the trophy in the comments below…. That one is for all of us!
Because I wouldn't have won anything without your votes, comments and love. ///

chapters.title: Chapter 735 - 735: Ingenious
chapters.content:
(Leo's POV)
Leo was genuinely surprised to see Luke arrive alongside PinkLotus, as he half expected Luke to stay away from this conflict knowing that he might have to face his ex-guild members and friends.
However, while Leo was surprised that Luke came, he was even more surprised to see him arrive with a spark in his eyes, as his demeanor looked absolutely focused and his eyes seemed to be brimming with determination.
"I'm glad you came, brother… though I hope you don't chicken out at the last minute," Leo said, his tone half-teasing, half-serious, as Luke merely shrugged in response, looking utterly unfazed by the remark.
"I've thought this through carefully, and I'm certain this isn't a rash decision," Luke began, his voice steady and resolute. "I've severed my ties with the DarkSky Guild—I'm my own player now, free to make my own choices and today, I've chosen to stand by my brother, and that's all that matters.
If my old guildmates are upset or feel betrayed by my actions, that's their burden to bear, not mine. You can't live a free life if you're always worrying about what others think of you. I know what I'm doing, and I'm ready to face whatever consequences come my way," he declared with conviction, leaving Leo momentarily at a loss for words.
'Is this really my brother?' Leo wondered as he knew exactly how Luke had always been a chronic people-pleaser, which made this transformation today all the more remarkable.
It was a testament to just how much Luke had grown as an individual, and it made Leo feel untold emotions.
"Come here," Leo said, pulling Luke into a bear hug as a tear of pride slipped down his cheek.
For Leo, he hadn't felt this proud of Luke since the day he earned his first money and used it to buy a small gift for both Elena and Leo.
Back then, that day had been special because it was the day Luke graduated from being a dependent in the house to becoming the man of the house, which was a transformation Leo remembered vividly.
And now, that same feeling of pride surged through Leo once more, as his brother seemed to have taken another leap forward—this time from being a habitual people-pleaser to standing tall as his own man.
"You're ready!" Leo said, patting his brother's shoulders, as Luke looked at him like Leo had perhaps lost his mind.
*Cough*
*Cough*
Coughing ever so slightly, PinkLotus drew some attention to herself at this time, as although Leo usually did not like her much, today he felt unusually generous.
"Oh come here you–, you're the biggest change in my brother's life, I know you made this happen" Leo said, as he walked over to PinkLotus and enveloped his arms around her in a hug, which absolutely bewildered PinkLotus.
Unlike Luke, she did not put her arms around Leo when he hugged her, however, she did not push him away either.
If it were a pervert who tried to do this, she would have probably cut him down to small pieces, however, PinkLotus knew Leo was not a pervert.
Infact, Leo was not even a very emotional guy in general, as his usual expression when looking at PinkLotus was one of disgust, which made this sudden burst of love even more absurd for her.
"Thank You…. Thank You" Leo mumbled before pulling away, as PinkLotus stood there stunned, unable to process what was going on for many seconds.
Then, eventually a shiver ran through her body making her tremble violently, as goosebumps ran over all her skin.
'Did 'TheBoss' just hug me?' she wondered, as it seemed to be the most absurd experience of her life.
"Lord Father…. I approve your choice in a breeding mate, that one has good proportions, but perhaps we should fatten her up slightly more to make her perfect–" Dumpy said from a distance, as for him, it was the first time he witnessed Leo showing affection to a woman of the opposite gender.
"Fool, this woman is not for me… it's for my brother" Leo replied, making both PinkLotus and Luke's face flush red, as although both had some feelings for each other, they were still not in the openly accepting phase of what their relationship was.
"When did I ever tell you she's mine? You'll make her misunderstand…. Alia, I've never… that, it's not me" Luke said, trying to clarify, as his words only made PinkLotus turn even more red.
"It's not me either…. Your brother doesn't talk to me at all in private and turns his face away from me when I come visit" PinkLotus clarified, as Leo squinted his eyes and judged the atmosphere between the two.
"So you're telling me…. You guys train together everyday…. Spending hours online in a remote first. A man and a woman, and then you visit each other in real life twice or thrice a week…. But you're not dating?" Leo asked, as if it was the most absurd thing ever, as Luke smacked him hard on the head.
"No you fool, we are not!" Luke replied, as instantly Dumpy came charging from a distance and pointed his sword a couple feet away from Luke's face.
"Hit Lord Father again and I will cut you down, even if Lord Father calls you family" Dumpy said threateningly, as Luke instantly raised an eyebrow in response.
"Oh really now?" He said in a surprise voice, as he pulled out his own sword, looking Dumpy straight in the eye.
"You don't scare me… Frog" Luke said, as Dumpy grew to his full massive 45 feet tall size in response.
"Don't test my patience…. Puny human" Dumpy replied, as Leo immediately stepped between the two and pointed his palms out towards both.
"I think that's enough…. We will have plenty of enemies to kill soon, there's absolutely no need to point swords at one another" Leo said, as Dumpy shrunk back down immediately.
"As you command Lord Father" he said, bowing his head in subservience as Leo patted him lovingly.
Meanwhile, Luke also sheathed his sword and glanced towards PinkLotus, who still looked slightly flushed from the previous conversation.
Luke coughed, and averted eye contact once again, as he just began to hope that the awkward atmosphere would pass soon enough.
Thankfully because of his scuffle with Dumpy, the worse had already passed and Leo now seemed more keen on getting a move on rather than lingering on the topic of his and PinkLotus's relationship.
"We will attack Gatusso town first…. It's just an hour's walk from here, but we'll get there in 15 minutes if we ride Dumpy…." Leo said, as both PinkLotus and Luke seemed surprised by his decision.
"Gatusso Town? But aren't we headed to Bernabeu City to fight with the Whitesabers?" PinkLotus asked as Leo wagged his index finger to signal a 'No'.
"Cervantez probably already knows that the WhiteSabers are marching with their full strength towards Bernabeu, it's dumb to join them where they're prepared.
I'm thinking we hit them in safe areas where they must have pulled their troops from, such as Gatusso, because although it's a big town it's of not much strategic importance because of its geographical location.
The defences there will be low and routing the defending DarkSky guild forces there will destabilize the region" Leo said, as his words seemed to be oddly convincing for PinkLotus to hear.
Although on one hand, if WhiteSabers lost in the main war, the victory or defeat as Gatusso was not going to matter much, on the other hand what Leo theorized was not wrong as well.
If their goal was to win the war, attacking Gatusso was a dumb choice, however, if their only intention was to destabilize and cause chaos, it was the easiest and juiciest target.
"But what about the main war?" Luke asked, as Leo flicked his hair up with a swagger.
"I don't care about the main war…. I just want to see the DarkSky guild humiliated and burned.
In my understanding, the war for Bernabeu is unlikely to conclude in a single day, it will at least go on for a few, giving us enough time to join them later if we want, or not join them at all if we don't.
Depending on how the war progresses, we can make the best decision on what's good for us" Leo said, as his POV really enlightened Luke on how to think.
As a logical and by-the-book strategist, Luke could never come up with a strategy as crazy as Leo, as it was not the most sound one to win the war.
However, it was somehow petty, genius and shady at the same time, putting Luke at a loss of words on how to describe it.
"Climb on Dumpy, we leave now–" Leo instructed as he himself climbed onto Dumpy's right shoulder, and once Luke and Alia climbed on his left, Dumpy leapt into the sky, heading straight for Gatusso town.

chapters.title: Chapter 736 - 736: Betrayal
chapters.content:
(Gatusso Town)
Just like how the WhiteSabers had pulled away their soldiers from their usual stations for the decisive war at Bernabeu, the DarkSky guild had too, leaving only a small regiment behind to keep law and order.
Currently, only 3600 soldiers were left to defend Gatusso town of the usual regiment of over 15,000, with the rest being drafted for war.
"Man I'm so glad I did not get drafted for war…. I'm one of the weakest members in the guild, which is why they always put me in the vanguard for the cannon fodder wave. If I would have been drafted, I was pretty much guaranteed to die early and lose a couple levels" A DarkSky member said, as he expressed his satisfaction for not being drafted to his colleague.
"Naww… I'm pissed they didn't draft me, I'm lagging behind and the dream to become a top 10,000 ranked player is slipping away. I need a big war to hopefully have a good performance and progress.
I even volunteered to go, however, just like you,I'm one of the weaker members too, so they did not take me" The colleague replied as he seemed slightly disheartened that the guild did not take him.
However, as the two bantered about whether or not they should have been drafted to war, they had no idea about the threat approaching them at breakneck speed, as at this moment, Lord Dumpy was jumping through the land to arrive at Gatusso with breakneck speed.
"Man this war is an easy win…. The WhiteSabers are not The Uprising, they won't be able to do shit against us, we are the DarkSky" The guild member argued, as he tried to convince his colleague that not going to the war was a mistake.
"To be fair, the uprising isn't shit either without 'TheBoss', however, I don't think any army can win a war when 'TheBoss' participates in it. That man is like a gaming god" the colleague replied, as the guild member shrugged his shoulders in agreement.
"Let's just hope, we never have to meet 'TheBoss' in a fight. If the entire righteous faction can't get that man then I don't know who can" the guild member said, as right when he said these words, a giant frog flew over the towns shoddy spiked wooden walls and leaped straight on top of a stone house, damaging it's ceiling.
*CRASH*
The loud impact was heard town-wide, as everyone turned at once to look at what caused the disturbance, only for a dagger to be impaled straight into their eye.
-12,500 CRITICAL HIT!
"Who?" Muttered the DarkSky guild member as his colleague dropped dead, as at that moment he saw 'TheBoss' disembarking from his giant pet, a murderous gleam shining in his eyes.
"B-b-b-BOSS!" He shouted, trembling as Leo gave him a curved smile.
Never in his life had Leo seen someone so genuinely scared out of their wits just from his presence, but it looked like his legend and fear was finally starting to spread, becoming big enough that just his presence struck fear into the heart of his enemies.
"Go… inform Cervantez that his father has finally arrived in town" Leo said, as he spared the trembling man before him, just so that he could strike fear into the heart of an enemy that wasn't even present here.
**********
(Meanwhile Cervantez)
Cervantez was busy looking over at the enemy camp forming a few miles off the city walls of Bernabeu.
The capital city had already been closed down, with no citizens allowed to enter and leave, as a martial law was enforced.
Although it was a city under the West Duke, upon Cervantez's insistence, he imposed a martial law, just because Cervantez did not wish to take a chance of any rebel sympathizers causing internal problems for them while they mounted a defence against an external threat.
"Their forces are at least 100,000 strong, maybe 120,000. They have about 20,000 mounted warriors and some siege weapons, No wonder the WhiteSabers are called one of the best guilds in the game, they definitely are not a weak bunch" Cervantez commented, as he subtly appreciated what the WhiteSaber Guild had been able to achieve within the game so far.
"Unfortunately for you though, this is where your journey ends…. For today you have challenged an enemy that you simply cannot surmount" Cervantez said, as just as he was about to turn away from the city wall and return to his war-station, a guild member came running towards him with a panicked face.
"Guildmaster! Guildmaster! Open the guild chat immediately…. Please, it's an emergency! It's 'TheBoss'.... THE BOSS" A guild member said, as he stumbled and fell to Cervantez's feet.
"What happened?" Cervantez inquired as he opened the guild chat.
[The Boss has invaded Gatusso town and is killing anyone and everyone wearing a DarkSky guild robe! We are no match for him. We are being slaughtered. ]
[The Boss has the giant frog with him, they're killing everyone….. and it looks like the goddess PinkLotus is fighting with him too, and… and…. It looks like Vice Guild Master Skylion is here too!]
[Vice-Guildmaster has betrayed us… he's suplexing DarkSky members, he's fighting as intensely as the rest]
Just these three messages caused a shit-storm to brew within the DarkSky guild, as most guild members started to lose their minds.
Even Cervantez could not believe what he was reading, as he could not understand why someone would even bother attacking Gatusso? It wasn't a strategically important location.
However, what baffled him more was that Luke was involved in the attack, as although Luke had left the guild, Cervantez never expected him to hunt down his own ex-guild members.
"So…. You've finally shown your true colors Skylion, I guess my kindness meant nothing to you" Cervantez said as he felt the pain of Luke's betrayal sting his heart.
"Very well then…. I guess it's a lesson learned. Since you've abandoned the guild first, I'll treat you accordingly the next time I see you" Cervantez said, as his face turned ominously stoic.

chapters.title: Chapter 737 - 737: Upsetting Allegations
chapters.content:
(Luke's POV)
It took Luke less than 30 minutes, working alongside Leo and the others, to completely annihilate every last member of the DarkSky guild in Gattuso Town, finally liberating it from their control.
During this brief but intense battle, Luke gained a newfound appreciation for the formidable companions he had joined in this war and took the opportunity to measure himself against them.
In his assessment, Leo stood far above the rest as the strongest, with Dumpy the ancient swamp frog's immense power trailing closely behind—though its full capabilities were difficult to gauge.
Following them was PinkLotus, her skill undeniable, while Luke himself clearly ranked as the weakest of the group.
'Yeah… this is exactly where I need to be', Luke thought, surprising himself with the positivity of his reflection.
'Unlike when I am with the DarkSky guild, I'm not the strongest here—I'm the weakest. And that's what will make me grow' Luke thought, as a soft smile spread on his face.
"I'm the only non-master warrior in this group, I need to improve fast" Luke muttered to himself, as he felt his desire to become stronger and better, growing with each passing moment.
"Brother, I think we are done here, I'm going to log-out, I'll see you on the other side" Leo said, waving him goodbye, as after conquering the town, Leo simply logged out of the game, half-way through the gaming session, without even caring how much daylight was still left for them to enjoy.
"What? Why does he even do this?" Luke muttered in confusion, as he simply shook his head and chuckled.
Then, with Leo gone, he opened the global forums for a moment, to take a look at what the people were talking about, as was his daily habit, however, when he logged into the global forums, he surprisingly only saw a bunch of hate comments directed at him.
"Skylion, one of the top players of the game and an ex-DarkSky guild member, has betrayed all of us. He's a dirty little snake attacking his own guilds stronghold after leaving on his own accord"
"I looked up to SkyLion as a DarkSky guild member, in my heart his position was as unshakeable as the heavens.
When he participated in the grand tournament and was dropping his opponents on their heads via suplexes, I was the loudest cheer in the crowd, however, today when he dropped me on my head, I started to despise him.
I've never hated someone as much as I hate him, for i lost 3 levels from dying by his hands and also dropped my (epic) ranked sword upon death, that took me 7 months of savings to buy.
This setback is going to cost me a lifetime to recover, and for this situation to have arisen because I met one of my heroes is just deplorable.
Skylion is a snake"
"At this point, Skylion should just leave the lion out of his name and change it to a snake, because he loves to bite the hand that once fed him"
"I was sad when Skylion left the guild… but now I'm glad we got rid of such a toxic and unstable guy–"
Luke felt his heartbeats rising steadily when he read these hate comments, as he could feel the rage building inside him.
He was sure that it wasn't him that had betrayed the DarkSky guild, but the guild that had betrayed him, however, he was too much of a gentleman to expose what had gone down behind the scenes.
He had taken a dignified exit from the guild and was now his own man, however, the forums painted him as if he were still an active guild member who backstabbed them.
"These guys make me sick to my core" Luke mumbled as he closed the forum chat and closed his eyes to relax.
He could feel the rage bubbling within him, as he struggled to hold his calm.
At his core he was a guy who cared about his public view too much and seeing himself being bashed online with all this hate messed up his mindset big-time.
However, unlike before, he felt better equipped to tackle it today, as instead of snapping back and bantering on the forums, he simply took in a deep breath and focus on his mental peace instead.
"The world can say what they want about me, but the fact remains that I gained two levels today from this war.
I'm rapidly improving by coming here and am also getting a chance to use my untested skills in practical combat, getting used to a new fighting style.
Today was hence a productive day, and nothing can upset me about it" Luke said to himself, as let inhaled and exhaled deep breaths trying to bring his heart-rate down.
"You okay? You're breathing a little uneasy…" PinkLotus asked when she saw Luke struggling in a corner, as immediately Luke smiled and gave her a thumbs up.
