"Yeah, I'm okay, don't worry" he said, putting forward his best face, as although PinkLotus was not convinced by his reply, she simply nodded and smiled back.
She knew that this war was always going to be hard on Luke, however, so far he seemed to be handling it exceptionally well.
He fought without showing his opponents any mercy and did not shy away from killing them rather brutally.
He was here with the intent to fight, which made PinkLotus feel satisfied in his performance.
However, while Luke's performance today impressed her, Dumpy's performance outright shocked her, as the frog, who was also a swordsman seemed to be both faster and stronger than her.
Dumpy's strength impressed her today to the point where she felt on the edge to ask the creature for a spar, however, when she realized it was an NPC and not even a human one, she restrained herself from the embarassment.
'Its just a stupid pet…' she thought, however, while she thought Dumpy was just a stupid pet, his strength still left a deep impression in her mind.

chapters.title: Chapter 738 - 738: War Begins
chapters.content:
(The next day, Bernabeu)
Next day outside the Western Capital City Of Bernabeu, the WhiteSaber guild's decisive war for their future finally began.
Early in the morning, the guild's beast tamers ordered their load carrying pets to mobilize the siege machines, while the guild's mages and tanks protected the convoy from being hit from range.
Oxes, Donkeys and Horses were mobilized in large numbers, dragging the massive war machines like trebuchets and mortars ahead, as the DarkSky defenders watching from the city walls raised the alarms.
"The enemy is moving…. The enemy has made a move! Everyone get to your battle stations. Focus! Focus! Focus!" A DarkSky guild team captain shouted, as he prepared his team for war.
Following the order, the guild members scrambled to their positions atop the high stone walls, each armed with bows, crossbows, and staffs that glowed faintly with magical energy.
Archers within the group in particular, formed tight ranks, their group captains shouting orders to notch arrows and hold fire until the enemy came within range, while behind them, shield-bearers braced massive iron-reinforced barriers against the parapets, ready to deflect the inevitable onslaught.
Meanwhile, from the siege lines below, the beast tamers barked sharp commands, and their beasts of burden heaved with renewed vigor.
Trebuchets groaned as their armatures were loaded with boulders, while mortars were carefully aligned by teams of engineers sweating under their heavy armor.
"Turn it two more degrees to the left…"
"The wind speed is changing irregularly, put a 5% margin of error in your calculations…"
"Faster, Faster, Faster… This is just the first volley"
"You're not coiling the spring hard enough, Push! Push! Push! We need maximum range–"
Said the engineers as talked amongst one another, getting their war machines ready for action.
*HONKKK*
At that point, a distant sharp piercing horn cut through the morning haze—and the WhiteSaber army ground to a halt.
Silence followed, broken only by the creaking of wood and the distant rustle of wind over the battlefield, as the engineers made the final adjustments to their war machines.
"Fire!"
Then came the orders, carried down the ranks by messengers weaving through the crowd, as the trebuchets loomed into motion, their great arms pulled back and locked into place, as on the command of the guild master, the first volley was launched.
Massive stones sailed through the air with a low, guttural roar, arcing toward the city walls.
Watching the volley come, the DarkSky defenders shouted warnings as the projectiles closed the distance.
*BOOM*
A few of them hit against the wall, crashing against the fortifications with deafening force, as chunks of stone and dust rained down on those below, but the walls held firm... At Least for now.
"COUNTER FIRE!" A DarkSky captain said, as the defenders retaliated almost immediately.
Arrows and thunderbolts rained down from the walls and sky in a deadly barrage, their sharp whistling growing louder as they pierced the ranks below.
*KABOOOM*
*SHUA*
WhiteSaber's mages raised shimmering barriers of light to protect their forces, while healers scrambled to treat the wounded.
In response, the trebuchets and mortars fired again, joined by the crackling energy of offensive spells launched from WhiteSaber's battle-mages.
Overall, fiery explosions began to erupt in every square inch of the walls, forcing the DarkSky members to operate under maximum focus.
The siege was underway, and what had initially started as the measured movements of armies was rapidly descending into chaos.
The smell of smoke and burning wood mixed with the metallic tang of blood, signalled the beginning of a long, brutal battle, as the WhiteSaber army slowly but surely forged ahead.
********
(Meanwhile the Whitesaber guildmaster)
The WhiteSaber guild master observed the progress of his guild from the backlines, as he orchestrated the march ahead to the best of his abilities.
The plan today was not to push all the way in, unless the city wall crumbled, but just to keep the siege machines safe and damage the walls enough to hopefully break them in the coming days.
The guildmaster knew that the most important asset of the guild right now was not the expensive war machines, but the morale and manpower they had, which was why he prioritized saving lives over conserving ammunition.
He understood that if the guild lost too many people on the first day, the morale would plunge to unprecedented lows, which was why he had instructed all captain's to prioritise survival.
All guild members were given the freedom to fire as many arms and drink as many potions as they needed, ensuring that no one hesitated in the heat of battle.
"Keep fighting," he muttered under his breath as he observed the battlefield, as the eastern wall of Bernabeu, battered by constant volleys, began to show faint cracks, though it still held firm.
The WhiteSabers plan was simple, which was to not waste manpower until the city walls crumbled and they had a clear point of entry, as the guildmaster understood that trying to fight hard before that was just plain stupid.
With the enemy having the advantage of a walls protection and elevation, a reckless charge was bound to fail, which was why he remained patient.
Meanwhile, on the battlefield, the freedom to act as needed kept the WhiteSaber forces agile.
Archers launched arrow after arrow with no concern for reserves, while mages hurled fireballs and drank replenishing potions at a relentless pace.
Healers too worked in tandem, using their restorative spells and potions to ensure the frontline remained intact, as the guild focused on keeping their losses to a minimum.
Overall, the start of the war was pretty evenly matched with the Duke and DarkSky defending forces not losing much men and the city wall still holding.
While the WhiteSabers also did not lose too many men, while accomplishing their goal to somewhat weaken the city walls structure.
The momentum of this war now hung by a narrow thread, and it seemed like whichever side made the first breakthrough, would now control the momentum of this fight.

chapters.title: Chapter 739 - 739: StaleMate
chapters.content:
(Cervantez's POV)
Despite all his shortcomings as a friend, when it came to running a guild, Cervantez was an absolute machine.
Standing atop the Bernabeu City walls, He stoically observed the stalemate as the WhiteSaber guild walked towards their own death.
While on the surface, it looked like the WhiteSabers were an impressive guild, having thousands of engineers, dozens of war machines and an impressive supply of ammunition for their archers to use, in reality they were absolutely nothing in comparison to the DarkSky guild, who were currently merely conserving their strength.
Having prioritised quality over quantity and having controlled the critical supplies of the game for a long time, the DarkSky guild was no stranger to war.
Not only did the guild members have years of experience fighting the demons at the borders, but they also had access to vast reserves of ammunition of their own, which far surpassed anything the WhiteSabers could ever hope to muster.
The smoke that arose from smithy's run by the DarkSky guild, never wore thin throughout the year, as no matter night or day, the production never stopped.
"Good, everything is going as planned…. Inform Lysa and Tor to get ready, it will soon be time for the 'intervention'." Cervantez said, as once the Whitesabers approached the one kilometre mark outside Bernabeu City walls, he activated plan 'Intervention'.
Plan intervention involved the DarkSky guild going all-out to intervene and slow down the enemy's advance, as once Cervantez gave the command to activate it, not only did Lysa and Tor get ready, but so did Jess and his archers, who cracked their necks and began circulating their mana.
"Archers… darken the skies." Jess commanded, as immediately a terrifying volley of arrows were unleashed into the air, nothing like what the Whitesabers had seen before.
Up till now, the DarkSky archers had held back, firing nothing but basic volleys that served only to test the enemy's resolve. But now, the time had changed.
Suddenly, the air above the battlefield came alive with thousands of projectiles, as unlike before, this time the arrows shot seemed to be of the special skills kind, changing their nature mid-air.
[Arrow Replication]
Each arrow split into dozens mid-flight, creating a deadly rain of projectiles that seemed endless.
[Rapid Shot]
The next wave was a barrage, faster than the eye could follow, filling every gap in the air left by the previous volley.
[Armor-Break Shot]
These arrows glowed a menacing red, tearing through shields and heavy armor as though they were paper, as the sky above Bernabeu turned black with arrows, blocking out the sun as the storm descended upon the WhiteSaber guild.
Meanwhile, on the ground, the WhiteSabers braced against the onslaught.
Shields were raised, barriers conjured, and mages worked frantically to deflect the deadly projectiles.
However, despite their best efforts, casualties mounted quickly.
Screams echoed across the battlefield as men and women fell under the relentless hail. Healers ran from one injured soldier to the next, pouring potions and mana into their comrades to keep the line intact.
"Hold the line! We're almost there!" shouted a WhiteSaber captain, his voice hoarse but unwavering.
Yet, despite the chaos, the army continued its march forward, dragging their siege engines closer to the walls with sheer determination.
Soon, as the WhiteSaber forces reached the 1km mark, Cervantez lowered his arm once more.
"Lysa, Tor, it's time. Show them what we're made of." he said, as the messenger standing beside him wasted no time relaying the order.
Within moments, the massive gates at the eastern and western ends of the city groaned open, and the ground began to tremble.
From the gates emerged two single-file columns of mounted warriors, their armor gleaming and blue banners snapping in the wind.
Lysa and Tor led their respective units with stoic precision, barking orders to their riders as they formed into battle formations outside the walls.
Ten thousand mounted soldiers now flanked the WhiteSaber army. Once their ranks were set, Cervantez gave the final signal.
"Charge."
Like a tidal wave, the riders surged forward, their lances and swords glinting in the morning sun. The thunder of hooves drowned out the sound of battle as they closed the distance to the enemy front lines with terrifying speed.
Panic rippled through the WhiteSaber ranks as the charging cavalry threatened to envelop their flanks, as for a brief moment, it seemed as though the line would break, throwing the entire formation into disarray.
But then, as if choreographed, the WhiteSaber guild executed a maneuver that turned the tide. The frontlines parted into neat corridors, creating straight, open paths leading directly to their rear.
From these corridors, their backlines surged forward with practiced precision. A contingent of heavy infantry and Uprising guild members charged headlong into the oncoming cavalry, meeting them with a thunderous clash of steel, as they seemed to have long predicted this move.
"So it begins…." Muttered the WhiteSaber guildmaster, as if Cervantez was a great guildmaster, he was no slouch either, as he had long foreseen such a maneuver.
In terms of pure quality, there was no equal to the DarkSky guild, as not even the uprising could take them on in a clean battle.
However, when they were debuffed by 35%, the Uprising guilds men were more than a match for them, as the frontlines turned into a bloody contest of steel.
Swords clashed against swords, spears clashed against spears and spells clashed against spells.
The entire frontline turned into a mish-mash of allies and enemies, while from the back the war machines continued to hurl their projectiles.
For now, the stalemate continued, however with how intense the fighting was, something had to give and soon.
*******
(Meanwhile Leo)
Leo observed the developing battle through livestreamers on the forums and while he did not have an unimpeded picture like Cervantez or The WhiteSaber guildmaster, he could gather information of his own.
He was already on his way to Bernabeu, being only an hour away from the battlefield, However, he had still not made-up his mind on whether or not he would join the war now.
For now he continued to observe, as he waited eagerly for the stalemate to break.

chapters.title: Chapter 740 - 740: Changing Tides
chapters.content:
The frontline fight between the uprising and the DarkSky guild members was a sight to behold.
In terms of overall levels and proficiency, The DarkSky guild members were about 10-20% higher levelled compared to their Uprising peers and their skills were of a superior grade too.
With the global level average being around 320, this gap was a difference of 30-60 levels, which was significant when viewed on a macro level.
While the average Uprising rebel was levelled 320-350, right around the global average or only slightly better, the average DarkSky guild member was levelled around 350-380, significantly ahead of the global curve.
To add to the situation, most within the DarkSky guild, only practised skills of the (Epic) rank or higher and seemed to carry weapons and armour of (Gold) grade or higher.
This was much better than their rebel counterparts who often foraged and looted what they could find from corpses and roamed around in mis-matched sets of the best gear they could find, instead of a uniform set.
However, despite these differences, the two sides were more or less evenly matched in battle today, solely because of the -35% debuff applied on the righteous faction players which was like the great equalizer.
The debuff forced the DarkSky guild members to sweat in action against opponents that were not really on their level, as they were beaten back for strength and pace, making openings in defence hard to come by.
Just like the demons, the rebels also fought with raw aggression rather than discipline and strategy, as they weren't a highly organized force capable of executing intricate maneuvers, but were instead a rag-tag group of misfits that relied on sheer determination and relentless energy to win.
This made fighting against them feel like a constant challenge, as there was no breathing room given for even a second, with every exchange of moves being a potential life/death scenario.
However, if one could stay disciplined under the relentless pressure, not opening up defence and holding the battle lines tight then the rebel threat was easy to neutralize.
Apart from raw aggression and equal numbers, the rebels did not have much else going for them, while the DarkSky soldiers had the advantage of 'Experience' behind them.
Having fought and held off demons at the borders several times, the DarkSky members were now comfortable entrusting their backs to one another in battle, fighting as a unit instead of individuals, which made their overall defence much more robust.
In war, battle line shapes and tactics played a huge part in how effective a group was as a unit, and this was where the battle scales tipped in the favor of the DarkSky.
While the rebels fought solo, the DarkSky fought as one, and slowly their defensive resilience turned to offensive brilliance, as once the shape of the rebels frontline became irregular, gaps opened up for the DarkSky guild to overwhelm individual rebels two versus one, changing the whole momentum of the battle.
Slowly but surely, the evenly matched dynamic broke into an outmatched dynamic, as despite having a 35% debuff, the DarkSky guild members began overwhelming the rebels through sheer brilliance of tactics.
"Duhan! Don't charge too far, you're breaking our shape, pull back"
"Dorothy! Don't become too aggressive, let the wounded run back, don't chase"
"Jake! What the fuck are you even doing, hold back your unit!"
Tor shouted, as he oversaw the unfolding battle and controlled his men to hold steady.
Lysa too did the same on her end, as although she was a battle mage capable of wreaking AOE havoc, for now she focused on troops management, seldom casting spells and mostly remaining focused on the overall battle-shape, ensuring that none of her men strayed too far.
As the hours passed, the Uprising was slowly but surely decimated, to the point where three hours later they only had a tenth of their force left.
"Retreat! We are being picked apart for fun now…. Uprising members retreat!" The uprising commander yelled, as finally when the situation became unmanageable, he ordered a retreat to save the levels of as many of his men as he could.
This of-course left the WhiteSaber guild troops behind them vulnerable to a counter-charge, as unfortunately for them, even after hours of bantering the Bernabeu City walls with projectiles, they could still not destroy a section completely.
There were areas where they destroyed a significant portion off the top, or where a 50% section was broken off, however, even in such areas, the intact wall height was still 10-15 meters tall, making it impossible for an army to charge through.
They needed more time to blast open a clear opening, however, with the Uprising guild members facing an unexpected defeat, their remaining options looked feeble.
"Guildmaster, the uprising members have started to retreat… What do we do now? This is beyond our expectations–" A panicked guild member asked the WhiteSaber guildmaster, who watched the unfolding war with sweat pouring down his brows.
"Prepare for battle–" he said stoically, However his heart was already clouded with the grim thoughts of defeat.
This situation was not ideal, however, with things not going their way, this was all they had.
**********
(Meanwhile Cervantez)
"Guildmaster, the Uprising have started to scramble and retreat, the comments by the live watchers on the forums are overwhelmingly positive.
They are calling us 'The Last Hope of the righteous faction' and lauding us for holding strong despite the debuff.
Our impression as the number one guild is solidifying in public minds…. Everything is going exactly as you hoped for" A guild member informed Cervantez, who smiled happily at this news.
Everything so far was going exactly how he anticipated it to go, and currently he seemed on-track to win this war.
"Good…. Keep up the pressure now" Cervantez said stoically, as he did not allow himself to celebrate the victory so early, however, internally, he was beyond exhilarated at this moment, just like every other DarkSky member.
—------
///A/N - I'm back home from China guys, thankyou for your patience these few days.
Special shoutout to the patron ElGuap0 for the massage chair.
Bonus chapter counter - 1120/2500. ///

chapters.title: Chapter 741 - 741: Entry
chapters.content:
(Leo's POV)
Leo was unsure about whether he wanted to join the war or not, until he stumbled upon what the global comments section said about the whole situation.
"Look at the Uprising failing miserably to beat back debuffed DarkSky members, just goes to show how they aren't really powerful at their core, but just opportunistic bullies"
"If the Uprising members did not have the stats advantage, I don't think they would be able to sweep through the southern and central regions like they are right now…."
"The DarkSky guild is truly made up of the best of the best, you can see it in their stamina management and troop rotation. They don't let anyone take the heat for too long and have each other's back"
"The DarkSky is the #1 guild in the world, The Boss is a fearsome force alone, but the DarkSky guild is the most influential, they are the hope of the west!"
"Alright, I've made up my mind… I'm going to take refuge in the west and help the DarkSky guild beat back the rebels! Even if they capture StrongHaven City, the west will always be a righteous faction safe haven!"
"Long Live the West! Long Live Guildmaster Cervantez! Long Live DarkSky!"
"This war is sealed… if the rebels can't help the dirty WhiteSabers capture Bernabeu, there's no way they can do it on their own, we will observe a massacre soon…"
"The WhiteSabers prided themselves for their war machines, boasted about it on the forums, however, even when given hours, they simply cannot bring down one city wall…. Their machines and engineers are a joke"
"Not even 'TheBoss' personally joining this war can now change its fate…. The WhiteSabers are done for"
It wasn't until Leo read these comments that he felt the petty urge to join this war, just to prove a point.
He was live streaming peacefully and did not intend to join a losing war, as he could technically enjoy a much larger slice of the west if he captured it using uprising men instead of helping the WhiteSabers, however, when he saw the DarkSky and Cervantez being praised, Leo decided to join this fight, just for the sake of ruining their good name.
"Alright Dumpy, off to war we go–" he commanded, as Dumpy began to speed up, trying to cover the last 5 kilometers, until he entered the battlefield, while Leo himself began to channel his entire mana, replicating a move he [Copied] not too long ago.
**********
(At the battlefield)
The WhiteSabers were disheartened when they saw the Uprising retreating.
The war engineers at the front lines began to tremble, their loading speed slowing down, as they feared for their inevitable deaths.
Thoughts of desertion began to creep up in the minds of many, as they looked around, hoping that they weren't the first ones to run, however, with the collective bunch not running, nobody wanted to be the first to break ranks.
"Prepare for battle…. Incoming!!!" Shouted the captain's who readied their men for war, however, there was a nervous edge to their voices, which made the men feel as if even the captains were afraid to fight.
However, at this moment, when all signs pointed towards a WhiteSaber defeat and the momentum of the whole war was about to change, a multi-colored arrow suddenly shot past everyone's head, flying straight towards the section of the wall that seemed to be most damaged.
*WHIZZZ*
The arrow, buzzing with energy, zoomed past the soldiers drawing everyone's attention, as for a second, everyone turned to see what was going on.
*KABOOM*
A loud explosion rang from the Bernabeu wall, as out of nowhere an opening was created in the wall with a huge section being blasted clear.
The [Rainbow Shot] with all its power, managed to utterly destroy the remaining half of the wall that stood strong, opening a clear and open path to entering the Bernabeu City.
"Who?" Muttered the men on the frontlines, as they had no idea as to which mage managed to pull off this incredible move within their guild, However, watching the wall crumple gave many amongst the WhiteSaber the spark of hope that they seemed to have lost just a moment ago.
*Cheer*
*Shouts*
*Indiscernible screams of joy*
It started slow, but soon developed into a ruckus, as for some reason a primal cheer went up from the WhiteSaber backlines as they seemed to witness something unbelievable.
It started small, a few thousand men chanting, However, it soon grew into the biggest cheer one had ever heard, as over a hundred thousand men began to cheer at the top of their lungs, when they saw 'that' man joining the war.
With his black robes fluttering clearly against the wind and his giant green frog unmistakable under his feet, 'TheBoss' seemed to join the war from the side of the Whitesabers and with just his entry alone, the whole energy around the WhiteSaber camp seemed to change.
It was an indescribable feeling for most, watching him charge into battle headfirst, as nobody expected to see him here.
At this point, it was the legend that surrounded his name that gave the men behind his back the courage to follow, as although he gave no flashy speeches, and no commands to follow him, the WhiteSaber guild members felt their feets moving automatically, as they charged as one.
"BOSS! BOSS! BOSS!" A chant erupted, as more so than their own guild, the players seemed to believe in the man fighting solo.
For most, he was a gaming god now who could do no wrong and when they saw him finally join the fray, jumping off his frog and killing a few men upon landing, somehow they felt like the war was as good as won.
"Follow the boss!"
"Charge! To the wall!"
"There is an opening…. The city is ours to take!"
"Give the enemy no quarter!!!!"
The WhiteSaber captain's roared, their voices full of confidence now, as once again, the war for the control of the West took an unexpected turn, this time because of the entry of just one man.

chapters.title: Chapter 742 - 742: Old Opponents
chapters.content:
Cervantez frowned as he spotted Leo entering the battlefield atop Dumpy.
'Why would someone like TheBoss waste his time on this conflict when he still had a throne left to claim?' he wondered, as he clicked his tongue.
But while Leo's presence only earned a frown, Cervantez's expression twisted into something far darker when he noticed Luke fighting alongside him.
As he saw Luke fighting with his sword and shield, hatred boiled in his chest, clouding his thoughts with raw fury.
"You dare show your face here?" Cervantez muttered, his knuckles white as snow as he clenched his sword in a death grip.
If not for his responsibility to remain behind and guide his guild, he would have thrown himself into the fray without hesitation, ready to confront Luke head-on. But for now, he forced himself to stay rooted, his body trembling with restrained rage.
"It's the fairy PinkLotus!" Someone muttered beside him, as Cervantez's gaze then veered to the fourth character joining the war, which was none other than PinkLotus, his crush.
Complicated emotions arose in his heart as he saw PinkLotus fight alongside his enemies, however, he quickly turned his gaze away from her, unable to understand why his thoughts felt so clouded whenever he gazed upon that woman.
"She's fighting with my enemies, so why can I not bring myself to dislike her? It's almost like my body won't allow me to dislike her, but I don't understand why?" Cervantez muttered, as at this point he began to realize that his infatuation with PinkLotus was not normal, however, he could not wrap his head around why exactly he felt the way he felt.
"Guildmaster your orders?" A subordinate said, disturbing Cervantez when he was contemplating, as suddenly Cervantez jolted back to reality and regained the focused look in his eyes.
"The wall has been breached, prepare for battle. Get our knight squad to form a phalanx near the opening and inform the Duke that a tough battle might be underway soon" Cervantez said, as the subordinate frantically typed his orders into the guild chat and then rushed to carry the rest to the West Duke's war camp.
"Also inform Tor and Lysa to restrain 'TheBoss' as long as they can. Only the two of them working together may stand a chance to slow him down" Cervantez said, as another subordinate relayed the orders to Tor and Lysa.
With 'TheBoss' joining the fight, the whole dynamic of the war had changed and the difference on a macro level became visible, as he alongside his colleagues carved open a path through the disciplined DarkSky formation, like it was butter.
************
When observed from a distance, the way 'TheBoss' fought was nearly impossible to believe.
Cervantez focused on the movement of his feet from the second he disembarked and even after a full 12 minutes had passed, 'TheBoss' was yet to take a single step back, as he did not pause for even a moment to break his advance.
In 12 minutes, he faced dozens of DarkSky soldiers, yet not once did he step back to dodge or deflect a blow, nor did he pause in one location for too long, as he seemed to be constantly advancing at a steady pace.
Mage, Rogue, Hunter, Knight, Swordsman, Paladin, it did not matter what class the opponent was, as against 'TheBoss', nobody stood a chance.
It was a one-sided domination, as it seemed like he was fighting against children, rather than proper opponents.
"Not good…. The Boss is too strong!"
"Can anyone stop this man?"
"We are the DarkSky, we mocked the righteous faction for not being able to take him down together, but when we face him alone, we aren't any better either"
The common DarkSky guild members quickly realized that they were not strong enough to take down 'TheBoss', and not even strong enough to scratch him.
However, burdened with the duty to stand and fight, they still fought valiantly against the gaming god, albeit to no major success.
[Groundshaking Punch!]
A voice boomed from the distance, as Tor arrived before Leo with quite the flair.
*Boom*
*Tremble*
His attack caused a mini earthquake to form, knocking many men, friends and foes alike off their feet, however, Leo remained unfazed.
"I have been waiting for our rematch since you beat me at the Grand Tournament ages ago… I guess it's finally time" Tor said, cracking his neck, as he looked determinedly into Leo's eyes.
[Ice Layer] said a more delicate voice, as suddenly the entire ground between Leo and his opponents froze over, with Lysa entering the scene.
"You also owe me a rematch–" she said, as she too assumed a fighting stance.
"Ants" Leo replied, charging fearlessly on the thin ice surface, as despite the ice having nearly 0 friction to grip on, Leo glided on its surface with ease, as he closed down the distance between himself and Tor and Lysa.
[Berserker Barrage]
[Icy Winds]
Seeing Leo close down the gap, Tor and Lysa immediately used their combination moves, with Tor creating a stream of martial arts punches aimed to push back and block any advance, while Lysa summoned a gust of chilly winds, aimed at freezing an opponent right where they stood, making them and icicle.
It was the perfect combo move to effectively stop an enemy from advancing, and would most likely work on 999/1000 opponents, however, unfortunately for them, their opponent today was that 1/1000.
Slipping intentionally, Leo fell flat on his belly as he continued his gliding over the ice, avoiding Tor's martial punches from above.
While to counter Lysa's icy winds, he placed both his hands in front of his head, creating an aerodynamic arrow, where, his body naturally deflected most of the winds coming his way, allowing him to move through unimpeded.
This way, although he felt the chilly winds and a few small icicles did form on his black robes, it wasn't enough to stop him dead in his tracks, as he did reach his opponents, crashing into the dry rock, regaining his footing.

chapters.title: Chapter 743 - 743: Misunderstandings
chapters.content:
As Leo regained his footing, he pointed his dagger straight towards Tor's neck, however despite having the opportunity to take his head clean off, he paused right before he pierced it, as he pulled away.
He had done so for no other reason but to toy with his enemy's morale, as he assessed the gap between himself and his enemy to be large enough to not worry about it.
However, what he did not know was that by cancelling his strike at the last moment, he accidentally avoided a fate of assured death.
"How? How did you know that I activated that move? How did you avoid my trap?" Tor asked in shock, as suddenly blood began to trickle out of his lips and his ears.
Within seconds, he dropped to his knees before dropping dead as his HP bar dropped from 100% to 0% in a matter of five short seconds.
'What the fuck just happened here?' Leo wondered internally, as he did not understand what happened, however, with his own body being okay he did not care too much for it either.
His opponent had used the move [Shared Fate] to drag Leo down with him, and had Leo even so much as scratched him during that period, he would have died for sure.
[Shared Fate] was a berserker class special skill, which upon activation tied a berserker's fate with that of their opponent, which meant that if the Berserker died during the skills active period, so would their opponent.
However, on the down side, if the user of the skill did not die after 20 seconds of activation, they would suffer irreversible internal bleeding and die.
Having activated the skill when Leo began his dash, Tor had hoped to die quickly, dragging Leo alongside him, however, through some sheer luck, Leo managed to avoid being tied with the strings of [Shared Fate] by not attacking Tor despite having the chance.
For [Shared Fate] to mark him as an opponent, he needed to hit Tor once during the skills active period, however, with him being too egotistical to hit his weak opponent, Leo somehow avoided the grim fate of death, creating another misunderstanding about his abilities.
"You— you can look into the future, yeah? That's your main ability? Isn't it? You can look a couple seconds into the future…. That's the only way you avoided hitting Tor" Lysa said, her voice trembling as she involuntarily took a step away from Leo.
[Shared Fate] was the trump card that the DarkSky guild had prepared against Leo, and Tor was the only guild member who could wield it.
For [Shared Fate] to work, there were a lot of restrictions, such as:-
1) The opponent could not be more than twice as strong as the host.
2) The host had to be in perfect health condition and could not be damaged even slightly before the activation of the skill.
3) The skill could only be used once in 6 months, making it a burden to have on the skill-slot.
4) Despite executing everything correctly, the success rate for the skill to trigger was still only 80%.
It was a skill that only Tor, being a level 505 warrior could use against Leo who was now nearly level 999, as there wasn't a single other berserker within the DarkSky guild who could fulfill the first condition alone.
Having anyone else use it would guarantee failure and with the skill only usable once in 6 months it was dead-weight on one's skill slot.
It was impossible and cruel to demand any guild member to voluntarily give up a skill-slot for such a seldom used skill that still had only an 80% chance of success and hence the DarkSky guild had no-one else who cultivated this move.
It was supposed to be the ultimate contingency against 'TheBoss', who was ruthless and cold and it was a move that 'TheBoss' was never supposed to see coming.
The reason behind why Cervantez had chosen to send Tor and Lysa to the frontlines was because he anticipated 'TheBoss' interfering and hoped to deal with him early, however, that plan was not all but ruined.
The ultimate weapon that the DarkSky guild had prepared for months against 'TheBoss', had failed to deliver the kill when it mattered the most and it gave rise to a world of misunderstandings.
As per Leo's nature, it was unlikely for him to ever spare an enemy just to toy with them, as that simply wasn't his style of fighting.
He was a ruthless fighter to his bone, and hence when he spared Tor for the sole reason to toy with him some more, Lysa misunderstood this as him being able to look into the future, which absolutely terrified her as a player.
[Future Sight] was a rumoured divine move within the world of Terra Nova that had many urban legends about it but was never seen in use.
Not a single player in the world claimed to have obtained the divine skill scroll for [Future Sight] and even players who exchanged a life-time of MP to search for the whereabouts of that skill only received ambiguous clues in return.
However, today, Lysa seemed mistakenly assured that Leo was in possession of that skill, and she screamed it out loud over and over again, in a livestream being watched by millions.
"The Boss has future sight!"
"THE BOSS HAS FUTURE SIGHT"
"The Boss has…."
She repeated the same sentence over and over again in panic, until Leo silenced her with [The Kill Strike] as she died propagating a lie that was a figment of her own creation.
"If I say, that I don't actually have future sight, would you believe me?" Leo muttered once she died, however, his words only seemed to reinforce the beliefs of the onlookers that he did in fact have it.
To the world…. It was as if the biggest and best guarded secret of 'The Boss' had finally been exposed.

chapters.title: Chapter 744 - 744: Impossible
chapters.content:
(Cervantez's POV)
Even with his regressor memory, there were certain things in Terra Nova that Cervantez considered to be utterly impossible.
One of those was a player ever reaching the Level 1000 milestone, and the other was a player acquiring the [Divine] skill, [Future Sight].
Mathematically, reaching Level 1000 was an insurmountable feat for any single player. Yet, defying every law of common sense and probability, TheBoss stood on the cusp of that legendary milestone, with many months of game-time to spare, virtually assuring that he would somehow make it.
It was a feat that was not just exceptional, but also simply unrepeatable, as there was not one player in the universe who could do what 'TheBoss' did.
However, having witnessed TheBoss's exploits first hand, Cervantez could somehow still grasp, at least in part, the reasons behind him becoming level 1000.
But even now, despite everything he knew, Cervantez couldn't begin to comprehend how Leo had managed to acquire [Future Sight].
[Future Sight] was a move that was supposed to be impossible to master for anyone under the [Transcendent] realm, it was rumoured that even if one did find the skill scroll for the move, it was impossible to grasp the skill at the current level of players and even 'TheBoss' was no exception.
Being only a 'Master' level fighter, 'TheBoss' still had a long way to go before he became a transcendent level figure, which was why Cervantez could not wrap his head around how or why Leo could allegedly perform the move.
"No… it's impossible for someone to learn future sight, it can't be… but I also saw him pausing right before he killed Tor, it can't be a coincidence either.
So what's the deal with 'TheBoss' and his powers?" Cervantez wondered, as he bit his lip and thought about all the times where 'TheBoss' displayed abilities that he wasn't supposed to show.
'TheBoss' could somehow replicate any move that he witnessed being cast and Cervantez wondered if he saw someone using [Future Sight] and somehow learnt how to replicate it, even if doing so to a lesser extent.
"No… that's not possible either, there are no transcendent level figures in the world of Terra Nova. It's impossible he picked it from someone else using that move…." Cervantez murmured, as his inability to deduce the source of Leo's unexplained ability caused him to panic.
As per his memories, the skill scroll for [Future Sight] was last seen in possession of a brave NPC sailor 250 years ago within the game world, who tried to sail beyond the storms and try find new lands by relying on future sight to avoid danger.
While it's unknown if he succeeded or failed as per game lore, however, what is known is that he was the last known man in possession of that scroll, with many believing that it's now at the bottom of an ocean within a shipwreck, in the world's most dangerous waters.
"That's the last known place for the divine scroll, and I am sure that the uprising have not actively searched for a shipwreck yet near the western sea.
The Boss should most definitely not be in possession of that divine scroll, that's simply impossible…
But if not the scroll then what? Is it an artifact? Are the game developers cheating to help him?" Cervantez wondered, as the fact that his number one rival may potentially have future sight, bothered him greatly.
"If he does really have it, it's impossible to beat him in one versus one battle.
I'm sure he did not rely on that move during the second annual rankers event, which means he should have obtained it recently" Cervantez mused, as he thought back on how Leo fought during the second rankers event and felt assured that at least back then, he could not look into the future, as if he could, he would not be fighting the way he was.
"This changes everything….. winning this war might not be as simple as I imagined" Cervantez concluded in the end, as the legend of 'TheBoss' began to psychologically haunt him more, now more than ever before.
**********
(Meanwhile PinkLotus and Luke)
While Leo hogged all the spotlight fighting Tor and Lysa, PinkLotus and Luke silently dismantled the DarkSky defence.
Understanding their war tactics the best, Luke made sure to hit spots that would break the shape of the defence, allowing the charging WhiteSaber guild to easily run through the DarkSky front lines without facing too much opposition.
Compared to PinkLotus, Luke's fighting style did not have as much flair or raw explosive power, however, in terms of overall impact on the tide of war, he probably contributed twice as much as PinkLotus did.
PinkLotus on the other hand, flowed through the battlefield like a goddess of war, as she cut down the sea of opponents before her as if they were simply droplets of water in her path.
Compared to a few months ago, her fighting style now seemed way more fluid and refined, as she moved with a gracious beauty and seemed to have no wasted movement.
"Someone stop her! At this rate she will kill an entire legion within half an hour!" One of the DarkSky captains shouted, however, no-one on the battlefield was her match.
As a master warrior, her power, precision and skill control was vastly superior to her peers and it showed in the way she fought, with no-one being able to stop her fury.
"The enemy is overwhelming us! Retreat! All DarkSky troops pull back…. We cannot defeat them here–" A captain shouted eventually, as just a mere hour after PinkLotus and Luke joined the fray, the DarkSky guild ordered a retreat of their frontal troops, ordering them to come back into the safety of the city through the hole that the WhiteSabers had created in the city walls.
It was a clear change in tides, and against all odds it seemed like the WhiteSabers now had an upper hand in this war.

chapters.title: Chapter 745 - 745: War
chapters.content:
(Leo's POV)
As the DarkSky guild members who had advanced beyond the walls to challenge the Uprising began their retreat back to Bernabeu City, the next phase of the war officially commenced.
"Steady now, Dumpy. There's no need to chase them into the city. Let them retreat for now," Leo instructed, raising a hand to halt his companion's instinct to pursue, as he chose to wait and observe for now.
"As you command, Lord Father," Dumpy croaked obediently. His massive 15-foot frame shrinking as he compressed down into a tiny 5-inch form to conserve stamina for now.
"Charge after them, WhiteSabers! Don't let them run"
A commanding voice said from behind them, as when Leo turned, he saw the WhiteSaber guild master leading his men into war, as he rushed past Leo and Dumpy, passing them with a courteous nod.
"All the best–" Leo said, nodding back, as he paused and observed the WhiteSaber guilds attempt to enter Bernabeu.
For now, it seemed like the phalanx that had formed at the broken walls of Bernabeu had parted slightly to allow the retreating troops to re-enter, however, the man guarding the entrance seemed on-edge as they seemed eager to close that opening at the very first sign of danger.
There were around 6,000 DarkSky troops still alive outside the walls and the entrance was simply not big enough for all of them to slip-in before the WhiteSaber army caught up, which caused a bloodbath to erupt, right near the edge of the Bernabeu wall.
The jagged edges of the opening, still faintly glowing with residual energy from his [Rainbow Shot], framed the chaotic retreat of the DarkSky forces like the maw of a colossal beast swallowing its prey.
Dust and debris hung heavy in the air, mixing with the anguished cries of the wounded and the sharp commands of retreating officers.
The DarkSky guild members scrambled over rubble and through smoke, their formation completely shattered. Swords scraped against stone as exhausted soldiers stumbled over fallen comrades, some dragging bleeding allies while others cast desperate glances over their shoulders.
The once-disciplined ranks were reduced to fragmented groups, each fighting to reach the safety of the inner city.
But safety was a fleeting dream.
The WhiteSaber guild was relentless in their pursuit, and ruthless in their killing.
Their WhiteSaber knights, that began the war in gleaming white armor, now roamed around in red, their armours stained with grime and streaks of red, as they defeated the trapped DarkSky enemies ruthlessly.
Their battle cries pierced through the chaos, a stark contrast to the panicked shouts of DarkSky's retreating forces, who feared that the phalanx would eventually close before they had a chance to get-in or they would die before they reached it.
"Press them harder!" bellowed a WhiteSaber captain, his silver sword reflecting the blood red of his surroundings.
"Don't let them regroup inside the walls!" He said, as at his command, a group of WhiteSaber spearmen advanced in perfect synchronization, their shields interlocked as they drove deeper into the opening.
Behind them, battle mages unleashed torrents of fire and arcs of lightning, forcing DarkSky's rear guard to scatter.
Leo remained still, his sharp eyes tracking the flow of battle. From his position near the breach, he could see the ebb and flow of the war-tide shifting.
He could clearly see the DarkSky's attempt to mount a defensive line inside the breach was collapsing under the WhiteSabers' methodical assault, and how by retreating, Cervantez had chosen to sacrifice 3,000 of the 6,000 remaining men, without mounting any real fight.
"They're closing the opening" Leo muttered under his breath, his sharp eyes narrowing, as he saw the DarkSky phalanx closing the entry into the city, dooming thousands of their own soldiers outside, forcing them to fight and die without support.
"HEY WHAT ARE YOU DOING, OPEN THE WALL, I'LL LOSE SO MANY LEVELS IF I DIE"
"I'M RIGHT HERE. LET ME IN. I AM FROM YOUR OWN GUILD"
"Where's the captain? Has he retreated already? What a joke… we are left here to die alone"
"Sorry guys, it's too risky to keep the gap open, we have to close it now, or the WhiteSabers will flood the city with ease, sorry, we cannot take that risk—"
Leo watched patiently as the DarkSky guild turned on its own members, causing friction at the border, as within minutes the poor guys who were not allowed to enter died a horrific death.
Some cursed and swore their guild for this betrayal before they died, while some understood the guild's reason behind doing what they did and went more gracefully.
Wars were not won without sacrifice, and most soldiers understood this very well.
But understanding this grim fate did not make the reality any easier to bear, as the faces of those left outside the walls reflected a mixture of anger, betrayal, and resignation.
Some still fought, lashing out in futile defiance against the encroaching WhiteSaber forces, while others simply dropped their weapons and accepted their fate with resignation.
A lone DarkSky knight, his armor dented and smeared with blood, raised his sword in one final act of defiance. "Come then, cowards! Face me!" he roared, his voice breaking under the weight of exhaustion and despair.
However, the only response he received was a swift hail of arrows piercing his chest and throat, cutting his rebellion short as he crumpled to the blood-soaked earth.
Behind him, the WhiteSaber army continued its relentless advance, shields locked, spears thrusting forward in perfect unison.
Every step they took pushed the remaining DarkSky forces further back into chaos, further away from the safety of the sealed city gates, and soon, no DarkSky guild member remained outside the city walls.
The entire army was annihilated, leaving the WhiteSaber forces, face to face with the DarkSky Phalanx, who was now defending the opening in the wall bravely.
"WhiteSabers! Try and enter if you can—" shouted the DarkSky Commander Jess, as the first wave of WhiteSaber troops pushed their shoulders against the Phalanx, trying to push their opponents back.

chapters.title: Chapter 746 - 746: Breach
chapters.content:
Despite the full-scale war raging between the DarkSky and WhiteSaber forces near the wall, Cervantez found his gaze oddly fixed on Luke.
Amid the chaos of clashing steel, roaring war cries, and explosive magic, Luke stood on the battlefield looking calm and composed.
But it wasn't Luke's battle stance or his confident demeanor that held Cervantez's attention. No, it was the presence of PinkLotus beside him. She stood close, speaking to Luke with an easy smile, gesturing toward the distant skirmishes as if they were spectators rather than participants in a brutal war, and it was her excitement and Luke's steady responses that painted an image of familiarity—of friendship, even in Cervantez's mind.
And that was what gnawed at Cervantez. Luke wasn't supposed to matter right now. Cervantez had bigger priorities—strategic objectives, enemies to monitor, and key players to evaluate. Yet his focus stubbornly remained on Luke and the way PinkLotus interacted with him.
It wasn't jealousy or resentment—it was confusion. PinkLotus was an enigma, distant and untouchable even to those who stood alongside her in battle. She had a reputation for being aloof, even cold. And yet, here she was, speaking to Luke with warmth and energy, sharing a moment in the middle of a warzone.
Cervantez couldn't help but wonder—what had Luke done to earn that level of trust? And why, despite all his efforts to focus on the larger picture, did this sight make him feel so unsettled?
'I am a guildmaster… I am supposed to focus on the war …. I am supposed to focus on threats like 'TheBoss', but then why am I so disturbed with the sight of two people talking?' Cervantez wondered, as once again, he felt that there was something fundamentally wrong with his brain.
It wasn't his nature to worry about such things, however, oddly, whenever PinkLotus was involved, he seemed to behave unnaturally.
"Guildmaster! Guildmaster! There's a message from the camp of the West Duke–" A guild messenger said, as he rushed beside Cervantez and handed him an official message scroll.
Distracted, Cervantez grabbed the scroll and unflurred it in a hurry, only to find his eyes widening when he read the contents.
"The West Duke wants to face 'TheBoss' head on? This is perfect…. As a level 921 NPC, he's the only one that can hopefully match 'TheBoss' in battle" Cervantez muttered, as he handed back the message scroll excitedly.
Apparently, after finding out that the KingSlayer was here in person, the West Duke had decided to confront him in direct combat, believing that no-one else would be his match.
This of-course came as a welcome relief to Cervantez who was racking his brains on how to deal with 'TheBoss' who had future sight, However, with the West Duke taking that problem off his plate, he found himself now capable of focusing on other key issues.
"Very well then…. Tell the West Duke that we will support his battle against 'TheBoss' as much as possible and create a path for him to retreat should his life ever be in danger" Cervantez said, as the messenger quickly wrote it down and rushed-off to pass it on.
**********
The phalanx of the DarkSky guild remained unexpectedly resilient against the WhiteSabers advance for a few minutes at the start, however, quickly began to falter, when the enemy introduced their hidden weapon the devastating [Frost Grenades].
Frost Grenades were not just ordinary explosives, they were a unique weapon of war which were encased in crystalline orbs and infused with potent ice mana, that were engineered to shatter on impact, releasing an eruption of frigid energy that froze everything within a five-meter radius in a thick layer of frost.
What made them truly devastating, however, was their secondary effect, which was a chilling mist that lingered after the initial explosion, sapping the strength and agility of anyone caught within it.
For the WhiteSaber guild, these grenades were not just weapons, they were a hidden ace, a trump card they had hoarded for the right moment, as they had deliberately hidden this weapon for many years.
The [Frost Grenade] could only be obtained via one single dungeon in the world of Terra Nova, the 'Western Ice Dungeon' by defeating its infamous boss monster, the Yeti.
However, with the WhiteSabers holding exclusive control of the level 350 dungeon for years, they had become the only guild to amass a stockpile of Frost Grenades within the game.
The weapon had remained a secret from the rest of the player base, kept hidden even during their earlier campaigns. But now, with the fate of Bernabeu City hanging in the balance, the WhiteSabers unleashed them with ruthless precision.
*Kapish*
The first volley of Frost Grenades landed deep within the DarkSky phalanx, detonating in bursts of icy blue light.
Shards of frost splintered across shields and armor, freezing weapons in mid-swing and locking soldiers' boots to the rubble-strewn ground.
The chilling mist seeped into the formation, causing soldiers to shiver uncontrollably, their movements growing sluggish as their stamina plummeted.
"Watchout– the enemy possesses some funny weapons!" a DarkSky soldier warned.
"Hold the line! HOLD THE LINE!" a DarkSky captain bellowed, his voice cracking with desperation as his soldiers struggled against the freezing haze. But it was futile.
The WhiteSaber knights surged forward, exploiting the disarray caused by the grenades.
Their front liners dissolved into aggressive assault squads, breaking through frozen gaps in the DarkSky defence line.
Swords and spears drove into vulnerable openings, shields smashed aside frozen limbs, and the air was filled with the sound of shattering ice and dying screams.
"Another volley! Break them apart!" roared a WhiteSaber officer, his voice carrying over the din of battle, as upon his command a second wave of Frost Grenades flew overhead, bursting amidst the already weakened formation.
This time, the explosions created cracks in the DarkSky lines so wide that the WhiteSaber vanguard poured through them like water rushing through a shattered dam.
Leo, still observing from a safe distance, narrowed his eyes as he watched the phalanx collapse entirely.
The once-imposing shield wall of the DarkSky defenders crumbled as soldiers abandoned their positions, some attempting to flee back towards the safety of the deeper city, others falling to the merciless advance of the WhiteSaber assault teams.
The path to Bernabeu City's gates was now wide open.
"Push forward! Into the city!" the WhiteSaber guildmaster said, as the first wave of WhiteSaber forces surged through the breach, clambering over rubble and trampling the bodies of fallen enemies.
The walls of Bernabeu City, weakened and unguarded after the collapse of the phalanx, were no longer an obstacle to the WhiteSabers as with a collective roar, hundreds of WhiteSaber knights and soldiers flooded through the opening, spilling into the narrow alleys and plazas of the city.
The once-clear lines of battle dissolved into street-to-street skirmishes as DarkSky defenders attempted to regroup amidst the chaos.
Flames began to rise from several sections of the city as WhiteSaber mages unleashed fiery spells, targeting defensive chokepoints and key infrastructure.
Bernabeu City had been breached. The war was no longer confined to its outer walls and had now spilled into its very heart.
The fate of the city hung in balance, and with it, the fate of the west.

chapters.title: Chapter 747 - 747: A fight long due
chapters.content:
A few minutes after the Bernabeu walls were breached, Leo finally decided to make a move.
Signaling to Luke and PinkLotus to follow him, he entered Bernabeu City, having already sensed the presence of the powerful enemy who awaited him within.
The three figures moved through the shattered walls and into the ruined city streets, where small fights surrounded them everywhere.
Anywhere one turned, they could see a group of WhiteSaber players fighting against the DarkSky guild members or the Duke's forces, however, none of them dared interrupt the path of 'TheBoss'.
As Leo walked, allies and enemies alike parted to make way for him, as he simply moved past the city walls, towards the network of streets connecting every corner of Bernabeu City.
His destination was clear, moving towards the point where the concentration of mana felt the thickest, signalling the presence of an extremely strong opponent, who probably awaited his entry.
Leo walked at an unhurried pace, his posture relaxed but his sharp gaze scanning their surroundings.
Meanwhile, perched on his shoulder, Dumpy, in his miniature form, croaked softly, his golden eyes darting to every flicker of movement.
"The smell of fear lingers here, Lord Father," Dumpy said, his voice cutting through the stillness. "It reeks of weaklings and mongrels."
Leo smirked but said nothing. Behind him, PinkLotus walked with effortless grace, her sharp eyes betraying her readiness for conflict. Luke followed at her side, his hand resting lightly on the hilt of his sword, his face impassive as he studied the smoke and fire that now covered much of Bernabeu City.
Soon, as they rounded a corner into a large cathedral courtyard, their path was blocked by a towering figure clad in silver armor.
Standing tall amidst the rubble and ash, West Duke James awaited them. His ornate greatsword, etched with ancient runes, rested heavily against his shoulder, glowing faintly with embedded mana crystals.
"So, the infamous 'TheBoss' finally arrives," James said, his voice a deep rumble, carrying an authority that made the air feel heavier. "You walk these streets without shame, even after plunging an empire into chaos."
Leo tilted his head slightly, his smirk widening. "Chaos? Please. I prefer to call it… progress."
James' jaw tightened as his gauntleted fingers curled around the hilt of his sword.
"You butchered a child of an Emperor in cold blood. You stand here drenched in the blood of my dear colleagues and master warriors who were the pillars of this Empire. Do you feel nothing, 'TheBoss'?" James asked, but before Leo could respond, Dumpy puffed up slightly on his shoulder, croaking loudly.
"Mind your tongue, mongrel!" Dumpy snapped, his voice sharp and full of disdain. "You dare speak to Lord Father in such a tone? Look at you—clad in polished metal, pretending to be noble while trembling in your boots!"
James' eyes flickered towards the tiny frog, his expression momentarily faltering before returning to one of steely determination.
Leo chuckled, raising a hand to silence Dumpy. "Calm yourself, Dumpy. Let the good Duke speak. After all, this is his last chance to sound dignified before I put him in the dirt."
James lifted his sword, pointing it directly at Leo. "Enough. No more words, no more games. Today I shall make you pay for what you have done to this Empire"
Leo's smirk faded slightly, his eyes sharpening as he reached for the hilt of his dagger.
"Very well, Duke. Let's dance." He said, as he cracked his neck, while Dumpy jumped off and turned into an average 10 feet sized frog.
"SkyLion…. PinkLotus, you guys can go explore the beautiful city on your own, I've got him" Leo assured, as upon getting his approval, Luke and PinkLotus continued to walk ahead, leaving Dumpy and Leo alone to face off against the West Duke.
***********
(Luke and PinkLotus's POV)
The duo's movements were fluid and cautious as they navigated through the smoke-choked streets of Bernabeu.
But waiting for them in an abandoned plaza, standing amidst the wreckage of a once-grand fountain, was Cervantez—the Guildmaster of DarkSky.
His blue and golden guild robe billowed slightly in the warm updraft of nearby fires, and his sword hung loosely at his side, its polished edges reflecting the flickering orange glow of the flames.
"Skylion," Cervantez said, his voice low but carrying across the broken stones.
"We meet again…. friend" Cervantez said, disdain evident in his voice.
"Guildmaster," Luke replied evenly, his tone lacking emotion.
Cervantez took a step closer, his eyes narrowing as he studied Skylion.
"You know, there was a time I trusted you with my life. You stood by me, fought beside me. And now…" He gestured around them, at the burning ruins of Bernabeu. "…you stand with him. With 'TheBoss'. You bite the hand that fed you, and you kill the very people you swore to protect."
"You're a snake SkyLion. A despicable snake, and nurturing you has been the biggest mistake I've made in this life" Cervantez said, as his words made Luke inhale deeply.
"Really? Even after all this time, even after betraying me so hard, you still think you have the moral high ground here?" Luke asked, sounding hurt, as his eyes turned into two fireballs of fury.
"It wasn't me who decided to stand against 'TheBoss', it wasn't me who voted to make the West the last bastion of righteous faction hope. I sensed the downfall of the righteous faction before I ever happened, it was you and your vain pride that has now placed the DarkSky guild on the backfoot" Luke said, as he refused to give Cervantez an inch of moral superiority.
"Ha…haha….Hahahaha–" Cervantez chuckled, as he pointed towards Luke and covered his eyes like a maniac.
"You predicted the fall of the righteous faction? You think we have already lost bernabeu? Why? Cause 'TheBoss' is here?
Well alright, remove him and what are you on your own?
He's out there busy fighting the West Duke, can the loyal dog defend himself without help from 'TheBoss' and PinkLotus?" Cervantez questioned, as Luke simply drew his sword in response.
This was a fight long due.

chapters.title: Chapter 748 - 748: First Blood
chapters.content:
PinkLotus nervously bit her bottom lip as she watched Luke step forward, ready to face Cervantez in a one-on-one battle.
'Should I intervene?' she wondered, doubt gnawing at her confidence as she questioned if Luke could really win this fight on his own?
But despite her reservations, she wisely chose to stay on the sidelines— at least for now, as she understood that this fight meant a lot to Luke.
Win or lose, it was a necessary step for his growth.
The resentment he carried from what Cervantez had done to him back at the guild had festered for too long, and this confrontation was his chance to finally face it head-on.
'Go! Go! Go! Crush him Luke!' PinkLotus thought, as she silently cheered him on, her cheeks flushing slightly red, as she found her heart beating just slightly faster.
"Oh? So you've decided to fight fair SkyLion and face me alone? I thought for sure the beautiful lady here was your bodyguard" Cervantez commented, as he glanced between Luke and PinkLotus, feeling surprised to see that she wasn't making a move.
"He doesn't need me to guard him from the likes of you! Weaklings like you…. He can take them in his sleep" PinkLotus retorted coldly, as her words left Cervantez speechless.
'Did she just call me a weakling?' Cervantez wondered, as he first glanced at his sword and then towards PinkLotus in confusion.
He too was one of the four guardians in the second rankers event and was undeniably one of the strongest players of Terra Nova Online.
There was an argument to be made that he was not the strongest or second strongest player, however, there was no one who could deny him being top5.
Yet, PinkLotus called him a weakling, and that comment really pissed Cervantez off.
"I see…. You've already bewitched her SkyLion…. Just like you had bewitched me, making me think you're a friend. What a snake!" Cervantez said, as at this point Luke charged, feeling that the distance between himself and Cervantez was short enough for him to make a move.
*CLASH*
Sparks flew as Luke crossed swords with Cervantez.
Cervantez gripped his own sword with both hands, putting the force of his entire body behind it to push Luke back, while Luke held his sword with one hand and supported it with his shield from the blunt end to push Cervantez back with the force of his full body.
"ARGHHHH—"
"Come on now!"
Both of them gave this very first exchange their all, gauging the raw strength of one another, however, even after a full 30 seconds passed, no clear winner emerged.
*BREAK*
Both of them broke the move at the same time, staggering back two steps, however, while it seemed like the test of strength had ended in a draw, in reality it was Luke's win.
"Ha–" Luke said, his grin widening, as Cervantez's face turned dark.
Luke was a knight, his build was much more balanced compared to Cervantez, with his stat distribution being more evenly spread across all attributes.
Cervantez on the other hand had invested the most heavily under strength and speed to make the most of his magical swordsman class, leaving him more vulnerable defensively and on other fronts like dexterity and stamina.
Hence, for him to only be able to match Luke in a test of sheer strength was not a good thing, as it was supposed to be his strong suit, which was why, despite the duel ending in a draw, it was a small win for Luke.
[Flame Wave]
Flicking his hand, Cervantez used his signature AOE move, the [Flame Wave] as he tried to use his mana specialities to suppress Luke, now that raw strength had failed.
[Guardian Shield]
Placing his shield forward, Luke activated the [Legendary] grade move [Guardian Shield] which immediately parted the incoming fire around him, leaving him unharmed.
It was a new move that he had been mastering after he tore down his old skill-set, and hence it was a move that even Cervantez witnessed for the first time.
Unharmed, Luke came out of Cervantez's attack without so much as a speck of dust on his body, which made Cervantez feel slightly frustrated.
"I see you have picked up some new tricks SkyLion, is that courtesy of the beautiful woman standing behind you? Or your generous master Boss?" Cervantez asked, trying to stall for time while he prepared his next move, however, Luke did not fall for it.
[Heaven's Strike]
Activating the [Semi-Legendary] move he had purchased from the system store after the event, Luke used the move [Heaven's Strike] to unleash a powerful attack on Cervantez.
Pointing towards the sky, Luke manifested a radiant golden sigil above his head, glowing with an intense brilliance that pierced through the smoke and chaos of Bernabeu City.
From the heart of the sigil, a massive golden sword began to materialize, its edges sharp enough to split the heavens and its surface etched with ancient runes that pulsed with divine light.
"Heaven's Strike!" Luke's voice thundered across the courtyard as he brought his hand down in a sharp motion, commanding the golden blade to descend.
And upon his command, the colossal divine sword tore through the sky, blazing like a meteor, straight toward Cervantez.
Cervantez's sharp instincts flared with alarm. He had no time to evade, no time to strategize. His only option was to meet the attack head-on.
[Lightning Wave!] he roared, raising his single sword high above his head, his body crackling with surging blue mana.
With a powerful slash, he unleashed a furious arc of lightning, sending it racing upward to intercept the golden blade.
*KABOOM*
The two forces collided in mid-air with an ear-splitting crack, the energy backlash causing windows in the surrounding buildings to shatter and stone to fracture under the sheer pressure.
Lightning and divine light warred against each other, sending shockwaves rippling across the plaza.
But Heaven's Strike was relentless.
Despite Cervantez's best efforts, the golden sword began to overpower the lightning arc, pushing through the crackling resistance like an unstoppable force of nature.
Cervantez's eyes widened in realization. "No—!"
The divine blade pierced through his weakened defense, its radiant edge slashing diagonally across his upper torso.
The force of the impact sent Cervantez stumbling backward, his boots skidding across the cracked stone ground. Blood sprayed into the air, glowing faintly gold where the sword had made contact.
-4500
A sharp hiss escaped through his gritted teeth as his free hand flew to clutch the deep, searing wound now etched across his chest, still faintly glowing with residual golden energy.
His breathing was ragged, his grip on his sword trembling slightly as he struggled to remain upright.
Luke lowered his arm slowly, his sharp eyes locked onto Cervantez.
The golden radiance of Heaven's Strike faded into scattered sparks, leaving behind only the faint crackle of dissipating energy.
Cervantez took a step back, his sword trembling slightly in his hand as blood dripped down his chest, staining the stones beneath him.
For now the first exchange was over and it was Luke who had come out on top, drawing the first blood.
—------
