chapters.title: Chapter 749 - 749: A hard pill to swallow
chapters.content:
Cervantez found it hard to believe that he had been hit so easily by Luke.
His knees staggered, but not because he sustained any injury on his knees, but because he felt his mental state wobble.
'Is he stronger than me?' Cervantez wondered, as a large part of his brain immediately screamed 'No', however, there was a small part, which said 'Yes'.
The part of his mind that screamed 'No' was fueled by his male ego and the pride of a warrior. While he could grudgingly accept being surpassed by 'TheBoss', a man whose sheer dominance was undeniable, he could not stomach the idea of Luke—a man he once mentored—rising above him.
When Cervantez first entered this second life, his ambition was singular: to become the best. He had set his sights on the number one position, refusing to concede it even to 'TheBoss' at first. But as time passed, he realized he simply couldn't keep up. The gap widened, and eventually, he was forced to abandon that dream.
Instead, he shifted his goal—to become the strongest Guildmaster. It wasn't his original vision, but it was a consolation prize he could live with. At least, he reasoned, he could still be seen as one of the top three players in the world.
In his past life, 'TheBoss' and PinkLotus were untouchable stars, players so far above the rest that even Cervantez had to accept their superiority. But Luke? Luke was different.
Back then, 'SkyLion' had been just another player. He wasn't a top-ten ranker, nor was he ever considered one of the strongest solo fighters. His brilliance only began to shine towards the end of the game, a flicker of greatness that arrived too late to leave an indelible mark.
Cervantez's ego, the very force that drove him to train relentlessly and claw his way to the top, could not accept this reality—that someone like Luke, someone without extraordinary talent, could surpass him through sheer determination and hard work.
It was the one outcome he had never accounted for, the one variable he had dismissed outright. With the knowledge from his past life, Cervantez believed he was destined to remain "the best of the rest."
But now, as he stared at the blood dripping from the wound across his chest, the bitter truth began to sink in.
He wasn't even "the best of the rest" anymore.
The man who once served as his Vice-Guildmaster, a man who lacked the same advantages and privileged start that Cervantez had, now stood against him as a superior opponent.
This realization didn't just shake Cervantez—it shattered his self-confidence, leaving him with a gnawing void where his pride once stood.
'A lucky shot…. It has to be a lucky shot, otherwise it can't be… I can't be weaker than SkyLion! I have the best skills…. I have the best class, I- I cannot….' Cervantez thought, as he gripped his sword hard and tried to shake-off the injury and turn the tide of this battle.
"A lucky shot!" he spat, his voice trembling with anger and denial.
"But let's see you try and block this!" He declared, as he raised his sword high above his head, the blade glowing with an ethereal starlight.
Mana surged around him, whipping up a violent wind that scattered debris and dust across the ruined courtyard, until slowly but surely, the glow of the sword intensified, the blade now radiating an almost celestial brilliance, as if the stars themselves had been forged into its edge.
[Ethereal Sword Slash]
Cervantez roared, his voice echoing like a thunderclap as he brought his sword down in a devastating arc.
A crescent-shaped slash of pure energy erupted from his blade, tearing through the air with a piercing hum.
This was his strongest attack, the sheer force of which caused the stone pavement beneath its path to crack and disintegrate, and the shockwave to shatter nearby walls into clouds of dust and rubble.
Luke's eyes narrowed as the attack raced towards him.
[Guardian Shield] He muttered, as he relied on the same legendary move he had used earlier to block Cervantez's first attack.
Immediately, a shimmering barrier of pure light unfolded from his knight's shield, forming a radiant, semi-transparent wall of mana in front of him, with the barrier shielding him from the incoming attack.
*BOOM*
The two forces collided with an explosive shockwave, sending cracks rippling across the ground and blinding light bursting outward in every direction.
The impact forced Luke to be pushed back along the cobbled surface, forcing him to dig his heels into the fractured stone to somehow hold his ground.
"ARGHHHH—" Luke screamed, as he resisted the attack with all the might in his body, with every ounce of strength that he could muster.
At first, holding it back seemed impossible, however, as the attack lost momentum, slowly but surely, Luke gained some footing as he stood his ground bravely.
When the light finally faded and the dust settled, Luke stood firm, uninjured despite Cervantez's best efforts.
His breathing remained steady, his stance unbroken, and his armor untouched.
The only sign of the clash was a faint, thin gash etched across the surface of his shield, however, the metal still seemed solid enough to withstand a few more blows and wasn't completely broken yet.
Witnessing this outcome, Cervantez froze.
His sword trembled slightly in his hand as he stared at Luke, his expression a mixture of disbelief and horror.
"No…" he whispered, his voice cracking. "No, that's impossible. That was my strongest move… My best attack… You—You're not supposed to block that!"
Luke remained silent, his shield lowered slightly as his piercing gaze met Cervantez's frantic eyes.
"There's… there's no way you could withstand that. Not without some kind of trick—some secret that he taught you!" Cervantez's voice rose, his words dripping with raw frustration. "It's TheBoss, isn't it? He must have taught you something… something unfair… something beyond reason!"
His breathing grew erratic, his shoulders rising and falling with every uneven breath. His carefully honed composure—the foundation of his strength—was now crumbling before Luke's eyes.
"No, no, no… this isn't right!" Cervantez's voice wavered as he charged forward again, his sword raised high.
But something had changed. His movements, once sharp and precise, now carried a wild recklessness. His strikes lacked the discipline and calculated precision that once made him a force to be feared.
Luke parried the first strike with ease, his sword deflecting Cervantez's erratic slash. The second strike came sloppily from the side, and Luke sidestepped it with a calm pivot.
Another slash. Another deflection.
Cervantez was leaving himself wide open, and Luke could see it. Every overextended swing, every rushed lunge—it was like watching a man drowning in his own desperation.
"Your movements are too wide, Guildmaster," Luke said coldly, parrying yet another strike and stepping into Cervantez's guard.
With a sharp twist of his blade, Luke forced Cervantez's sword arm downward, leaving his opponent vulnerable.
Cervantez stumbled back, his face twisted in frustration and disbelief as Luke stood resolute, barely even breathing hard.
"Stop… stop looking at me like that!" Cervantez yelled, his voice breaking. "You're not supposed to be this strong, Skylion! You were never supposed to surpass me!"
But Luke didn't respond. His silence spoke louder than words, his calm, unyielding presence towering over Cervantez like an immovable wall.
Cervantez lunged again, wild and desperate. But in his frenzy, he wasn't fighting Luke the ex vice guildmaster—he was fighting Luke the avenger, who was finally venting his anger.
And Cervantez was losing.

chapters.title: Chapter 750 - 750: A satisfying end
chapters.content:
"You're not supposed to be this strong!"
"You can't possibly surpass me"
"Then why? Why? Why!!!! Why can't I hit you…SkyLion?"
Cervantez questioned, as with each statement, the Arc of his sword got wider and wider until it was wide enough for Luke to slip between.
Recognising the chance before him, once Cervantez staggered off balance, Luke dropped his active sword and shield in favor of wrapping his arms around Cervantez's waist, as he prepared for the [German Suplex]
Cervantez's eyes widened in despair when he realized what Luke was planning to do, however, before he could push Luke off, or do something about his iron grip across his waist, with a violent jerk, Luke hoisted him in the air, planting him straight on his head in one fluid motion.
*BAM*
-220
Cervantez felt an intense pain shoot up in his temple, as he felt all his senses numbing all at once.
It was a scene that he had witnessed several times before, when Luke was planting his opponents, however, he had never been on the receiving end of one.
'Move… I must move! Or else I'm dead' Cervantez thought, as he knew that the first Suplex was only but a prelude of what was to come next.
"Let me go! Let me go—" Cervantez protested, flailing his arms and legs strongly to try and slip out of Luke's death grip, but failing.
Luke held onto Cervantez with all his strength and ensured that he gave him another suplex, this one even stronger than the first.
*BAM*
-270
This time, Cervantez's helmet rolled clean off his head upon impact, exposing his bare blonde head to the elements, as once again he felt the sensation of his limbs leave his body.
He tried to fight back, but his protests grew more feeble as compared to before, as Luke hoisted him once more, planting him onto the ground yet again, for the third suplex in a row.
*BAM*
-290.
[SYSTEM NOTIFICATION:- You have been stunned for 3 seconds!]
A third suplex left Cervantez stunned as a trail of blood seeped onto his forehead from his temple, which had now been injured.
'Its over…' he thought, as he felt his body being hoisted yet again for a fourth Suplex, but his limbs unable to put-up any resistance.
*BAM*
-290
[SYSTEM NOTIFICATION:- You have been stunned for 3 seconds!]
Once again he was stunned, with the Suplex chain now activating, as Luke gained full control of this battle.
*BAM*
By the fifth Suplex, his skull cracked, causing critical damage, and by the seventh his HP dropped to a critical red level, with his stun period extended to a whopping 7 seconds.
"It's over guildmaster…. With this I pay you back for the betrayal…. We are even now" Luke said, as he planted Cervantez one last time on his head to end the fight for now.
[System Notification:- Congratulations Player 'Skylion' for defeating player 'DarkEmperor' (Level 589) in a fair duel.
You have gained
+1 level!
+1 Padded Silver Boots
+1000 Gold Coins]
*Huff*
*Huff*
Luke exhaled sharply after defeating Cervantez, as he seemed to be unconsciously holding his breath up till then.
With every Suplex, he poured all of his heart and frustrations out, as he felt the weights weighing down on his shoulders lifting with every blow he delivered.
He did not have to end this fight using the [German Suplex], if he wished, he could have simply taken Cervantez's head off when the opportunity presented itself and be done with it, however, he deliberately chose the most humiliating route.
He wanted the satisfaction of delivering every blow and for his opponent to feel powerless in his grip.
Hopefully, this loss would cause him to self-reflect and improve his ways, as Luke did not wish to make a permanent enemy of Cervantez.
If he improved, Luke very much wanted to mend their ties, however, he was no longer going to hope for it.
If it happened, he would welcome it, but If it did not, then he was not afraid to have Cervantez as his enemy either.
"Luke! You did it! You beat Cervantez! That was so cool—" PinkLotus said, as she hurriedly arrived beside Luke and congratulated him on the win with stars sparkling in her eyes.
The way Luke had fought this battle was a perfect representation of what he could achieve when he truly focused, as at his core, Luke was an exceptionally talented fighter, just like Leo and Alia.
Up-till now, he was too focused on guild work and other attachments to ever fully develop as a solo warrior, which was why he never outclassed Cervantez in combat potential.
However, ever since he left the DarkSky guild and focused on self improvement with the [Mind meditation manual] his growth had been extremely impressive, to the point where he could now defeat Cervantez without a scratch.
"Not bad…. SkyLion, I don't think anyone will debate you being the number 3 player in the game anymore…" A voice came from the distance, as when Luke glanced over, he saw Leo and Dumpy perched upon the top of a broken house.
"Le–, Boss! Since when are you here?" Luke asked, as Leo leapt off the wall and landed before him with Dumpy following closely behind.
"Oh please, the West Duke? He could have lasted longer against me if I were alone, but against both me and Dumpy? HA! hahahahahaha—" Leo laughed maniacally as he pulled Dumpy in for a hug.
"I merely assisted. It was all Lord Father's doing–" Dumpy said, as Leo rubbed his face affectionately against Dumpy's slimy skin, their bond having grown much closer now that Dumpy had matured sufficiently.
"In any case… that was a good fight, you should be proud. At this rate you will become a master warrior very soon!" Leo said, as Luke smiled heartily.
He too was waiting eagerly to become a master warrior, so that he could finally tell PinkLotus how he truly felt about her afterwards.

chapters.title: Chapter 751 - 751: An Easy Win
chapters.content:
(A few minutes ago, Leo)
If a single word could be used to describe West Duke James's fight against Leo, it would be 'Pitiful'.
The West Duke was supposed to be the strongest of the four Arch-Dukes of Unity Empire, who was also hailed as the country's best swordsman.
By all means, if it was a fair fight between Leo and the West Duke alone, Leo was bound to have a hard time taking him down, however, with Dumpy added in the dynamic everything changed.
The little frog had improved leaps and bounds after his first 'real' combat adventure alongside his Lord Father and Grandfather, and with him taking the initiative to confront and tie down the West Duke in a sword battle, Leo was granted the full freedom to move and attack the Duke on his own.
Straight from the get-go, as Dumpy charged ahead of Leo and crossed swords with the West Duke, it became clear to Leo, that both Dumpy and the Duke were more or less evenly matched.
Whether it was speed, strength, or technique, Dumpy lost out in no department to his vastly more experienced opponent, causing the West Duke to immediately widen his eyes in panic.
"What sort of a monstrosity are you? I've never heard of a beast being so strong?" The West Duke wondered, as according to the game's core engine, a beast like the Ancient Swamp Frog wasn't supposed to exist in this world.
It was only because Leo was able to hatch him out of a rare egg that a beast like Dumpy was born in this world, however, the impact of his birth was far-reaching.
For the NPC's of this world, they could never really take Dumpy as seriously as they were ought to, until they met him in person, however, by then it was usually too late.
Under Dumpy's relentless pressure, the West Duke eventually lost sight of Leo completely who used [Vanish] to completely hide his presence and be-gone with the wind.
And then the hunt began…..
Every passing second, the Duke could feel a creeping sensation on his neck, but he could never really be sure as to when or where Leo would attack from.
Forced to spread his senses thin, he got hit by Dumpy more than once in their battle, as he picked up small cuts and nicks on his otherwise ornate armor.
In the end, he never sensed Leo's [Kill Strike] coming, as Leo stabbed him from the back, ending his life as a great warrior in a rather pitiful fashion, in what could be described only as a dastardly death.
"You coward…. You didn't even face me fair and square–" James complained before collapsing on the floor as he spat a mouthful of blood.
"Duke, are you retarded or something? Why should I fight you fair and square? What are you to me? My childhood buddy I shared an underwear with? I'm the fucking rebel leader…. What did you expect?" Leo asked, as he plunged two daggers straight into the Duke's eyes for added effect, expediting his neural shutdown.
[System Notification :- Congratulations player 'TheBoss' for having defeated the master warrior 'Duke James' in battle.
You have gained
+2 levels….. ERROR! ERROR! ERROR! ]
[Global Announcement :- Error Error Error…. Global Announcement Cancelled]
[System Notification :- Congratulations player 'TheBoss' for reaching the level-cap imposed within the game. You are now at the highest level permissible.
You have gained
+1 Skill Slot! ]
[System Notification:- More rewards for your unprecedented achievement are now being calculated…. Please wait for a while before we distribute them]
A series of odd system notifications flashed before Leo, who looked at them with amusement.
He had no idea that level 1000 was the highest permissible level within the game, as he thought that life would continue as usual even after he crossed the level 1000 mark.
Having gained yet another skill slot was definitely a welcome change, as this meant that he now had 2 more empty skill slots that he had not yet used, giving him ample room to grow in the future without needing to change any of his core moves that he already knew.
However, the global notification being cancelled and the additional rewards being yet to be calculated felt weird to Leo, as it was a situation that had never happened to him before.
"I don't understand why there's a hold-up? It's not like I jumped from level 900 to 1000 in a single day, I was at 999 for a while now.
How hard was it for them to believe I was going to hit level 1000?" Leo wondered, as he shook his head in disappointment.
"I guess that means Captain Kid is going to visit me real soon" Leo mused, as he signalled for Dumpy to follow him and jumped atop the nearest tall house, hoping to gain a better view of the city.
*Thud*
Landing with a soft thud, Leo looked around, only to find Luke engaged in a high stakes duel against Cervantez nearby, which Leo enjoyed with the best seats in the house.
"Yes! Drop him on his fucking head brother!" He cheered from the stands, as Dumpy looked at the crude and unrefined way Luke fought with disdain.
"He could have finished the fight in one blow, Lord Father, this method of dropping the opponent on their head is simply inefficient" Dumpy complained, as Leo only smiled but did not respond.
He did not wish to encourage Dumpy to fight inefficiently and hence he did not contradict the frogs words, However, he did draw immense satisfaction from seeing his brother prevail over his longtime superior, as today, Luke finally felt like a proper fighter again.
"Well fought….It was a fine battle" Leo said in the end, as he walked up to Luke to congratulate him on his win, which Luke accepted with grace.
Both the Skyshard brothers had made big leaps forward today, however, Leo was yet to know just how significant his leap was.

chapters.title: Chapter 752 - 752: Misjudged
chapters.content:
(Present moment, Bernabeu City)
"So what's the plan now?" PinkLotus inquired, now that both the Duke and Cervantez had been neutralized.
"To be honest…. I don't really care about winning Bernabeu City. We can help the WhiteSabers out if we want, I reckon it would be a good leveling exercise for you two, but other than that, I have no other objectives left to fulfill–" Leo said, as he simply shrugged his shoulders and expressed his indifference to this war.
Glancing towards Luke, PinkLotus waited for his decision, as Luke once again gripped his sword and shield and seemed prepared for action.
"Yeah, I could use some levels" he said, as he signalled his desire to continue fighting, for which PinkLotus joined him happily.
The four proceeded to part ways then, with Luke and PinkLotus going their way and Leo and Dumpy their own, however, all four of them left a trail of dead bodies in their wake.
**********
(Meanwhile on the global forums)
The news of Cervantez's death spread like wildfire through the forums, as he suddenly lost 3 levels at once.
"Even Cervantez has fallen to 'TheBoss', can anyone stand against that man?"
"I don't think Cervantez fell to 'TheBoss', I saw a video of him fighting SkyLion, the ex- vice guild master of DarkSky. Here let me attach a link to that cam video (here)"
"Whoa! It's crazy to see that the ex vice guild master of the DarkSky guild is so much stronger than their actual guildmaster…. No wonder he left, he was more fit to lead the guild than his senior"
"With 'TheBoss', PinkLotus and SkyLion working together, does anyone else stand a chance? The three of them together are literally the 1,2,3 of the world"
"The Boss entering the war single-handedly changed the tides of the war for Bernabeu. This is no longer a fair game.
For a moment, I believed that the West could become a sanctuary for the righteous faction players…. That we could all perhaps rally behind the DarkSky guild and hope for protection against the uprising, however, TheBoss just showed how it was nothing more than a stupid dream.
As long as he's alive, nobody can stop 'TheBoss',".
"The West is going to fall…. The center is going to fall, the north is in a civil war and the south and east are already captured. The righteous faction is doomed, we picked the wrong side".
"Can we still rectify our mistake? Can we still jump ship and join the rebels? I don't want to fight for this losing faction anymore …"
There was sheer panic on the global forums related to the war in the west, as although Leo never intended to strike fear into the heart of his enemies, he accidentally did something he could never ever have anticipated himself.
************
(Meanwhile ChaosBringer)
"BRILLIANT…. LORD BOSS IS SIMPLY BRILLIANT" ChaosBringer cheered, as he threw up all the battle plans he had drawn into the air, as if they did not matter anymore.
"How can someone be so intelligent? How can someone be so ingenious? I'm nothing compared to My Lord…. Not even a speck of dust worth mentioning" ChaosBringer said, as he held his face between his palms and blushed like a newlywed wife on the first wedding night.
"Leader…. Leader, have you seen the comments on the global forums? Thousands of righteous faction players now wish to defect to the uprising. There are open inquiries for recruitment… what are your orders?" An underling asked, as ChaosBringer happily skipped his steps towards the underling and held both his hands in joy.
"Do you even understand what's going on here? Can you filthy mortal even comprehend the godliness of God Boss?" ChaosBringer asked, as the underling simply tilted his head in confusion.
"Dance with me…" ChaosBringer commanded as he began to jump and turn while holding hands with the underling, while laughing like a maniac.
There was an expression of pure bliss on his face as he danced around with the underling, as he looked to be fast approaching orgasm.
"I was stupid…. I questioned Lord Boss and his decision to go to the west as an unnecessary risk…. I thought the Lord was being stubborn in his desire to punish the Western Weaklings, but I could never understand his true motives" ChaosBringer began, as the underling tilted his head in confusion.
"If it were up to me, I'd have requested Lord Boss to join me in the central campaign, to help me capture StrongHaven, however, he's much smarter than me.
He went to the west, because he knew that it was the last backbone of the righteous faction players and he deliberately dismantled it.
Currently, I can just open the gates of recruitment for defectors into 'TheUprising', promising them bogus rewards if they rebel and open the gates of their town/ city for us, and sweep the battlefield without a major fight.
He's broken their backbone and has stolen any hope of victory, he's a genius beyond our wildest imaginations" ChaosBringer said, as he suddenly felt weak to his knees and buckled onto the floor, much to the worry of the underling.
"Such a mastermind…. And yet he behaves so humbly around me…. Never teaches me how to fight a war, when he can probably do the same job a hundred times better.
I'm sure this world looks like a chess board to him, but I'm definitely a piece he treasures dearly.
Oh my Lord Boss…. Your magnificence is truly blinding" ChaosBringer said, as he rolled around on the floor while giggling, looking like a completely mentally deranged person.
"So… what are your orders?" The underling asked, as ChaosBringer got back to his feet and straightened his robe.
"The Lord has done so much for us already, it would be a shame to not deliver StrongHaven for him by the time he returns…."
"Listen carefully soldier, this is the plan…." ChaosBringer began, as his eyes turned sharp and focused once again.

chapters.title: Chapter 753 - 753: The last chance
chapters.content:
(Global Forums – ChaosBringer's Announcement)
A notification reverberated across the global forums—a single post pinned to the top, marked by an ominous crimson insignia and the username [ChaosBringer]. By now, his name was infamous, synonymous with rebellion and chaos, a household name etched into the minds of every player.
The moment ChaosBringer's post went live, thousands of players clicked on it in an instant. Like wildfire, it spread across the forums, drawing in curious eyes and anxious hearts as its contents began to ripple through the player base.
It was a recorded message, with his sitting behind an oak table, as he delivered a speech with utmost sincerity.
"Brothers and sisters of Terra Nova Online, the time for delusion has ended.
The Righteous Faction is finished. The Emperor lies dead, his throne turned to ash, and his once-proud NPC armies scattered like leaves in the wind.
The West is sure to fall, the Center is burning, and the North is locked in an endless civil war. What remains of your so-called 'hope' is but the flicker of a dying candle in a storm.
When the Emperor fell, many righteous players faced consequences beyond imagination— debuffs beyond one's wildest dreams, but that... was merely the beginning.
Currently you stand at the precipice of annihilation. The Uprising is not an army. It is an inevitability. We are a tidal wave that will wash over every fortress, every city, and every bastion you cling to. And when we arrive, those who resisted us will face consequences far graver than those who fell with the Emperor.
But I am not without mercy. Lord Boss is not without mercy.
And hence, today, I extend a hand. A final offer. Open your gates to us. Raise the Crimson Banner of the Uprising over your cities and towns. Rally your people to rebellion, as those who do, will be welcomed into our ranks—not as prisoners, not as traitors—but as heroes.
All past crimes, debts, and sins will be pardoned. You will find a new purpose, a new home, and a place of honor in our grand vision. But make no mistake—if you refuse this final chance, if you cling to your crumbling walls and dying ideals...
You will not just lose your cities. You will lose everything.
The choice is yours. But know this: The Uprising does not wait. The Crimson Tide is rising. Choose wisely."
[End of Recorded Message]
***********
(Global Forums Reaction – Chaos Unleashed)
The forums erupted in chaos after ChaosBringer's post as thousands of threads sprang up in seconds, each more frantic and volatile than the last.
"This is a trap! He's a rebel, a liar, and a manipulator. If you fall for this, you're sealing your fate."
"You think he's lying? Look around! Every major city is losing ground. The fight for Bernabeu is going badly. The Emperor is dead. The Uprising is unstoppable."
"Guys, think logically. The Uprising doesn't need to lie—they're winning. ChaosBringer has no reason to bluff. This offer is real."
"I can't risk my guild's survival anymore. My city's defenses are barely holding up. I'm raising the Crimson Banner tonight."
"Cowards! Traitors! The righteous faction will prevail!"
"Prevail? Against TheBoss? Against PinkLotus? Against SkyLion? You're delusional. I'm not dying for a lost cause."
"I've been loyal to the righteous faction since Day 1... but this... this is bigger than loyalty. I need to survive. I can't risk dropping to sector E after the next evaluation"
After ChaosBringer's offer, many righteous faction players decisively decided to jump ship, as screenshots of secret rebellion began circulating, with many smaller righteous faction guilds deciding to defect.
In smaller towns and cities, banners of the righteous faction were torn down, replaced with the blood-red insignia of the Uprising, as the Uprising was given a free pass and a hero's welcome on their march to StrongHaven City.
In SilverHaven, an influential guild leader was seen leading their men to sabotage the city's gates.
In DawnFort, players disguised as guards assassinated key defensive commanders.
In BrightSpire, a healer's guild, once known for their pacifism, declared their allegiance to the Uprising, as one after another, thousands upon thousands defected from a sinking ship forever, further triggering a downward spiral.
"It's happening everywhere. Cities are falling from within. The righteous faction isn't even losing battles—they're collapsing."
"I switched sides tonight. I don't regret it. The Uprising was right all along."
"If you haven't switched yet, do it now. The cities are falling faster than anyone expected."
"I'll fight until the end. I'd rather die than kneel to ChaosBringer and his horde of lunatics."
"You say that now, but when the Crimson Banner flies over your city, we'll see if your resolve holds."
*********
(Meanwhile ChaosBringer)
ChaosBringer stood at the center of a grand war table, his hands gripping the edge tightly as reports flooded in.
"Leader, rebellion activity detected in 12 tier3 towns already. Gates are opening, commanders are falling, and righteous banners are being burned."
ChaosBringer grinned, his eyes glowing with manic satisfaction.
"This is the sound of an empire crumbling. This is the dawn of a new age. Lord Boss set the fire… and now the world is burning."
He leaned back, clasping his hands behind his back as he looked out over a map littered with flickering crimson lights.
"Initially I worried if I would be able to win StrongHaven for Lord Boss before the debuff period ended, but now, victory is all but assured…."
"Let them burn it all down. Let the righteous dogs tear each other apart from within, as when the smoke clears, the Uprising will stand victorious." ChaosBringer said, as he let out a satisfied smile.
Finally! It seemed like the mission that he got at the start of the game to topple the existing regime would finally be completed.
—-------

chapters.title: Chapter 754 - 754: A shocking message
chapters.content:
(On a remote and shadowed planet, hidden somewhere in the vast expanse of the universe)
On a planet cloaked in eternal darkness and biting cold, renowned across the galaxy as the ultimate refuge for fugitives and outlaws, resided Mu Fan—the infamous branch head of the Mu family.
She was currently residing on the dark planet because of fears of the universal government officials arresting her and hunting her down, however, she expected the situation to improve in the coming months, as the main family negotiated terms of her pardon.
The main family knew that she was too important an asset to be allowed to rot on a desolate planet, and hence they were sure to buy her pardon, as soon as anger surrounding her last assassination mission started to fade.
"Branch Leader! Branch Leader! You must see this…"
The voice of a small boy broke her meditation, as Mu Fan instantly became alert.
*Thud*
The peace and calm of her insulated wooden cabin was broken by the violent opening of the cabin door, as a gust of bone chilling wind flew in, instantly dropping the temperature within the cabin by a few degrees.
*Thud*
Shivering, the underling closed the door behind him and stumbled toward Mu Fan, clutching a piece of paper in his trembling hands.
Icicles seemed to have formed on the young boy's face, his breath freezing mid-air and leaving frosty traces on his skin as it escaped his nose.
His skin was blue and he seemed to be on the verge of going into a shock, if Mu Fan did not help him.
"Here… have this" Mu Fan said, accepting the piece of paper from his hands as she handed him a small vial of red fluid.
"Drink…. It's not wise to travel on foot during winter, no matter how many layers of clothes you wear. Drink or you won't survive this night" Mu Fan instructed, as under her vigilant watch, the poor underling clumsily opened the vial, consuming the contents within in one short gulp.
"Agh–" The young boy moaned instantly, as he could feel the liquid running down his throat and setting every cell within his body on fire, as suddenly all the cold that he felt seemed to thaw, with rejuvenating heat returning to his body.
"Th–Thank you, Branch Leader," the young boy stammered, his voice barely above a whisper, as Mu Fan nodded curtly before gesturing toward the far corner of her cabin.
"Sit there and try not to breathe too loud," she instructed, her tone cold and sharp as she unfolded the letter in her hand with practiced precision.
"Aye," the boy replied, retreating to the corner, where he sat quietly, clutching his knees and trying to make himself as small as possible, while the Branch Leader focused on the message.
'I wonder what the urgent message is?' he thought, his wide eyes sneaking glances toward her face, hoping to catch a glimpse of her reaction.
Mu Fan, despite being over forty-five, looked no older than twenty. Her youthful appearance, a result of her status as a grandmaster warrior, had remained untouched by time.
If not for her cold, unapproachable nature and lethal reputation, countless admirers would have dared to pursue her. But her demeanor, like an unyielding glacier, left no room for warmth or affection.
'As always, the Branch Leader's expression doesn't change at all...' the boy noted with a twinge of disappointment, as no matter how grave or urgent the situation was, her icy calm never seemed to waver, with today seeming no different.
But then, something shifted.
Her eyebrow twitched, her forehead creased ever so slightly, and her usually impassive face showed the faintest flicker of tension.
'It changed? Something in that letter actually made the Branch Leader react?'
The boy's breath hitched as he stared at her, eyes wide with disbelief. Whatever was written in that letter had managed to crack the Branch Leader's legendary composure, and this shocked even the underling to his core.
'Whatever is written within that letter has to be groundbreaking if it causes even the branch leader to break her usual calm. Thank the gods that I came here running as fast as I did' The underling thought, as he felt proud of himself for braving to travel during the winter, just to bring the Branch Leader this message.
**********
(Meanwhile Mu Fan)
A few months ago, the Mu family main branch had assigned her the duty of scouting and pleasing a promising talent who went by the name of 'Leo Skyshard'.
He was a prodigy on-top of one of the universal governments rehabilitation arc-ships, that had managed to reach the realm of a 'Master' warrior, while just playing the induction game.
While reaching the 'Master' status itself was not impressive enough to enter the eyes of the Mu Clan, the fact that he did it in record time and that he single handedly broke the balance of the induction game, caught the Mu family's attention, who assigned his recruitment to Mu Fan.
As per universal government rules, although Mu Fan could not directly recruit him before he landed on his destination planet, she sent him a Grandmaster meditation manual, to hopefully enter his good graces and receive priority for his recruitment when he landed.
She was supposed to monitor his progress through the months and was supposed to stay in touch with the ship's captain bringing that talent about his development, however, with the past months being as hectic as they were, she completely lost touch of the project, until today.
The message she received today was sent by the ship's captain to the Mu Clan 14 days ago, however, with her being forced into hiding, it took 14 days for the message to finally reach her hands after travelling a fairly dangerous path.
Usually, such updates on a potential recruitment candidate would not constitute an emergency, however, the contents of this letter oddly did.
The candidate had allegedly tapped into the genetic skill [Parallel Processing], opening the potential for him to be the inheritor of the Timeless Assassin's bloodline.
A possibility that broke even Mu Fan's calm facade.

chapters.title: Chapter 755 - 755: The Timeless Assasin
chapters.content:
The story of the timeless assassin was a taboo in the modern universe where gods were assumed to be immortals.
In the last 2000 years, since the 'Great Betrayal' occured, not a single God had died, and the universe seemed to have forgotten the reign of terror that the Timeless Assassin left behind, where even gods were punished and killed without mercy for their crimes.
However, with the timeless assassin dead and his methods to kill gods extinct, there was no longer any check or balance to the tyranny of gods, most of whom had grown quite unruly over the last 2000 years.
In the universe, while many types of races and classifications technically existed, there was only one classification that mattered most, which was the distinction between a three dimensional being called a 'mortal', and a four dimensional being called a 'god'.
A mortal, which was the name assigned to all warriors up-till the rank of a transcendent, was a being that existed within the constraints of space and time, a.k.a the three dimensions of reality.
They could be hurt using three dimensional weapons and could die quite easily if their physical body perished.
While on the other hand, a god was a warrior that had fully grasped the law of time, integrating themselves fully to the origin stream, making themselves impervious to mortal weapons.
For a god, reversing their body's state to a moment before sustaining an injury was as effortless as breathing. This ability meant that, even if wounded in battle, they could simply restore themselves to an uninjured state with ease, rendering the task of killing them nearly impossible.
They lived beyond the constraints of time and were hence not limited to existing in a single location, or a single physical body.
As long as their consciousness remained intact, a god lived on, which was why very few methods remained to kill such a being, with the Timeless Assassin having invented every last one of them.
As the reaper of gods, the Timeless Assassin was feared throughout the universe and hailed by all mortals as the upholder of justice and peace, however, after falling at the Great Betrayal 2000 years ago, his legacy was deliberately pushed into shambles.
Erased from history books and the minds of all mortals who lived at the time, the legacy of the Timeless Assassin was slowly wiped extinct in the millennia to come, with his name completely wiped off from the collective consciousness in the modern age.
Only historic families with untouchable records now remembered the name of the God Reaper, with most of these families hailing from godly bloodlines who did not wish to see his resurgence.
A few months after his death, the god of wisdom, who was one of the architects responsible for killing the timeless assassin, suddenly prophesied his return through one of his descendants in the future, which caused a frenzy amongst all gods to hunt down all those who bore the timeless assassin's blood.
Unfortunately for the gods however, the Timeless Assassin proved to be a prolific womanizer, with his blood running strong in many noble families, making it impossible for his genes to go completely extinct.
However, with the gods having knowledge of the exact traits to look out for when searching for potential candidates bearing the Timeless Assassin's blood, every single one of the Timeless Assassin's descendents were mercilessly killed when any of them even showed slight promise.
The trait [Parallel Processing] was one such genetic ability, which was known to be passed down only amongst descendents of the Timeless Assassin, which was why when Mu Fan read the report in her hand, felt as shocked as she did.
The captain that had sent out the message was sure to be a low levelled individual who did not understand the true significance of such a bloodline trait emerging in one of his passengers, as according to protocol, he was supposed to execute the possessor of such a skill on the spot.
*********
(Mu Fan's POV)
Mu Fan tapped the heels of her feet rapidly when she read the letter, as her brain began thinking about the potential consequence of letting such a man live at full speed.
Designated as the point of contact to recruit Leo Skyshard into the Mu Clan, Mu Fan knew that she was the only individual who currently knew about the kids true genetic heritage, which was why she found herself in the unique position to do something unorthodox.
'Earth?' she wondered, as the image of a backwater planet on the fringes of the universe, cut off from the bustling veins of the Rainbow Stream popped into her head.
'How could the blood of the Timeless Assassin, one of the most powerful and feared beings in history, survive and emerge in such an isolated, insignificant corner of existence?' she thought, her teeth grinding softly.
Earth was a mana-less planet, a place where no self-respecting god or transcendent warrior would bother setting even a single foot on.
And yet, here it was—a report confirming that a child, a passenger from Earth, bore the [Parallel Processing] trait.
Mu Fan couldn't suppress the chill that ran down her spine. This wasn't just some anomaly; it was fate laughing in the face of divine authority.
"Did the Assassin plan this? Did he foresee his blood spreading to the most remote corners of the universe, far beyond the prying eyes of the gods?" She mused, her fingers crumpling the edges of the message paper.
For thousands of years, the gods had hunted down every descendant, every flicker of the Assassin's legacy. And yet, in the forgotten ruins of Earth, a spark seemed to have survived.
A spark, which if used correctly, could help Mu Fan achieve her long-standing dream of revenge.
—-----

chapters.title: Chapter 756 - 756: Mu Fan's Decision
chapters.content:
Mu Fan carefully considered her next move regarding Leo Skyshard.
She knew that the consequences of being caught aiding him were dire—perhaps even a fate worse than death.
However, despite knowing the risks, she still had a desire to help him, on the off-chance that he could someday become the inheritor of the Timeless Assassin's legacy.
"The report from the ship's captain suggests that Leo Skyshard has not yet fully unlocked the ability [Parallel Processing] and it's only because of advancements in his meditation manual that he's slowly coming close to having active control over it.
Currently, the system only suspects that he may have an ability similar to parallel processing, however, without it being fully awakened, the system has not flagged it as a proper threat yet.
This can be considered a stroke of great luck, as if the system registered it as an awakened ability, someone higher up in the universal government would take notice right away and have him killed.
However, with him only being suspected to have the potential to awaken an ability that's bears similarity to parallel processing, no alarms have been raised yet.
Add to it a dumb captain who doesn't know what that ability really means, and I can perhaps salvage this situation" Mu Fan muttered, as she retrieved a fresh set of pen and paper and began to furiously write a message.
[Esteemed Captain Kid,
Thankyou for having reached out to me about the signs that Leo Skyshard may awaken an inherent genetic passive skill.
We at the Mu Clan understand how you reaching out to us about the same is out of the ordinary, and appreciate it greatly.
Hence we will compensate you handsomely for the same when you land on planet Terra Nova, ending your fruitful journey.
However, it concerns us deeply that our chosen target is awakening genetic abilities without being properly tested for his potential.
As you're aware, genetic abilities usually unlock as a batch, usually only after one has been administered with an awakening serum, and the fact that our top recruitment target is undergoing it without proper care, makes us fear for his future.
We hope that you can guide him to stop his current meditation training for a while, or sabotage it by lowering the mana concentration of his quarters, so that he doesn't accidentally fully awaken it before landing.
After all this is for his own good.
Of Course such actions would warrant additional rewards for your deepest understanding and the Mu Clan is anything but stingy.
Help us Captain and we will make sure you become the richest officer on your ship by a long shot.
Also, if possible, please delete all records indicating the possibility that Leo Skyshard may have a genetic ability as it will only make it more difficult for us to recruit him upon landing.
You're Truly,
Mu Fan]
Mu Fan swiftly scribbled down the message, rolled the paper tightly, and pressed a rubber seal on top to ensure it couldn't be tampered with.
Handing the sealed scroll to her underling along with another bottle of the warming red liquid, she fixed him with a sharp gaze. "Deliver this immediately—and waste no time."
"Aye" the underling said, racing out of her cabin and into the cold with a sense of purpose, as he knew that whatever it was that he carried in his hands today, was something extremely important.
**********
(Meanwhile Leo)
Unaware about how his fate was evolving, Leo continued playing Terra Nova Online in blissful ignorance.
The sun was about to set and the gaming day was almost over with the WhiteSabers having gained control of nearly 60% of the city.
At this pace. The WhiteSabers could fully control Bernabeu by tomorrow, completing a significant counter-attack in the fight to capture the West.
"Guildmaster, The West Duke's son, the NPC heir apparent has been spotted fleeing the city. The ducal NPC's have lost morale" A WhiteSaber messenger informed their guildmaster, as Leo overheard the message from the shadows.
He did not expect the West Duke's son, who was one of Luke's NPC friends, to flee this war, it did not seem in-line with his character.
'It could be a trap….' Leo thought, but shrugged his shoulders as he did not care enough to warn the sabers.
"Is that so? Did he really flee?" The WhiteSaber guild master leaned forward, his voice brimming with barely-contained excitement. The weight of victory seemed to already hang around his shoulders like a royal mantle.
"Yes, Guildmaster!" the messenger said with fervor. "Our scouts saw him retreating with a small group of retainers. The city is practically ours!"
A loud cheer erupted from the gathered guild members. Swords clanged against shields, staffs were raised high, and chants of "For the WhiteSabers!" filled the air.
The guildmaster, placing his arms around the two soldiers fighting closest to him grinned from ear to ear as he said "This, my loyal comrades, is the result of our unwavering strategy and unparalleled strength! We are no mere players—we are kings in this game, conquerors of cities!"
His words were met with an uproarious response, the echo chamber of cheers and affirmations growing louder with each passing moment. Around him, lieutenants nodded sagely, as if every word the guildmaster spoke were divine wisdom.
"Truly brilliant leadership, Guildmaster!" one officer exclaimed.
"No one else could have orchestrated such a flawless victory!" said another sycophant.
"The West Duke's forces crumbled like paper under your might!" a third voice joined in.
"I always supported your decision to enter this decisive fight, it was the right call" A fourth added, as everyone nodded in agreement.
Leo, still in the shadows, rolled his eyes at the scene. The over-the-top celebration, the blind arrogance, and the blatant self-congratulation—it was almost too much to stomach.
'Idiots,' he thought, slipping away silently from his vantage point.
'None of them even considered why the heir apparent would flee without resistance. Not a single one questioned the timing or the circumstances. If it is a trap, they'll fall face-first into it without even realizing it.' Leo thought, as he slapped his face at their apparent dumbness.

chapters.title: Chapter 757 - 757: Captain Kid's Visit
chapters.content:
As Leo had anticipated, mere minutes after reports confirmed that the West Duke's son had fled the city, powerful explosions erupted across all major government buildings and the Duke's palace, setting them ablaze in a synchronized inferno.
The young duke, meticulous in his retreat, ensured there would be no spoils left for his enemies to claim, even in victory.
By doing so, he significantly minimized the strategic and economic value of the city, effectively diminishing the WhiteSabers' gains from their conquest.
With the destruction of sewage lines, the ducal palace, and every key administrative building, the young duke guaranteed that even if the WhiteSabers captured the city, governing it in the aftermath would be an arduous and chaotic endeavor.
If the WhiteSabers were more alert, they could have avoided this fate by firmly taking control of infrastructure critical to city governance, however, it was a mistake they were going to learn from in the future.
"Log-out" Leo murmured, once he saw everything he needed to see playout, as with mere minutes left in the day's gameplay and the city already in chaos, he no longer felt the need to stay online.
*********
(Real World, The Arc Ship)
Leo fully expected to see Captain Kid the moment he logged out of Terra Nova Online, and, as anticipated, the moment he logged out, he heard the doorbell on his manor go off.
"Haha… right on time" Leo muttered, as he made his way to the door, where Captain Kid seemed to be waiting for him with a nervous smile plastered across his face.
"Master Skyshard…." He began, bowing slightly, as he honored Leo's status as a VIP guest.
"Captain" Leo said, nodding back, as although he did not bow, he acknowledged the captain's presence.
"I have some urgent matters to speak of– may I come in?" Kid asked, as Leo pointed the way to his well furnished living room, offering Kid a seat.
Kid chose the widest living room couch at the center to get seated, with Leo choosing the seat opposite from him for the conversation.
"The reason I'm here today is because you have hit the level cap….." Kid began, his expression serious.
"There's still close to 14 months of gameplay time left till we reach planet Terra Nova and we have already imposed on you the maximum possible gameplay restrictions that a player can receive" Kid said, as he let out a long sigh.
"As per protocol, we are supposed to limit a player's game-time once they hit the level threshold, but with you we cannot even do that anymore.
Which is why I came here today looking for possible solutions to this unexpected situation" Kid said, sounding half defeated, as he did not like having to negotiate such unfair terms and conditions, everytime something did not go the way the big corporations back home wanted them to go.
"I am open to lucrative offers, Captain…. Like you said, you're here to negotiate, so let's start with your top offer, what's the most you're willing to offer?" Leo inquired, as Kid let out a deep sigh once more, shaking his head in resignation.
"Not much…. 500,000 MP and some housing perks upon landing on planet Terra Nova. It's not a bad offer, especially from a monetary perspective, but it's not great either" Kid admitted, as Leo raised his eyebrow in confusion.
"What's going on captain? I don't seem to understand the full picture here" Leo said, as Captain Kid began to rub his hands earnestly, as he sheepishly began to tell Leo some secrets he wasn't supposed to talk about.
"There are three main parties that I'm answerable to at the moment, that have a say in how this situation ends up playing out.
Firstly there's the universal government, the organisation I'm employed at, who is the owner of this carrier ship and who also has the biggest say in your situation.
As per universal government rules, there is a formula in place for how much gaming time of a passenger they can reduce externally without it being considered as mental torture or the government robbing one of opportunity to flourish, and you have already hit that point.
This means that legally, no-one can force you to reduce your gaming time against your will anymore, however, there are other parties involved…." Kid began, as finally he revealed some juicy bits that Leo was not already aware about.
"The second party involved is our employer, the Unity Empire— who as you already know is the primary governing authority on Planet Terra Nova.
They have contracted us, the Universal Government, to transport you Earthlings from your home planet to Terra Nova, to address their critical workforce shortages and they are not happy with how you as a single player are disrupting their project.
The Unity Empire does not want earthlings to look up to a single player such as yourself as their role model and does not want the rebellion succeeding as a whole to topple the Unity Empire within the game.
The optics of such a situation does not bode well for them when they're trying to appear as all powerful overlords and hence they want you removed from the game world at any cost necessary.
For them, the quality of the entire batch of migrants is far more important than the individual success of a single player.
And with you continuing to massively disrupt the game world alone, they're not happy as things stand" Kid explained, as Leo carefully raised an eyebrow to his words.
"Finally, there's the third parties who are interested in your development and your development alone and have no vested interest in the batch of humans as a whole.
These are organizations like the one that has gifted you your meditation manual, who want nothing more than to see you flourish and develop to the limits.
These are the people who feel frustrated at the repeated attempts of the Unity Empire to suppress your growth, and for now they are your biggest allies" Kid said, as he laid out the whole situation for Leo to understand.

chapters.title: Chapter 758 - 758: Negotiations
chapters.content:
Leo listened intently to what Kid had to say and only after he was done explaining the general situation, did Leo draw some inferences of his own.
As per his understanding, the process of transferring and rehabilitating migrants from one planet to another fell under the purview of the universal government and although they could be rotten to their core, at least on the surface they had a moral code of conduct to follow, which prevented them from singling out or abusing a passenger without any plausible reason.
This situation however, greatly pissed off their employers, the Unity Empire, who did not appreciate the fact that Leo was single handedly spoiling this batch of migrants by having a greater effect on their mindsets and gameplay development than what could be allowed.
Finally, there were the outsiders, the ones who stood nothing to gain from this batch of migrants as a whole, but had eyes for its top talents, with Leo being their topmost priority.
These entities, who were potentially as strong as the Unity Empire if not even stronger, wanted Leo alone and wanted him to flourish even at the cost of others.
These entities were pissed that Leo was being stifled at every opportunity that presented itself by the Unity Empire, and wanted to ensure that they could not get their ways this time either.
"Hmm…" Leo muttered, soaking everything in, as Captain Kid nervously continued.
"I'm the sole decision maker on this ship, and usually it's supposed to be a simple job, but this time it's my very neck on the line.
I can't offend any of the three parties who hold a say in this situation, because if I do, I'm sure to be punished, and hence, I come here with a humble request of you negotiating a deal with me that keeps everyone happy" Kid said, as sweat beads began to visibly form on his head.
"I can alter the game settings slightly, because I'm afforded some creative control over the game as this ship's captain, and hence I can make it so that your clash against the Demon King comes as soon as you want it to, and under any circumstance that you want it to.
I know that your only remaining goal in this game is to defeat the Demon King and the Black Dragon Drogo, and I can deliver them to you on a silver plate.
But in return, I would request that you recuse yourself from the last rankers event that is scheduled to happen in a couple months and would also further reduce your remaining 108 days gaming time to just under 30 days….." Kid proposed, as he visibly began sweating buckets at this point.
"That's not enough Captain…. 108 days is enough for me to kill the black dragon and demon king on my own terms…. And I don't need your help for it.
500,000 MP is an astronomical sum of money, yes, but like you said, it's also not enough for me to back away.
We are still about 450 days away from landing, and I have less than 1 in 4 gaming days remaining to play Terra Nova Online as is.
It gets boring around here, Captain, the monotony is hard to break.
500,000 MP, the VIP sector, none of it is enough to kill boredom and hence I'm not going to take your offer.
The Unity Empire can suck my balls, or come after me when we land, but I'm not trading my future growth potential away for mere money…. Besides, I'm on the cusp of being an Emperor, so how will I enjoy all that hard work I've put in for all these years if you take the little gaming time I've left away?" Leo asked, as he simply rejected the captain's current offer.
"What if we give you something else?
What if we give you a guarantee to resurrect Ben Faulkner, so that you don't have to pool all that money for his resurgence yourself.
That way, not only can you rest assured that your master will be with you when you land, with his memories intact, but also get to keep all your hard-earned money that you've made so far, so that you don't land on Terra Nova as a poor man.
To sweeten the deal, I can even add an information pack for you, something to forewarn you about the politics and dynamics of the new world you're about to enter…. Just so you have a heads up" Kid asked, as he finally gave Leo an offer that was too good to pass up on, even for Leo.
"Give me all that, plus the 500,000 MP, and I'll agree to knocking my gaming days to half of what's left, at 59–" Leo said, still holding his ground, as although he found the current offer good enough already, he still pushed his luck even more, sensing the desperation in Kid's eyes.
"Th– that's too much, I'm not sure I can negotiate such a deal, the resurrection of Ben Faulkner will already cost more than the maximum compensation I'm allowed to offer… this is ridiculous" Kid protested, but Leo heard none of it.
"Take it or leave it Captain, this is my bottom line" Leo said, as he rudely placed a palm to Kid's face, looking away from him in disgust.
"There's no hurry to reply today…. Let me know of your decision tomorrow, once you have communicated with all three interested parties about our conversation" Leo said, as Kid let out a deep sigh before standing up from his seat.
"You're one tough negotiator…. Master Skyshard" Kid said, as he took his leave.
"And you're too spineless for your own good Captain" Leo whispered, once he left as he slammed the door of his manor shut.
It seemed like once again he had hit an achievement he wasn't supposed to hit, and once again his rewards were going to come with penalties that he did not want.

chapters.title: Chapter 759 - 759: Kid's Decision
chapters.content:
Over the next two days, Captain Kid felt a headache befalling him from all sides, as the situation in the world of Terra Nova worsened even more.
With Bernabeu City falling completely under WhiteSaber control, the probability of the rebels gaining complete control over the Empire in the coming weeks rose to a whopping 92%, making their absolute victory a near certainty.
To make matters worse, the morale of the few remaining righteous faction loyalists seemed to plummet after facing successive defeats, making many jump ship to the rebel side.
This of-course was an outcome that the Unity Empire Government back on planet Terra Nova was not too thrilled about, as they increased their scrutiny of Captain Kid's handling of the situation, and demanded that drastic measures be taken to remedy the inevitable rebel win.
All in all, with Leo refusing to reduce his gaming time, Kid found himself in extremely hot waters with the Unity Government, who now deemed Kid to be 'incompetent' and wanted to place pressure on the universal government to change the Arc Ship's command structure, and replace Kid as captain.
"I don't see how any of this is my fault… if they wanted to make the Unity Empire invincible, they should have requested the world setting to be that way from the get-go…." Kid grumbled, as he did not appreciate the fact that he was being admonished despite not making any mistakes.
"Even if I finish this mission without being replaced as Captain, I'm sure my career is going to take a nosedive afterwards.
No new employer would want to hire me if they read the feedback that the unity government is threatening to give me at the end of this trip.
However, if I do end up helping them, I'll break the already fragile game balance and the universal government will fire me for excessive interference–" Kid said, scratching his near bald head, as he pulled a few strands out.
He knew he was walking on thin ice, but just couldn't figure out how to navigate this mess safely.
Then, unexpectedly he got interrupted when his private communication device buzzed with a new urgent message.
It was a message from Mu Fan, the designated point of contact for the Mu Clan in their pursuit to recruit Leo Skyshard.
It was a message that Kid had been expecting for days now, however, was disappointed not to have received sooner.
Now, as the notification blinked on his private communication device, a wave of relief washed over him, as the message seemed to be written in a happy note.
'At least someone is happy with my services…' Kid thought, as he read the letter with utmost sincerity.
The Unity Empire might have been sharpening their knives, ready to carve his career into irrelevance, but the Mu Clan—an influential and resourceful faction—still saw value in him, and was even promising him unimaginable rewards for his cooperation!
'Its a way out…. If I choose them, I can get out of this mess safely' Kid thought, as suddenly he saw a clear path out of the mess he currently found himself in.
"Interesting" Kid mused as he leaned back into his chair and stared at the Mu Clan's insignia displayed on his communicator.
The Unity Empire Government was already painting him as incompetent, and even if he bent over backward to fix the game balance, it was unlikely he'd be rewarded or even given credit.
The Universal Government was also watching him like hawks, and any further intervention in the game world could see him fired on the spot.
But the Mu Clan? They weren't bound by bureaucratic red tape. They operated in shadows and with results, not empty promises or scapegoating, and if he played his cards right, he might not only escape this mess unscathed but emerge wealthier and more secure than ever before.
'Who needs the Unity Empire's empty praise or flourishing mission report anyway?' Kid thought, as he decided to go for the side that was offering him more benefits rather than threats.
His lips curled into a sly grin as the plan began to take form in his mind. The Mu Clan was offering him a golden parachute—one tied directly to Leo Skyshard. If Leo became their prized asset, Kid could ride that wave all the way to comfort and safety.
And so, he made his decision.
"Screw the Unity Empire," he muttered under his breath. "From now on, my only priority is Leo Skyshard and the Mu Clan."
**********
(A few minutes later)
After letting the rush from making his mind cool down, Kid opened the letter from My Fan once again, carefully re-reading all her requests.
1. Lower the mana concentration in Leo Skyshard's quarters to halt his meditation progress.
2. Sabotage his meditation training subtly.
3. Delete all data suggesting Leo might awaken genetic abilities.
The first two points puzzled him. The Mu Clan had expressed such interest in Leo, yet here they were, asking him to prevent Leo's progress. Shouldn't they want him to grow stronger? Wouldn't that serve their interests better?
But then again, Mu Fan's wording had been clear—it was for his own good.
Perhaps there was a delicate timeline at play to awakening his genetic potential that he as an outsider wasn't privy to.
Genetic Awakening was a common process in the upperclassmen of the universe that belonged to a special bloodline with bloodline ability running dormant within them. However, for the majority of the universe, they were born without any inherent abilities and hence had no knowledge about the subject.
Kid as a Captain knew that Genetic Awakening was a process that did happen in society and that different factions achieved it differently, however, he was not sure about the Mu Clans awakening methods.
The Mu Clan was an organisation that operated mostly in shadows, and their reasoning often followed logic inaccessible to commoners like him.
Kid sighed and shook his head. "Not my job to understand. Just my job to execute."
With a few quick taps on his control panel, Kid began the data purge. Files containing genetic markers, meditation efficiency logs, and system-flagged anomalies related to Leo Skyshard were systematically wiped from the ship's internal database.
Poof. Gone.
Next came the trickier part: sabotaging Leo's meditation training.
The ship's environmental controls were advanced, but fine-tuning mana concentration in an individual's quarters without raising suspicion required precision. Kid's fingers hovered over the interface as he adjusted the settings, carefully lowering the ambient mana density in Leo's quarters to a level just above noticeable. It wouldn't stop Leo entirely, but it would slow his progress significantly.
Step one, complete.
Now came the planning phase. Kid knew that Leo was stubborn and relentless in his training. If subtle sabotage didn't deter him, he'd have to find another way to convince the boy to stop meditating altogether.
Perhaps a fabricated error log warning of 'unstable mana flux'? Or maybe… an emergency maintenance drill requiring Leo to leave his quarters for a few weeks time?
The more Kid thought about it, the clearer his path became. He'd play this carefully, inch by inch, step by step.
As he leaned back in his chair, rubbing his temples, he felt something he hadn't felt in weeks—control.
The Unity Empire might have written him off, but the Mu Clan had thrown him a lifeline, and he intended to hold on tight.
"Leo Skyshard," Kid muttered, staring at the monitor displaying the young player's quarters, "your fate is now tied to mine. Don't mess this up for both of us."
With that, Captain Kid began drafting his next moves, fully committing himself to the Mu Clan's agenda, and unknowingly setting into motion events that would ripple far beyond his control.
In particular, his decision to wipe Leo's genetic logs and warnings from the ship's data was sure to wreak unprecedented chaos on the universal stage when discovered, as anything related to the 'Timeless Assassin' was a topic that invited direct fury of the Gods.
As a low level citizen, one who did not even know about the legend of the Timeless Assassin, Captain Kid naturally had no idea about the chain of events he had just placed in motion, however, for good or for worse, his choice today had irreversibly changed the future of the universe.
**********
