chapters.title: Chapter 760 - 760: Self- Reflection
chapters.content:
(Leo's POV)
It was a day just like any other for Leo, where he was meditating with his Marrow Meditation Manual, however, his progress today seemed much slower than the previous day, which was a regression in meditation speed that was hard to conventionally explain.
'What's going on? Why is it taking me so long to produce new cells today?' Leo wondered, as somehow he felt as if his body was just unable to absorb mana at a sufficient rate, slowing down his meditation progress.
However, although he was slower than usual, Leo did not suspect any foul play by the Ship Operators, as he had no reason to think that anyone would want to sabotage the speed of his meditation outside the game world.
Instead, he wondered if he was making a mistake in the absorption process, or if he was too focused on making new cells that his mind did not have enough energy left to focus on other tasks.
"Odd… the meditation manual isn't pointing out any problems with me. I'm sorry sure the scroll would point it out if I was making some mistake that I could otherwise avoid, but the fact that it's not displaying any warnings means that the fault is not with me…." Leo muttered, as he decided to unexpectedly cut his meditation session for the day short and focus on physical practice instead.
It had been 3 days since he rejected Captain Kid's preliminary offer, however, the ship's Captain had not reached out to him since.
He had neither been pressured to reduce his gaming time nor informed that his conditions had been accepted, placing him in a limbo where he was unsure about his own future.
"I hope they don't outright ban me from the game–" Leo mused, as he picked up his practice daggers and began to warm up in the manor's training area.
To prepare for any unforeseen circumstances, he had avoided logging into Terra Nova for the past three days, hoping to conserve every remaining gaming day he had left. However, with the situation in the game world growing increasingly volatile, he knew he was going to be inevitably forced to log in tomorrow.
He had hoped to hear back from Captain Kid before he logged back in, but with the Captain not actively seeking him out, he could not go look for him either, as looking desperate now would only make his negotiating position weaker.
*Stab*
*Stab*
*Stab*
Throwing his daggers with streamlined precision, Leo began his physical training for the day with dagger throwing, as he worked on his aim and his ability to throw daggers in a curved arc.
Currently, he could accurately place a 15° curve on his dagger throw arc, with pinpoint accuracy, while only a rough accuracy with a 30° or higher curve.
His goal was to someday learn the 90° dagger throw, so that he could take out opponents behind the cover of a wall/obstacle without risking exposure.
It was apparently possible upon reaching [Perfect] mastery of a weapon, but so far he was nowhere close to that realm.
"I once again have two empty skill slots, bringing my potential skill tally to 8…." Leo muttered to himself as he trained, as he let his mind wander about what sorts of skills he still lacked as a warrior.
In more ways than one, he was a complete Assassin having every necessary skill needed for stealth and assassination, however, he lacked any skills related to self-regeneration and healing.
After having fought several 'Master' level fighters in the game over the past few weeks, Leo understood that having a self-regeneration skill was extremely important, however, he just could not wrap his head around a suitable option.
The most-effective healing skills were all restricted to the 'Healer' class players and consumed a lot of mana to perform.
Spells like [Greater Heal] drained nearly 50% of the mana bar of an average level 450 player, which was too expensive a cost for Leo to bear even as a level 1000 maestro.
For him, he needed something more subtle, something passive that could heal his micro-injuries fast and clot his blood incase of a major wound, however, could not find anything matching the exact profile.
So far, he got-by from carrying lots of stamina and HP potions, however, to fight against the Black Dragon, Leo knew that he had to learn every skill that he could.
The second skill he singled out to learn was any skill related to proper defence.
So far, his superior speed and reflexes were the only defence he had, however, with yet another empty skill slot at his disposal, Leo knew it was time for a change.
Dodging a blow was not always an option in a high-stakes battle and having active defensive measures under such situations was a huge advantage.
If he were to be restricted as a 5 skill-slot player, Leo would probably never waste a skill slot on defence especially when his speed and reflexes were so high, however, given the luxury to have one, it was not a bad choice to make.
Any skill that could deploy a body barrier, or reduce the impact of an incoming blow by 30-50% could be a game-changer in a life/death battle and Leo understood this all too well.
Unlike the healing skill where he found no suitable options to learn, Leo knew exactly what sort of defensive skill he wanted in his arsenal, with him already having singled out three choices.
[Full Cover]
[Mana Barrier]
[Damage Control]
All three of them were Semi-Legendary skills whose skill scrolls were available for purchase in the market and Leo planned to buy one in the near future.
The fight for the Empire was going smoothly and was likely to conclude within this week, leaving Leo with only one last milestone to focus on.
A milestone that would be the ultimate test of his gaming journey so far.
The fight against the Demon King and the Black Dragon Drogo.

chapters.title: Chapter 761 - 761: A tough deal
chapters.content:
Just as Leo was busy wondering about his flaws as a warrior and the areas where he could still improve, his training session was interrupted by Captain Kid, who walked towards him with an obvious glee plastered all over his face.
"My apologies for interrupting your training session, Master Skyshard," he began, as Leo paused his training and nodded in acknowledgement.
He had been expecting Kid to visit for a while now and was hence happy to see him arrive.
"I submitted your proposal to the Unity Government, and they have decided to accept it with open arms," Kid said, as Leo raised an eyebrow of confusion.
His demands had been nothing short of outlandish, however, the Unity Government seemed to have accepted it anyway, which came as a bit of a surprise to Leo.
"They have agreed to pay for the cloning of Ben Faulkner, on-top of paying you 500,000 MP, for reducing your current gaming hours to half its level.
However, they have only one small condition in return" Kid said, as Leo gestured for him to explain the condition.
"They have requested that you give up the powers belonging to the Emperor immediately to a regent after assuming the throne.
In other words, they have requested that although you remain the Emperor on paper and in power, you do not act as one in practice, handing over all the practical work to a regent of your choice.
Additionally, they have requested, that in-case the righteous faction starts to fight back, trying to get a piece of the land back after your coronation, that you are to not personally suppress them, until they become a large enough threat to challenge StrongHaven" Kid said, as Leo found this request to be extremely odd.
The Unity Government wanted him to immediately appoint a regent upon coronation and not suppress a righteous faction resurgence till they were considered a big enough threat?
These were absurd conditions with veiled motives hidden beneath that Leo could not see through for now.
"What are these absurd conditions? Do they even make sense?" Leo asked Kid, who merely shrugged his shoulders in indifference.
"I am but the messenger here. The decision is yours" Kid replied, as he did not sell the offer to Leo anymore.
Having already decided that he was going to attach his future with the Mu Clan, Kid was no longer worried about the issues between Leo and the Unity Government, only coming to visit him here today as an official messenger.
In some ways, Kid could already envision the considerations that the Unity Government may have had in mind behind making such a request, as although it seemed absurd it was anything but.
If Leo appointed Luke, Amanda or anyone from his family as his regent, it was sure to upset the uprising leadership, who were sure to be dissatisfied with such a decision.
With the right manipulation behind the scenes done by the game operators, such dissatisfaction could be used to sow discord and create a rift between the uprising guild, making their institutional stability hollow from within.
On the other hand, if Leo did appoint ChaosBringer or some other high ranking official from the guild to the position of the regent, the ship operators could still threaten him/her into a reduced gaming time penalty and various other tactics that would force the regent to work in shadows against their own organization.
While Leo was already penalized to the maximum level possible, the same could not be said for other members of uprising leadership, who could be strong-armed into unfavorable contracts or forced to accept unacceptable in-game missions.
This was probably the play that the Unity Government was hoping for, as once they removed Leo out of the way, they hoped to control his regent and tear down the rebel movement from the inside out.
It was a classic strategy of bringing down an Empire through internal problems and Kid could see it as plain as the day.
However, despite understanding the possible potholes behind such an offer, he did not offer Leo any advice and let him arrive at his own conclusions.
"Hmm…. What about the information pack? Do I get that too?" Leo asked after a while of thinking, as Kid blinked before nodding vigorously.
"Oh yes, yes, you get a very important information pack too, one that's usually reserved for military officers serving in the universal government" Kid replied, as Leo stroked his chin while mulling over the offer.
Halving his already few remaining gaming days did not seem like the best course of action, but the benefits far outweighed the difficulties here.
He had already hit the level cap within the game, meaning that no matter how many enemies he killed anymore, he was going to see no extra boost in stats, making levelling within the game utterly useless.
The only reason he wanted to kill the Demon King and Drogo was to gather enough MP to resurrect Ben Faulkner, but with that procedure becoming an assurance, he could also accept a loss against the Demon King in-case he suffered one, putting a lot of pressure off his shoulders.
Finally and most importantly, he had nothing else left to achieve in the game anymore as he felt confident that he was already the strongest warrior in the Unity Empire by a longshot.
There was not a single player or NPC within the Unity Empire that could rival his strength, and he felt slightly purposeless and lonely at that peak.
He had to wait until landing on planet Terra Nova now to look for new challenging opponents to beat, and although he wanted to enjoy the success he had built through hard work, he somehow felt that even with his remaining gaming days halved, he still had enough time to do it anyways.
"Very well then… I accept your offer" Leo said, as Kid beamed in joy.
He had successfully brokered a deal acceptable to both parties, navigating expertly through tough negotiations.

chapters.title: Chapter 762 - 762: Information Device
chapters.content:
After signing the contract, Leo found himself being handed over an unusual-looking device and a metallic CD by Captain Kid.
The device resembled a mix between a headset and medical equipment, with small magnetic nodes arranged along its structure.
"This," Kid began, gesturing to the device, "is the information pack I promised. But instead of simply reading it like a regular data file, you'll need to use these specialized modular electromagnetic plugs. Once attached to your head, they'll transmit the data directly into your brain via electromagnetic propagation."
He paused briefly, allowing Leo to examine the equipment.
"This method of information transfer is standard for military-grade encryption. It prevents unauthorized access by ensuring the data can only be deciphered through this specific device. Every message classified above a certain encryption rank on Terra Nova is delivered in this format," Kid explained, pointing out the key magnetic nodes Leo would need to position on his temples and the back of his head.
Leo inspected the CD as Kid continued, "This disk contains both your unique passkey and the encrypted message. When you're ready, slot it into the device, and the data transfer will begin. However," Kid's voice grew serious, "be aware that the CD can only play the message twice before it self-destructs. Pay close attention, Leo. Absorb every detail and make notes on anything critical. You won't get a third chance."
Leo gave a firm nod, acknowledging the gravity of Kid's words. "Understood, Captain. Thank you."
Captain Kid extended his hand, and Leo grasped it firmly.
Clap.
For a brief moment, their eyes met. Kid's usual sharp demeanor softened as a faint smile crept onto his face.
"The MP promised in the contract will be credited to your account by the end of the day," Kid continued. "Additionally, upon landing, you'll receive one resurrection token. Take it to a cloning facility, and you'll be able to recreate Ben Faulkner without issue."
Leo nodded in gratitude, his expression serious as Kid turned on his heel, ready to depart.
But just as he began walking and took a couple steps, Leo's voice cut through the moment, stopping him in his tracks.
"Captain… one more thing."
Kid turned, his brows slightly raised. "What is it?"
Leo hesitated briefly, choosing his words carefully. "During my meditation earlier today, I noticed something… strange. It felt significantly more difficult than yesterday. There wasn't any obvious reason for it. Do you… have any idea why?"
The question lingered in the air, heavy with uncertainty as Kid froze for a moment, his expression carefully neutral, though Leo detected a flicker of something—concern, perhaps—crossing the Captain's face.
"You had trouble meditating?" Kid repeated, his tone quieter now, edged with genuine confusion as he turned fully to face Leo again.
For a moment, they stared at each other, the weight of unspoken thoughts hanging between them.
Kid's sharp eyes studied Leo's face carefully, searching for any hint of suspicion or malice in his expression. But there was none. Leo's gaze was steady, his brow slightly furrowed with genuine confusion, not accusation. And even his previous tone had been curious, uncertain even, but never confrontational.
That was the key detail that allowed Kid to remain composed. If Leo had suspected foul play, his voice would have been sharper, his stance more aggressive, and his question would have been framed differently. But Leo wasn't even close to connecting the dots. He had no idea that Kid had subtly sabotaged his training regimen the previous day—just enough to cause strain without raising alarms.
A minuscule tweak in the mana flow readings of the equipment was usually imperceptible to most players, but apparently Leo had caught on.
Not fully, but he knew something was off.
'He doesn't know the full picture,' Kid thought, maintaining his calm exterior. His brief moment of hesitation fading as his mind raced to construct a plausible explanation. He allowed a slight shrug to roll across his shoulders, feigning ignorance.
"Meditation can be… unpredictable, Leo," Kid said, his voice smooth and measured. "Sometimes, it's not about external factors but internal ones. Fatigue, mental distractions, or even residual stress from intense activity the day before can make the process more challenging. Your body might just be adapting to the increasing load of your abilities."
Leo seemed to consider this, his expression softening slightly as he nodded along. Kid pressed on, reinforcing his alibi.
"Take some time to rest tonight. Clear your mind before your next session. Sometimes a little reset can work wonders. But if the problem still persists, do let me know and I'll send a ship engineer to check your meditation room"
Kid offered a small, reassuring smile, one that didn't quite reach his eyes. Leo accepted the answer without further probing, giving another thoughtful nod.
"Yeah… maybe you're right. Thanks, Captain."
Kid turned once again, this time walking away without pause. But deep down, he couldn't shake the faint edge of unease creeping up his spine. Leo might not suspect anything now, but Kid knew one thing about Leo Skyshard: he wasn't someone who ignored inconsistencies for long. If Kid wanted to keep his secret buried, he'd need to tread carefully in the days ahead, or the notorious assassin that claimed the lives of entire armies within the game, could very easily sneak into his quarters and claim his life for messing with him instead.
'Holy shit…. Why did I ever decide to mess with this freak?' Kid wondered, as he recalled some of Leo's most infamous moments within the game world and reminded himself that he was not a sane man to be around.
Leo Skyshard, despite the amiable and composed facade he presented to the world, was, at his core, a cold and calculating predator. Behind those sharp eyes and calm demeanor lay the mind of a man who could dismantle an opponent—physically, mentally, and strategically—without a flicker of hesitation.
If Captain Kid ever slipped—if he ever let even the faintest hint of his sabotage become apparent—he knew exactly what awaited him.
Leo wasn't the kind of man to let betrayal slide. No, Leo Skyshard didn't believe in mercy for those who tried to undermine him. He would unravel Kid piece by piece, exposing every weakness, exploiting every vulnerability, and, when the time came, ensuring that Kid would regret ever crossing him.
And hence he needed to be careful.

chapters.title: Chapter 763 - 763: Information Pack (1)
chapters.content:
Leo walked back to his room, the strange information device in hand, uncertain of what to expect once he activated it.
"I wonder what kind of information I'll find inside?" Leo murmured as he settled into the plush chair in his luxurious bedroom.
With a focused expression, he began carefully connecting the modules to his head, each click of the attachments echoing softly in the quiet room.
He tried to follow Kid's guidelines precisely, attaching every module exactly where it was supposed to go.
"I hope this is right…" he said at the end, as although he did connect the device to the best of his abilities, there was always a risk of brain damage when trying odd devices on the mind.
[Insert message CD here]
A white label with black text read, as Leo placed the information CD within, causing the device to boot-up automatically.
[Checking user identity….]
[Confirming identity…..]
[Loading message….]
[Boot-up complete, Displaying message]
The device said through a speaker, as once the device was ready to project the information, it began doing so, directly into Leo's brain.
************
The sensation that Leo felt after the message device activated was similar to logging into the world of Terra Nova, but slightly different.
While logging into the game daily felt like a routine experience, this felt slightly foreign, which was mostly the reason behind why Leo felt uncomfortable at first.
Then, as he found himself completely immersed in the message world and relaxed, the message finally began to play, with a small pixie fairy flying in front of him.
"So cadet from outer world! You have finally decided to join the most prestigious institution in the whoooole of universe! Congratulations!" The fairy said in the most childish and shrill voice, as Leo almost let out an involuntary laugh.
The fairy seemed to believe he was a new military recruit and was apparently treating him as such.
"It's my understanding that your knowledge about the wider universe and its accepted practices is a bit lacking because you have come from a different planet, but that's okay, for today, me, pixie will tell you all you need to know!" The small fairy said as it flew excitedly around Leo's head.
"Firstly, let's talk about planets where you might be deployed to complete your missions!" The fairy said, as the background behind her shifted from green fields and trees to two split screens, showing two spherical planets.
Then, the pixie twirled in the air, her tiny wings leaving a faint trail of glittering light as the two planets behind her began to rotate slowly on the split screen.
One glowed with bright neon lights and metallic structures reaching into the skies, while the other shimmered with hues of green, gold, and deep brown, its forests sprawling endlessly under clear blue skies.
"Alright, cadet! Pay close attention because this is super important!" the pixie chirped, her voice ringing with exaggerated enthusiasm. "The universe, vast and endless as it is, can broadly be divided into having only two types of planets: Technological planets and Ecological planets!"
The left screen zoomed in on the first planet—the Technological Planet. Leo's eyes narrowed slightly as towering skyscrapers made of gleaming steel and glass came into focus.
On the technological planet, the roads were filled with sleek, hovering vehicles snaking through the air as they crisscrossed between the mega-structures.
Mechanical drones zipped around like metal bees, while cybernetically enhanced humans walked briskly, their glowing cybernetic limbs reflecting the city's ambient neon glow.
"Technological planets," the pixie continued, "are marvels of scientific advancement! Here, technology reigns supreme. Everything you can think of—teleportation corridors, flying cars, state-of-the-art medical facilities, cybernetic augmentations—everything is available and in constant use! Think of them as cities of light and steel, constantly buzzing with energy and invention."
Leo watched as the camera panned across a bustling marketplace where vendors sold futuristic weapons, mechanical limbs, and holographic gadgets. In the background, a massive teleportation corridor glowed with vibrant blue light as travelers blinked in and out of existence in a seamless stream of movement.
"However!" The pixie's voice rose as she fluttered to the other side of the split screen, where the second planet began to dominate the display. "Ecological planets are completely different!"
The view shifted to reveal a sprawling forest, ancient trees towering so high that their branches disappeared into the clouds. Rivers shimmered with crystal-clear water, cascading into waterfalls that roared with life. Amidst this paradise were villages—small, humble settlements made of stone, clay, and natural mortar. Structures rose organically, blending into the environment as though they had grown directly from the earth.
"On Ecological planets, all forms of modern technology are strictly forbidden!" the pixie emphasized, her tiny finger wagging at Leo as though he were already guilty of breaking this sacred rule. "No flying cars, no cybernetic implants, and not even advanced medical devices are allowed. These planets live and breathe in harmony with nature. Their cities are built using stone, clay, and natural materials, not concrete and steel."
Leo felt an odd sense of calm wash over him as he observed the serene beauty of the ecological world. It was an untouched paradise, yet there was something almost intimidating about its raw, unyielding natural power.
"The universal government has clear rules about engagement on these planets," the pixie continued, her tone growing serious. "On Technological planets, warfare and enforcement rely heavily on advanced weapons and technology. Armored mechs, plasma rifles, and orbital strikes are all fair game. But on Ecological planets?"
The camera panned to a group of warriors standing atop a hill under a stormy sky. They wielded swords glowing with raw mana, bows that shot ethereal arrows of light, and staves crackling with elemental energy.
"Fighting on Ecological planets must be done using primitive weapons—swords, bows, spears—and, of course, mana. The moment you draw advanced technology into an ecological world, you've committed a crime against universal law. And trust me, cadet, the consequences are not worth it."
The two planets faded, leaving only the pixie hovering before Leo, her wings fluttering softly.
"So there you have it!" she said with a flourish. "Two different worlds. Two completely different sets of rules. And you, dear cadet, might find yourself on either one, so remember the rules of both!"
"Next, we talk about the different types of enhancements you can possibly undergo at the military–" The fairy declared as with a clap of her tiny hands, the background behind her shifted again, and Leo braced himself as the next segment of the message began.

chapters.title: Chapter 764 - 764: Information Pack (2)
chapters.content:
"Next, we talk about the different types of enhancements you can possibly undergo at the military–" The fairy declared as the background behind her shifted again, fading from the serene imagery of Ecological and Technological planets into a sleek metallic chamber.
Rows of glowing glass cylinders lined the walls, each containing a swirling, luminous liquid of different colors. Holographic DNA strands floated in the air, rotating slowly as lines of alien script ran alongside them.
"Enhancements, cadet, are the cornerstone of every elite soldier's power in the universe!" the pixie declared, flitting in front of a glowing blue vial suspended mid-air.
She placed her tiny hands on her hips and looked Leo square in the eye. "Now listen carefully because this isn't just trivia—it's so you don't go gawking at someone with snake eyes or horns and embarrass yourself in front of a decorated officer."
Leo smirked slightly at the pixie's warning but straightened up, ready to listen.
"Alright! The military offers three primary types of enhancements to its soldiers. Each has its benefits, risks, and, most importantly, rules. So let's break them down one by one!"
"Firstly the Genetic Correction Serum"
A golden vial floated forward, spinning slowly, light refracting off its shimmering contents.
"This is the Genetic Correction Serum, and let me tell you, cadet, this little vial is practically liquid gold!" The pixie twirled in the air, and a holographic display projected strands of DNA being meticulously repaired and rewritten.
"After a soldier serves for at least five years, they become eligible for this serum. It's designed to fix genetic flaws and imperfections—anything from predispositions to hereditary diseases to structural deficiencies caused by malnutrition or environmental damage."
The display shifted, showing a silhouette of a human figure gradually growing taller and more muscular.
"If your genetics held you back from achieving your true potential—like, say, you were supposed to be a 6'4" hunk but ended up 5'9" short king—this serum corrects that. It also enhances muscle density, resulting in a 10–20% increase in strength and mass after the therapy."
Leo leaned forward slightly, his curiosity piqued.
"And before you ask—yes, it's completely safe. This serum is one of the biggest reasons people dream of joining the military. Who doesn't want to reach their peak physical form effortlessly?"
The golden vial faded, replaced by a swirling silver one.
"Second Hybridization Serum"
The pixie crossed her arms and gave Leo a stern look. "Now, cadet, this next serum is where things get wild."
The silver vial began glowing faintly as the display projected figures with glowing snake eyes, clawed fingers, and elongated limbs.
"The Hybridization Serum allows soldiers to integrate traits from other species into their own bodies. Think of it as... borrowing nature's best features."
The display zoomed in on specific examples—an officer with orcish strength, another with cat-like eyes that glowed in the dark, and one with snake-like fangs dripping venom.
"Strength, vision, agility, venomous bites—you name it. But—and this is a big but—there's a heavy price for this power."
The pixie's wings drooped slightly as her voice turned serious.
"Soldiers who undergo Hybridization usually become sterile. Their reproductive cells are harvested and frozen before the procedure, just in case they want kids someday. It's a steep price to pay, but the enhancements are often worth it in the eyes of those who choose this path."
Leo frowned slightly at the implication but said nothing.
The silver vial faded, and a crimson one took its place.
"Finally a Racial Change Serum"
The pixie hovered slightly higher, her expression a mix of awe and caution as she gestured to the crimson vial.
"Compared to species like elves, demons and vampires, species like humans, dwarves and goblins just don't have the same sort of physical dominance, or ceiling for growth, and hence the military offers this third and final choice for individuals from weak species like human"
The display projected humanoid figures slowly transforming—humans turning into elves, orcs, dwarves, and even demons. Their features changed gradually, skin tones shifted, horns and pointed ears appeared, and their physiques adapted to match their chosen race.
"This serum doesn't just tweak your genes—it rebuilds your DNA from the ground up. Want the durability of an orc, the agility of an elf, or the raw magical power of a demon? This serum makes it possible."
The pixie's tone darkened slightly.
"But it comes with significant risks. First, there's a 50% chance of becoming sterile, and second… your lifespan often gets cut in half compared to your original species."
The display faded, leaving only the crimson vial glowing ominously.
"Those who take this serum become something beyond human, but they pay for that power in ways most people can't imagine."
The three vials—golden, silver, and crimson—hovered side by side before fading away entirely.
The pixie flew closer to Leo, her bright, glowing eyes locking with his.
"Now, cadet, I told you all this not just to stuff your brain with trivia, but so you don't act like an ignorant rookie when you meet an enhanced soldier."
She pointed a tiny finger at him.
"You'll see people with rhino horns, glowing reptilian pupils, scaled arms, and even shadowy demonic wings. They're not monsters, mutants, or creatures—they're soldiers, and every scar, every enhancement they bear comes with a story and sacrifice."
Leo nodded solemnly, understanding the weight behind her words.
"Good!" The pixie clapped her hands, and the background began shifting again, the neon laboratory fading away.
"Now that we've got that cleared up, let's move on to… hmm, what should we talk about next? Oh! Let's discuss ranks and responsibilities in the universal military! For it may be useful in your journey!"
The scene shifted, and Leo prepared himself for the next wave of information as the pixie grinned mischievously.
A series of military badges appeared before her, with the first one being a simple design with one stripe, and the last one being an intricate medal with lots of carvings and design work going into it.

chapters.title: Chapter 765 - 765: Information Pack (3)
chapters.content:
Leo listened to the fairy delve into the intricacies of military ranks and promotions. While the subject didn't captivate him as much as the earlier revelations, he still managed to grasp the key points amidst the fairy's animated explanations.
The most significant detail was the structure of the first five years of military service—a period universally recognized as automatic promotion years.
Regardless of a cadet's performance, competence, or battlefield achievements, every soldier ascended five ranks during this time. These promotions came with increased pay scales and, most notably, the administration of the Genetic Correction Serum as a reward for their commitment and perseverance.
The fairy emphasized a critical statistic: 70% of cadets voluntarily left the military after completing this five-year milestone.
The reasons were clear and practical. During those five years, soldiers incurred zero housing or food expenses, allowing them to save substantial sums of money.
More importantly, they received genetic correction therapy, a procedure so rare and prohibitively expensive in civilian markets that it was practically unattainable outside military service.
Equipped with their savings and genetically optimized bodies, many former cadets transitioned smoothly into careers as adventurers, mercenaries, or specialized guild operatives.
The wealth of guilds scattered across the universe eagerly welcomed these individuals, valuing their discipline, adherence to orders, and teamwork-oriented mindset—traits deeply ingrained through military training.
However, despite their physical and mental conditioning, these ex-cadets often lacked real combat experience. Their deployments during the initial five years primarily revolved around asset protection, riot control, and logistical oversight—roles with low mortality rates and relatively comfortable conditions.
Yet, this structure served an essential purpose for the military. It acted as a filtering mechanism, allowing commanders to identify exceptional talent among the recruits. Those who demonstrated outstanding skills, strategic acumen, or leadership qualities were fast-tracked into prestigious career paths, often bypassing the slow climb through mid-level ranks.
In essence, the first five years of military service were not just a career foundation but also a launchpad. For some, it was a gateway to freedom, wealth, and independence. For others, it marked the beginning of distinguished military careers, carved out through merit and perseverance.
The fairy emphasised on how Leo had to strive for excellence in case he did want to continue in the military post the first five years, as the first significant pay-bump only arrived at the sixth promotion, when one was promoted to the role of 'Squad Captain'.
From the rank of Squad Captain onwards, all promotions were based on merit, and it usually took one 30-35 years serving the military with an exemplary record to be promoted to the rank of 'Major'.
Ranks beyond Major, depended purely on one's track record, ability to handle meetings with politicians and Gods, and a hell lot of luck.
On average the youngest 'General' in the military, even those of the lowest rank were 60-70 years of age, having served the military for over 50 years, while all the top-most Generals were over 100 years of age and powerhouses in their own right.
For Leo, all this was not important right now, however, in-case he did encounter a military man in the future, it was good to know what their journey must have been like, to get a feel for their character and importance.
"Lastly, let's talk about your food and lodging in the military, and the culture we promote at the universal military—" The fairy said, as the last topic that she touched was the socially accepted customs of the universe.
There she explained how sexuality had nothing to do with reproduction, and how it was acceptable in the military to have partners of any species, gender, race and sex.
Leo almost had a deja vu listening to the fairy repeating sentences such as "Any discrimination on the bases of race, gender, species or sex will result in the cadet being subjected to the martial court" as these were the sentences he was used to hearing back on Earth.
It was funny how there was no discrimination in the universal military on bases of skin color, which was prevalent on Earth, as apparently when one's species itself was considered weak and pathetic, it did not matter if one was a white human or a dark skinned one.
However, despite the lecture on how all relationships were acceptable, Leo felt no urge to open his rear-end for exploration, as although 75% of all military recruits swung both ways, Leo knew in his heart that he only had the hots for Amanda.
"There are three main holidays that we celebrate universe wide in a calendar year and they are…." The fairy began, as the last topic she touched was culture and how there were 3 main holidays in the universe, observed on every planet regardless of whether it was ecological or technological.
It was something interesting to know, but once again Leo tossed it to the back of his mind, as the automatic recorded message reached its end, with the fairy waving him goodbye.
[Do you want to replay the message? You can replay it one more time.]
The machine asked, as Leo pressed yes, just to watch all that information play out once again, with him focusing on minute details this time that he might have missed during the first run.
At the end, the device powered down automatically and after a series of static noises, a burned disc was ejected out of the main machine and a smoky smell enveloped Leo's entire bedroom.
"The military does not take any chances with their information machines eh?" Leo chuckled, as he disconnected the modular connectors to his head and organised the information he had just learnt.
In many ways, what he learnt today was invaluable, as it could help him better negotiate his deal with any clan/ guild that wished to recruit him upon landing.
However, in other ways he was still slightly disappointed with the information he gained today, as he expected much more.
The universe he was heading into felt vast and incomprehensible, filled with layers of complexity he had never imagined.
With every new piece of information he uncovered, the weight of his ignorance grew heavier.
This new universe wasn't just different from Earth—it was an entirely alien reality, governed by rules, cultures, and technologies beyond anything he had ever known and that made Leo both excited and nervous for his future.

chapters.title: Chapter 766 - 766: A historic win
chapters.content:
(Leo's POV, Terra Nova Online)
By the time Leo logged back into the world of Terra Nova, a full five days after the attack on Bernabeu City, the game world had shifted dramatically.
For one, ChaosBringer had successfully captured all the central territories leading up to StrongHaven City, with the once-proud bastions of the righteous faction having crumbled one after another to the mighty rebel army, allowing them to march unimpeded straight to the gates of StrongHaven City.
Inside, a couple of million loyalists—soldiers, mercenaries, and desperate citizens—stood ready to defend the capital city's towering walls, however, their chances to hold the rebel army for long seemed grim.
As per ChaosBringer's conservative yet confident assessment, all that stood between the uprising and the throne was the fall of StrongHaven City walls, as with a powerful and morally motivated army of 3.5 million strong, victory was all but assured for the rebels once the city gates opened for them.
As of this moment, the rebels had encircled the city entirely, choking off all supply and escape routes, making the fall of StrongHaven City no longer a question of if, but when.
The righteous faction players within no longer trusted one another, as there had been more than one attempts to betray the faction and open the gates, but unfortunately none were successful.
Nobody communicated with the other properly and the overall atmosphere was one of distrust and demoralization, with everyone constantly thinking about switching to the other side.
ChaosBringer's promise to reward all those who joined the rebel forces before the fall of StrongHaven City had compelled countless defenders to betray their own. Yet, despite the tide of deserters and opportunists, a handful of die-hard loyalists remained steadfast, refusing to abandon their posts, ensuring that even against all odds, the city still stood strong.
"What's going on here, ChaosBringer? What happened to your promise of welcoming me with a red carpet?" Leo typed as he logged into the game, his words laced with mild dissatisfaction.
There was no denying ChaosBringer's impressive success—or the fact that he had achieved feats few commanders could dream of.
However, with Leo's limited gaming days ticking away, mere success wasn't enough.
Leo had expected to log in and claim the throne, to see his victory already secured. Instead, the sight of StrongHaven's defiant walls still standing left him slightly displeased with ChaosBringer's inability to deliver on his implicit promise.
Naturally, on the other end of the text, ChaosBringer turned ghastly pale at being rebuked for the first time ever, as he felt like digging a hole and burying himself in it, for having disappointed Lord Boss.
************
(ChaosBringer's POV)
Even ChaosBringer felt a simmering frustration as the walls of StrongHaven City stood unyielding against him.
The march to the city gates had been almost effortless, a victorious procession through fallen territories. Yet now, those final gates seemed to mock him, defying every strategy he had employed.
Yet, despite his disappointment, there was a feeling within ChaosBringer that told him that there was little more he could do at this point, as without there being internal instigators to try and open the gates for the rebels, attacking the city walls in an open war was a reckless choice to make.
"Lord Boss expects more from me, but these damn righteous faction insects are making me look like a fool."
"This is the first time he's rebuked me. If I don't prove myself here, it'll leave a permanent stain on my reputation in his eyes."
"I'm sure if Lord Boss were leading this mission himself, StrongHaven would have already fallen. Perhaps… this is my limit," ChaosBringer muttered under his breath, gnawing nervously on his long nails.
The path to victory was clear—ChaosBringer could order hundreds of thousands of rebel troops to charge the gates, sacrificing lives in a desperate attempt to batter them down. But the cost in blood was a price he wasn't eager to pay if he could avoid it.
He had studied the WhiteSaber Guild's assault on Bernabeu City. They had possessed massive siege weapons, experienced engineers, and a highly coordinated team to break through fortified walls. The Uprising, however, had none of those advantages.
For ChaosBringer's forces to breach StrongHaven's gates, they would need to rely on the ancient and brutal strategy of battering rams—a direct, bloody confrontation that would claim countless lives, and hence it was a strategy he had long avoided.
But Leo's final message left him no choice:
"I'm on my way from the West to Center. It'll take me roughly 12 hours to reach StrongHaven City. You better capture it by then…."
The weight of that single message crushed any lingering hesitation. There was no longer room for caution, no space for hesitation.
"All men, prepare for war."
The order echoed through the internal group chat, carrying the weight of inevitability. Every rebel soldier received their battle roles, weapons were drawn, and the Uprising braced itself for a blood-soaked assault.
The time for hesitation had passed. Now, it was war.
************
The final battle for StrongHaven had been nothing short of bloody, dramatic, and brutal.
When ChaosBringer gave the command to charge, the rebel army surged forward like an unstoppable tide, crashing against the towering walls of StrongHaven City with pride and gusto.
War horns blared across the battlefield, a sound both triumphant and ominous, as millions of rebels pressed forward in unison.
The defenders of StrongHaven fought back with disciplined attack patterns and unyielding resolve.
From behind reinforced walls and firing slits, volleys of arrows and mana projectiles rained down upon the advancing rebel forces. Spells of fire and lightning lit up the night sky, striking devastating blows into the densely packed rebel formations below.
Yet, despite the relentless counter attacks, ChaosBringer remained unwavering in his resolve.
His commands, constant within the guild chat, reminded all captains and military leaders to keep the intensity high and the press on.
"All forces, continue to push. No matter the losses, push with everything you have!"
The strategy was clear: breach one of the city walls at any cost, create chaos within the city walls, and force the defenders to split their focus across multiple fronts.
However, this was easier said than done.
Wave after wave of rebel forces charged at the heavily fortified City Gates, carrying makeshift battering rams reinforced with whatever enchanted steel they could salvage.
Archers and mages provided covering fire, pinning down defenders perched atop the walls, while explosive spells targeted the gate's hinges and structural weak points.
Yet despite the best efforts of the rebels, the city walls held strong for the first hour of the assault, until the first signs of structural weakness began to appear on the East Gate of the city. Where the city gate began to creak and weaken.
After an hour of relentless assault, with the bodies of thousands piling at the gate's base, the wood and steel of the East finally seemed to buckle, as with an ear splitting crack, the East Gate splintered and fell inward.
"The east gate is down! All units, charge!" ChaosBringer typed furiously, as he directed all forces on the Eastern Gate to swarm the city.
And as per his command, Rebel forces poured into the city through the broken East Gate, flooding the narrow streets and alleyways.
Chaos erupted as the rebels clashed with the defenders in brutal close-quarters combat, but the defenders, now overwhelmed and disoriented, struggled to reform their lines as rebels swept through residential districts and strategic choke points.
But ChaosBringer's plan went further than just clearing the streets.
The rebel forces that breached the East Gate didn't just aim to conquer—they aimed to dismantle the defenders' cohesion entirely.
Swift-moving squads fanned out, striking at key defensive positions near the North and South Gates, slaughtering the commanders holding those gates strong, as they sowed panic and confusion amongst defender ranks.
Panic spread among the defenders at the North Gate as rebel forces approached from behind, as with the defenders now fighting on two fronts, their resistance began to crumble.
The heavy iron gates groaned as rebel squads worked in unison to force them open.
As eventually, with one final coordinated push, the North Gate gave way.
With the south gate also following suit shortly after.
With three gates now breached, the entirety of StrongHaven City was laid bare to the rebel army and the remaining defenders, realizing the futility of resistance, began to scatter.
Some surrendered outright, others fled into the depths of the city, hoping to escape the slaughter, but none were allowed to go too far, as the rebels hunted each and every single righteous faction player down without exception.
By late afternoon,ChaosBringer stood at the breached East Gate, his face pristine and his make-up untouched, as he strolled into StrongHaven City with a big smile on his face.
"It's over," he whispered, as the final coordinated assault saw the rebel army spread across the city like wildfire, consuming every district, every barricade, and every defender that dared to resist.
The defenders had fought bravely, but the weight of ChaosBringer's relentless strategy had proved too much.
By the evening, the red banners of the Uprising flew high above StrongHaven City's tallest towers as a system notification flashed across ChaosBringer's vision:
[System Notification: StrongHaven City has fallen. The Uprising has claimed victory!]
[All participating members are awarded with 5,000 MP.]
5000 MP was an astronomical sum for most players, a sum they could not imagine earning in their entire lifetimes, but ChaosBringer didn't celebrate. His focus was already elsewhere—on the one person whose opinion truly mattered.
[Lord Boss: Well done, ChaosBringer. I'll arrive shortly. Prepare the throne room for my arrival.]
ChaosBringer let out a deep, shaky breath, the weight of the past 10 hours finally sinking into his exhausted bones.
"At least I didn't fail him…" he muttered under his breath, as without wasting another moment, he turned and began making his way toward the city's central fortress.
Lord Boss was going to arrive in StrongHaven City shortly and he needed to roll out the red carpet for him and welcome him properly as promised.
Tomorrow was going to be a historic day for the uprising, when Lord Boss assumed the throne, and he needed to ensure that everything for that day was perfect.

chapters.title: Chapter 767 - 767: Coronation (1)
chapters.content:
(Early next morning, StrongHaven City)
As Leo arrived at the Western Gate of StrongHaven City alongside Dumpy, the sight that unfolded before him was something he could never have anticipated in a million years.
Leo had always assumed that "welcomed with a red carpet" was just a metaphor—a throwaway phrase meant to convey respect and grandeur.
So, when he had texted ChaosBringer a day ago, informing him that he expected to be welcomed with a red carpet, he had spoken figuratively. However, it seemed ChaosBringer had taken it quite literally.
Stretching out from the massive, splintered gates of StrongHaven City and running straight into the heart of the fortress was an actual velvety red carpet. Its deep crimson hue was pristine, unmarred by dust or blood, making it seem almost absurdly out of place amidst the war-torn ruins surrounding it.
On either side of the carpet, thousands of rebel soldiers stood in perfect formation. They had been thoroughly instructed on how to greet Lord Boss when he passed and had been forced to tidy themselves up and look presentable for today's ceremony.
Now, as they stood waiting for Leo to pass them, their armor gleamed with a spotless shine, their weapons were sheathed in ceremonial fashion, and their faces bore expressions etched with a mix of awe and reverence.
They stood shoulder to shoulder, forming an unbroken corridor of steel and loyalty.
Ribbit.
Dumpy let out an impressed croak, his wide swamp-frog eyes blinking at the extravagant scene before them. Leo, on the other hand, could only sigh internally.
"You've outdone yourself, ChaosBringer," he muttered.
As if summoned by his name, ChaosBringer appeared, flanked on either side by two of the most strikingly beautiful rebels to join the uprising—at least by conventional beauty standards. Yet, despite their presence, it was ChaosBringer who commanded attention.
His makeup was flawless—a pristine canvas of dark lines and sharp angles accentuated his angular face. His regal, dark robes billowed slightly in the faint breeze, and his golden pauldrons caught the light with every movement.
He walked with a practiced grace, his sharp eyes scanning the soldiers, occasionally pausing to scold one who dared slouch even slightly.
But the moment ChaosBringer caught sight of Leo approaching, all that composed grandeur seemed to crumble away.
In one fluid motion, ChaosBringer dropped to his knees and then fully prostrated himself on the crimson carpet, his forehead touching the ground, as his voice trembled with reverence.
"My lord, my ruler, rightful master of this Empire," ChaosBringer said, his voice carrying across the silent ranks of soldiers. "Your loyal servant has awaited your arrival with bated breath. The throne of StrongHaven City is yours, as it was always destined to be. I beg your forgiveness for making you wait even a moment longer for your crown."
The silence that followed was profound. Thousands of soldiers watched, holding their breath, awaiting Leo's response.
Dumpy let out another croak—this one almost sounding…judgmental.
Leo stepped forward, his boots sinking slightly into the plush carpet. His piercing gaze falling upon ChaosBringer, who still hadn't lifted his head.
"Rise, ChaosBringer," Leo said, his voice calm but firm. "You've done well. Better than most could have managed. Be proud of what you achieved here."
ChaosBringer's shoulders visibly relaxed as he slowly rose to his feet, though he kept his head slightly bowed in deference.
"Thank you, Lord Boss. Today, all of this—all of StrongHaven City—stands as a testament to your vision. Please… the throne awaits you."
Leo allowed himself a small smirk as he walked past ChaosBringer, his black robe trailing behind him as he stepped further onto the grand carpeted path.
The crowd of soldiers erupted in synchronized chants.
"LORD BOSS! LORD BOSS! LORD BOSS!"
"EMPEROR! EMPEROR! EMPEROR!"
The sound thundered through the ruined streets of StrongHaven City, shaking stone and stirring ash.
With Dumpy hopping dutifully beside him and ChaosBringer falling into step just a pace behind, Leo began his procession toward the fortress—the throne of StrongHaven awaiting him at the end of the path.
"First Brigade, Salute your EMPEROR on my command, 3…2…1… GO!"
*THUD*
*SWOOSH*
As Leo covered a miniscule distance of 20 meters, the captain of the first Brigade demanded that his brigade salute their emperor, and as asked, the soldiers all stomped their right foot and unsheathed their weapons to create a guard of honor for where Leo walked.
A soft smile spread on Leo's face, watching this greeting, as this was a scene straight out of a cliche movie that he never expected to repeat in real life.
It was every man's dream to become King one day, however, not many got to experience it.
"Second Brigade, Salute your EMPEROR on my command, 3..2…1…. Go!"
*THUD*
*SWOOSH*
As Leo walked another few meters, the second Brigade saluted him, and it was at that point that Leo realized that the saluted was going to be a recurring theme until he reached the throne room.
Chaosbringer had not only arranged for the red carpets and the soldiers to wait on him, but he had also organised the chants and the salutes, as he tried his hardest to ensure that Leo's coronation was as memorable as possible.
"Nice…" Leo muttered, as although externally, he remained impassive, only nodding at the captains who saluted him in acknowledgement.
However, internally he had already turned into a ball of mush, his intense blush only hidden by his mask, as the fact that he was going to be 'Emperor' finally sunk in.
There were over two hundred and fifty million players from his batch of the Arc Ship alone in the world of Terra Nova, and Leo could confidently say that each and every one of them would trade places with him in a heartbeat if the opportunity presented itself.
However, despite the sheer millions that played this game, it was only him who was going to ascend to the throne of Unity Empire at the end, a milestone that could help cement his legacy as the greatest player alive.

chapters.title: Chapter 768 - 768: Taking The Throne
chapters.content:
Leo's march towards the Unity Palace was unforgettable.
Every brigade captain, from the first division to the 180th, saluted him as he made his way to the palace. At the end of the procession, citizens from the slums and the downtrodden lined the streets with banners and flowers in hand, their faces alight with hope and joy.
"Lord Boss, please fix the plumbing in the slums!"
"Lord Boss! We're so happy to see you assume the throne!"
"Long live the Emperor! May your rule bring us into the golden age!"
The commoners cheered for him wholeheartedly, their voices filled with a desperate longing for change. They wanted him to lead them into a new era, and their unexpected love for him genuinely baffled Leo.
He had half-expected the common populace to hate him after everything he had done. Yet here they were, showering him with adoration. At least a few, it seemed, still appreciated him.
As Leo reached the Unity Palace gates—the very place where, not too long ago, he had committed the massacre of a lifetime—the scene that unfolded before him was anything but grim.
Flowers of every imaginable color blanketed the gates, forming a vibrant, fragrant carpet that rivaled even the red velvet path he had just walked. The scent of lilies, roses, and wildflowers mingled with the cool morning air, their petals scattered by gentle breezes.
Garlands adorned the statues in the garden, each one a symbol of the rebels' hope and reverence for their new ruler.
To Leo, however, they were mere opulence. He had no care for flowers or their natural beauty, and so the effort, while elaborate, felt mostly wasted on him.
As he approached the palace gates, the atmosphere shifted dramatically.
The disciplined, stoic presence of soldiers faded, replaced by an entirely different kind of reception. Lining the grand entrance and stretching into the palace's opulent halls were countless women, each more dazzling than the last.
Clad in silken dresses and adorned with glittering jewelry, they greeted him with exuberance. Their voices, soft yet enticing, rose in a chorus of cheers and playful giggles.
"Lord Boss, welcome!"
"Your Majesty, you look so dashing today!"
Some cast him bashful glances, their cheeks flushed with anticipation. Others, more daring, leaned forward to accentuate their curves. A few pressed their hands against their chests, squeezing just enough to highlight their cleavage, hoping to catch his eye. The air grew thick with their perfume—a heady mix of jasmine, roses, and exotic spices—creating an intoxicating haze.
Leo couldn't help but laugh at the extravagance of it all, his deep chuckle reverberating through the corridor. But his stride remained steady and focused. He paid them no heed, his sharp gaze fixed ahead. Beside him, Dumpy hopped with an air of indifference, while ChaosBringer followed closely, his expression a mix of pride and nervousness.
"ChaosBringer," Leo said, his tone laced with amusement. "Did you organize this little spectacle as well?"
ChaosBringer hesitated, his painted face twitching slightly. "I... thought it would be a fitting tribute to your greatness, Lord Boss."
Leo chuckled again. "I already have a woman," he clarified, his attention already shifting back to the grand hallway ahead.
The procession of beauties continued to cheer and swoon, but none succeeded in breaking his composed demeanor.
Finally, the massive double doors of the throne room loomed before him. As they swung open, revealing the vast chamber within, the chaos of the outside world faded, replaced by an almost reverent silence.
The throne room was cavernous, its high ceilings and polished floors already scrubbed clean of the bloodstains Leo had left behind during his last visit.
The room was nearly empty, save for the topmost leaders of the rebellion. They stood in a semicircle near the base of the dais, their heads bowed low in deference. Each represented a pillar of the Uprising's strength—strategists, warriors, and diplomats who had worked tirelessly to bring this moment to fruition.
Leo's gaze moved past them, drawn to the throne itself. It sat atop a raised platform, an imposing seat carved from a single block of black marble veined with streaks of gold. Its high back was crowned with the symbol of the phoenix, its wings outstretched as if in flight.
For a moment, Leo stood still, his eyes fixed on the throne. A faint smile played on his lips as he let the gravity of the moment wash over him. This was what he had worked for—what he had fought for. The throne of the Unity Empire was finally his.
Taking a deep breath, he strode forward, each step echoing through the silent hall. ChaosBringer and Dumpy remained at a respectful distance, watching as their leader approached the culmination of their efforts.
As Leo reached the base of the throne, he paused. He turned to face the gathered leaders, his piercing gaze sweeping over them before finally ascending the steps. Each movement was deliberate, calculated, as though he were savoring the significance of every second.
At last, he stood before the throne. Placing a hand on its armrest, he felt the cold, smooth surface beneath his fingers. Closing his eyes for a brief moment, he inhaled deeply, letting the weight of the moment settle into his bones.
Then, with a calm, confident motion, he lowered himself onto the seat.
The room held its breath.
And then, with a resonating chime, the system spoke.
[Global Notification: - The Unity Throne has been claimed by player 'TheBoss.'
He is now the Fifth Emperor of the Unity Empire.
Congratulations to player 'TheBoss.']
The notification rippled through the world of Terra Nova, flashing across the interface of every player, no matter where they were. A hush fell over the game's countless regions as players paused to process the news.
In the throne room, the leaders dropped to their knees in unison, their voices ringing out in a chant.
"All hail Emperor Boss! Long live the Emperor!"
Leo leaned back in the throne, one hand resting on the armrest as his other gently scratched Dumpy's head. A smirk tugged at the corners of his lips as he surveyed the flood of notifications on his screen.

chapters.title: Chapter 769 - 769: Assuming Command
chapters.content:
[Global Notification: - The Unity Throne has been claimed by player 'TheBoss.'
He is now the Fifth Emperor of the Unity Empire.
Congratulations to player 'TheBoss.']
[System Notification:- Congratulations player 'TheBoss' for assuming the Unity Empire throne. You currently control 55% of the once established boundary.
Please strive towards bringing all unity territories under your rule. ]
[System Notification:- You have completed one of the game's core quests 'Become The Emperor' ….. calculating rewards]
[System Notification:- integrating the Empire Wide panel, to your gaming screen. You can now make policy decisions and issue quests that will effect the entire Empire. ]
A series of notifications flashed before Leo's eyes the moment he assumed the Unity Throne, which came as a welcome distraction to his rapidly pulsing heart.
The Emperor's seat felt oddly comfortable to sit in. It was tilted at an angle where it not only provided excellent back support but also made him seem casually disinterested in everything happening in the courtroom below.
'I only control a meagre 55% of the established boundaries? Well that's not wrong since, I am yet to officially control the North and West, but still, it dampens the mood slightly' Leo thought, as he closed the first system notification tab and focused on the next.
'The rewards? I hope you give me something more than just the MP promised….' Leo thought, as seeing how the system was still calculating what he should get, he swiped it away too.
[System Notification :- The imperial panel is now available for use.]
The third system notification seemed the most interesting, as when Leo tapped on the imperial panel and called it up, he got access to a plethora of information he was previously unaware of.
[ The Unity Empire Overview: ]
Territory Controlled: 55% of the former Unity Empire's boundaries.
Capital: StrongHaven City (New Seat of Power).
Population: Approx. 218.5 million (inclusive of only NPCs under controlled regions).
Military Strength:
Active Military: 32 million troops.
Reserves: 2.1 million troops.
Special Forces: 120,000.
Economy:
Treasury: 150 Billion Gold coins + Countless treasures.
Tax Rate: 15% across controlled territories.
Trade Agreements: None (All existing agreements nullified post-uprising).
Political Stability: Low (Loyalty of the populace divided between rebels and remnants of loyalist factions).
---
[ Imperial Commands Available: ]
1. Legislative Actions:
Adjust tax rates.
Create new laws or revoke old ones.
2. Military Operations:
Issue deployment orders.
Mobilize troops for specific campaigns.
3. Diplomatic Initiatives:
Initiate peace talks.
Declare war or alliances.
4. Empire-Wide Policies:
Assign empire-wide quests to players.
Set development priorities (e.g., infrastructure, military, economy).
---
[ Immediate Notifications: ]
Northern Territories Report: Opportunistic Guilds not allied to rebels or previous imperial factions are seizing territory for themselves.
Western Frontier: Reports of rogue factions attempting to claim independent control over key cities.
Economic Alert: Treasury funds insufficient for large-scale infrastructure projects.
—--------
Leo studied the interface with growing intrigue. The depth of control the imperial panel provided was astonishing, and the potential for gameplay mechanics seemed endless.
With just a flick of his wrists he could potentially issue an Empire wide quest for all players to take part in, or change the tax rate for all NPC to bear and face little to no consequences for his actions.
"Is this what absolute power feels like?" Leo muttered under his breath, as his eyes rolled over to the active military section.
The active military—32 million troops—was now his to command. This included soldiers who had, just a day ago, been fiercely defending the Unity Empire against him and his rebels.
"How…?" Leo muttered, leaning forward slightly in his throne. The absurdity of the situation struck him like a bolt of lightning.
In any real-world setting, such a shift would be unthinkable. Soldiers, commanders, and generals didn't simply lay down their weapons and swear fealty to the man they had been trying to kill mere hours ago. The grudges, the bitterness, the memories of betrayal—those didn't vanish overnight.
But here, in the game world, things were different. The moment he claimed the throne, it was as though the system had flipped a switch, erasing the barriers of loyalty and allegiance. The imperial forces, bound by the game's mechanics, were now his. Their unwavering resistance had melted away the instant he became Emperor.
He opened the military interface with a flick of his wrist, the details filling his vision.
---
[Active Military - Unity Empire Forces]
Infantry: 22 million
Cavalry: 7 million
Siege Units: 2.8 million
Aerial Units: 100,000
Naval Forces: 100,000
[Special Forces - Unity Empire Elite]
Vired Corps: 50,000 (Stealth operatives, assassins, and saboteurs)
Arcane Guard: 30,000 (Elite battle mages)
Iron Vanguard: 40,000 (Heavy armor specialists and shock troopers)
---
The Unity Empire military mostly consisted of infantry and cavalry troops that were best suited for land warfare.
About 70% of these troops were deployed along the borders, to thwart the demon threat, while only 30% were stationed inland, with less than 1% being in the capital.
The Unity Navy was more or less a joke, with only 100,000 active personnel whose main job was to ensure that pirates did not rob merchant ships floating from east to west and back.
The Aerial Units were useful but mostly deployed along the Northern boundary where they performed scouting duties and carried out tactical raids against the demons on rocky terrains.
More or less 97% of the active military was tied up in active duty roles, leaving Leo with only about 3% of the forces and the special forces that he could call upon to complete personal missions.
The Virex Corps, the infamous imperial dogs could help him hunt and punish any individual player he disliked, whereas, the arcane guard and iron vanguard could be used to bully small-time guilds.
'Oh I love this…' Leo thought, as although the Unity Empire Military wasn't as good as he hoped it would be, with the soldiers already ready to accept his command as their Emperor, he had no other complaints.
—------

chapters.title: Chapter 770 - 770: Reactions
chapters.content:
(Meanwhile the global forums)
The reactions on the global forums to Leo becoming the Emperor were quite wild, despite most anticipating this day to come sooner or later.
"TheBoss is now the Emperor, does this mean he has unrestricted access to the royal treasury? I wonder what types of treasures are in there…. I guess this automatically makes 'TheBoss' the richest player, even richer than Leo Skyshard the number one merchant"
"TheBoss has reached the pinnacle of gaming. Imagine being the Emperor of a game millions of players play. He's truly beyond exceptional"
"Nah…. Someone ban 'TheBoss' from the game. His success is honestly too demoralizing for the rest of us. I won't even be surprised if he kills the Demon King next and annexes the whole continent…. That man is mad, he might just do it"
"Will 'TheBoss' actually work to restore stability in the region? Without the NPC of the kingdom issuing quests and with the supply routes for merchants overrun, the whole economy is in shambles. There's no steady supply of goods and it's hard to level up. I hope he addresses such problems and is not just focused on enjoying the game for himself"
"The uprising are the new rulers? Is it time to quit the game?"
"Man, I wish I could go back in time and become best friends with 'TheBoss'. He has the biggest golden thighs of this game"
"Did anyone else notice the beauties squeezing their boobs for 'TheBoss' when he was on his way to the throne? The man did not even spare them a glance, but quite a few of them were tens"
"The dark age of gaming begins today…. The most vile man is not the Emperor"
"Terra Nova Online is a biased game, the gameplay does not allow players with more spiritual and intellectual tendencies to shine.
It's all about who has the biggest fist–"
"The Boss is the new law of the land… and we have no clue, what he can and can't do…. Can he imprison millions of players for dissent? Can he appoint nobles and give away land as he pleases? Nobody knows but him"
The players debated the future intensely.
Some were happy that 'TheBoss' became the new Emperor, others were curious as to what his newfound powers meant, while a select few were unhappy, and they vented by writing long rants on the forums to feel better for themselves.
*************
(Meanwhile Jacob)
Jacob was quite proud of Leo for becoming the next Emperor, albeit within the game world.
As a father he derived the greatest joy from watching his children succeed in life and lately, Leo and Luke gave him no reasons to complain.
Leo had already reached the pinnacle of what one could within the game world, while Luke was following quickly behind.
In his recent fight against DarkEmperor, Luke had defeated the number 2 ranked player with ease, which made Jacob quite proud of his achievements.
Although he was a father who had minimal role in watching his children bloom into the flowers they became today, he still felt satisfaction knowing that they were poised for a better life than one he could have ever given them if he stayed at home.
"I'll always continue watching over you both from the shadows…. Help in whatever small way I can–" He murmured, as now that Leo was Emperor, he made his new goal to eliminate any anti-emperor sentiments and rebel movements that would arise in the coming days.
************
(Meanwhile Luke and PinkLotus)
Luke and PinkLotus were both back in the abandoned forest, at their usual training spot near the waterfall when the system notification for Leo becoming Emperor flashed past their screens.
"About time…" Luke muttered looking at the notification, while PinkLotus only smiled faintly, as she paused her training for a while.
Both of them, just like millions of other players, already knew that this day was going to come sooner or later, however, unlike weebs who watched the whole livestream, they only became aware of the phenomenon once the global notification rang out.
"Your brother keeps shattering new records every month…. At this point I think over 80% of all global announcements have been triggered by him and him alone" PinkLotus said, as Luke gave her a proud smile.
"Well, I guess I raised him right" Luke replied, sticking his tongue out, as PinkLotus burst into a joyous laughter.
Their relationship had taken a slight turn on their way back from Bernebau city, as while on the road, the two awkwardly held hands at first before slowly growing comfortable to one another's touch.
Both blushed hard after their first contact, which took Luke a lot of courage to make. However, once they did intertwine their fingers, neither pulled away, even as their palms grew sweaty and clammy from hours of contact.
It was on the third evening of their journey back to the training spot when it finally happened.
The sun was setting, casting golden hues over the dense forest path, and the air was warm with the faint hum of cicadas. PinkLotus had tripped over an exposed root in the path, and Luke instinctively caught her before she fell, their faces suddenly inches apart.
For a moment, neither moved, the world around them fading into nothingness. Luke's heart hammered in his chest as he stared into her eyes which looked seductive and inviting.
PinkLotus's breath hitched, her lips slightly parted as if caught mid-thought.
"I... uh—" Luke stammered, his voice barely above a whisper.
But PinkLotus smiled, her usual composed demeanor giving way to something more vulnerable. "You're not going to make me do all the work, are you?" she teased, her voice soft and playful.
Luke's cheeks burned, but he didn't pull away this time. Summoning every ounce of courage, he leaned in, his lips brushing against hers in a kiss that was as awkward as it was sweet. It lasted only a moment, but it felt like an eternity—a perfect, fleeting eternity.
When they pulled apart, both of them were flushed, avoiding each other's eyes for a few beats before PinkLotus broke into a giggle. "That… wasn't so bad," she said, her smile radiant.
Luke chuckled nervously, rubbing the back of his neck. "Yeah… I guess I didn't mess it up too badly."
PinkLotus reached out, intertwining her fingers with his once more. "Not bad at all," she replied, her voice warm and reassuring.
From that moment on, the journey back to the waterfall felt lighter, their stolen glances and shared laughter making every step memorable. Their first kiss, though unplanned, had left a mark neither would soon forget.
Now, although they had not made their relationship official, they were close to doing so, with both having admitted how they felt for one another.

chapters.title: Chapter 771 - 771: The new regent
chapters.content:
(ChaosBringer's POV)
ChaosBringer's eyes shimmered with tears of joy as he watched Leo ascend to the throne.
For most, this moment was a defining victory for the Uprising, but for ChaosBringer, it was the culmination of a grueling journey filled with relentless toil and sacrifice.
No one else truly understood the blood, sweat, and tears it had taken ChaosBringer to place a man on the throne, for only he carried the full weight of what he had endured in silence.
The first six months of the Uprising had been the darkest. Membership was sparse, and with no funds to offer salaries or incentives, keeping the group afloat had felt like an impossible dream.
But everything changed during the Grand Tournament. ChaosBringer had bet everything—every coin, every ounce of hope—on 'TheBoss' winning, and his bet paid off big time.
He won every bet he placed, yielding a fortune beyond expectation, and that became the turning point in the Uprising's history.
The influx of money breathed new life into the struggling rebellion, allowing it to expand and solidify its presence.
The next pivotal milestone was the capture of their first viscounty, an achievement that finally put them on the map, garnering interest from 'TheBoss', who joined their ranks officially.
As from then on, the Uprising's growth was meteoric.
With 'TheBoss' spearheading campaigns, the ragtag group of rebels transformed into a formidable force.
What had started as a desperate movement became the empire's most feared rebellion—a juggernaut capable of toppling the throne itself, and today that dream had been realized, with 'TheBoss' finally assuming the throne.
ChaosBringer's pride swelled as he stood in the throne room, knowing every step of the arduous journey had led to this moment of triumph, as although the history books would probably not remember his role in this campaign, he knew without a shadow of a doubt, that he was the kingmaker behind TheBoss's reign.
"ChaosBringer, come here—" Leo said, calling him to the throne, as for a moment, ChaosBringer felt utterly confused by the summon.
Leo had only assumed the throne a mere few moments ago and ChaosBringer expected him to do something grand, or hold a big speech, but he did not.
Instead, he gestured for ChaosBringer to approach the throne, which made ChaosBringer's heart nervously skip a beat.
*Gulp*
Gulping, he nervously walked towards the throne, standing one step beneath the level where the throne was, as he bowed his head in respect.
"How may I serve you? My Lord?" ChaosBringer asked, as Leo simply gestured towards the seat of the prime minister in the room.
"I'm appointing you as my regent, you will have complete authority over the Empire and shall answer to no-one but me.
I'm an assassin not a ruler and I don't know the first thing about running an Empire, nor do I have any interest in running it.
Becoming the Emperor was a personal project, but now that I've achieved it, I don't really care for it" Leo muttered, as with a flick of his finger, he appointed ChaosBringer as his regent, transferring him countless powers to rule the Empire.
ChaosBringer stood frozen, his eyes wide as the faint hum of magic filled the air.
Before him, a glowing screen materialized—its shimmering interface displaying the Empire's vast resources, military divisions, economic controls, and countless other tools of governance.
The very same panel that Leo had access to now rested in ChaosBringer's hands, a symbol of his newfound authority as regent.
For a moment, he couldn't move. The weight of what had just been bestowed upon him pressed down like an iron mantle.
The rights to control the Empire—the military, the treasury, the laws—were his to exercise. With a flick of his fingers, he could raise armies, alter tax laws, or issue decrees that would ripple across the land.
He swallowed hard, his gaze flicking between the glowing screen and Leo's calm, almost dismissive expression.
ChaosBringer's voice trembled as he spoke, his usual dramatic flair taking on an almost reverent tone. "M-My Lord… This... this is too much. You trust me with this? With everything?"
Leo waved a hand dismissively. "You've earned it, ChaosBringer. More than anyone else. Besides, you're the only one I trust to do this right. I'm not cut out for ruling; you are."
The simplicity of Leo's statement struck ChaosBringer harder than any battlefield blow ever had. His knees buckled, and before he could stop himself, he dropped to the floor, his forehead touching the cold marble in a deep bow.
"My Lord, my Emperor… I am unworthy of such trust, but I swear upon my very soul, I will not fail you," ChaosBringer declared, his voice thick with emotion. "From this day forth, your will is my law, your vision my purpose. I will carry your Empire to heights never before seen, or I will die trying."
Tears streamed freely down his face as he looked up at Leo, his expression a mixture of awe and fierce determination. "You have given me a new purpose in life, my Lord. I will never betray your faith, no matter what trials come. I swear it."
Leo's lips twitched into a faint smirk. "Good. Now get off the floor. Show some spine as my regent, your weakness sullies my name."
ChaosBringer stood, his hands trembling slightly as he reached out to the glowing screen before him.
