The interface responded to his touch, the options and controls dancing beneath his fingers like a living thing. As he began to familiarize himself with its features, his confidence swelled, mingling with the unwavering loyalty that now burned brighter than ever in his chest.
"This Empire," ChaosBringer muttered, his voice steadying, "will be the greatest the world of Terra Nova has ever seen. I will make sure of it."
"Good. Because I've got other, more important things to do." Leo declared as he stood up, and without another word strode out of the throne room, leaving ChaosBringer alone with the tools of power.
It was a responsibility ChaosBringer had not imagined in a million years.
He never expected to be appointed regent, but because Leo did appoint him, his loyalty towards Leo skyrocketed and became unshakeable.
'Come what may… I will never betray your trust' ChaosBringer thought, as he made a resolve to never betray Leo, even if it cost him his life.

chapters.title: Chapter 772 - 772: I am the best
chapters.content:
Dumpy followed Leo outside the throne room, hopping with a big smile on his face.
"We are never returning to this place ever again are we? Lord Father?" Dumpy inquired, as Leo glanced silently towards his pet, before breaking into a big smile.
"Most likely… yes–" Leo said, as Dumpy began to snicker and laugh.
This was the Lord Father he knew and respected.
Everyone else in the world might strive to be Emperor.
Might dream of the day they ascended the throne, but for Lord Father it was but another mundane achievement.
"Might I interest Lord Father in some of the beauties waiting for you outside these halls? In my understanding there are quite a few who are plump and ready to plant your seed in" Dumpy asked, as Leo chuckled out loud.
"Come here–" Leo said, slowing his pace, as he allowed Dumpy to hop beside him, their pace now in sync.
"Listen carefully Dumpy, for its a life lesson I will probably never be able to teach you again….." Leo muttered in a low-tone, as Dumpy listened with his ears perked up.
"Things like women…. Politics… Kingdom management…. Even merchant stuff…. It's all best left for spineless men who can never hope to be the ultimate warrior.
However, if your goal is to be the ultimate warrior, then you should focus on one thing and one thing only, which is your own strength" Leo said, as he rubbed Dumpy on his head and patted him on his back.
"Men like you and me, we are born to fight. Not to be tied down to one seat.
Today, it doesn't matter if I appoint ChaosBringer as my regent, or his sister…. If they betray me I can seize the throne with my own power, as even if the world is against me, I have the confidence to win against the world all alone.
It's a cocky way to live. You might even say, I've become too full of myself, but I can no longer put on the facade of humility.
At Least not in front of you.
I am the best, and I'm not shy to admit it.
The world fears me and I say they should.
I've worked hard to be feared, and I'll be damned if I let some throne cage me while I'm still in my prime" Leo whispered, as with a final pat to the back he pulled away from Dumpy, letting him digest the words he just spouted in silence.
'He is the best….' Dumpy thought, smiling wildly, as that thought made him feel warm and fuzzy in his heart.
For him, his Lord Father was always the strongest, but hearing him admit that felt satisfying on more levels than one.
'That's right… we can't be caged by a stupid throne! We were born to roam and terrorize the world. Me, Lord Father and Lord Grandfather are warriors. We belong on the battlefield' Dumpy concluded, as he followed Leo with his chest filled with pride.
This was a defining moment in his life, a lesson he was never going to forget for as long as he lived.
From this moment onwards, his life's goal was to become the ultimate warrior just like his Lord Father, while everything else faded to the background.
**********
(Real World, the Arc Ship, Sector B, ChaosBringer's POV)
Just as ChaosBringer logged out of the game, he was surprised to see three unexpected guests sitting in his apartment, seemingly waiting for him on his dining table.
Watching their relaxed demeanor and elvish features, ChaosBringer immediately discerned their identity to be the ship operators. However, seeing them intrude his living quarters this way, felt surprising nonetheless.
"Player ChaosBringer…. I'm the Captain of this ship, Captain Kid. It's a pleasure to meet you" Kid said, gesturing for ChaosBringer to take a seat, which ChaosBringer accepted with grace.
"Please make yourself at home, Captain, although I see you're already using my utensils and supplies, do let me know if you need anything else" ChaosBringer said, as he looked towards the coffee cups that Raven and Raya had in hand.
*Cough*
Coughing slightly, Raya blushed pink, taking a sip from the cup shyly.
This was all technically ship property, and not the passengers, but it still felt awkward to be called out for it.
If it were any other man, they would have felt flushed to see Raya blush before them, however, her charm had no effect on ChaosBringer, who looked at her with nothing but apathy in his eyes.
'Dirty Bitch…' ChaosBringer thought, containing his anger, as he patiently waited for Captain Kid to discuss business.
"ChaosBringer, you've been appointed regent by 'TheBoss', which has given you unprecedented access in shaping the future of the game world.
It's quite a milestone and we wish to congratulate for it–" Kid began, as ChaosBringer accepted the compliment and nodded curtly at the Captain's words.
"It's indeed a matter of great personal pride for me that Lord Boss has appointed ME as regent…. I will not fail him" ChaosBringer said, as at that moment, Captain Kid awkwardly exchanged glances with Raven and Raya.
"Well, we are here today to ask you to do exactly that. We wish to offer you an opportunity to become a double agent and for that, we will offer you unprecedented benefits.
You just need to secretly sabotage the hold of the rebels over the Empire and help the righteous faction take back control of the throne.
And for your services, we will shower you with MP, money, real life benefits, information packs and pretty much anything that you desire" Raven suggested, as for a moment the atmosphere in the room became incredibly tense.
No one could predict how ChaosBringer would respond to the offer, and while they hoped he would accept it, allowing the Unity Government on Terra Nova to finally ease its grip on their throats, nothing was certain until he signed the papers.
They had offered him open terms… he could get anything he desired as long as he became a double agent, and Captain Kid felt certain that only a fool would reject such an offer.
A fool that they knew ChaosBringer was not.

chapters.title: Chapter 773 - 773: An offer no-one can refuse
chapters.content:
"And for your services, ChaosBringer, we will shower you with MP, money, real life benefits, information packs and pretty much anything that you desire—" Raven suggested, as an awkward silence enveloped the room.
9/10 players were never going to refuse an offer like this, and it was precisely this knowledge about human nature that prompted the Unity Government back on planet Terra Nova, to come up with this plan.
They had forced Leo to appoint a regent in their last agreement, precisely because of this knowledge about human nature, as according to their calculations, Leo was either going to appoint a regent from his family, or from the top leadership of the uprising.
If he appointed a family member as regent, the unity government intended to exploit that decision to create gaps within the uprising, to sow discord and unhappiness amongst top management and somehow rotting the organization from the inside out.
And If he did not. They intended to turn the uprising leader he appointed as regent into a double agent, and have him betray Leo's trust in the end.
It was a full-proof plan, with little to no chance of failure, however, unfortunately, they picked the wrong man to turn on Leo.
"So let me get this straight…." ChaosBringer began, his voice emotionless as he pointed out the facts.
"You want me to betray my lord's trust and not run the Empire to match his vision, but rather run it to match yours? Is that what you're asking from me?" ChaosBringer asked, as Raya nodded fervently in reply.
"Exactly, that's precisely what we want you to do," Raya confirmed, her voice steady and sure while her eyes gleamed with barely concealed excitement.
"I see…" ChaosBringer said, leaning back in his chair, as he crossed his arms over his chest.
A slow, almost lazy smile began to creep across his face, as though he were savoring some private joke.
For a while he said nothing, but only glanced at his shining nails, before eventually tilting his head from side to side as he let his gaze linger on each of the three ship operators.
"Anything I want for a reward, correct? Inside or outside the game?" he repeated, his voice soft, teasing, almost indulgent.
"Anything," Raya replied without hesitation, leaning forward slightly, her expression serious. "Whatever you desire. Money, MP, real-world privileges—whatever it takes. You name it, and it's yours."
ChaosBringer's lips quirked into a wider smile, his fingers tapping rhythmically on the armrest of his chair. "That's quite the offer."
Captain Kid nodded, his demeanor confident and his tone smooth. "Indeed. It's not just an offer; it's a golden opportunity. One that few would even consider refusing."
ChaosBringer chuckled softly, his painted eyes glinting with amusement. "It would take a special kind of fool to refuse something like this, wouldn't it?" he said, his voice light, almost conversational.
Captain Kid grinned, his confidence bolstered. "Precisely. We're glad you understand the gravity of what's on the table. With your intellect and skill, you're exactly the kind of person we want for this."
The tension in the room seemed to ease, the ship operators exchanging subtle glances that betrayed their growing certainty.
ChaosBringer appeared to entertain their proposal, his thoughtful expression and deliberate movements lending an air of seriousness to the discussion, as he seemed to be genuinely interested.
Rising from his seat with deliberate grace, ChaosBringer stretched, rolling his shoulders as though shedding the weight of responsibility. He paced toward the edge of the room, his steps slow, measured. Every movement seemed calculated to draw out the moment, heightening the anticipation in the air.
"So, let me get this straight," he said, his tone measured and contemplative, as though he were truly weighing the gravity of their offer. "You're saying I could have riches, power, influence—everything I've ever dreamed of—just by agreeing to this arrangement?"
"Exactly, you just have to say yes here and sign a contract" Raven interjected eagerly, his confidence growing with every passing second.
ChaosBringer turned to face them, his hands gripping the back of his chair lightly, his painted nails tapping against the polished wood. His expression remained pensive, thoughtful.
"And all it would take," he continued, his voice dropping slightly, "is for me to sabotage the empire. Betray my lord—the man who entrusted me with his vision, his empire, and his trust. Is that the price?"
For a brief moment, the operators faltered, but Captain Kid quickly stepped in, his tone smooth and practiced. "It's not betrayal," he said, his voice calm and persuasive. "It's strategy. Ensuring stability for the future. A way to secure your place at the top while—"
ChaosBringer cut him off with a subtle motion of his hand. The smile that spread across his face was not warm or reassuring—it was sharp, glacial. "Ah, I see," he murmured, his voice almost playful. "Only a fool would refuse such a generous offer."
Captain Kid's confidence surged, and he exchanged a knowing glance with his companions. "Precisely. We knew you'd see reason," he said, pulling out a stack of papers for ChaosBringer to sign, as he fumbled to find his pen.
"If you can just sign here…" Captain Kid said, passing the pen to ChaosBringer, however, instead of gripping it, ChaosBringer let the pen fall with a Thud, as the expression on his face darkened.
For a moment, the room was silent save for the soft hum of the Arc Ship's systems. ChaosBringer's expression was unreadable as he studied the trio before him. Then, slowly, his smile began to fade. The amusement in his eyes vanished, replaced by something far colder and infinitely more dangerous.
"But here's the thing," ChaosBringer said, his voice dropping into a deadly monotone. He straightened, his imposing figure casting a long shadow over the table. "I'm not a man who trades loyalty for coins. I'm not someone who forgets who lifted me from the dirt and gave me purpose."
The operators froze, their confidence draining as ChaosBringer's words cut through the room like a blade.
"You think I'd betray him?" he continued, his voice rising slightly, sharp with contempt. "Betray the man who entrusted me with everything he built? The man who trusted me to uphold his vision?"
He leaned forward suddenly, his palms slamming onto the table, making them flinch. "I would rather die," he spat, his painted eyes blazing with fury. "I would rather throw myself into the void than betray my Lord Boss."
The silence that followed was suffocating. ChaosBringer straightened, his gaze piercing as he pointed to the door. "Get out. And don't ever insult me like this again."
Captain Kid, his face pale, nodded stiffly. Raya and Raven hurriedly gathered their things, their earlier confidence shattered. As they scurried out of the room, ChaosBringer's voice followed them, low and filled with icy resolve.
"CHAOSBRINGER'S LOYALTY is NOT for sale. Not now, not ever."
When the door slid shut, ChaosBringer stood alone, his fists clenched at his sides.
Slowly, he turned back to the dining table, staring aimlessly at the empty chairs. His loyalty was unshakable, his purpose clear. For Lord Boss, there was no limit to what he would do—or what he would refuse.
No matter what, ChaosBringer could never betray him. For his trust was worth more to him than any money or reward.

chapters.title: Chapter 774 - 774: The Ploy
chapters.content:
ChaosBringer felt a fuming sense of anger bubble within him once the Arc Ship Operators left.
If they could approach him with such a bullshit offer, they could certainly approach other Uprising members too, corrupting the organisation from the within and trying to make it hollow from the inside out.
'I need to beware of my own members in the future….. there's no need to report this incident to Lord Boss, but I need to be wary of everyone under me from here on out. There could be snakes everywhere' ChaosBringer concluded, as although he did not utter a word, knowing full well that the ankle monitor on him was always listening, he resolved to be wary of everyone in the future, even if they were old friends.
While he did not understand why the ship operators would stoop so low and try to bring down the uprising using such shallow means, he did not need to understand the bigger picture to decide that he did not wish to betray Lord Boss.
For good or bad, ChaosBringer had decided to wholeheartedly serve that man till he died, and that loyalty was unlikely to change.
For him, Lord Boss was a worthy master to serve who was both ruthless and generous at the same time, and hence for ChaosBringer, the greatest joy in life was to make his master proud.
The promise of unlimited money or power could excite other gamers, but for him, only the approval of his master mattered.
**********
(Meanwhile, Raven, Raya and Captain Kid)
The trio walked back to their quarters in utter disbelief after ChaosBringer kicked them out, as this was one outcome they never saw coming.
"Motherfucker baited us…." Raven complained towards the end, as when he retrospected how ChaosBringer acted, he realized that ChaosBringer did not need to indulge them as much as he did if he only wished to reject them towards the end.
But he purposefully baited them into thinking that he was considering their offer, although he had long made up his mind to turn them down.
It was a brutal bait and switch, and the three of them had fallen face first into the trap.
"His loyalty is admirable, but it's going to create a hell lot of headache for the rest of us, as the Unity Government is not going to be happy with ChaosBringer rejecting their offer" Kid said as he massaged his temples, already envisioning the headache that awaited them in the future.
"What I don't understand is why can't the Unity Government take the loss and let the matter be? It's just a game, the Empire toppling within it means nothing much–" Raya complained, as both Kid and Raven sighed at her words.
The three of them already knew the answer to this question, and although Raya complained about it, she knew she was just being dramatic, as in her heart she understood the game as well as the other operators.
Legally, the Unity Government could not prevent the landing migrants on planet Terra Nova to work for any organization that they wanted.
The humans from Earth could hence choose to work for the Unity Government, they could choose to work for their enemies the Demons, or a third party entirely and nobody could prevent the humans from making that choice.
However, out of the 250 million humans that were being transported, less than a million were likely to be actively recruited, while the rest were sure to become low-skilled labor for the Unity Government, bolstering their population numbers.
While in the game Terra Nova Online, the demons were depicted as an evil race and the main opponents of the humans, in reality the demons were not a backward race, consisting only of brain dead warriors, but were a genuine force to be reckoned with, that were both smart and welcoming to strangers.
The Unity Government needed this batch of humans to mostly serve as cannon fodder against the demons in the great ongoing war, which was why they paid the universal government a pretty buck to design the game Terra Nova Online as they did.
The game not only allowed the unskilled humans to evolve into low levelled warriors capable of casting spells and fighting for survival, but also imprinted the image of demons being evil in their minds, which was precisely what the government wanted.
However, what they did not want was for the players to believe that they could topple the Unity Government if they rebelled, or have any hopes of considering rebellion, incase they ever grew unhappy with the government in the future.
While it was still likely that over 90% of all humans landing on Terra Nova, went-on to serve the Unity Government, with all players having witnessed a successful uprising within the game, there was a high chance that they tried to replicate something similar, if they became dissatisfied with the government and their policies, which was exactly why the government was trying to crush the current rebel movement as hard as they did.
The unity government did not want the humans from Earth to believe that 'One Man' could change the outcome of a war, or that a rebel movement could actually topple the status quo someday, and hence they tried to undermine 'TheBoss' and his rebel movement at every turn.
As employees in-charge of the Arc Ship, Captain Kid and his staff had no other choice but to indulge the clients that had hired them to transport and train this batch of migrants, which was why, although they did not approve of their methods on a personal level, they were still forced to carry out their orders regardless.
"Well alright, time to report ChaosBringer's decision to the Unity Government officials and hear them scream profane insults over the headset.
I'll see you both later" Captain Kid said with a heavy smile, as the trio reached the staff area.
"All the best Captain, hold strong" Raven replied, as both him and Raya gave the Captain a proper salute.

chapters.title: Chapter 775 - 775: Catching The Fault
chapters.content:
(One week later)
A week slipped by in the blink of an eye, yet Leo's meditation progress remained frustratingly stagnant compared to his rapid pace ten days prior, leaving him increasingly irritated and uneasy.
Initially, Leo accepted Captain Kid's explanation that stress or overwork might be hindering his ability to meditate effectively. But after a week of thorough rest, avoiding any strenuous training or exercise, he expected a significant improvement in his meditation pace.
When no such improvement occurred, he became convinced that something deeper was at play, and that the issue wasn't merely mental fatigue.
Determined to uncover the root of the problem, Leo began testing various theories.
His first step was to change his meditation location, moving from the designated chamber to his bedroom. The results were immediately clear. Outside the specialized meditation room, his pace dropped to a mere third of his already reduced speed, underscoring the importance of a mana-rich environment for effective meditation.
"Maybe there's a fault in the equipment in my meditation room?" Leo wondered aloud. "Could it be leaking ambient mana?"
To confirm his theory, he decided to try meditating at Amanda's manor one day, and to his surprise, his meditation speed there returned to its normal, accelerated pace.
"So it's definitely an issue with my meditation room," Leo concluded, his thoughts racing.
"I'll have to report this to Captain Kid. The room is still holding mana better than its surroundings, but not well enough." Leo murmured, as he did not suspect any foul play at this stage.
In his mind he found no reason for Captain Kid or any other Arc Ship Operator to knowingly sabotage his training speed and hence he did not think that the reduced mana flow to his chamber was a deliberate conspiracy.
Instead he attributed it to simple mechanical failure and reported the incident as such.
********
(Captain Kid's POV)
As if the chaos caused by ChaosBringer refusing the Unity Government's offer wasn't trouble enough, Captain Kid now faced another dilemma.
A report landed on his desk, stating that Leo had already identified a fault in his meditation equipment and was demanding it to be fixed, as the discovery forced Kid to act swiftly.
Not wanting to risk tarnishing his image before someone as unpredictable as Leo Skyshard, Kid arranged for engineers to be sent to Leo's manor under the guise of routine maintenance.
They then "fixed" the supposed malfunction, while Kid slowly restored the parameters to his room back to normal from the shadows.
Satisfied with the resolution, Leo remained oblivious to the interference.
But for Kid, the situation was far from resolved, as with Leo's meditation room restored, the likelihood of his training pace returning to its usual speed was high—a prospect that created an entirely new set of headaches for him.
Kid had been tasked with keeping Leo's meditation progress in check, and failing to do so could have dire consequences.
Being already under scrutiny from both the Unity and Universal Governments due to his questionable handling of the ship's command, Kid couldn't afford another misstep.
Offending the powerful Mu Clan, his last remaining allies, was a risk he dared not take, as now, more than ever, he needed the Mu clan's support to ensure that the future after his retirement as a captain remained bright.
"The only way to sabotage his training speed now is to go in and steal his meditation manual under the cover of the night.
The only problem is that intruding on that mad man's property is a risk to my life.
That madman will kill me before I even have a chance to yelp, and such a risk can't be taken" Kid concluded, as the only way out of this situation for him seemed to be by stealing the manual.
However, doing so was easier said than done.
Leo Skyshard, the number one player within the game world was an equally formidable fighter outside it as well and Kid had no confidence to win against him in a one vs one fight.
Under normal circumstances, he could have easily delegated such a mission to an underling. However, under universal government laws, theft against passengers was a punishable offence and ordering a subordinate to commit a felony on his behalf also posed a significant risk.
If the underling decided to report him to the ethics committee, Captain Kid could find himself facing the martial court upon landing, and it was a consequence he could not afford to gamble with.
This only left him with the option to do it himself without anyone catching a whiff of his true intentions. However, the timing of the theft needed to be absolutely perfect.
A single misstep could see him lose it all, but it was a risk he was forced to take, for the sake of his own bright future.
"Life is hard… these last few months my trouble seems to be never ending.
I better be compensated fairly for my troubles, because if not, I'll genuinely fall into depression in the coming days".
**********
(Meanwhile Luke)
A fortnight had passed since Luke first kissed Alia, and the two finally formalized their relationship as lovers only today.
Despite being mature adults, they both behaved like scared children when they decided to reveal their relationship to Leo and Amanda, as while the duo was not afraid of Amanda's reaction, they genuinely feared what Leo would say.
"Your brother hates me… HATES, I don't think he will take the news of us dating too well—" PinkLotus said, as she and Luke moved nervously towards Leo's quarters.
"My brother does not hate you, you will be fine…. I'm more worried he will hate me after I declare I love you" Luke replied, as PinkLotus hit him hard on his shoulders.
"Your little brother adores you, you can murder Amanda and he still won't hate you, you're just being silly–" PinkLotus said, as the two tried to uplift each other before breaking the news to Leo.
Both terrified of his potential reaction.

chapters.title: Chapter 776 - 776: Confession Of Love
chapters.content:
Leo was enjoying his alone time with Amanda cooking dinner, when he suddenly heard a knock on his door.
"Come in brother–" he said, half expecting it to be Luke alone, for he had invited him over for dinner tonight, so that the three of them could eat together just like old times.
However, as both Luke and PinkLotus entered his home, Leo raised an eyebrow, half-expecting PinkLotus to challenge him to a fight.
"No, I am in no mood to fight you today. For one you're not strong enough, and for another you have nothing to offer me for my time, as I'm no longer even interested in gaining a favor from you" Leo said, instantly shooting down PinkLotus before she even had a chance to get a word in, as Alia's face darkened at his remark.
"She's not here to fight…" Luke said, covering for his lover, as that statement caused Leo to raise his brow.
"The battle maniac is here to enjoy a simple dinner? Now that's a first….. please make yourself at home" Leo said, as he did not think too much of it and happily invited Amelia to join them for dinner if she wishes to stay.
"Ouch–"
Leo cursed, as he felt Amanda pinching his non-existent belly fat, as she drew his attention to the red faced Luke and Amanda, trying to draw his attention towards the obvious signs that he had missed.
"Leo…. Try to read the room…. At Least look at them before you speak" Amanda said, as she encouraged Leo to drop his focus from the vegetables he was chopping and to redirect it to how Alia and Luke were standing, as just their posture alone told a complete tale.
Both stood quite close to one another, with Alia standing before Luke, her head ending right below Luke's chin.
Luke, also red faced, had his arms placed nervously on Alia's slim waist, as the two clearly seemed intimate with one another.
"Oh?" Leo said at first, his face turning into a frown, as he analysed the implications of such an intimate posture.
However, after the reality sink in, he eased back up, as after a casual shrug of his shoulder, he accepted their relationship readily.
"Congratulations…. I guess?" Leo muttered, sounding unsure, as both Alia and Luke breathed a collective sigh of relief.
Unbeknownst to Leo, both of them seemed to be holding their breaths, waiting for his approval and although it was not a big deal for him, it seemed to mean a world for them.
"OH MY GODD. I CAN'T BELIEVE IT…. CONGRATULATIONS!" Amanda shrieked in joy, as she pushed away Luke and hugged Alia first, leaving Luke to awkwardly scratch his nose as he waited for his turn to be hugged.
"You dog! When did this happen? You have to tell me everything!" Amanda said after a while as she shifted from hugging Alia to hugging Luke, as she seemed genuinely happy for the couple.
"Leo… come hug them!" Amanda demanded, but Leo refused to comply, only giving a double thumbs up from a distance instead.
"I'm good, but I'm happy and all–" he said, before locking eyes with Alia as he tagged her as "Potential Sister In Law".
"You're not mad or anything?" Luke inquired nervously, as Leo shifted his glance between the couple before shrugging once more.
"Nah, why would I be mad? I knew that you liked her for a while now. I just hoped that you did not follow through on it, because I couldn't imagine PinkLotus as the motherly type of woman back then.
However, over time I've realised that she's a pretty nice human being and if you are happy with her then I'm happy for you both.
Hell, I'll even stop insulting her for no reason now that she's family, but it will take me a while to genuinely warm up to her.
But I'll try my best" Leo replied, as his response made Luke chuckle joyously.
This was the first serious relationship of his life and with PinkLotus he genuinely felt like he had hit the lottery.
A master warrior who was the queen of a hundred million hearts, she was genuinely the definition of a princess.
As a man, Luke could not hope to get a better partner, which was why he felt lucky that she loved him back.
On the other hand, PinkLotus found stability and peace in Luke's company, as he felt like an anchor in her life that stabilized her and made life more beautiful for her.
She genuinely enjoyed his company and his charm, and although there were bits she wanted him to improve on, she just took it as an ongoing project, where she hoped to mold Luke into her ideal man.
Overall, the duo were madly in love with one another. With them getting increasingly hanky panky with each other in and out of the game.
However, while they did it sneakily up till now, with them declaring their relationship to Leo, they no longer needed to be discreet about it anymore.
"Are you planning to tell mom about your love affair anytime soon?" Leo asked Luke, who shook his head vehemently from one side to another in response.
"Not yet…. Maybe after we reunite upon landing?" Luke replied as Leo gave him a thumbs up.
They were still in too early of a phase into their relationship to make any public announcements, especially to their mother who was prone to get overly excited about such news.
Leo hence supported Luke's decision to only break the news after a while, once they had spent a considerable time with one another, so that they were sure that they indeed wanted to become each other's better half.
"Hey Leo…. Thanks for accepting my love" Luke said at the end, as although he did not really want to, Leo hugged his elder brother momentarily, patting him on the back.
"Man up brother…. Your girlfriend seriously has more balls than you" Leo replied, as both brothers chuckled out loud.

chapters.title: Chapter 777 - 777: Regrets
chapters.content:
(Game World, Terra Nova Online)
Weeks passed in the game world, and though Leo never returned to oversee his Empire after assuming the throne, ChaosBringer worked tirelessly to manage its affairs in his absence.
ChaosBringer's unwavering dedication ensured that every challenge and loose end was swiftly dealt with, solidifying the Uprising's dominance as the region's rulers and upholding the authority of 'TheBoss.'
One of ChaosBringer's first major actions as regent was formalizing the surrender of the Northern Guilds. This agreement had been negotiated long before the Uprising seized the throne, a strategic move designed to minimize resistance in the Empire's consolidation. However, the guilds' promises remained unofficial until now, leaving room for potential dissent or betrayal.
ChaosBringer ensured there would be no such opportunity, as meeting with the Northern Guilds' representatives in a grand ceremony, he made it clear that reneging on their earlier agreements would not be tolerated.
Under his watchful eye, the guild leaders reaffirmed their loyalty to 'TheBoss,' formally swearing to govern the Northern Territories as vassals of the Empire, and further promising to uphold central law and to only operate within the framework of imperial rule.
By making the northern surrender official, ChaosBringer expanded the Uprising's control over the Empire to 79.3% of the total land, with only the Western region now left to capture.
This swift and decisive action ensured that the transition of power was seamless, leaving no room for uncertainty or rebellion in the hearts of common citizens of the Empire.
As for his second act, ChaosBringer implemented a series of policies to quell dissent and restore normalcy to the war-torn Empire.
Employing a calculated mix of punishment and welfare, he skillfully wielded the carrot-and-stick approach to solidify the Uprising's control over the land, while also gaining the loyalty of its common citizens who did not approve of them much.
The first set of policies targeted NPC rebels and dissenters.
For NPC rebels and law-breakers, ChaosBringer enacted harsh penalties for any acts of insubordination or rebellion, ranging from heavy fines to public trials and, in extreme cases, permanent imprisonment in the prison cells of StrongHaven City.
For players, the penalty was different, punished as direct imprisonment for 6 months, regardless of the crime.
Known NPC noble dissidents were stripped of their lands and titles, their properties redistributed to loyal subjects and friendly rebel guilds who helped the Uprising in their win.
ChaosBringer ensured these punishments were not only severe but also highly visible, sending an unmistakable message that defiance against the Uprising and its rule would not be tolerated.
At the same time, ChaosBringer introduced sweeping reforms aimed at improving the lives of the common people.
Tax rates across the Empire were temporarily reduced to 10%, alleviating the economic burden that months of war had placed on farmers, merchants, and laborers.
Grain prices were subsidized, ensuring no family would go hungry as the Empire rebuilt.
While public works projects, such as rebuilding damaged infrastructure and repairing trade routes, were launched to create jobs and stimulate the economy.
To further win over the populace, ChaosBringer established new social welfare programs, including free medical aid in every major city and scholarships for promising young students to study at previously private imperial academies.
These measures earned him cautious respect from the common folk, who began to see the new regime not as an oppressor, but as a government capable of bringing stability and prosperity.
He also set up an empire-wide bounty system to root out rogue players and previous regime loyalists who were still evading the law, as he allowed citizens to participate in maintaining peace while earning rewards.
These bounties not only reduced the threat of lawlessness but also provided an outlet for adventurers and guilds to integrate into the new system, further strengthening the Empire's hold.
Through these dual strategies, ChaosBringer maintained a delicate balance. By crushing rebellion with an iron fist while simultaneously offering tangible benefits to the people, he left little room for opposition to gain traction. His policies quickly took effect, fostering a sense of order and progress across the Empire.
The results were undeniable. The common citizens, weary of conflict, began to welcome the new regime, while would-be rebels thought twice before challenging the might of the Uprising.
ChaosBringer's calculated efforts ensured that the name of 'TheBoss' was spoken with a mix of fear and respect, as the Empire edged closer to complete unification.
*********
(Meanwhile Cervantez)
Ever since the loss at Bernebau, Cervantez found his life going down in a downward spiral, until he hit a rock bottom today, with 4 of his guild elders resigning all at once.
The cracks within the DarkSky guild first began to show after the humiliating loss at Bernebau, as after that defeat, although the guild did not lose much land, they lost a lot of face.
Fingers were pointed and the blame was passed around on the other for the loss, with many fingers pointing at Cervantez and his inefficient strategy.
Screaming and fights in the guild headquarters became a common sight, and the once cohesive guild that seemed invincible, began to fall like a house of cards, right before Cervantez's eyes.
"It was a mistake to let SkyLion leave, guildmaster, not only was he our strongest individual fighter, but also our chief battle strategist.
We have many other elders in the guild. But his loss was irreplaceable–" Tor told him after the loss, as Cervantez felt his blood boil at the statement.
'Not only was he our strongest individual fighter….' that statement made Cervantez physically buckle over in pain, as he refused to believe that SkyLion was stronger than him, even now.
However, after the comprehensive loss that he faced against him in a one vs one fight, Cervantez eventually accepted that statement as the bitter truth, although he was reluctant to admit it at first.
In hindsight he did realize that letting SkyLion walk away was a massive mistake on his part.
Not only was he a loyal friend, but he was also someone Cervantez could rely blindly to run the guild, and yet he had let him go out of petty ego.
After being chosen as one of the four defenders in the last rankers event, he had began feeling as if he was better than the rest of the masses and that he needed no-one, but that was not the truth.
Luke had been the heart and soul of the guild just as much as him, and if he did not wish to fight against his brother, Cervantez should have supported him, or at least handled the situation better.
The decision to not join the war against the rebels could have been taken by just the two of them without needing to consult the other members, however, Cervantez did not do it because he was desperate to prove his worth to the world.
In his head, he felt like he was playing the game too safe and hence the gap between himself and 'TheBoss' was only widening, and that he needed to do something dramatic to bridge that gap, but he was wrong.
By choosing to gamble it all, he was now losing it all, as he could have become sole the overlord of the West and enjoyed unbelievable prosperity, if only he bent the knee to 'TheBoss', who was an opponent he could not hope to rival anyways.
"I had it all…. The best guild, the best friend, the best opportunity….. but I blew it all away.
A second life was not enough, I might have to re-do this all over again if I want to do it right" Cervantez muttered to himself, as he thought about how, if given the chance to play the game all over again once more, he could definitely become the game's best player this time around.
However, all those regrets were for naught, as facing the resignation of 4 guild elders in Tor, Cola, Lysa and Toni, he could not worry about anything else at the moment.
The White Sabers had been advancing consistently since their win at Bernabeu, and the common members of the DarkSky guild had began to abandon the sinking ship in droves.
Despite the generous benefits that Cervantez had offered them since they joined and despite all the help and nurturing he provided them.
The elites of the game left his guild the moment it began to falter, with most receiving better offers from rival guilds who were happy to poach them.
Cervantez's decision to exclusively recruit elite players had come back to bite him spectacularly, as while they were undeniably powerful assets, they were also notoriously fickle.
With countless guilds eager to poach them, they felt no obligation to remain loyal when the tides turned and that was a fatal flaw for an organization that had extremely limited members to start with.
Their departures weren't personal—they were practical, calculated moves toward greener pastures as for the first time, Cervantez realized the flaw in his approach.
A guild wasn't just built on strength alone. It was built on loyalty, camaraderie, and shared purpose.
By valuing power above all else, he had created a guild of mercenaries, not comrades—and now, he was paying the price for his decisions.

chapters.title: Chapter 778 - 778: A daring move
chapters.content:
(Real World, The Arc Ship, Captain Kid's POV)
Days turned into weeks, and Captain Kid's frustration over Leo's meditation progress continued to mount.
Leo kept progressing steadily in his meditation and with each passing day he seemed to spend more and more time meditating, while rarely taking any breaks to sleep, eat or train outdoors.
Yet, despite his growing desperation, Kid found no viable opportunity to sneak in and steal Leo's manual, as Leo rarely left his residence these days, apart from the few hours of physical training that he conducted daily in the outer grounds just outside his house.
Theoretically it was possible for Kid to try and sneak-in while Leo trained outdoors, however, the timing was too tight.
Kid knew better than to attempt a theft while Leo was still awake and within close proximity, as the risks of such an operation were far too great.
Instead, Captain Kid waited for the day Leo would log back into Terra Nova Online, hoping that Leo's time in the virtual world would provide him with the window he needed.
But to his dismay, Leo showed no intention of returning to the game anytime soon.
With his remaining gaming days severely limited, Leo had no desire to waste a single hour on trivial matters, which was why he never logged in.
Instead, every day was meticulously dedicated to sharpening his skills and pushing his physical and mental limits in the real world, which was a decision that left Kid utterly frustrated.
Time was a luxury that Kid could ill-afford to squander, as every day that Leo trained without interference, he grew closer to becoming a grandmaster, which was an unfavorable outcome for Kid, all things considered.
Leo's progress edged him closer to undergoing a natural genetic awakening, an outcome the Mu Clan was desperate to prevent, as him undergoing awakening with one just a single skill unlocked could potentially reduce his odds of undergoing a full multiple skill awakening in the future, lowering his value as a top fighter to the Mu Clan.
For Captain Kid, failure was not an option.
If he couldn't find a way to sabotage Leo's progress and keep him in check, he risked losing the Mu Clan's patronage—who were his only remaining leverage and protection in this hostile universe.
The very thought of being cast aside by his powerful backers sent a chill down his spine, as Kid knew he could not afford to offend them.
Hence after 2 weeks of inaction, Kid decided that he could not afford to wait much longer.
The stakes were rising fast, and if he did not act soon, he risked finding himself on the losing end of a game that he had no choice but to win.
*********
It was during one of Leo's daily training sessions, where he looked especially focused on training, that Kid decided the moment to finally carry out the heist had come.
With Leo preoccupied and the manor sprawling and isolated, this was as good an opportunity as he was ever going to get, and hence, Kid decided to risk it all.
Steeling himself, Kid left the staff quarters and made his way towards the VIP sector, where he especially chose the route that opened right behind Leo's manor to enter the sector.
His palms were damp, and his heart raced faster with every step he took toward the VIP sector, as although he was not a morally perfect man, he was not a thief either.
Committing a crime made him feel nervous, as he still feared the potential consequences of his action, should he get caught.
A thousand excuses ran through his mind, contingency plans for what he would say if Leo caught him.
As he wondered if he could feign curiosity? claim he was checking on the state of the meditation equipment, or pretend he was delivering a report?
But deep down, Kid knew none of these excuses would hold water, as Leo wasn't the dumb type that could be fooled easily, nor was he the type to easily forgive such intrusions.
The risk was enormous, but failure to act was even worse.
Soon he entered the vip sector, and reached the vicinity of Leo's manor, where he approached the back entrance to Leo's manor with great caution.
His every step was light and deliberated as he approached the manor's back entrance as the vastness of the VIP sector worked in his favor, with its sprawling grounds devoid of people making it easy for him to enter undetected.
With Luke and Amanda logged into the game world, he had no-one else to worry about, as those were the only two people in a wide radius apart from Leo.
*Swoosh–*
As he approached the manor's back-door, the system recognised his access to Leo's quarters and slid open, as although Leo's VIP quarters were off-limits for all other staff members, as the Captain of the ship, he still held entry access to every corner of the ship.
A privilege limited to captain's only.
Inside, the air was cool and quiet, the faint hum of the ship's systems being the only noise he could hear.
Kid moved slowly, using only the toes of his feet, as he tried his best to make as little sound as possible.
The tension in his chest was unbearable at this moment, his ears straining for the slightest sound that might indicate someone was near.
Soon, he slipped through the hallways, his mind racing.
"Don't make a sound. Don't make a sound," he repeated to himself, his movements instinctive and his breathing shallow.
Eventually, as he reached the door to the meditation room, he paused, hand hovering over the handle.
His heart thudded violently, each beat like a drum in the suffocating silence.
Carefully, he turned the knob and pushed the door open just enough to slip inside.
And as soon as he was in there, he spotted the object of his heist, Leo's meditation manual, placed near a low table in the room.
Kid crept forward, his every nerve on edge.
His fingers brushed the cover of the manual, the smooth surface cool to the touch.
For a moment, he hesitated, as though reconsidering the heist at the last second.
But then, with a swift motion, he tucked the manual into the hidden compartment of his jacket, and buttoned it back up, like he did not just commit a crime.
Turning back toward the door, he moved with even more caution, closing it silently behind him.
The weight of the manual felt heavy against his chest, as though it were accentuating his guilt with every step he took, however, Kid suppressed the guilt instantly.
His steps quickened, his body trembling, as his nerves finally started to give way as he made his way out of Leo's manor.
Kid didn't dare linger. The moment his boots hit the soft ground outside, he broke into a sprint, his body moving on pure adrenaline.
Within seconds, he left the back entrance far behind him, the VIP sector stretching out like a lifeline.
"Must be quick—" He muttered, as he did not dare pause until he reached his own quarters, as for a good 12 minutes he sprinted like there was no tomorrow.
"Huff– Huff—"
Once within the safety of his own quarters, Captain Kid slammed the door shut behind him, his chest heaving as he struggled to catch his breath.
He quickly recalled his jog from Leo's manor to the staff quarters, trying to recall if anyone saw him running, but no-one came to mind.
"Nothing unexpected happened…. I'm good for now" he muttered, as with trembling fingers he pulled the meditation manual out of his jacket, its weight feeling far heavier now than when he had first tucked it away.
Then, moving swiftly to his work-desk, Kid pulled open a hidden compartment beneath its surface and placed the manual within, with the hidden compartment locking itself once again, as he pressed a hidden button to the side.
The manual was now secure and completely hidden from prying eyes.
Taking a moment to compose himself, Kid wiped the sweat from his brow with the sleeve of his uniform.
His reflection in the room's polished surface revealed that he now stood with disheveled hair and a flushed face.
If anyone were to see him like this, it would become obvious that something was off, as usually Kid always looked prim and proper and his attire was never out of shape.
And hence, to avoid unnecessary suspicion, Kid grabbed a damp cloth and began tidying his appearance by smoothing his hair and straightening his uniform until he looked as though nothing unusual had happened.
Then, with one last deep breath, Kid stepped out of his quarters and returned to his duties aboard the ship, his expression calm and composed, as he tried to pretend as if everything was normal.
To anyone who saw him, Captain Kid appeared as composed and unremarkable as ever, with nothing to hint at the daring act he had just committed.
But beneath the calm facade, the weight of his actions gnawed at him.
His eyes darted nervously toward the cameras overlooking Leo's training grounds, where Leo continued his drills, seemingly unaware of the heist.
The theft was complete, but the true storm had yet to hit.
For now, Kid was safe as long as Leo remained oblivious to the missing meditation manual. However, the moment Leo discovered the theft, chaos was certain to erupt.
As the Captain of the ship, Kid knew he would inevitably be summoned to investigate the incident. Yet, he felt a twisted sense of reassurance, knowing full well that as the sole individual with access to the ship's surveillance recordings, he held the advantage in the investigation.
The evidence that could convict him was firmly under his control, and with no one else able to review the footage, Kid was confident no one could tie him to the crime—at least for now.

chapters.title: Chapter 779 - 779: Enraged Leo
chapters.content:
Leo felt genuinely perplexed when he returned to his meditation chamber after training, only to find that his meditation manual was missing.
Leo knew he was an absent-minded person who occasionally put the kitchen cutlery in the wrong shelf, however, he knew that he did not misplace the meditation manual, as he never took it out of the meditation room in the first place.
The meditation manual was not a device for portable use like a smartphone, and hence Leo never took it out, making this situation feel extremely bizzare to him.
"What the hell? Where the fuck did my meditation manual go?" Leo wondered out loud, as although he was sure that he had not misplaced it, he still began to search for the manual all around the meditation room and then in his own bedroom.
However, after not finding the manual for half an hour, Leo finally got really frustrated, as he straight up suspected foul play.
"Somebody has got to be fucking with me. It can't be Amanda or Luke, those two will never play such a prank on me…." Leo muttered, as he began narrowing down the list of suspects.
"It can't be anyone from the lower sectors, for the VIP sector is an isolated space. Let alone stealing, they can't even enter this area"
"That leaves PinkLotus and the staff members, who have access to the area.
However, I don't think PinkLotus did it. She's just entered into a relationship with my brother and seems keen to form a good relationship with me.
Also, it goes against her personality to do something so underhanded, which means it's definitely one of the staff members" Leo concluded, as he grit his teeth hard, his bloodlust leaking.
"Elandor is my housekeeper and although he looks polite, I would not clear him of suspicion…."
"Then there's Raya and Raven. Those two talk too much… and although I seem to have a good relationship with them, I still wouldn't put it past them to do something so underhanded–"
"Captain Kid could have done it too, that guy behaves too sly for his own good, and I don't trust him one bit"
"Or it could be someone else entirely who I've never interacted with. Either way, I need this situation resolved as soon as possible.
I cannot meditate without my manual and I cannot risk staying idle" Leo complained, as he stormed out of his house in fury, picking up his training daggers as he marched straight towards the staff quarters.
***********
"ELANDOR! ELANDORRRR—" Leo screamed as soon as he walked out of his manor, as the poor housekeeper, hearing his shouts rushed towards Leo in haste.
"Yes, Sir Leo?" He asked in confusion, as he did not understand the reason behind Leo's apparent rage.
"I've been robbed… Elandor, someone has stolen my meditation manual, you wouldn't happen to know anything about it would you?" Leo asked, as Elandor trembled at the question.
Leo's murderous gaze made him flinch, as although he had nothing to do with the crime, he still felt frightened to face Leo when he was in this mood.
"I– I, I have no idea sir Leo, I don't know anything about it….. Are you sure it's not misplaced within your own manor?" Elandor asked, as Leo tightened his grip on his dagger, his knuckles turning white as he pointed the dagger towards Elandor.
"Do I look like I've not checked my house already, Elandor? DO I LOOK LIKE I AM NOT SURE OF WHAT I'M TALKING ABOUT?" Leo asked, as Elandor began to tremble uncontrollably at his questions.
"I– I, I don't know anything about it, Sir Leo, please believe me…. Theft within the Arc Ship is unprecedented. Every corner of the ship is under surveillance, it would be dumb to even attempt a theft.
And even if theft is attempted, stealing a meditation manual is just plain stupid.
You cannot unbind a meditation manual from its host unless you kill the host, so stealing the manual alone is pointless.
Nobody but you can use that manual to meditate" Elandor explained, as his reasoning left Leo even more enraged.
The idiot who had stolen his manual could not even use it for anything productive, but had still committed the crime just to fuck with Leo, making Leo even more enraged than before.
"Don't you dare lie to me Elandor, because if you do…. It won't end well for you… if you've stolen my manual you can still give it back to me and I will just take it as a bad prank and forgive you.
I promise I won't hurt you, but if I find out later that you had it, I will show no mercy" Leo threatened, as Elandor broke into tears.
"I'm innocent, I have nothing more to say here… and I don't appreciate you suspecting me. I've done nothing but serve you to the best of my abilities Sir–" Elandor replied, as although he was now crying, he maintained a defiant eye contact against Leo.
For a moment, Leo looked into his eyes, trying to see if the housekeeper was lying to him or not, but it did not seem like he was.
There was nothing but honesty in his eyes, which seemed a little hurt that Leo would even suspect him of committing such a crime.
"I'm sorry Elandor, it's just… the manual is too important for me" Leo said, his voice softening just a little as he gave the housekeeper a small hug.
He did not mean to threaten the innocent, however, he did not wish to come off as weak, until he knew that the man was indeed innocent.
"It's okay Sir Leo, whoever did this crime would have entered the vicinity of your manor and would be caught by the security camera.
If you go to the Captain, he will immediately find the perpetrator for you.
In the end, the Arc Ship is but a giant metal tube, your manual has to be somewhere up here. The thief can't go far" Elandor said, as Leo nodded in agreement to his words.
"The thief can indeed not go too far" Leo repeated, as he continued to make his way to the staff quarters.

chapters.title: Chapter 780 - 780: MadMan
chapters.content:
Kid felt a rollercoaster of emotions unfolding in his belly as he watched Leo rage and flip-out about missing his manual.
At first he hoped that Leo would just assume that he misplaced it and not make a ruckus about it. That he would somehow wait for a few days, before civilly reporting the issue to appropriate authorities, but Kid seemed to have hoped for too much.
As soon as he became sure that the manual was not in his Manor, Leo immediately grabbed his daggers and rushed out of his quarters with the intention to kill, which made Kid's blood pressure drop massively.
He felt light headed and buried his head within his hands, as he saw Leo storm out of his quarters, with the intention to kill anyone he found guilty of messing with him.
"He won't find out…. He won't find out…. He won't find out…" Kid kept assuring himself, as he nervously began to bite his own nails.
However, what unfolded next gave him a moment of hope.
Instead of shouting his name, Leo instead summoned Elandor. The housekeeper for VIP ground 1. Who just like Kid had access to enter Leo's manor.
"Yes! Put all the blame on him…. Interrogate him, nick him and leave a cut. He is your criminal—" Kid hoped, as he saw Leo interrogate Elandor in rage.
However, nothing seemed to come out of it in the end.
After a few tough questions, he hugged Elandor and let him go, turning all his focus to the staff quarters once more, as his decision to acquit Elandor of all crimes, once again made Kid feel sick in his stomach.
"Fuck! Elandor was the perfect scapegoat. If everything went wrong, I could have planted the manual in his quarters and framed him for the crime.
Goddamn it. I wasted a big chance" Kid realized, as he cursed himself for his own stupidity.
He had completely forgotten than Elandor also had access to Leo's quarters and could be used as the perfect scapegoat, squandering a perfect opportunity to prepare a fall guy.
"Alright, what's done is done. I need to calm myself now and act surprised, when he eventually comes up to me.
I cannot mess this up! Or else I'm dead—" Kid realized, as he slapped his own cheeks and prepared his best poker face.
Knowing full well that Leo was on his way to his office, he shut-down all surveillance monitors and made his way to the joint work room, where Raya, Raven and other staff members were performing their daily duties moderating Terra Nova Online.
"Good Evening everyone, how does today's game day look?" He asked upon reaching the work area, as the staff members glanced towards him before submitting a usual report.
Without Leo in the game world, there was nothing groundbreaking that took place, which made the overall report mundane.
All in all, Captain Kid tried his best to appear normal and pretend like nothing out of the usual, however, internally he was sweating buckets, as he knew that Leo could drop in now at any given minute.
************
(A few minutes later)
"CAPTAIN!!! CAPTAIN KID!!!" Leo roared, his voice reverberating through the halls as he stormed toward the workroom.
Two Arc Ship staff members trailed behind him, their faces pale and filled with unease. They tried to calm him, to make him listen to reason, however, their feeble attempts were simply drowned out by Leo's furious strides and fiery gaze.
The heavy doors to the workroom hissed open, and Leo stepped inside, his presence an explosion of energy that immediately silenced the chatter among the staff.
Without missing a beat, he pulled a dagger from his side and slammed it into the metal floor with such force that it embedded itself deep into the plating, the metallic clang echoing sharply through the room.
Everyone froze.
"You!" Leo shouted, pointing a finger that swept across the stunned room. "Someone has stolen my meditation manual, and I need to get it back right now!"
The staff exchanged nervous glances before immediately setting aside their tasks, focusing entirely on addressing Leo's demands.
The tension in the room thickened like smoke as whispers filled the air, each staff member looking more confused than the last.
Raya stepped forward hesitantly, her brow furrowed. "Sir Leo, I don't mean to downplay the seriousness of this, but… stealing a meditation manual is pointless. It's bound to you alone—it's completely useless to anyone else."
"Exactly!" Raven chimed in, his voice firmer and less hesitant. He stepped forward, his sharp eyes meeting Leo's fiery gaze. "And what's more is that threatening the staff and damaging Arc Ship property isn't going to help you. If anything, it could land you in serious trouble."
Leo's head snapped toward Raven, his expression darkening, however, oblivious to Leo's rage, Raven pressed on, undeterred. "This is the real world, Leo—not your game. We work for the Universal Government, not the Uprising or your empire. You might be 'TheBoss' in Terra Nova Online, but here, you're still subject to the laws of the ship. If you keep causing trouble—"
Raven's words were cut short as Leo lunged forward, his speed blinding. In the blink of an eye, his hand wrapped tightly around Raven's neck in a death grip. Raven gasped, clawing at Leo's iron-like fingers, but the pressure didn't ease.
Leo raised another dagger with his free hand, its edge gleaming as he pressed it lightly against Raven's throat. The room collectively recoiled, and even Captain Kid, despite his secret excitement, found himself holding his breath.
Leo leaned in, his voice dropping to a deadly growl. "I'm subject to Universal Laws and will be punished upon landing? Very well, I'll accept that punishment. But unless I find my manual, I'm sparing no one in this room."
His eyes burned with an intensity that sent chills down every spine in the room. "You will all die by my blade," he promised, his tone eerily calm, "and there's nothing you can do to stop me, for I am stronger than all of you."

chapters.title: Chapter 781 - 781: Threat For Threat
chapters.content:
Nobody on the Arc Ship had truly grasped just how far gone Leo was from being a calm, rational human being—until he uttered the chilling words:
"You will all die by my blade, and there's nothing you can do to stop me, for I am stronger than all of you."
This wasn't a declaration of frustration or an idle threat.
It was the unfiltered promise of a man who had severed himself from the constraints of reason, morality, and fear of consequence.
Leo's words carried the weight of unbridled madness, spoken with the conviction of someone who no longer cared about societal rules or universal laws.
They weren't the words of a decent human being navigating a system of order—they were the words of a predator standing at the top of the food chain, daring anyone to challenge him.
Threatening staff, slamming daggers into the floor, holding someone hostage at knifepoint—these were not the actions of a man tethered to civility.
These were the actions of an unhinged individual, someone who had long since crossed the line between a warrior driven by purpose and a madman confident in his own power and rage.
Leo was no longer afraid of consequences because, in his mind, there were none.
Instead, he felt as if he was the consequence.
And oddly enough, despite of how cockily he behaved, he was not wrong.
There was not a single warrior amongst the staff who could rival him in combat, and if he indeed decided to engage them in combat there was not a single one amongst them who could stop his rampage.
Hence, although he could potentially face grave consequences for his threats once they landed.
At this very moment, aboard the Arc Ship isolated in space. He was the apex predator, and he wasn't shy to show it.
"Okay, Leo," Kid interjected, his voice steady despite the storm of nerves raging inside him. "We understand your concern, and we'll get straight to it—but first, let my staff member go."
He stepped forward slightly, his hands raised in a gesture of peace, though his eyes flickered nervously toward the dagger pressed against Raven's throat.
The room fell silent, the tension palpable as every staff member held their breath, waiting to see what would happen next.
Leo didn't move, his grip firm, his eyes locked onto Kid with a mix of disdain and calculation. Kid swallowed hard but continued speaking, summoning every ounce of courage he could muster.
"Leo, listen to me," Kid said, his tone hardening. "If you so much as injure a single one of my staff members, this ship doesn't land. Do you understand me? I am the only one who knows how to safely bring the Arc Ship down, and if I decide not to cooperate, everyone on board—including your loved ones—dies."
The words hit the room like a thunderclap, and for a moment, even Leo's fiery gaze faltered.
"I could fly this ship into a star," Kid continued, his voice gaining strength. "I could crash it upon entry into the atmosphere. There is no manual override, no emergency fail-safe. You, Leo—no matter how strong you think you are—don't have the knowledge to stop me. So if you want to land on planet Terra Nova safely, I suggest you lower your weapons and let my staff do their job."
Leo's eyes narrowed, his expression a dangerous mix of rage and reluctant understanding. For a moment, the room held its collective breath, as if the entire ship had paused to witness the standoff.
Then, with a sharp exhale, Leo released Raven from his grip, though the dagger in his other hand remained poised, now pointing directly at Kid.
"Don't think I won't do it," Leo growled, his tone low and menacing. "I'll put a blade through you the second I think you're stalling."
Kid met his gaze, hiding the tremor in his chest behind a mask of defiance. "You're free to try," he replied calmly. "But if you kill me, you'll doom everyone on this ship—including yourself."
The room was deathly silent, the staff frozen in a mix of fear and awe as they watched their captain stand up to the unhinged madman before them.
In that moment, Kid became a hero in their eyes—a leader who had the courage to confront a bully, even when the odds were stacked against him.
'A man worthy to be called captain'
'No wonder he's our superior!'
'A true man's man!'
That was how most staff members looked at Kid now, completely unaware of the real thief that he was.
In reality, his threats were as empty as his words, as the ship did not need any manual assistance from him to land or take-off.
The flight path was pre-determined and he could not veer it off-course even if he wanted to, so the threat to slam it into a star was also bogus.
Nonetheless, with Leo unaware of the truth behind this threat and with Luke and Amanda's life also at risk, he backed off from his challenge, hoping that Kid would keep his word as promised.
"I'm going to my cabin now, where I can access the feeds and all the security cameras. If someone did steal your manual, it won't take me more than 48 hours to find the culprit, so I request that you stay patient till then—" Kid continued, as Leo finally lowered his dagger at the assurance.
"Very well. I'll give you 48 hours to find my manual Captain, but if you don't ….. then I will return angrier…. That much I promise" Leo said, as he turned to leave the room, but paused to pick his training dagger embedded in the floor up first.
"Can't waste it, you guys are too stingy with your supplies" he taunted before leaving, as it wasn't until he actually left the room that the staff breathed a collective sigh of relief.
"What an absolute psycho!" Raven complained, touching his throat, as a clamour of discussion broke out, regarding what to do next.

chapters.title: Chapter 782 - 782: Self Preservation
chapters.content:
As soon as the doors slid shut behind Leo, the staff work room erupted in a clutter of voices.
The tension that had gripped the air moments earlier dissipated and it was replaced by a mixture of relieved sighs and frantic chatter.
Staff members huddled together, their faces pale, their hands still trembling from the encounter.
"Captain, I don't know how you kept your cool," Raya said, her voice shaky as she leaned against a console for support. "He's completely unhinged! Did you see the way he held that dagger? He was ready to kill Raven on the spot."
"That man has lost his mind," Raven snapped, rubbing his neck where Leo's fingers had dug into his skin. "He's a lunatic! He spared me today, but how long will it be until he actually hurts someone?"
"I can't believe we're stuck on a ship with him," another staff member muttered. "This isn't Terra Nova Online. There are laws here—rules. He can't just go around threatening people like this!"
The frustration in the room boiled over, and the staff quickly turned their attention to solutions. Voices overlapped as they threw out ideas, some more drastic than others.
"We need to lock down the VIP sector," someone suggested. "Restrict his movements to his manor. Revoke his access to the rest of the ship."
"That won't be enough," Raven argued. "We should report him to the Universal Government. What he did today was criminal—holding someone at knifepoint, damaging ship property? He should be flagged as a threat the moment we land."
A murmur of agreement rippled through the room, though a few staff members looked uneasy.
"Are you insane?" Raya interjected. "Flagging Leo means making an enemy of TheBoss. Do you really want to do that? He's the strongest player in the game and, let's face it, probably the most dangerous person on this ship."
"Better to make an enemy than to wait until he snaps," Raven shot back. "What if he decides to take his rage out on someone else next time? What if it's one of us?"
As the debate escalated, Captain Kid raised a hand, commanding silence. The room fell quiet almost immediately as all eyes turned toward him.
Despite the turmoil raging inside, Kid kept his expression calm and his voice steady.
"Enough," he said firmly, his tone brooking no argument. "I understand your frustration, but I need everyone to take a step back and think carefully about this."
The staff exchanged uneasy glances, but no one spoke as Kid continued. "Yes, Leo's behavior today was extreme. But it's not who he is at his core. He's under immense pressure, and while that doesn't excuse his actions, it explains them. Reporting him or locking him down won't solve the problem—it'll only make things worse for all of us."
"But Captain—" Raven started, only to be cut off by Kid's sharp glare.
"No," Kid said, his voice cold and unwavering. "Let me make this clear: if anyone here takes action against Leo without my approval, they will answer to me. Do I make myself clear?"
The weight of his words settled over the room like a heavy blanket. Some staff members nodded hesitantly, while others simply looked away, unwilling to meet his gaze.
Raya, however, broke the silence. "You're incredible, Captain. After everything he's done, you're still willing to defend him?"
"Yeah," another staff member chimed in. "Most people would've folded, but you… you're something else."
"Truly a captain worthy of respect," someone muttered, and the sentiment quickly spread.
Kid forced a modest smile, inclining his head slightly. "It's not about defending him," he said. "It's about keeping the peace. We all want to make it to Terra Nova safely, and that won't happen if we're at each other's throats."
Inside, however, Kid was far from calm. His outward composure masked the storm of nerves churning in his gut.
He knew the real reason he couldn't let Leo be punished was not out of some heroic nobility, but because if Leo fell, Kid's carefully constructed safety net would crumble with him.
Without Leo's implicit protection as 'TheBoss,' and his status as an important talent and genius, Kid stood to lose his leverage with the Mu Clan, which was an outcome he was unwilling to accept.
Every word he spoke now, every decision he made, was driven not by nobility, but out of self preservation.
When the staff finally dispersed, Kid returned to his private quarters instead of his work-cabin, the weight of the day's events pressing heavily on his shoulders.
Closing the door behind him, he leaned against it, letting out a shaky breath.
For the first time since the encounter, he allowed himself to feel the full extent of his anxiety.
"They think I'm a hero," he muttered, a bitter laugh escaping his lips. "If only they knew the truth."
His gaze drifted to the hidden compartment where Leo's meditation manual was securely tucked away. Its presence was a constant reminder of the web of lies he had spun.
The staff's admiration, their misplaced trust—it all felt like a cruel joke. But as much as he hated the deception, he knew he had no choice.
Kid sat down at his desk, rubbing his temples as the adrenaline began to fade. The game he was playing was dangerous, and the stakes were higher than ever. One misstep could unravel everything, and yet he couldn't stop now.
"Just a little longer," he whispered to himself. "I just need to keep this going a little longer."
For now, at least, he was still in control. But for how much longer, even Kid couldn't say.
He had promised Leo that he would find his manual within the next 48 hours, but he wasn't sure on how to do it?
He couldn't just place it back into Leo's apartment and pretend like it was never lost, as that would only make Leo even more paranoid.
And he couldn't not give an answer either, as the mad man was ready to kill over it.
Either way, he was in big trouble.

chapters.title: Chapter 783 - 783: Proof
chapters.content:
Upon returning to his manor, Leo immediately began tearing through every corner of the space, determined to confirm beyond any doubt that the meditation manual was nowhere to be found, as he did not want to humiliate himself later if the manual did end up being within his own house.
Drawers were pulled open, shelves were swept clean, and cushions were flung across the room in a frenzy. Every corner, no matter how unlikely, was thoroughly searched, but his efforts yielded nothing.
The manual was not within his manor, and now he felt certain about that fact without a shadow of a doubt.
Hence, if one were to secretly plant the manual in his house later. He would not fall for it, and know full well that someone sabotaged him on purpose.
Leo's frustration about the whole situation grew with every passing moment.
The meditation manual was important for him, for it was his main tool for improvement currently. And without it, he felt like a runner forced to sprint on a treadmill, expending energy but going nowhere, as just natural training of his skills alone was not enough to yield any important results.
"This is insane," Leo muttered to himself, clenching his fists. "Someone is deliberately messing with me. But who? Why? What's the point if they can't even use the manual themselves?"
The questions circled his mind like vultures over a carcass.
Was this an attempt to throw him off his training?
A poorly thought-out prank?
Or something more sinister?
Regardless of what it was, Leo knew that he couldn't sit idle and wait for answers.
Time was of the essence in any crime, and every moment without the manual being located felt like a major setback.
Then, just as he was about to start flipping over his bed frame, he heard footsteps approaching.
The door creaked open, and Luke stepped in, his brow furrowed in concern as he took in the chaotic state of the room.
"Leo? What's all this noise about?" Luke asked, folding his arms, as he was surprised to see the littered furniture all over the VIP manor.
Leo looked like he had properly raged in the place, ransacking everything he could get his hands on, leaving only the immovable pieces of furniture intact.
"Did you lose something?" Luke questioned, as that was the only reasonable explanation that came to his mind for Leo doing something like this.
Leo straightened, his frustration momentarily replaced by a sliver of relief at seeing his brother, as he replied "Someone stole my meditation manual, brother"
"I've searched everywhere, and it's not here. I know it's not misplaced. Someone took it."
Luke's expression darkened.
"Are you sure it's stolen? But who would do such a thing? The only ones with access to the VIP sector are you, me, Alia, Amanda and the staff.
The three of us won't do it, so…." Luke murmured, as Leo agreed immediately with his line of thought.
"Exactly my point…." Leo said, as Luke raised an eyebrow in response.
"How did they do it?" Luke questioned, as Leo shrugged his shoulders in response.
"I don't know, but the Captain says there's surveillance cameras all around. Whoever did this, they will find within 48 hours who it was" Leo said, as Luke nodded solemnly.
"We should trust the captain for now, but it doesn't mean we can't investigate on our own in the meantime" Luke suggested, as it was Leo's turn now to be surprised.
"How?" Leo inquired, as Luke's face turned into a sly grin.
"Footprints. The house has two entrances—the main entrance and the back door, right? If someone entered or left recently, we might be able to trace their steps." Luke explained, as without another word, the brothers grabbed a portable light and headed to the main entrance first.
The training ground outside the front door was a flat expanse of dirt and sand, frequently used by Leo and Alia for training and sparring practice.
The ground was littered with faint footprints, but a closer inspection revealed nothing out of the ordinary.
"These are all ours," Luke said, pointing to the distinct patterns. "Yours, Amanda's, Alia's and mine. No one else has been here recently."
Leo gritted his teeth. "Then it must be the back door."
They hurried to the rear of the manor, where the environment was different.
The back entrance opened onto a patch of slightly damp ground, its surface soft enough to capture clear impressions of anyone who walked across it, and Leo's sharp eyes immediately picked out a footprint that didn't belong.
"Here," he said, crouching down and gesturing for Luke to join him.
The footprint was distinct, larger than Amanda's but slightly smaller than Leo's, and it led away from the house in hurried strides. The direction was clear—it pointed toward the staff quarters.
"It's not one of ours," Luke confirmed, his tone grim. "And whoever it was, they were in a rush."
Leo studied the trail with a cold intensity.
"They made a mistake leaving this behind. I'll make sure it bites them." He concluded as he pulled out a dagger and began cutting a precise block of the mud where the footprint was embedded.
Luke watched silently, his arms crossed as Leo carefully lifted the block and carried it back towards the apartment where they placed it within a cooking utensil.
Thankfully the mud block was thick and sturdy enough to hold the impression intact, making it a perfect piece of evidence.
"This footprint will lead us to whoever did this," Leo said, his voice steady but filled with unshakable determination. "No one messes with me and gets away with it."
"Yep, yep, let's wait for the Captain to give us something back, if we can notice the footprints, I'm sure the Captain can straight up catch the culprit.
Because if not, it means he's involved in this whole mess" Luke said, as Leo gave him a firm handshake.
"I knew I was not crazy. Something really was up!" Leo said, as Luke chuckled out loud.
"Of Course you're not crazy, brother. Why would you even think so?" he assured, as Leo gave him a genuine smile.
**********
(Meanwhile, Captain Kid)
