Guys, the ending event for the book is fixed by webnovel for 25th Feb, but I have roughly only 45 chapters left till the end.
So the release rate may become patchy going forward.
Thankyou for your understanding.
But on the plus side, the new book will be launched around 15 Feb, so there's that.///

chapters.title: Chapter 794 - 794: A strange encounter
chapters.content:
After sharing the location of the mana vein with ChaosBringer, Leo continued his exploration of the Gu Clan Chambers until he stumbled upon the patriarch's quarters, where the skill scroll was said to be stored.
The room was located at the absolute dead-end of the Gu family chambers and was, by far, in the worst condition of the entire structure.
Half the ceiling had already caved in, allowing piles of mud and roots to fall through, while all sorts of plants and weeds sprouted from the cracked furniture and moist floor tiles.
Yet, despite its semi-destroyed state, the room somehow retained an undeniable air of authority. Its austere arrangement, coupled with the remnants of intricate craftsmanship, hinted at the power and prestige it once represented.
At the center of the room stood a pedestal carved from smooth obsidian, its polished surface faintly reflecting the dim glow of the purple flowers clinging to the walls.
Resting atop this pedestal was the scroll Leo had been seeking, encased in a crystalline shell that shimmered faintly with an almost otherworldly light.
Inside the casing lay a single piece of paper, seemingly untouched by the ravages of time.
"This has to be it," Leo murmured, his eyes fixed on the scroll.
The palpable energy radiating from it left no room for doubt about its significance as without hesitation, Leo moved closer, his anticipation building with each step.
Standing before the pedestal, he reached out and placed his hand on the crystalline casing.
However, unexpectedly, the moment his fingers made contact, a powerful surge of energy coursed through him, leaving him momentarily breathless.
Suddenly, his surroundings twisted and blurred, the room dissolving into an expanse of boundless darkness as his consciousness was abruptly pulled into another dimension.
When the haze cleared, Leo found himself in an ethereal, seemingly infinite space and before him stood a regal man with a neatly groomed silver moustache and piercing golden eyes that radiated both overwhelming power and a profound melancholy.
The sheer weight of the man's presence was enough to send a shiver down Leo's spine, as Leo had no doubt in his mind that the man was much stronger than him.
[ ????? Sovereign. Lv (????) ]
It was a first time in a long time that Leo had failed to inspect the status bar of a character within the game, as by now he was used to being the strongest in town.
Yet, facing this peculiar man, Leo once again felt like a newbie, for the man was clearly much more powerful than he was.
"You're not a member of my clan… are you?" the man said, his voice laden with sorrow.
His gaze lingered on Leo, scrutinizing him with an intensity that made it feel as though he could see straight through him, as before Leo could formulate a reply, the man raised his hand and waved dismissively.
Suddenly, Leo felt a force unlike anything he had ever encountered before, and in an instant, he was yanked forcibly out of the separate space, his consciousness flung back into the game world.
"What the hell?" Leo muttered, staggering slightly as the room reformed around him.
His mind spun with vertigo, the surreal encounter leaving him disoriented and shaken.
"What was that? Captain Kid's tablet didn't mention anything like this!" he cursed under his breath, as his trembling hands worked to remove the crystalline casing over the scroll.
Afraid, he tried to grab the scroll and leave before he encountered that strange man again, as with trembling fingers, Leo touched the parchment scroll.
[System Notification: You have obtained the skill scroll [Blade Switch] (Semi-Divine).
Congratulations to the player 'TheBoss' for finding yet another semi-divine artifact.]
The system's familiar chime confirmed his possession of the scroll, concluding his quest, as wasting no time, Leo turned to leave, eager to escape the dark, humid chambers of the assassin alliance.
"We got what we wanted, Dumpy. Let's head back," he said, his voice steady despite the lingering unease.
Navigating his way out took 30 minutes, but even as he ascended back to the surface, Leo couldn't shake the memory of what he had just experienced.
The encounter with the mysterious man gnawed at his mind, leaving him with more questions than answers.
"I'll ask Captain Kid about it later," Leo decided, making a mental note as he finally stepped into the fresh air of the forest above.
***********
(A few hours later, The real world, Captain Kid's office)
"You got yanked into a separate space? And met a sentient man there? And he had question marks above his head where the level should be?" Kid asked, his tone a mixture of surprise and curiosity.
Even for someone in his position, what Leo described seemed to tread into unfamiliar territory.
"How do you not know what I just experienced? Don't you design and control every aspect of the fucking game?" Leo snapped, his frustration evident as he glared at the so called Captain of the Arc Ship.
Kid scratched the back of his head awkwardly, clearly uncomfortable under Leo's scrutiny.
"Well… we do control a lot of aspects of the game," he admitted, "but skill scrolls? That's a completely different story."
Leo raised an eyebrow, his disbelief growing. "What do you mean, a 'different story'? You're telling me you can manipulate almost everything else, but not the mechanics behind these scrolls?"
Kid sighed, resigned to Leo's fury.
"Look, the skill scrolls we have in Terra Nova Online aren't exactly our property. They're provided to us by the clans who donate them as part of their contribution to the game world. But here's the catch— they don't give us free rein to mess with their clan secrets. They usually attach special conditions, and those conditions are encrypted. It's part of the agreement we sign when integrating their scrolls into the system. So while you might think I know what happened to you, I actually don't."
Leo crossed his arms, still unconvinced. "So you're saying the Gu Clan encoded their scrolls, and that's why I got pulled into that weird space?"
"Exactly. Think of it as an extra layer of security or maybe even tradition. My best guess is that the Gu Clan added a unique piece of code to the [Blade Switch] scroll, one that activates when someone attempts to claim it. That code likely creates the dimension you were pulled into. What you experienced is entirely tied to the Gu Clan's programming—it's not something we directly control or even fully understand."
Leo's eyes narrowed, irritation flickering across his face. "So, all you've got for me is a 'guess'? That's your big explanation?"
Kid winced under Leo's gaze. "Pretty much. And to be honest, my guess is as good as yours on this one. The clans don't share their methods with us—they only give us the finished product, so to speak."
Leo rolled his eyes, exhaling sharply. "Unbelievable. The 'all-powerful Captain Kid' doesn't even know how half the stuff in his own game works."
Kid shrugged helplessly. "Hey, you're not wrong. But that's how it is when you're dealing with egotistical clans guarding their secrets like treasure. You're lucky the scroll didn't kill you outright for not being a Gu Clan member."
"Comforting thought," Leo muttered sarcastically, his irritation still simmering as he was forced to drop the matter for now.

chapters.title: Chapter 795 - 795: A heartfelt apology
chapters.content:
(Luke's POV)
As Luke received the system notification inviting him to the fourth annual rankers event, he let out a deep sigh of relief before instantly accepting it. This was the moment he had been preparing for over the past several months—a final chance to prove his worth among the best players in Terra Nova Online and get the forward momentum necessary to propel him towards becoming a 'Master'.
A flash of light enveloped him, and within seconds, he found himself teleported to the pre-game space—a serene, grassy field with a single towering tree at its center, the same as the one a year before.
The air buzzed with anticipation as the top 10,000 rankers began appearing one after another, their unique armor and weapons gleaming under the sunlight.
Luke scanned the crowd, his sharp eyes immediately catching sight of a familiar figure standing under the tree.
His father, Jacob.
The man looked older than Luke remembered, his posture slightly slouched and his expression hesitant. Their gazes locked for a brief moment, and Luke could see the uncertainty in his father's eyes. It was clear he wanted to approach, to say something, but the weight of their shared past kept him rooted to the spot.
Luke's emotions churned—a mixture of anger, sadness, and an almost reluctant acknowledgement.
He still couldn't forgive the man for abandoning their family, yet seeing him here now, knowing how he had been working so hard over the past months to keep their mother happy and to try and bridge the gap within the family, something within Luke stirred.
After a few seconds of hesitation, Luke gave him a curt nod of acknowledgement before looking away, silently signaling that he wasn't ready for a conversation, but their relationship was on the right path.
As he turned his gaze back to the field, a blur of bouncing melons caught his attention.
"Luke!" PinkLotus called out cheerfully, dashing toward him with an infectious grin. Before he could brace himself, she threw her arms around him, snuggling into his chest like a cat seeking warmth.
"Wha—" Luke stammered, his face turning as red as a tomato as the public display of affection drew the attention of more than a few rankers nearby.
The reactions were immediate. Heads turned, conversations paused, and whispers rippled through the crowd. PinkLotus wasn't just any player—she was widely regarded as the goddess of Terra Nova, her beauty and prowess unmatched. Seeing her act so chummy with another man left more than a few onlookers seething with jealousy.
"Lia, people are staring!" Luke hissed under his breath, but PinkLotus merely giggled, tilting her head up to meet his flustered gaze.
"Let them stare," she teased, a mischievous glint in her eyes. "I'm proud to have you by my side, Luke. Why shouldn't they know that?"
Her words only deepened his embarrassment, and he tried to gently pull away, but her grip remained firm.
"Relax," she said, patting his chest. "Focus on the event, not them."
Despite her words, Luke couldn't ignore the jealous stares drilling into his back. He cleared his throat awkwardly, grateful when PinkLotus finally stepped aside, though her presence continued to command attention.
As he steadied himself, his gaze shifted again, landing on another familiar figure approaching from the edge of the field.
It was Cervantez.
The man's expression was complicated, a mix of respect and something else—something darker.
"It's been a while, SkyLion," Cervantez said as he stopped a few steps away.
His tone was neutral, but there was an edge to it, as though he was trying to gauge Luke's reaction.
"Not that long since I suplexed you, I reckon" Luke replied evenly, refusing to be rattled.
A soft smile spread on Cervantez's face as he alternated his gaze between Luke and PinkLotus, complex feelings arising in his chest as he saw them acting as comfortable with one another as they did.
However, suppressing the disgust he felt, Cervantez let out a deep sigh as he admitted what he wanted to for a long while.
"I apologise for my previous behaviour, SkyLion. You may not know it but the guild is crumbling and the guild members are leaving en-masse.
Despite all I've done for them, apart from a handful still sticking around, nobody is willing to stay, and it's only now that I realize just how flawed my methods were in the past.
I know that trust that's broken once can never be reforged, so I don't expect us to become best friends again, but I just wanted to apologise to you once, because I owe you that much.
Back then, I should have been more accommodating of your request….. the DarkSky guild was as much yours as it was mine, but I was naive and foolish.
I hope you can forgive me for it someday" Cervantez said, as he sounded genuinely sorry for his previous behaviour.
For a moment, Luke found himself unable to respond to Cervantez's comments, as just like Cervantez, he too was suppressing a lot of pent-up emotions at this moment.
However, with PinkLotus's comforting presence by his side, he soon snapped back to reality, as he gave Cervantez a measured nod.
"The next time we run into one another, there will be no warmth between us, but there won't be any hostility either.
I'm grateful for all you've done for me, as it is a fact that without you I wouldn't be the player I am today.
So let's call us even" Luke said, as he extended his hand for Cervantez to shake.
"Thankyou—" Cervantez said, accepting that handshake, as after casting one last complicated glance at the duo, he walked away, feeling as if a boulder had been lifted off his chest.
His apology to Luke was one long due, and it felt good to finally have it done.
"Are you okay?" PinkLotus asked Luke once Cervantez was out of earshot, as Luke nodded with a big grin.
This unexpected apology was one he had long hoped for, and its arrival brought him a quiet sense of relief and satisfaction.

chapters.title: Chapter 796 - 796: The final rankers event
chapters.content:
A few seconds after all the rankers accepted the invite and gathered in the pre-game space, Raya appeared before everyone, her beautiful appearance immediately enrapturing the attention of many.
The murmurs quieted instantly when she descended from the branches of the central tree, as many rankers who had seen her during previous events immediately recognised her this year as well.
*Thud*
She landed delicately in front of the crowd, her piercing green eyes scanning the rankers as she smiled warmly.
"Welcome, rankers," Raya's melodic voice rang out, commanding everyone's attention. "This year marks the fourth and final annual Rankers Event of Terra Nova Online. Each of you has proven yourself worthy by rising through the ranks and overcoming countless challenges to stand here today. Congratulations."
The players erupted in cheers and applause, their excitement uncontainable. Raya raised her hand to silence them, her smile widening slightly.
"As always, this event will push you to your limits. Only the strongest, smartest, and most resourceful among you will prevail. But before we dive into the rules, there is an important announcement to make."
The air grew tense as Raya's gaze swept across the crowd, her voice taking on a slightly teasing tone. "To maintain fairness in this year's Ranker Event, Emperor 'TheBoss' has not been invited. For if he were, let's be honest—none of you would stand a real chance at victory."
The crowd froze for a split second before an explosion of cheers and laughter erupted, the relief among the rankers almost tangible.
"Finally!" someone shouted.
"About time we actually have a shot!" another added, pumping their fist in the air.
"If he's not here, we can actually aim for the number one spot!"
It seemed like Leo's dominance was a well known fact within the game world now, and none of the other players even hoped to compete against him.
Luke caught a few players visibly relaxing their tense shoulders, their faces lighting up as if they had just won the event outright.
PinkLotus, standing beside him, chuckled softly, amused by the collective joy.
"Well, that's one less unbeatable monster for them to worry about," she whispered, nudging Luke playfully. "You should thank your brother for sitting this one out."
Luke gave a faint smirk but stayed quiet, his thoughts turning to Leo. The truth was, with Leo absent, the field did feel a lot more open. However, that didn't mean the event would be a cakewalk.
Raya waited patiently for the commotion to die down before continuing. "Now, with that out of the way, let's move on to the event details. As always, the Rankers Event will consist of two rounds. The preliminary round is a monster-slaughtering challenge where you will compete to score points. Only the top 100 players will advance to the second round—a PvP battle royale to determine the ultimate winner."
The atmosphere shifted instantly, excitement giving way to intense focus. The rankers leaned in, eager to hear the finer details.
"For the preliminary round," Raya explained, "you will be teleported to a vast hunting ground teeming with monsters. Each type of monster carries a different point value based on its difficulty. Your goal is simple: kill as many monsters as you can within the allotted time and score enough points to secure your spot in the top 100."
She waved her hand, and holographic displays appeared in the air, listing the point values for different monsters.
"Remember," Raya continued, her voice taking on a sharp edge, "you are competing against each other. The hunting grounds are limited, and the monsters won't respawn. If you hesitate or lose focus, someone else will claim the kill—and the points, so remember to keep your wits about you.
Also, there are no points sharing. So even if you injure a monster, if someone else claimed the kill, they will receive all the points.
Which is why teaming up is useless."
Luke clenched his fists, his resolve hardening. He glanced at Cervantez, who stood a short distance away, his arms crossed and his expression unreadable.
"Finally," Raya said, her tone lightening as she smiled once more, "let me remind you that this event is just about individual glory. The rewards this year are exceptional, ranging from semi divine-grade weapons and armor to unique skill scrolls. So give it your all and show us what you're made of."
With a snap of her fingers, the tree's branches began to glow, and the ground beneath them shimmered with magical energy.
"Prepare yourselves," Raya announced. "The preliminary round begins in five seconds. Good luck, rankers."
As the magical energy intensified, Luke's heart raced. He tightened his grip on his daggers, his mind already strategizing.
"Let's do this," he muttered to himself, his determination unwavering as the event was about to begin.
*********
(The event space, Luke's POV)
As the magical energy faded, Luke found himself in the event space: a sprawling wilderness filled with opportunities—and dangers.
The terrain was varied but straightforward, with patches of dense forest, rocky clearings, and scattered streams cutting through the landscape.
Already, rankers were dispersing in all directions, their weapons drawn as they raced to claim the best hunting grounds, and Luke wasted no time either.
His eyes quickly scanned the surroundings, noting the types of monsters that were visible.
Frost wolves roamed in small packs nearby, their glowing red eyes betraying their aggression, while larger beasts loomed farther out.
Each type carried its own risk and reward, with frost wolves being worth a meager 10 points and the larger creatures promising much more.
A system notification flashed in his vision: [Preliminary Round, 'The Hunting Grounds' : Duration - 3 Hours. Top 100 scorers advance.]
Luke adjusted his grip on his sword, his mind already working through strategies.
Frost wolves might not be worth much, but taking out a pack quickly could still give him an early lead.
However, just as he was deciding whether or not to engage the wolves, he saw a charging mega-bull heading in his direction, worth a massive 180 points.

chapters.title: Chapter 797 - 797: Luke Shines
chapters.content:
Luke wasn't expecting to face a giant bull as his first opponent, but he couldn't afford to be picky—not in this event.
The mega-bull was a towering behemoth with obsidian horns and crimson eyes, barreling across the field towards him with terrifying speed. Its massive hooves thundered against the ground, sending tremors through the air as it plowed forward, its sheer presence making the surrounding rankers freeze momentarily in fear.
Before Luke could face it, one unfortunate ranker stood directly in its path, his blade raised in a futile attempt to intercept the beast.
"Hold it!" the man shouted, bracing himself, but his effort was in vain.
The bull didn't even slow. With a flick of its massive horns, it sent the man flying like a rag doll, his body crashing through the underbrush with a sickening thud. Gasps and murmurs erupted from the other players nearby, some of whom were backing away in fear, clearly deciding that the bull wasn't worth the risk.
Luke clenched his jaw, his grip tightening on his sword and shield as the beast's blood-red gaze locked onto him next.
"Alright, big guy," Luke muttered under his breath. "Let's dance."
As the bull closed the distance, Luke raised his shield and activated [Guardian Shield]. A shimmering golden aura enveloped him, fortifying his defenses and bracing him for the impending collision. The beast slammed into him with a deafening crash, the impact rattling Luke's bones and sending a shockwave through the ground.
But unlike the unfortunate ranker before him, Luke stood firm, his boots digging into the dirt to absorb the force. The bull was pushing against him, its massive frame straining to overpower him, but the golden aura of [Guardian Shield] held strong.
"Damn, you're strong," Luke grunted, his muscles straining as he held his ground. The sheer feat of stopping the bull earned him a few impressed glances from nearby rankers who had witnessed its destructive power firsthand. However, those impressed gazes soon turned into opportunistic hunger, as several rankers began closing in on his location, contemplating stealing Luke's kill.
"No point coming here—I'm ending this fight now!" Luke declared, noticing through his peripheral vision how a few rankers were zeroing in on him.
Activating the skill [Blazing Cyclone], Luke enveloped his sword in flames as he spun in a fiery whirlwind, slashing at the bull's legs and torso. The beast bellowed in pain, its movements becoming more erratic as the flames seared its hide.
"Still standing? Let's fix that," Luke growled, leaping back to create some distance. As the bull lowered its head for another charge, he channeled all his energy into [Heaven's Strike]. His sword began glowing with a brilliant white light, crackling with raw power.
Timing his move perfectly, Luke sidestepped the charging beast and brought his sword down with a devastating overhead strike. The radiant blade sliced clean through the bull's neck, its massive body collapsing to the ground with a thunderous crash.
[System Notification: You have defeated a Mega-Bull (Level 500). Points Earned: 180.]
Luke exhaled, adrenaline still coursing through his veins. "One down," he muttered, wiping the sweat from his brow.
"No scraps for the scavengers," he added, meeting the disappointed eyes of the rankers around him who had hoped to capitalize on his fight.
No sooner had he caught his breath than the ground was trembling again. Emerging from the nearby trees were more high-ranking beasts—dire bears, venomous wyverns, and shadow panthers—all converging on his location.
"Oh? It seems like this event is designed to keep the pressure on, forcing competitors to stay on their toes," Luke muttered, finding nothing suspicious in the moment.
He didn't yet realize that all these high-level monsters were only converging on his location, leaving the other rankers undisturbed.
"Bring it on," he said instead, charging forward to meet the incoming threats head-on.
What followed was a whirlwind of combat, where Luke moved like a seasoned warrior, his shield deflecting lethal blows while his sword cut down beast after beast.
The system notifications piled up in rapid succession, his score climbing steadily as he dispatched one monster after another.
By the time the first hour had passed, Luke was standing amidst a field of fallen creatures, his point total increasing nicely.
**********
(Meanwhile on the global forums)
This year, just like every other year, the common players logged into the livestream of the Rankers Event, eager to watch the best players in the game compete for the ultimate rewards.
The global forums were ablaze with activity, as countless threads and posts flooded in, dissecting every detail of the event.
And this year, with 'TheBoss' out of the competition, the spotlight finally shifted to others, giving them the recognition they had long deserved.
[Thread: SkyLion's Unstoppable Opening!]
> GamerBlitz99: Did you guys see that opening fight? SkyLion tanked a mega-bull's charge like it was nothing. NOTHING! He's already sitting at the top of the leaderboard!
NoobHunter69: Honestly, that guy's defense is insane. I've never seen anyone use [Guardian Shield] so efficiently.
SwordFanatic: Don't forget his offense! That [Heaven's Strike] was so clean! He made it look easy.
CasualRogue: SkyLion's always been impressive, but with TheBoss out of the way, this might actually be his year.
TumbleFan42: OUR KING IS RISING!!! SKY PRIDE!!!
---
[Thread: Finally, no TheBoss!]
> StealthMage24: Can we all take a moment to celebrate the fact that TheBoss isn't here this year?
ChaosSlayer: For real, the guy's too OP. Every year, it's just him destroying everyone else.
PuddyLover: True, but you can't deny he's entertaining. Kinda miss seeing him wreak havoc.
ArcheryPro88: Nah, I'd rather see someone else win for a change. TheBoss always felt like he was playing on another level entirely.
ShadowAssassin22: Rumor has it he wasn't banned but voluntarily didn't participate. That's even scarier.
NoobHunter69: If he's sitting out, he probably thinks this event isn't worth his time. That's how OP he is.
---
[Thread: DarkEmperor's Comeback?]
> VoidHunter: DarkEmperor is back, and he's already slaying it. Did you see how he took down that wyvern? Effortless.
MagicFury: Yeah, but he's always great in prelims. The real question is, can he survive the PvP round? He's been struggling there the last few events.
ShadowAssassin22: If he keeps playing this smart, he'll be one of the finalists for sure.
FlameMage: DarkEmperor vs. SkyLion is the match I want to see. Who else agrees?
---
[Thread: PinkLotus is the Queen we need!]
> MageEnthusiast: I know we're talking about SkyLion and DarkEmperor, but can we talk about PinkLotus? She's out there taking names!
LotusFanatic: She's always so graceful, even in battle. Watching her fight those shadow panthers was like watching art in motion.
TankWarrior77: I just don't get why she hangs out with SkyLion. She could team up with anyone.
LotusFanatic: SkyLion and PinkLotus are the power duo we didn't know we needed.
StealthMage24: Power duo? Please, don't slander my queen. She's mine!
---
The discussions raged on, opinions flying back and forth as netizens debated strategies, speculated on alliances, and placed bets on who would rise to the top.
For the first time in years, the absence of TheBoss made the competition feel open—like anyone could emerge victorious. Yet, amidst all the chatter, one thing was clear: the players who had stepped into the spotlight weren't holding back.

chapters.title: Chapter 798 - 798: Conclusion Of The Rankers Event
chapters.content:
Four hours passed by in a breeze, and Luke managed to solidify his lead at the top of the charts by over 200 points. A massive gap, considering the number two spot was held by PinkLotus with 1,800 points, already 400 points ahead of the number three, DarkEmperor.
As Luke wiped the sweat from his brow, panting from his relentless streak of battles, a familiar system notification appeared in his vision.
[System Notification: Attention Rankers! The preliminary round will conclude in 5 minutes. Prepare yourselves for the final tally!]
Luke exhaled deeply, stepping back from the carcass of yet another venomous wyvern he had slain. He glanced at the leaderboard displayed in the system menu and felt a surge of satisfaction as he saw his name, SkyLion, firmly at the top with 2,000 points.
"What the… I'm in the lead?" he muttered, genuinely surprised. He hadn't expected to dominate the preliminary round so thoroughly, but the scoreboard didn't lie. While his relentless efforts accounted for much of his success, Luke remained blissfully unaware of the subtle intervention that had steered high-value monsters his way throughout the event.
The last five minutes passed without much incident, as most rankers focused on securing their positions rather than taking unnecessary risks.
When the final system notification rang out, the hunting grounds dissolved into golden particles, and the surviving rankers were teleported to a new location.
Luke blinked as his surroundings changed to a grand coliseum-like space, its architecture a blend of medieval and futuristic designs.
Standing amidst the top 100 qualifiers, he took a moment to scan the crowd.
[System Notification: Preliminary Round Complete! The top 100 rankers have been seeded into the tournament brackets. Match pairings will now be determined.]
As the notification flashed, a massive holographic board appeared in the sky, displaying the names and ranks of all 100 qualifiers. Luke noticed his name at the very top, followed by PinkLotus, DarkEmperor, and other familiar names.
"To ensure fairness," Raya's voice rang out, addressing the rankers, "the top 100 players have been seeded into an elimination-style bracket. The number one seed will face the number 100 seed, the number two seed will face number 99, and so on. This ensures the strongest rankers do not clash prematurely."
Luke smirked as he realized the advantage of being the top seed—he would face the weakest qualifier, someone who had barely scraped into the top 100.
The match-ups began populating on the holographic board, and Luke's opponent was revealed: ShadowHawk, a name he didn't recognize. A quick glance at the stats showed ShadowHawk had finished the preliminary round with just 400 points.
"Perfect," Luke muttered under his breath, gripping his sword. "Let's see if this ShadowHawk can even last five minutes."
As the match-ups were finalized, Raya's voice echoed once more: "Prepare yourselves, rankers. The first round begins in ten minutes. Good luck."
*********
Luke vs Shadowhawk was a brief fight that ended with Luke defeating his opponent in just under 30 seconds in a one sided beatdown.
Although he was not a 'Master' warrior yet, Luke was far stronger than an average ranker, with much faster reflexes and moveset thanks to his daily practice of the 'Mind Meditation Manual'.
His opponent, an Assassin Class player, was at a significant disadvantage against him with his high defence and balanced build and his strategy of wearing opponents down.
ShadowHawk barely managed to get a few strikes in before Luke countered with a perfectly timed [Blazing Cyclone], sending the Assassin flying across the arena.
The system notification confirmed his victory:
[System Notification: SkyLion has defeated ShadowHawk. Time: 27 seconds.]
Luke sheathed his sword and left the arena with a calm expression, his mind already focused on the next round.
The second round proved to be slightly more challenging. His opponent, IronFang, was a tanky Berserker who relied on brute force and relentless aggression.
The fight dragged out for almost five minutes as IronFang's near-impenetrable defense tested Luke's patience. However, a calculated use of [Heaven's Strike] broke through the Berserker's guard, and Luke finished him with a clean slash to the torso.
[System Notification: SkyLion has defeated IronFang. Time: 4 minutes, 52 seconds.]
By the quarterfinals, Luke's confidence in his own skills and abilities had skyrocketed.
His opponent, FlameCaster, a Mage Class player, posed a unique challenge. The battle was a spectacle of fireballs and shield parries, with Luke gradually closing the distance to neutralize the mage's ranged advantage.
However, once within striking range, Luke unleashed a flurry of attacks, forcing FlameCaster to concede.
[System Notification: SkyLion has defeated FlameCaster. Time: 6 minutes, 18 seconds.]
This victory for him meant that he was poised to face 'DarkEmperor' in the semi-final round next, who had also advanced through the tournament nearly untested, setting up the stage for an exciting rematch between two of the game's best players.
Despite having won their last bout, Luke did not underestimate Cervantez at all in the semi-finals when the two of them clashed, as he knew that Cervantez must have learned and evolved a lot from their last fight.
And just as he expected, Cervantez had indeed evolved significantly since their last fight, with him having found a solid way to counter Luke's suplex, by ensuring that he never got caught in it.
Continuously fighting at an arm's length away, he stayed away from Luke's grappling range, ensuring that Luke had to work hard for his victory.
However, win he did, as after a lengthy battle that lasted over 1 hour 23 minutes, it was Cervantez's endurance that proved to be inferior to Luke, who finally managed to land a critical blow on his slow and tired opponent to secure the win.
"Good Fight!" Luke commented once they were done, as netizens throughout the global forums applauded this fight as the best they've ever seen in the world of Terra Nova Online.
It was the most evenly-matched and tactically genius bout that showed the peak of the knight class versus the magic swordsman class that was probably never going to be recreated again.
Finally, for the finals, contrary to Luke's expectations, PinkLotus decided to forfeit the match right at the start, choosing to kiss him at the centre of the battleground instead, as she gifted him the eventual victory of the fourth and final rankers event.

chapters.title: Chapter 799 - 799: Power Ranks
chapters.content:
(Leo's POV, the real world, Arc Ship)
Leo marched onto Captain Kid's cabin in a happy mood post Luke's win in the final round of the rankers tournament.
Their plan to ensure his victory appeared to have worked flawlessly, evident in Luke's sheer exhilaration as he shared the joy of his triumph with Leo after logging out of the game.
The four of them celebrated his victory briefly at their home before Leo headed over to meet Captain Kid, however, Leo hoped for him to have won after defeating PinkLotus, but her forefitting the match wasn't too bad either.
Leo stepped into Captain Kid's cabin, the door creaking softly as it closed behind him.
The Captain stood quickly, a mix of nervousness and eagerness flashing across his face.
He knew he had done a good job and was expecting Leo to praise him for it, but still felt nervous about what he was going to say.
"Well, Captain," Leo began, his voice casual but carrying an edge that kept Kid on his toes. "You didn't mess our plan up. I suppose that's worth something."
Kid let out a breath he hadn't realized he was holding and forced a grin. "I'd say more than something, wouldn't you? Luke's victory was a masterpiece. Perfectly executed," he added, scratching the back of his neck, "I can't say I expected PinkLotus to forfeit the final match like that, but I controlled every other variable perfectly."
Leo smirked, leaning against the edge of Kid's desk. "Yeah you did nice captain, I might let you off from your slave collar really soon if you keep this up. Also yeah, I too did not expect sister-in-law to just forefit the match, considering her otherwise competitive nature, however, it seems like she's more fond of my brother than what I give her credit for."
Kid nodded, agreeing with his assessment. "In my defense, no one could've predicted she'd just hand him the victory—and kiss him in front of millions, no less. It was a bold move, but… kind of a perfect ending, don't you think?"
Leo's smirk widened, though his eyes held a flicker of amusement. "Perfect for the viewers, maybe. I doubt the rankers who lost to Luke feel the same."
Kid laughed awkwardly, clearly relieved that Leo's mood seemed lighter than usual.
"So, now that Luke's win is a done deal, as long as I complete imparting outer world knowledge to you for 25 more days, I'll be a free man right?" Kid asked nervously, as he writhed his hands.
Leo didn't respond immediately. Instead, he leaned back in the chair across from Kid's desk, his gaze drifting toward the small cabinet in the rooms corner.
"Sure. As long as the lessons you impart me everyday are meaningful, I'd say you have paid me back fairly" Leo agreed, prompting Kid to let out a sigh of relief.
Now that the most difficult aspect of his freedom was already completed, the rest was easily manageable.
"Well, now that Luke's win is behind us," Kid said, clearing his throat and straightening in his seat, "I think it's a good time to move on to today's lesson."
Leo raised an eyebrow, his relaxed posture shifting slightly. "You're eager to teach today, huh? What lesson have you prepared for me today?"
Kid leaned forward, his fingers drumming lightly on the desk. "I thought we could cover something practical—something you'll need to know as you step into the wider universe. Specifically, the treatment and expectations for warriors at different levels…. And the difficulty to reach that tier."
Leo gestured for him to continue, his interest mildly piqued.
"Alright," Kid began, pulling up a small holographic display from his desk. "In the universe, warriors are broadly categorized into tiers: Amateurs, Masters, Grandmasters, Transcendents, Monarchs, Demi-Gods, and Gods. These titles aren't just for show—they define your status, rights, and opportunities in society."
He paused, allowing Leo to absorb the hierarchy.
"The 'Master' realm," Kid continued, "is the absolute minimum requirement for being acknowledged as a true warrior. Without reaching this level, you're little more than a glorified amateur, treated as expendable and lacking basic rights. Those below Master level are often relegated to cannon fodder in wars, grunt work in mercenary groups, or menial labor for powerful organizations. They struggle to survive and unless they belong to some proper family, live miserable lives."
Leo's eyes narrowed slightly, his expression growing serious. "So you're saying you have to reach Master to even be considered a citizen?"
"Exactly, in most places it's like that, being a master means you get proper burial rights, travel rights and so on.
While amateurs aren't exactly treated the same as animals, there are many practical freedoms that they don't enjoy" Kid confirmed.
"Once you hit the Master realm, things change. You're given basic rights, acknowledged as a proper individual with value, and actively recruited by organizations. At this level, you can expect reasonable compensation for your skills, training opportunities, and even some political privileges depending on the planet or faction you're part of."
Leo nodded thoughtfully, the implications settling in. "And Grandmasters? What about them?"
Kid's expression shifted, a hint of awe creeping into his voice. "Grandmasters are in an entirely different league. To be a Grandmaster is to be revered, not just respected. They're seen as the backbone of elite organizations, the ones who command armies, lead divisions, and hold sway over entire regions."
He leaned back, letting the weight of his words linger. "A Grandmaster is a symbol of stability and power. They're rare, even on a universal scale. Wherever they go, they're treated with a mix of fear and admiration. But it's not just the status—it's the influence they wield. A single Grandmaster can turn the tide of a war."
Leo's gaze didn't waver as he absorbed the information. "So, being a Master is survival. Being a Grandmaster is dominance."
"Precisely," Kid replied, his tone growing more solemn. "But it's not just about power. It's about the responsibilities and expectations that come with it. Grandmasters don't live simple lives. Most are Emperors, powerful generals and rule over continents."
Leo leaned forward slightly, his curiosity now fully piqued. "And what happens when someone surpasses even that? What does it mean to be a Transcendent?"
Kids breath hitched at that question, for now was the real interesting part.

chapters.title: Chapter 800 - 800: Power System
chapters.content:
(Leo's POV, the real world, Arc Ship)
"And what happens when someone surpasses even that? What does it mean to be a Transcendent?" Leo asked, his curiosity piquing as he couldn't even begin to fathom the kind of power a Transcendent-level warrior would wield.
Currently, as a Master warrior, the path to becoming a Grandmaster already felt arduous.
Despite his considerable talents, his progress indicated he'd need at least two more years to reach that stage.
And hence, the idea of transcending even beyond Grandmaster seemed almost mythical, a distant, unattainable horizon.
"Transcendent warriors," Kid began, his usual confidence giving way to reverence, "are on an entirely different playing field."
Kid's voice lowered slightly as if discussing something sacred. "Transcendent warriors are the overlords of planets. They don't just control cities or regions—they oversee entire planets. Their power is the stuff of legends. They can destroy cities in minutes, and their attacks can shatter mountains. Entire armies would crumble before a single Transcendent."
Leo's fingers tapped against the armrest of his chair, his eyes narrowing. "So, they're not just warriors—they're forces of nature."
"Exactly," Kid agreed, leaning forward. "Their names and deeds are etched into the annals of universal history. Even the most powerful organizations treat them as VIPs. No city, faction, or empire dares to disrespect them. At this stage, warriors begin to reverse the effects of aging on their bodies. A Transcendent can live for hundreds and hundreds of years, maintaining their peak condition."
Leo nodded slowly, the weight of the explanation sinking in. "And the gap between a Grandmaster and a Transcendent? How big is it?"
"Massive," Kid replied without hesitation. "The difference between every tier up to this point is about a hundredfold. A Grandmaster might seem invincible to most, but in the presence of a Transcendent, they're little more than a pebble before a boulder."
Leo let out a low whistle, a flicker of disbelief crossing his face. "And after that? What about Monarchs?"
Kid's lips curled into a faint smile, one tinged with admiration. "After Transcendents, we reach Monarchs. They're even rarer—a thousand, perhaps less, in the entire universe. Monarchs aren't just warriors; they're the patriarchs of vast clans that span multiple planets. They're the overlords of entire planetary systems."
He paused, his voice softening. "Monarchs are beings who walk with unparalleled authority. They exude charisma, power, and wisdom. Even Gods respect them, and their influence shapes entire galactic territories."
"And their strength compared to Transcendents?" Leo pressed, leaning forward.
"This is where the pattern shifts," Kid explained. "The leap from Transcendent to Monarch isn't a hundredfold. It's about ten times. A significant leap, yes, but not the staggering chasm we've seen before."
Leo's brow furrowed. "So, it's more of a transitional stage?"
"You could say that," Kid replied. "But don't mistake the smaller gap for insignificance. Monarchs command immense power, and their influence is unmatched below the divine tier."
"And beyond that? What about the Gods?" Leo asked, his voice steady but tinged with intrigue.
Kid inhaled deeply. "Demi-Gods….. Gods come after demi-gods, first there are demi gods"
Leo raised an eyebrow. "Demi-Gods? Sounds a bit… over the top."
Kid chuckled softly. "It's not just dramatic—it's fitting. Demi-Gods are beings on the cusp of divinity. Their raw strength though comparable to Monarchs, is bolstered by their nascent understanding of universal laws. It's this grasp of higher principles that sets them apart."
"A Demi-God is about ten times as strong as a Monarch, completing the usual tier system. However, while they're almost divine, living for thousands of years, they're not quite Gods yet, for they can still be hurt by mortal weapons.
So. Theoretically, any (Semi-Divine) level blade that you wield in the world of Terra Nova Online, can hurt a Demi-God, but the same doesn't apply for God's"
Leo's fingers tightened on the armrest.
"Oh?" he said in surprise, as Kid nodded.
"Gods are the apex of existence. They've mastered the laws of space, time, and existence itself. They exist outside the confines of three-dimensional reality. They're not just immortal in the sense of living forever—they are literally untouchable.
They cannot be harmed by physical weapons and have simply transcended every physical limitation of the universe by mastering the laws of space and time."
Leo didn't respond immediately, his gaze distant as he processed the gravity of Kid's words. "So, Gods… they're untouchable. Completely beyond reach."
"Exactly," Kid confirmed. "They are the ultimate beings. Nothing short of another God could rival their power. Their lives are shrouded in mystery, but their influence is felt across the universe. Their mere existence shapes reality."
Leo exhaled slowly, leaning back in his chair. "So, the journey from Master to Grandmaster is just the start."
Kid nodded. "It's a steep climb, Leo. But understanding the hierarchy is essential if you want to navigate the universe. Each tier brings not just power but respect, enemies and a whole new set of challenges."
"Never underestimate the climb, Leo. It's a path few survive. Not because they are not talented, but because the higher you grow in power the more political turmoil you face.
Gods don't want other individuals becoming Gods if they don't like them, and will do everything in their power to stop someone they don't favor from becoming one.
Which is why the climb to the top largely depends on your backing, and why the universe is linearly divided into a few strongest powers" Kid concluded, as Leo let out a deep sigh.
The politics of the actual universe were much more complicated than the world of Terra Nova Online, and although he was the Emperor and the top dog here, he was soon going to be relegated to the bottom all over again.
—--------

chapters.title: Chapter 801 - 801: Learning Blade Switch
chapters.content:
Life without meditation felt painfully mundane to Leo, for he had become a maniac that could no longer sit idle and pass time cooking and painting like an ordinary person.
Meditation, that once felt like a challenging chore, had slowly become something he enjoyed—an addiction he couldn't shake.
Hence, now, in its absence, he felt like a drug addict in withdrawal, restless and irritable without his daily dose.
With the meditation manual safely stored at home, the constant urge to meditate, even for just an hour a day, gnawed at him, for without meditation, all his hard-earned new-blood cells were bound to die within 120 days, undoing months of painstaking progress.
The instructions in the marrow meditation manual were clear: until he reached a 50% replacement rate, his body wouldn't learn to produce the new cells on its own. And at his current 22% replacement rate, Leo could already feel himself regressing—his strength, reflexes, and vitality slipping away bit by bit.
'This is so frustrating… I'm going to grow weaker in the coming days,' he thought grimly, as seeking a distraction from his predicament, Leo shifted his focus to mastering [Blade Switch].
Blade Switch was, by far, the most complicated technique he had ever encountered.
While he had grasped its fundamentals in the game-world, bringing that knowledge into reality was proving to be a monumental challenge.
The technique worked by creating an accelerated mana pathway between two points in space, allowing the caster to traverse those points at nearly instantaneous speeds.
This gave the illusion of teleportation, though it did not break the laws of space and time.
The brilliance of Blade Switch lay in its ability to propel the user at three times the speed of sound.
For distances under 50 meters, this resulted in travel times so brief they felt instantaneous.
The method by which the technique achieved these speeds involved enchanting a blade with a mana thread that connected the caster's mana core to the blade.
This thread then acted as a super-elastic rope, instantly contracting when recalled, pulling the user toward the thrown dagger at staggering speeds.
However, the technique had its limitations.
Since it didn't involve actual spatial distortion or true teleportation, the path between the two points had to remain unobstructed.
Walls, barriers, or narrow gaps would result in injury—or worse, a complete failure of the technique.
For instance, if a dagger was thrown through a window and Blade Switch was activated, the caster would need the window to be wide enough to pass through unharmed, or they could end up stuck or injured trying to squeeze through the gap.
However, despite this limitation, Blade Switch was an invaluable tool in an open battlefield, where its speed and precision gave users a decisive edge.
Mastering it, however, required Leo to push both his body and his mana control to their absolute limits, for just understanding this technique's basic fundamentals was no child's play.
As per the skill scroll in the game, mastering the technique required mastering three different fundamental techniques—each as complex and demanding as the skill itself.
The first step was learning how to create the hyper-elastic mana rope. This rope served as the core mechanism of Blade Switch, connecting the caster's mana core to the dagger they threw. It had to be extraordinarily resilient, capable of withstanding the incredible tension created by pulling a human body at three times the speed of sound.
The elasticity and strength of this mana rope had to be perfectly balanced—too weak, and it would snap; too rigid, and it wouldn't provide the acceleration required for the technique. This required an extreme level of mana control and precision, as the rope needed to respond instantly to the caster's recall command without losing stability.
Thankfully for Leo however, he had already learnt how to alter the properties of mana and how to shape them into threads while he was mastering [Shadowbind] and hence he had some knowledge on how to approach this problem through trial and error.
The second step to mastering the technique however, was to learn how to reinforce one's body to withstand the immense forces generated during the journey.
The sudden acceleration to supersonic speeds could easily snap the spine or cause severe internal injuries if the body wasn't adequately prepared.
This involved creating a layer of mana reinforcement around the caster's bones and joints, particularly the spine, to prevent whiplash or structural damage. In addition to this, the user had to master the art of casting a barrier around themselves to minimize air resistance. Without this barrier, the sheer drag from the air at such high speeds could cause burns, tears, or even dismemberment.
The third and final step was attaching the mana thread to the dagger in such a way that the thread's pull didn't interfere with the dagger's flight path.
The thread had to remain tethered securely to the dagger, yet the dagger itself needed to remain unaffected by the thread's tension—free to fly straight and true. This required a delicate calibration of mana flow, ensuring that the thread's force only acted on the caster when recalled and not on the dagger itself.
A poorly executed attachment would result in the dagger veering off course or the thread snapping prematurely, rendering the technique useless.
Once these three fundamental techniques were mastered individually, the real challenge began: putting them together seamlessly.
Blade Switch demanded not just technical skill but also impeccable timing and instinct. The user had to throw the dagger, activate the mana thread, reinforce their body, and recall the thread all in one fluid motion—executed with split-second precision.
Even the slightest hesitation or misstep could lead to catastrophic failure, making this technique one of the most dangerous to learn but also one of the most rewarding to master.
And thankfully for Leo, the challenging nature of mastering the technique was the exact distraction that he needed in his mundane daily life, for he could place all his brains behind how to solve the problems he faced during training and remain entertained as he killed his non-gaming time.

chapters.title: Chapter 802 - 802: First Phase
chapters.content:
Over the next two months, Leo struggled a lot with the Blade Switch technique, finding the transition from the VR world to reality far more grueling than he had initially expected.
Unlike in Terra Nova Online, where his stamina and mana could be replenished with potions, the real world had no such conveniences.
Every mistake drained his energy, and every session of training took a real toll on his body, forcing him to finally acknowledge the rigid limitations of human endurance.
At his peak, Leo could only train rigorously for about two hours before exhaustion set in, and pushing beyond that only led to diminishing returns.
For the first time, he experienced the true burdens of training in a real-world setting—burning muscles, aching joints, and the frustratingly slow process of recovery that no elixir or super recovery food could accelerate.
Each morning, he would wake up sore from the previous day's exertions, and no matter how much he willed himself to move faster, his body demanded its due rest.
He quickly realized that without proper recovery, he wasn't going to make any meaningful progress.
Thus, Leo had to adapt.
He adjusted his schedule, ensuring he ate high-protein meals to aid muscle recovery and maintained strict rest cycles.
And although he had always taken care of his body, this was the first time he had to do so with such a methodical approach—tracking his calorie intake, his mana expenditure, and the optimal rest needed between training sessions.
If he didn't do this, his energy levels would be drained too fast, and his training would suffer.
However, even with all these adjustments, progress came painfully slow.
The first phase—creating the hyper-elastic mana rope—was deceptively simple in theory but incredibly difficult to execute.
Despite possessing knowledge on how to create mana threads from nothing, Leo struggled to add an elastic nature to them.
At first, his attempts would snap apart as soon as any force was applied, his mana dissipating like a brittle thread under tension.
Other times, he would overcompensate, making the thread too rigid, which resulted in it failing to contract properly, leaving the dagger hovering awkwardly midair instead of pulling him towards it.
For weeks, Leo tried different techniques, experimenting with various mana compositions, adjusting his flow, and reinforcing the structure of the rope.
But no matter what he tried, something always felt off.
He knew he was close—so damn close—but the difference between 'almost right' and 'perfect execution' was like trying to cross an ocean with a single step.
And every failure only tested his patience further.
There were nights he laid in bed, staring at the ceiling, replaying his mistakes in his head, trying to find the one missing piece that kept him from success.
Then, one afternoon, in the middle of his hundredth attempt that day, something clicked.
He wasn't thinking about the process anymore. His hands just moved, his mana flowed effortlessly, and in that instant, he felt the connection stabilize.
The mana rope, for the first time, held firm, and even tugged at him like he wanted to, pulling him towards the dagger, albeit at a considerably slow speed.
'What happened? What did I do right?' Leo wondered, trying to introspect as to why he succeeded on this very attempt, and after trying for a couple more times, he finally understood the secret sauce.
The secret, Leo realized, lay in harmonization—the perfect synchronization of his mana flow with the elasticity of the rope.
Before, he had been trying to brute-force the technique, molding the mana thread into a hyper-elastic rope purely through structure alone.
But the key wasn't just in the construction; it was in the way mana pulsed through it.
Mana was never meant to be static—it was energy, constantly in motion.
And by allowing it to ebb and flow naturally, instead of trying to force it into an artificial rigidity, the rope could contract and expand dynamically, maintaining the perfect balance of flexibility and strength.
'It's not about controlling it perfectly… it's about guiding it,' Leo thought, realization washing over him, as with renewed determination, he repeated the process, this time focusing on breathing with the mana, syncing its pulse with his own heartbeat.
As he did so, the thread formed more easily, stretching taut but never breaking, flexing under the strain yet never losing its tension.
On his next attempt, he threw the dagger forward, and when he willed the rope to pull, it reacted far smoother than before.
There was still resistance—his body was sluggish compared to what the finished technique demanded—but it was no longer a failure.
It was a stepping stone.
Day by day, attempt after attempt, he fine-tuned the process.
He experimented with different levels of mana flow, adjusting the density of the rope, tweaking its elasticity ever so slightly.
Some days, he found success, the rope pulling him forward in a controlled motion.
Other days, the thread snapped midway, sending him stumbling face-first into the dirt.
But progress, no matter how slow, was still progress.
Within the first week, he had managed to create a mana rope that could consistently pull him toward the dagger at a controlled speed—far slower than the actual technique's final form, but stable.
By the end of the first month, he had doubled the speed, feeling the sharp tug of acceleration, though nowhere near the supersonic pull required to execute Blade Switch at its full potential.
It was around this time that his body started to adjust to the demands of the technique.
His mana reserves, once rapidly depleting from inefficient execution, started to last longer.
His muscles, initially stiff from the unnatural force exerted on them, slowly adapted to the abrupt pulls and movements.
By the sixth week, Leo could successfully execute the pull at nearly twice the speed of sound—still not the full effect of Blade Switch, but enough to feel the sheer force of movement rattling his bones.
And with that came the next hurdle: his body wasn't ready for it.
The whiplash was brutal.
Each time he successfully increased the speed, the sudden acceleration sent shockwaves through his spine and limbs, leaving him battered and sore.
His vision blurred from the sheer momentum, and more than once, he ended up crashing into a tree or rolling across the training ground like a ragdoll.
'If I don't reinforce my body properly, I'll break before I ever master this,' Leo realized grimly.
And so, as he finally perfected the first stage, he knew it was time to move on to the second.

chapters.title: Chapter 803 - 803: Mastering Blade Switch
chapters.content:
(Leo's POV – The Arc Ship Training Grounds)
Mastering the first phase of Blade Switch had taken two long, grueling months, but now came the part that truly tested his endurance: reinforcing his body for the supersonic impact and perfecting the mana tether to the dagger.
It was one thing to be pulled at three times the speed of sound. It was another thing entirely to survive the journey.
Leo had already felt the consequences of failing to reinforce his body properly.
The first time he successfully executed the high-speed pull, he had nearly blacked out from the whiplash.
The sheer force of acceleration rattled his spine, skull, and organs, leaving him dazed for hours afterward.
His muscles screamed in agony, and he woke up the next morning feeling like he had been run over by a freight train.
And if that wasn't bad enough, the air drag at such speeds felt like a million tiny blades slicing against his skin.
Even with his master level body and new blood cell given durability, the pressure of air resistance threatened to tear him apart.
Giving him the clear indication that if he wanted to survive this technique, he had to reinforce his body properly.
*********
Leo approached Phase Two the same way he did with Phase One: breaking it down into components.
The goal was twofold:
Firstly, to reinforce his skeletal structure, especially his spine, to withstand the abrupt acceleration.
Secondly, to create an aerodynamic mana barrier to negate air resistance.
The first task was difficult, but not impossible.
Leo was no stranger to body reinforcement techniques.
He had already hardened his skeletal structure through the Marrow Meditation Manual, making his bones denser than the average Master warrior.
However, the problem wasn't just about durability—it was about shock absorption.
His body needed to distribute the impact evenly, or the sheer force would cause his spine to compress like an accordion.
The solution?
Leo had to layer his mana defenses around his skeletal structure, not in a rigid way, but in a manner that let his body flex slightly upon impact—like how a tree bent in a storm instead of snapping outright.
This required precise mana control, something Leo was naturally skilled at.
It took him two weeks of trial and error, reinforcing different muscle groups and shifting mana distributions, but eventually, he found the right balance.
Now, whenever he used Blade Switch, he could feel his mana absorbing the shock, spreading the force evenly throughout his body instead of concentrating it on a single vulnerable point.
The second issue—the air drag—was trickier.
At the speeds he was moving, even the air felt like a solid wall.
Leo had to figure out a way to make himself aerodynamically stable while moving at supersonic speeds.
For this, he studied the way wind flowed around projectiles.
He quickly realized that a single-layered barrier wasn't enough.
Instead, he had to create a compressed mana field shaped like a spearhead around himself, minimizing air resistance.
At first, his barrier collapsed the moment he moved too fast, causing him to violently tumble through the air.
But with enough adjustments over another two weeks, he perfected it.
Now, whenever he moved, the mana barrier wrapped around him like a second skin, parting the air smoothly instead of fighting against it.
Meaning that at last, Phase Two was complete.
********
With his body finally reinforced for supersonic movement, all that remained was the final challenge—perfecting the mana tether so that it only affected him and not the dagger.
At its core, Blade Switch functioned by connecting the user to the thrown blade through a hyper-elastic mana thread.
But the issue was balance.
If the thread was too rigid, it would pull the dagger backward toward the caster instead of pulling the caster toward the dagger.
If the thread was too loose, the connection would snap prematurely.
Leo needed a way to anchor the tether to the dagger while ensuring that the dagger remained unaffected by the pull.
This turned out to be one of the trickiest aspects of the technique.
For weeks, every time he executed Blade Switch, the dagger either veered off course, got dragged backward, or wobbled unpredictably in the air.
It was frustrating beyond belief.
He needed to find a way to lock the dagger in place midair for just a fraction of a second, allowing himself to reach it before it moved further.
Then, after another month of trial and error, he finally discovered the missing link.
Instead of attaching the tether to the dagger directly, he needed to anchor the thread to a fixed point in space.
By forming a micro-mana lock around the dagger's tip, the blade remained momentarily suspended when the pull was activated, allowing him to be dragged without affecting the dagger's trajectory.
It was a minor adjustment, but it made all the difference.
Now, Blade Switch finally worked exactly as it was supposed to.
Five months later, on the final day of his training, Leo stood at the edge of his training grounds, a familiar dagger in his grip.
His heart pounded, but this time, it wasn't out of frustration.
It was out of pure excitement.
He took a deep breath.
Then, with a flick of his wrist, he threw the dagger forward.
At the same time, his mana thread latched onto it, forming a stable connection.
His spine was reinforced. His barrier was active. The dagger was locked in place.
And then—he pulled.
BOOM!
Leo vanished from his spot.
In less than a blink, he reappeared exactly where his dagger was, landing in a controlled stance.
No tumbling. No jarring impact. No wasted motion.
For the first time since he started training, he had executed Blade Switch perfectly.
A grin spread across his face.
"Finally," he muttered.
After five months of relentless training, he had done it. He had mastered the semi-divine technique blade switch to (Basic) mastery, completing all the ingredients that he needed to finally face the Demon King in battle.

chapters.title: Chapter 804 - 804: The Boss Is Back
chapters.content:
(Terra Nova Online, StrongHaven City)
The game world had changed significantly in the five months since Leo had last logged in, as the countdown to the Arc Ship's landing neared its final stretch.
7 months from now, the Arc Ship was going to arrive at its destination, Planet Terra Nova, and the excitement for the landing seemed palpable now.
With the final system evaluation already complete and the journey's end in sight, many players had lost the motivation to chase power and rankings, opting instead to take their final year in Terra Nova Online at a more leisurely pace.
Rather than grinding endlessly for strength, these players chose to enjoy the wealth they had accumulated over the years.
Bars and restaurants thrived as players indulged in luxuries they had once ignored in favor of relentless leveling.
The once-obsessed rankers who had spent every waking moment sharpening their skills were now seen lounging in cafés, savoring delicacies, or simply wandering the beautifully crafted cities they had never taken the time to appreciate.
With no further risk of relegation to Sector E and no chance of being promoted to a better life, the game's meta had shifted entirely—and it was this drastic change that surprised Leo the most when he finally logged back in.
For the first time in years, the longest queues weren't outside weapon shops, but at the finest restaurants, as Leo couldn't help but shake his head in disappointment as he witnessed this scene.
"The fools who won't work hard right now will have worse lives once we land…. This is not a time to relax, this is the time to work your ass off!" Leo noted, as he finally realized the difference between the informed elite and the common man.
Him, having knowledge of what the future held for mankind, could never see himself idling his life away like this, however, to the uninformed player who believed in the lie of a green new planet and a brand new life upon landing, working hard now without any incentive made no sense.
To them, it seemed like it was finally time to enjoy the wealth they had so painstakingly collected over the years, however, it was in fact a stupid decision.
"Well… what else can you expect? Stupid people make stupid choices, that's just how they are–" Leo concluded, shrugging his shoulders, as he made his way towards the Royal Palace.
The entire gaming world had not seen or heard a whisper of 'TheBoss' in the past 5 months since he assumed the throne, and it was finally time to remind everyone that he was still alive—
********
(At the Palace Gates)
Leo approached the grand palace gates, walking with his usual confidence. Unlike his usual tendency to sneak past obstacles or bulldoze through them, he decided, for once, to enter like a normal person.
But the moment he stepped closer, a guard in black and gold Uprising guild armor held out a hand, stopping him in his tracks.
"Hold it, sir," the guard said firmly. "The palace is off-limits to the general public. Entry is only permitted for uniformed 'Uprising' guild members."
Leo blinked. 'Did this idiot just—'
The guard gave him a once-over, his lips twitching in slight amusement. "Hah, I'll give you credit for the effort, though. Good costume. You got the whole 'TheBoss' vibe down—the robes, the broken mask, the level concealment—but you're not fooling me."
Leo stared blankly, unsure whether to be amused or insulted.
"What?" he asked flatly.
The guard smirked, shaking his head. "You think I haven't seen a hundred imposters like you before? It's practically a trend at this point. Every few days, some wannabe dresses up like 'Lord Boss,' puts on a mask, conceals their level, and strolls up here acting all high and mighty. But you can't fool me."
Leo was silent for a moment. Then, rubbing his temples, he let out a long, exasperated sigh. "Oh, for fuck's sake."
"You see," the guard continued, crossing his arms smugly, "the real 'Lord Boss'? He's got a presence. An aura so overwhelming that you feel it before he even opens his mouth. You, my guy? You just look like another roleplayer trying his luck."
Leo's brow twitched.
His grip tightened into a fist before he forced himself to exhale and relax.
There was no need to kill the idiot…..
Yet.
"You are… the most intelligent guard," Leo finally said, his voice oddly pleasant. "What's your name, player?"
The guard straightened proudly. "Name's RedWolf."
Leo extended his hand. "Nice to meet you, RedWolf."
RedWolf hesitated for a brief moment before scoffing and taking the handshake.
That was his first mistake.
The moment their palms met, Leo's grip tightened like a vice.
RedWolf's confident smirk vanished, replaced by sudden wide-eyed panic as pain shot through his fingers.
-120
Crack.
His bones protested violently.
"HOLY SH—"
Before he could finish his sentence, Leo yanked him forward effortlessly before shoving him aside like a ragdoll, sending him tumbling against the palace walls.
The next second, Leo pivoted on his heel and kicked the heavy iron gates open.
The massive doors—each weighing several tons—swung open violently, the metal screeching as they slammed against the walls.
"Fake my ass," Leo muttered as he dusted off his sleeves, striding in like he owned the place.
Which he did—
The deafening boom of the doors being forced open had every guard in the vicinity rushing forward, weapons at the ready, alarm flashing in their eyes.
Dozens of them surrounded Leo within seconds, hands gripping swords, spears, and staves.
"What's going on? Who—"
Then their eyes landed on him.
Silence.
A stunned hush fell over the palace entrance as recognition dawned upon them.
Leo let the moment linger before speaking, his voice casual, yet carrying an undeniable weight.
"Move," he said simply.
"The Emperor is here."
Awe spread across their faces.
And, as one, the guards all stepped aside.
The Emperor was here!!
—------

chapters.title: Chapter 805 - 805: Bold Declaration
chapters.content:
As Leo walked into the throne room, he found ChaosBringer already on his knees, waiting for him.
It was clear he had already heard of Leo's arrival—the commotion at the palace gates had undoubtedly reached him—prompting him to prostrate himself at the very entrance of the throne room in welcome.
"I greet the Great Emperor, the ruler of this land, the protector of the people, the greatest warrior to ever exist, the ever merciful, the most terrifying—"
Leo raised an eyebrow, his lips twitching slightly at the excessive string of titles.
"That's enough." He raised a palm, signaling for silence.
"Apologies." ChaosBringer immediately fell quiet, his voice cutting off mid-sentence as he remained kneeling. His head stayed bowed low, hands resting on his thighs in absolute submission.
Everything about his posture radiated deference—not just as a subject before a ruler, but as a man kneeling before something far greater.
After a brief pause, he finally lifted his gaze to meet Leo's, his expression one of unwavering devotion.
"It has been the greatest honor of my life to care for the empire in your absence," ChaosBringer declared, his voice laced with emotion. "Every decision I have made, every law I have enforced, has been in service of your will. I can only hope that it meets your satisfaction."
Leo studied him for a long moment, his lips curling into a silent smile.
Truth be told, he did not give a single flying fuck about the Empire or how ChaosBringer had governed it in his absence. The intricate details of rule, the policies enacted, the administration—it all meant nothing to him.
What did matter, however, was the fact that despite his absence, ChaosBringer and everyone under his command still understood one fundamental truth: they worked under him, and they were held accountable to him.
As their ruler, maintaining an aura of absolute authority was paramount. A leader who was not feared was a leader who was not respected.
And as Leo observed ChaosBringer's every movement, every subtle inflection in his voice, he was pleased to see the unmistakable tension lurking beneath his composed demeanor.
ChaosBringer was eager for approval yet prepared for rebuke—ready to bear whatever judgment Leo saw fit to bestow.
"Did you get the message I sent you regarding the mana mines?" Leo asked, recalling the last message he had sent ChaosBringer about the location of the mana mines near the ancient Assassin Alliance ruins.
ChaosBringer, still kneeling, nodded immediately. "I did receive it, My Lord, and I dispatched some of our Uprising Guild members to explore and extract its resources."
He paused momentarily, as if recalling the difficulties they had faced. "There were… complications at first. A powerful beast had been guarding the mines, and the underground labyrinth was unstable, riddled with collapses and dangerous terrain."
Leo arched an eyebrow, silently urging him to continue.
"But we managed to overcome those problems," ChaosBringer assured, his tone shifting to one of pride. "Not only did we successfully mine the mana stones, but we also recovered rare artifacts from the remnants of the Assassin Alliance. Some of them were damaged, but a few are in pristine condition."
He straightened slightly, his chest puffing out just a bit as he delivered the final report. "I am pleased to inform you that this entire endeavor alone contributed enough wealth to cover nearly 15% of our annual budget. The funds have already been allocated to purchasing much-needed resources to reinforce our border security against the demons."
Leo remained silent for a moment, absorbing the information. A well-executed operation, a significant financial gain, and an improvement to the empire's defenses.
'Not bad–' he thought, as he nodded in approval.
"And what of the border situation with the demons?" he asked, his voice calm yet commanding.
ChaosBringer's posture stiffened slightly as he prepared his response. "There have been minor issues along both the Eastern and Northern borders. Nothing catastrophic, but… problematic nonetheless."
He exhaled before elaborating. "The Eastern front has been dealing with supply chain disruptions. Our outposts there rely on a continuous flow of rations and equipment to hold the lines, but due to interference from systematic demon raiders, our shipments of weapons and rations have been delayed or outright destroyed."
Leo tilted his head, waiting for the rest.
"As for the Northern border, the issue isn't resources but morale," ChaosBringer continued. "The constant skirmishes have been dragging on with no end in sight. Soldiers are growing tired of the endless cycle of small battles that lead to nothing. No real gains, no decisive losses—just a slow, grinding war that has started to drain us both economically and strategically."
Leo nodded, seemingly unbothered by the challenges. He straightened his posture before flashing a slow, dangerous grin.
"It's your lucky day," he declared. "For I am here to solve all your problems. If I succeed there won't be a demon problem anymore, and if I lose, it won't be our problem anymore!"
ChaosBringer and the gathered officials looked up at him, intrigued but cautious.
However, Leo's next words sent a visible ripple of shock through the throne room.
"Send an envoy to the Demon King," he instructed. "Inform him that it's time to end this fight once and for all."
"Tell him that I propose a grand fight—me versus him. A battle where the winner takes all."
Murmurs broke out across the room as the weight of the proposal sank in.
ChaosBringer in particular widened his eyes in disbelief, as he alone understood just how dangerous this proposal was.
"If he wins," Leo stated matter-of-factly, "he gets the Empire. But if I win, I take the entire Demon Kingdom."
The murmurs turned into hushed gasps. The audacity of such an offer was unprecedented.
Leo's gaze was like steel as he delivered the final decree. "The sky is not wide enough for both of us. Only one of us may remain."
He let those words settle before finishing with a chilling finality, "If he is man enough, he will accept my offer. If not, then we prepare to march into demon lands and end this war on our terms."
The room fell into stunned silence.
"I don't want any innocent to die, this can end just between me and him. Hell, he can even bring his overgrown lizard to the fight. But if it comes to war, then there will be war. Either way, the Demon Kingdom shall be mine!" Leo declared, as ChaosBringer's face betrayed a flicker of alarm before he quickly masked it.
He glanced around, noting the expressions of shock, admiration, and, in some cases, sheer disbelief among the gathered officials.
They wondered if Leo was serious, or was he just testing them?
But ChaosBringer knew that Leo's words were not a bluff.
Leo never bluffed. But what he proposed did not seem easy or possible in this case.
However, if there was any man who could pull it off, it had to be him. For ChaosBringer had never seen Leo pick a fight that he could not win.
"As you command, My Lord… an envoy shall be dispatched at once." ChaosBringer said, as he deepened his bow.
'The sky isn't big enough for both of us–, what a domineering line to say. Only my Lord can say something like this,' he thought, as his eyes welled up with reverent tears.

chapters.title: Chapter 806 - 806: A crazy challenge
chapters.content:
(The Demon Capital City, Gorthalon)
A few days after Leo's bold declaration, an envoy of three human messengers, all fluent in the Demon Tongue, arrived at the massive, iron-plated gates of Gorthalon, the heart of the Demon Kingdom.
Escorted by the notorious Demon Count Vaugn, they were led through the shadowed streets, where grotesque lower demons watched them move from the shadows, their glowing eyes tracking their every movement.
Their destination was the Demon King's Palace, a colossal fortress made from weirdly shaped stones, where the Demon King and the Black Dragon resided.
From there, they were ushered directly into the Demon Courtroom, where the full might of the Demon Council awaited them.
Unlike the structured order of human courts, a full-audience Demon Court was a spectacle of raw, unbridled power—an assembly where only the strong were allowed to speak, and the weak were drowned out.
