And amongst the prideful high demons gathered that day, none seemed to be keen on letting humans speak.
The moment the envoys stepped inside, the chamber immediately erupted into jeers and mockery, demonic voices echoing like guttural growls in the vast hall.
"Puny humans, you better pray this meeting goes well, or you'll be the main course for tonight's feast!"
"Watch your tongue when speaking to the Demon King, or we shall remove it!"
"What do you weigh, tiny human? 150 pounds? My left leg weighs more than that!"
Their insults, spoken in perfect Demon Tongue, were laced with menace, their sharp-toothed grins making it impossible to tell whether they were joking or making real threats.
However, despite being flanked by dozens of high-ranking demons, the one that the messengers immediately feared the most, was unquestionably the Demon King himself.
The great third Demon Ruler Anos.
Seated at the center, upon a throne carved from blackstone and the bones of his enemies, the Demon King exuded absolute dominance.
His crimson eyes burned like molten embers, his massive frame draped in regal yet battle-worn armor.
Every breath he took seemed to carry the weight of an ancient storm, his mere presence thickening the air.
For Eren and Daemonacles, this was not their first time standing before the infamous Demon King. The memory of their last audience with him—where they were equally intimidated was still fresh in their minds.
Figir, however, was new to this experience. His fingers twitched ever so slightly as he looked at the Demon King, though he quickly steadied himself, reminding himself of why they had come.
"Silence…." Anos said eventually, raising his palm, as the Courtroom fell into order.
Then, with a sharp motion, Count Vaugn stepped forward and kneeled on the floor with one knee, as he began the introduction.
"Your Majesty, the human envoys have come bearing a message from the NEW Emperor of the Unity Empire, apparently the humans have experienced a regime change" Vaugn introduced, as silent murmurs spread throughout the room.
"Yes, scouts informed me that there seems to be a regime change in the human lands, and I was curious if it was indeed my friend 'TheBoss' who took the throne or not?" Anos asked, as Eren gulped a mouthful of saliva at the mention of the word 'Friend' in reference to 'TheBoss'.
"Indeed, Great King Anos, it is as you say. The new Emperor is indeed Lord Boss, who has assumed the throne for the past six months" Eren replied, as Anos nodded in acknowledgement.
"I hope he understands what it means to be King now…. I hope my words of advice will guide him for the days to come" the Demon King said, as murmurs of approval spread throughout the room.
"The Demon King even nurtured the new human Emperor. As expected of Great King Anos!"
"So the new human Emperor is a friend of the King? As expected, he must have helped him from the shadows!"
"The human Emperor should have come here personally to thank the King for his help. Sending messengers is impudent!"
"Did they come bearing gifts? I don't see any gifts–"
Misunderstandings began to spread within the Demon Council because of the Demon King's words, however, all the kind comments and goodwill turned into rage, once Daemonacles made his next statement.
"We are here to deliver a message on behalf of the Human Emperor, my Lord, if you don't mind…." Daemonacles urged, as Anos gestured for him to read the message.
Daemonacles unfolded the scroll sent by ChaosBringer, his fingers tightening slightly around the parchment as he prepared to read.
The court fell into a patient silence, all eyes locking onto him, as clearing his throat, he began.
"From the desk of His Imperial Majesty, Emperor 'TheBoss' of the Unity Empire—"
"To Demon King Anos of the Demon Kingdom—"
"The war between our nations has persisted long enough, and I'm sure that you agree that it is time for it to end, not through endless battles, but through a decisive conclusion."
"Thus, I propose a final battle."
"You versus me. A duel between kings, where the winner takes all."
"If you win, the Empire is yours, and we become vassals of the Demon State.
But if I win, the Demon Kingdom shall belong to me."
"The sky is not wide enough for the both of us to exist as the highest authority in this world, and hence I propose that one of us steps down."
"If you are man enough, you will accept my challenge and we shall settle this amongst one another, without sacrificing the lives of the men under us.
But If not, then prepare for war, for the Empire will march into Demon Lands."
"Decide, Demon King. The fate of your people rests upon your answer."
The moment the last word left Daemonacles' lips, the entire court froze.
For a heartbeat, silence hung in the air—thick, suffocating.
Then—
"HOW DARE HE?!" a noble roared, slamming his fist into the stone floor hard enough to crack it.
"BLASPHEMY!" another bellowed, his claws digging into the armrest of his chair.
"The human wretch summons OUR KING like a common gladiator?"
The chamber erupted into chaos.

chapters.title: Chapter 807 - 807: Challenge Accepted
chapters.content:
Leo knew, long before he sent the declaration of war, that Anos had no choice but to accept.
Just like him, the Demon King had built his reign on the same principle—"Fake it till you make it."
Both ruled not just with power, but with perception, fully aware that the moment even the slightest crack appeared in that perception, the illusion of invincibility would shatter.
And when that illusion crumbled, so would everything they had built.
Anos wasn't invincible. He wasn't overwhelmingly stronger than the Demon Counts who served under him.
In reality, his position was as precarious as it was prestigious.
Currently, his name was spoken with fear and reverence, whispered in awe as the warrior who had once tamed a Black Dragon as a mere boy.
But in truth, he was not some untouchable deity.
If fought on fair terms, he could very well lose to one of the Demon Counts beneath him.
Yet, his power remained unchallenged for one reason—no one dared to test him.
The aura of absolute dominance he projected kept his subjects in check, forcing them to kneel not because they had to, but because they believed they must.
And as long as that belief persisted, his rule remained unshaken.
But should doubt creep in… should even one whisper of his mortality reach the wrong ears, the fragile balance of fear and loyalty that sustained his rule would begin to collapse.
That was why Leo knew Anos would never refuse his challenge.
The Demon King couldn't afford to.
To reject a duel against the human emperor would be to admit weakness.
And in a kingdom where strength was the only currency, weakness was a death sentence.
By denying the fight, Anos would open the floodgates for the Demon Counts to question his power.
"If he fears a mere human, what else is he hiding?"
"If he refuses battle, then is he even worthy of being king?"
"If he won't fight for his throne, perhaps someone else should take it."
Once those questions took root, his entire kingdom would descend into chaos.
That was why, from the very moment Leo sent his challenge—
The fight had already been decided.
Yet, when the words of the human emperor's declaration finished echoing through the grand Demon Court, the hall erupted into chaos.
Fury.
The air was thick with it.
Angry murmurs turned into open outrage, and soon, the chamber trembled under the roars of high-ranking demons.
"The audacity of these humans!" one noble spat, his claws digging into the stone bench.
"They insult the Great Demon King with such disrespect! Who do they think they are? Let me fight the Human Emperor first, if he survives he can face the King–" another snarled.
"To think they would even dare propose such an absurdity—"
The council was in uproar, demons slamming their fists onto tables, their magic flaring as they spoke over one another in outrage.
Only one figure remained utterly still.
Anos.
The Demon King sat on his throne, unmoving. His eyes, crimson as burning coals, remained locked onto the scroll in the messenger's trembling hands.
Then, he rose.
And the throne room fell deathly silent in an instant.
Not because Anos demanded it.
Because the sheer weight of his presence commanded it.
Slowly, he stepped forward, each footfall a measured, deliberate movement, his gaze never leaving the envoys.
Then, at last, he spoke.
"A duel?" His voice was calm—too calm. Deceptively so.
"A single duel to decide the fate of empires?" He asked, his voice conveying just how absurd he found this whole situation to be.
Eren and Daemonacles tensed as Anos's lips curled into something that was neither a smirk nor a snarl—but something in between.
"Do these humans truly believe that I require a duel to claim their lands?"
His voice was quiet now, but it carried across the vast chamber like a blade pressed against the throat of every soul present.
"Do they think I need to accept such a ridiculous offer to conquer them?"
His presence swelled, magic crackling in the air. Some of the weaker demons in the chamber instinctively flinched, lowering their gazes.
"I do not need a duel to lay waste to the Unity Empire. I could march my legions into their lands and burn their cities to the ground before their so-called emperor even had a chance to beg for mercy.
And that's already me being merciful. For if I march myself, then nothing but ashes shall remain where human cities once stood."
A wave of approval surged through the court, the demons nodding fiercely, some even growling in agreement.
Anos let them have their moment.
Then, just as quickly, he silenced them again with a single gesture.
"However..."
His tone shifted, the amusement creeping into it now, a slow, predatory smirk forming.
"If their new emperor seeks to entertain me with such an offer..." He tilted his head slightly. "Then who am I to deny the humans a lesson in power?"
A ripple of confusion spread through the room.
"Your Majesty?" one of the Demon Counts hesitantly asked.
Anos turned back to the envoys, eyes glinting with something between mockery and intrigue.
"Very well. I accept his challenge. But let us make one thing clear—"
The air thickened, as if reality itself was bending under his next words.
"I shall not fight alone."
Gasps rang through the chamber.
Even the human envoys stiffened.
Anos's smirk deepened.
"If we are to make this a spectacle, let us do it properly."
"I shall fight alongside Drogo, the Black Dragon."
The weight of those words crushed the remaining murmurs into stunned silence.
"Let the humans see with their own eyes what it means to stand before the Demon King in his full glory"
His voice turned sharp.
"Let them watch as their so-called emperor is reduced to nothing but ash beneath my feet."
He turned to Count Vaugn.
"Inform them. The duel shall take place at the eastern border. There will be witnesses from both sides. This shall not be a mere duel."
His eyes burned.
"This shall be a lesson in respect."

chapters.title: Chapter 808 - 808: Reactions
chapters.content:
News of the impending battle between the Demon King and 'TheBoss' spread like wildfire the moment The Uprising guild and ChaosBringer himself confirmed the reports on the global forums.
At first, ChaosBringer had hesitated to make the duel public, wary of the implications should Leo lose.
In his opinion, the strategically safe option was to hold the duel in private, and then boast about a victory should Leo win, or bury the fact that he lost without letting many people know.
In his strategic opinion as the regent, a defeat in front of thousands could cripple Leo's legacy in the minds of the players, which was an outcome he wished to avoid more than losing control over the Empire.
However, when Leo instructed him to make the event as grand as possible, turning it into a spectacle that neither side would ever forget, ChaosBringer had no choice but to obey.
Preparations for the event began in full swing, with a temporary arena and seating arrangements being constructed near the Eastern Border, where thousands from both the human and demon factions would gather to witness the legendary showdown.
However, it was the hype on the global forums that ballooned out of control.
The moment ChaosBringer's official post confirmed the duel, the Terra Nova Online forums exploded with discussion.
---
[Thread: What the Hell is 'TheBoss' Thinking?!]
User: ArcaneWanderer
> Bro, we're SIX MONTHS away from landing, and this lunatic is still out here chasing glory. Who does this??
User: SilverHawk42
> I don't get it either. Most of us have already made our fortunes. We're enjoying the last year of the game, chilling in luxury, and here comes 'TheBoss' betting his entire Empire on a fight with the Demon King AND The Black Dragon.
User: FrozenEdge
> Tbh, that's why he's 'TheBoss' and we're not. We settle when we're comfortable. He's out there trying to write history.
User: BigMilkersOnly
> My respect for 'TheBoss' has skyrocketed after this decision. He went silent for the last 6 months, did not participate in the rankers event, and I think he was secretly training hard to bring down the Demon King all this time.
I think he's ready now, which is why he has thrown out the challenge. Trust me when I say this guys…. 'TheBoss' is not just going to win, he's going to obliterate the Demon King in PvP battle.
User: KingSlayer69
> Y'all are so dramatic lmao. He's just a greedy bastard. Dude already owns the most land, the most wealth, the most prestige—and still, it's not enough for him. If I were him, I'd retire and enjoy the wealth I made, because if not, what was the point of all that struggle? What did he achieve by being number one?
User: Reckless
> ^ This. Some people just don't know when to stop. He could have coasted for the rest of the journey. Instead, he's literally waging war on the most powerful demon in the game for the sake of MORE.
---
Across hundreds of threads, players debated whether Leo's decision was reckless or legendary.
Some admired his relentless ambition, calling him the greatest player in the history of Terra Nova Online. Others criticized him, saying he was risking too much too late into the game.
Yet, one thing was undeniable—
The hype for the duel was reaching unprecedented levels.
---
[Thread: Place Your Bets – 'TheBoss' vs. The Demon King]
User: BloodFangHunter
> I wager 500 MP on 'TheBoss' winning. I don't care what y'all say, he's never lost a fight that mattered.
Since the value of gold coins in the game is depreciating fast, I'm going to bet with MP for those who have the balls to accept it.
User: ShadowMonarch
> LMFAO. You do know he's fighting THE BLACK DRAGON too, right? Even if he was a match for the Demon King (which is debatable), that dragon alone is a world boss-level monster.
Defeating him is impossible—
User: InfernoMancer
> That's exactly why this is going to be the greatest PvP event in the game's history. Nobody's ever pulled a stunt like this before. Win or lose, this fight is going to be one for the legends.
User: ValhallaBound
> Agreed. At the end of the day, whether you love or hate him, 'TheBoss' is the only one in this game who still plays like it's life and death.
—
The boss's decision to fight the Demon King brought in a new spark of excitement to the game world that was not present within it for many days.
Players, no matter where within the game world, started making their way towards the Eastern Border, eager to watch this epic fight unfold live before their very eyes.
The game world had lost most of its meaning anyways, and with more and more players no longer interested in levelling or growing stronger, an event like this certainty piqued their interest.
The fight was no longer just about the Empire vs. the Demon Kingdom.
It was about legacy.
The greatest player of Terra Nova Online was about to put everything on the line, in one final, all-or-nothing war.
And the entire world was watching.
Some hoped for him to win, some hoped for him to lose. However, everyone was curious to see how it ended.
'TheBoss' had never lost a fight before, and his haters desperately wanted to see him lose just once before the game concluded.
On the other hand, The Demon King and the Black Dragon were the most hyped antagonists of the game world.
Memories of them destroying the Southern Capital City a few years ago still remained fresh in the minds of many who witnessed it live, or saw the destruction clips on the forums later.
To them, it seemed inconceivable that a player could challenge or hope to defeat such beings, however, because it was 'TheBoss' making the challenge, they wondered if it was truly possible?
Such was the aura that Leo had developed as a player over the years, that even when he fought the most improbable of fights, nobody could really count him out.

chapters.title: Chapter 809 - 809: Dumpy's Growth
chapters.content:
(Dumpy's POV, Terra Nova Online)
In the five months that Leo had been absent from the game world, Dumpy had undergone a radical transformation, pushing himself to evolve beyond his previous limits.
His looks, that were once marked with a childish roundness, or excess baby fat, were completely gone now.
Discarded in full, just like his cute and clumsy attitude, that was now replaced with a measured calm of an adult.
Now, Dumpy looked powerful—his limbs thick with solid muscle as his once soft exterior was now replaced with a firm, battle-hardened texture.
Over the last five months, his head crest had grown more pronounced, giving him a regal and imposing appearance, while his paws had sharpened to the point where they behaved akin to claws, capable of carving through solid rock with ease.
No longer a young frog—he had become a behemoth, a true apex predator of the battlefield.
As now, at his peak size, he stood larger than an adult dragon, towering at 85 feet in height and spreading 50 feet in width.
His sheer mass alone was enough to intimidate, and when he moved, the ground trembled beneath him like rolling thunder.
But his growth was not limited to size or physique—for his very biology had evolved into something far more deadly.
His spit, once merely corrosive, had now transformed into a devastating weapon.
A single drop of his saliva could set entire trees ablaze upon contact.
While a glob of it could melt through boulders within seconds, reducing them to nothing but bubbling molten rock.
Infact, the venom in his body had grown so potent that even the air around his expelled spit carried a toxic presence, capable of making lesser creatures collapse instantly, their nerves shutting down in violent spasms.
But perhaps the most terrifying change was his skin.
Dumpy had always carried a natural poison in his skin, that he could secrete at will, but now, that poison had grown so strong, that whenever Dumpy let it out, it unintentionally started to disrupt entire ecosystems.
For starters, if he chose to bathe in a small stream, the entire river downstream would turn into a poisonous wasteland, killing thousands of fish and plant life within minutes, as even the most resilient of creatures—those with natural resistance to toxins—were sure to find themselves weakened, their bodies slowly shutting down from prolonged exposure.
Yet, for all his newfound deadliness, Dumpy was not just a mindless brute and over the past few months, his speed, combat ability, and battle instincts had also grown sharper.
For months, he had trained against his Lord Grandfather, Ben Faulkner, and after surpassing the old warrior in raw power and speed, the two had shifted from simple sparring to advanced combat scenarios, to provide Dumpy with a new challenge everyday.
These were no longer fights where the strongest won outright—they were tests of strategy, adaptability, and survival.
Everyday, Ben forced Dumpy into disadvantageous conditions, where brute force alone would not be enough to triumph.
And it was these battles that had shaped Dumpy into a refined warrior, rather than just a destructive force.
Yet, for all his progress, he was still one step away from taking that final leap to becoming a Grandmaster, as although the final battle against Drogo drew closer, he still found himself eluded from that final step that would make him a warrior of equal standing to the black dragon.
********
(Leo's POV, Terra Nova Online)
After months away, as Leo finally laid eyes on Dumpy training with Ben, he almost couldn't believe just how much his pet had grown.
The once pudgy, excitable frog that had clumsily followed him around was gone, and was replaced by a towering, battle-hardened behemoth, moving with terrifying precision and purpose.
The air shimmered with heat as Dumpy's latest attack left a section of the training ground melted beyond recognition, his venom turning stone into nothing but molten slag.
Even Ben Faulkner, the ever-composed master assassin, took their spar seriously, his blade flashing through the air as he parried Dumpy's powerful blows.
The frog had become a true monster—one worthy of legend.
Yet, the moment Dumpy sensed his arrival, he dropped everything.
Abandoning his spar with Ben, the giant frog immediately turned toward Leo, his deep, resonant voice carrying over the battlefield.
"Greetings, Lord Father, I have been patiently waiting for your return."
Leo's lips curled in amusement. Despite everything, Dumpy's devotion remained unchanged.
"Dumpy."
"Master."
Leo said, as both him and Ben exchanged brief nods.
Then, Leo's gaze instinctively flickered toward Dumpy's status bar, and the glowing numbers above his head nearly made him do a double take.
(Ancient Swamp Frog, Level 1677)
Leo blinked, exhaling softly.
Dumpy had completely surpassed him in raw strength.
And yet, despite his staggering power, there was no arrogance in his posture, no overinflated ego from his newfound status.
Instead, Dumpy lowered his massive head, pressing it slightly into the dirt in a show of respect.
He had not forgotten who he belonged to and that fact alone brought a pleased smirk to Leo's face.
"You've grown strong, Dumpy," he admitted, glancing at the scorched battlefield they had been training on.
The land itself had warped under the sheer force of his pet's training—entire sections of the ground melted away.
"Strong? This brat is not just strong, he's so strong that he can accidentally end my life while training.
He's that strong!" Ben noted, as there seemed to be genuine fear in his voice as he said these words.
"Haha, is that so?" Leo asked, as Dumpy blushed innocently.
"Lord Grandfather over praises me…. I'm still a fledgeling" Dumpy replied, as Leo felt impressed by his growing maturity.
The old Dumpy would have simply accepted the compliment, or exaggerated his strength to get more praise from Leo, however, the current him was more mature.
The current him downplayed the compliment, because with compliments came expectations, and as an adult Dumpy realized that it was better to keep expectations low and to over deliver, than to keep them high and under deliver.

chapters.title: Chapter 810 - 810: Banter
chapters.content:
"The fight against the Demon King is in four days, Dumpy. The horned maniac is my problem, but until I take him down, I need you to hold back that overgrown lizard." Leo said, as the moment the initial pleasantries were over, he cut straight to the chase without wasting any more time.
However, as he spoke that sentence, Ben, who had been casually sipping on a health potion, nearly choked, spitting out his drink, as he looked at Leo in shock.
"What? You're fighting the Demon King in four days? When did you decide to do this? And have you absolutely lost your mind?!"
His shock was palpable. The sheer absurdity of what Leo had just announced sent his old bones trembling—not with fear, but with sheer frustration.
Ben was the only one Leo kept out of the loop on his intentions to fight the Demon King, as he knew that the old man would never approve of the idea.
Ben had grown up with fear and reverence against the Demon King ingrained in his bones and hence, Leo knew that he would never approve of such a fight, which was why he deliberately hid the news from him.
However, knowing how he could no longer hide the news anymore, Leo waved his hand dismissively, as he tried to downplay the significance of the fight.
"It's a whole thing, Master. If I win, I annex the Demon-Kind into the Unity Empire, unify the whole continent under my rule. You know, the usual."
Ben's left eye twitched. "The usual?"
"It's the way to attain long-lasting peace," Leo continued, completely ignoring his master's growing exasperation.
"And what if you lose?" Ben asked, his voice cracking, as Leo simply shrugged in response.
"Well, if I lose… the humans are toast, so let's hope I don't." He replied with an innocent smile, as Ben resisted the urge to slap him hard.
For a solid two seconds, Ben stared at him in absolute silence, contemplating his entire life's decisions—especially the one where he took Leo in as his disciple.
Then, as he felt his anger rise, he felt a headache forming in his brain, as he finally began to vent in-order to not pop a vein.
"Stupid… I've raised a stupid disciple."
Ben clutched his head in despair, his voice cracking under the sheer weight of the situation. "Oh my god, I got blinded by his talents and forgot to impart onto him lessons of common sense."
He took a deep breath, then another, then another—but it wasn't working.
"And to make matters worse, the fool is stronger than me now, and I can't even hit him because he's all grown up!" Ben said, as instead of being affected by the breakdown, Leo beamed at the compliment, seemingly unfazed by everything else his master said.
"I think you're overreacting, Master. It's just a fight against a strong opponent. Nothing I can't handle. After all—"
He flexed.
"I am the strongest."
Leo declared, as at this moment, Dumpy, sensing the need to reinforce his master's confidence, rumbled in agreement.
"I agree with Lord Father. We can take the Demon King and the dragon down. For me and Master together—"
He puffed out his chest proudly. "We are unstoppable!"
Ben slapped his forehead.
"DON'T!"
He pointed a trembling finger at the giant frog, his frustration boiling over.
"Don't encourage him, you overgrown toad! If there's one person I trust less than him in battle, it's you!"
At that moment, Ben realized something deeply unsettling.
His reckless disciple was leading an equally reckless beast into the most high-profile battle in history.
The world was doomed.
"Do you not remember when we faced the demon king previously? Do you not remember how he reduced an entire city to ashes? Do you not remember how we ran for our lives that day?" Ben asked, his tone now turning serious, as finally Leo acknowledged his concerns.
"I do remember it master, but I'm a lot stronger since then. Also, someone has to put the Demon King down eventually. And who better to do it but me?
A dozen soldiers die at the border every week. The netizens live in constant fear of being uprooted from their lands.
It's about time someone put and end to this—" Leo replied, as he spoke with a conviction that Ben had not seen in him before.
"And what if you die?" Ben asked, his voice finally breaking completely, as he looked at Leo with watery eyes.
"I don't care about the Empire boy as much as I do about you and the fat toad…. The Demon King and the Dragon, they're dangerous….. and I don't have the heart in this old age to see you hurt" Ben said, as finally he admitted what was bothering him the most.
"I–" Leo began, but paused, as he could not find the right words to reply in this situation.
Ben's concern was genuine, and Leo did not have the heart to downplay it with a joke.
Thankfully for him though, the little frog did not have any such inhibitions, as just when the atmosphere seemed to be growing awkward, he said a dialogue so unbelievably manly, that words started to fail even Ben.
Dumpy said… "You're right, Lord Grandfather, we may die in this fight!"
"But it takes a real man to die and then come back without dying, and luckily for myself and Lord Father, we are real men"
Dumpy declared, as he sheathed his swords and crossed his arms to hit a cool pose.
"Damn right we are!" Leo agreed, hitting the same pose, as looking at the master-disciple duo of goofballs, Ben couldn't help but crack-up.
"Oh, what will I do with you fools? If only I could go back in time and teach you lessons in common sense instead of combat" Ben lamented, as Leo happily slung his hand over his shoulder.
"I mean, it's more important to be strong, master, because even Emperor Julien D Evanus had common sense, but he's dead now—" Leo countered, as once again Ben found himself to be speechless in front of his logic.

chapters.title: Chapter 811 - 811: It Begins
chapters.content:
(Four Days Later, The Temporary Arena Constructed Near the Eastern Border)
The temporary arena where Leo was set to fight the Demon King was absolutely massive in size.
Constructed in just under a week, it was by no means an architectural marvel, but its sheer scale was still staggering to behold.
Spanning over a kilometer in length and one and a half kilometers in width, it straddled both human and demon lands, creating an unofficial middle ground where the fate of both factions would be decided.
Towering stone battlements encircled the fighting grounds, reinforced with mana-infused metals to contain the sheer destruction that was bound to unfold.
It wasn't perfect—ChaosBringer knew that a warrior of Leo's caliber could easily break through the barriers if he wanted—but given the limited time, this was the best he could manage.
At the very least, the reinforced walls were sturdy enough to absorb shockwaves and mitigate indirect attacks, which was the bare minimum to ensure audience safety.
The match wasn't scheduled to begin for another day, yet the stands were already overflowing with spectators—hundreds of thousands of them.
Humans and demons alike had packed themselves into the makeshift viewing areas that were nothing more than primitive wooden stands held together by support beams.
Though crude, they served their purpose, and despite the long wait ahead, no one was willing to risk losing a prime spot for the greatest duel in history.
On one side sat the human forces—a sea of players and NPCs draped in armor, robes, and all manner of enchanted artifacts. Their expressions were arrogant, everyone wanted to look their best and everyone was checking the other one beside them out, to see who was more wealthy within the game.
Opposite them sat the demonic horde, their numbers just as vast, if not greater.
However, unlike the humans, who maintained some semblance of civility, the demons showed no signs of it.
They wore minimal clothing, mostly sitting bare chested, as they flexed thief muscles towards the humans, trying to intimidate the other side with their sheer natural size and strength.
And as if that wasn't enough already, they soon began to snarl and growl at random intervals, their deep, guttural voices weaving into a chaotic, deafening chorus.
At first, the humans ignored the provocation, but as the hours dragged on, it evolved into a full-blown competition to see who could be louder.
Every few minutes, a thunderous wave of human cheers and chants would shake the arena, only to be immediately drowned out by the demons' roaring counterattack.
It was no longer just a duel.
It was a war of pride.
And neither side was willing to back down.
"Fucking demon's, they think they're the bomb screaming like that? I'm so pissed—"
"Bro, look at them flexing their chest muscles at us? That pisses me off, because I'm sure they have peas for brains, but I can't shout intelligent insults at them because they won't even understand"
"Gosh, we need a Mr.Olympia here, we need someone with a physique who can put the demons to shame! Where are the sector E worker ants when you need them!"
"Well I can't believe I'm rooting for 'TheBoss' to win now. I came here hoping to see the Demon King kick his ass but the opposing demons made my blood boil.
Now I want him to win, just because I want to rub it in their obnoxious faces"
The players commented, as they discussed amongst themselves how much they hated the demons, leading to the hatred burning brighter.
"Look at the tiny humans? They want to challenge our king? They want to take our lands? Who do they think they are?"
"Look at them…. They don't even look like they eat proper meat. The Lowborn demon's can easily wipe the floor with them, they look so fragile"
"Nonono, I think you give them too much credit, I think the wives of the Lowborn warriors can easily wipe the floor with them. The humans are just snotty and arrogant, who rely of their machines and tactics to win fights.
One on one, they're dead—"
"Well I'm just excited to see the Demon King in action. I'm rooting for the human to do his best, just so that I can see the King use a fraction of his true strength to crush him.
It's been so long since we last saw the Demon King in battle. It's going to be legendary!"
The demons spoke in demon tongue, as just like the humans, they too insulted the other side and built up anticipation for the fight that was to come.
Some talked about strategy, about how the fight would play out.
Some talked about the future, about how with an endless amount of human slaves the Demon Kind was going to usher into a new golden age.
Whereas there were just a very few who genuinely took this fight seriously and were worried about the consequences of the loss.
********
(Meanwhile ChaosBringer)
ChaosBringer secretly began preparing the armies to stand guard and stop the demon invasion if Leo did indeed lose the fight.
Although ChaosBringer trusted in Leo's judgement and genuinely believed he could win, he also took it upon himself to prepare for the scenario where he did not.
Since his agreement with the Demon King was not a legally binding one, ChaosBringer did not intend to honor it should Leo actually lose, and hence he secretly prepared the armies to hold the lines and thwart off the Demon Advance, should Leo fall tomorrow.
"I hope the day where I have to defy your will does not ever come, My Lord, but I refuse to give up the Empire you have so painstakingly conquered to the demons on a whim.
Please win, for it will break my heart to defy your orders…." ChaosBringer said to himself, as he genuinely prayed that Leo did not lose tomorrow.
—------
/// A/N- Anddd it begins. The fight we have all been waiting for! ///

chapters.title: Chapter 812 - 812: Anos and Drogo
chapters.content:
(The Demon King's castle, a few hours before the fight)
A few hours before the fight, Anos found himself unable to rest.
The feeling had crept up on him slowly over the past few days, growing stronger with each passing moment, until now—on the eve of the battle—it had settled into a heavy weight in his chest.
It wasn't fear.
No, Anos was not afraid.
It was something else.
Something like a tight, lingering unease that gnawed at the back of his mind, refusing to be ignored.
He was restless, his thoughts pacing even when his body remained still, as every second that passed made him feel caged, suffocated by the weight of expectation.
It wasn't the battle itself that concerned him, but the implications that came with it.
The eyes of his people would be on him tomorrow, watching, judging, waiting to see if he still deserved to wear the crown, and the anxiety to perform, to prove his worth weighed him down.
"I'll only wear myself out, by pacing around like this…." Anos muttered to himself, as with quiet but determined steps, he walked toward Drogo's chambers, the only place that he knew would provide him with the comfort that he seeked.
Drogo lived in a cavernous den outside his castle, and as his oldest and only friend, he was the only one Anos could turn to in this eleventh hour.
"May I come in?" He said, as he stepped through the massive stone archway, leading to Drogo's home.
Upon the sound, the black dragon shifted slightly, lifting his enormous head from where he had been resting.
Their eyes met—golden against crimson.
And without missing a beat, Drogo smirked.
"What happened? You look like you lost your calm there, old friend. You're sweating like a pig," the dragon rumbled, his deep voice laced with amusement.
Anos let out a slow breath, crossing his arms as he leaned against one of the stone pillars.
"Yes… I'm feeling restless." He admitted, not ashamed to show weakness in front of his closest ally.
"Tomorrow's fight is arguably the biggest challenge I've faced yet, and the human boy I'm about to face worries me," Anos said, cracking his knuckles, waiting for Drogo to offer him some reassuring words.
Drogo chuckled, the sound reverberating through the cavern as he adjusted his wings.
"That human boy is strong, I'll give him that," he admitted.
"But you have me by your side. Even if you're weak, with me present by your side, there's no chance you'll lose." Drogo explained, his confidence absolute.
Anos let out a low scoff, shaking his head. "I know I'm not losing, old friend. I know no one can beat you." His voice was firm, unwavering.
And yet, the weight in his chest remained.
Drogo caught the hesitation in his tone instantly, his smirk fading slightly.
"Then what is it?" Drogo asked, his golden eyes narrowing slightly.
However, it seemed to be a question that Anos found genuine trouble articulating, for he turned extremely quiet for a while.
"I can't afford to show weakness, Drogo. Not even for a second." He said after a while, his voice quieter but no less intense.
"You and I both know that I am not truly as untouchable as my lore portrays me to be. My strength… it's not as absolute as my people believe it is. I rule because they believe I am the strongest. But, the moment that belief is shaken, the moment even a single whisper of doubt takes root, my rule will begin to crumble."
He ran a hand through his hair, his jaw tightening.
"Do you know what the Demon Counts have been doing these past few months?" he asked bitterly. "They've been watching. Waiting. Testing the limits of my patience. None of them dare to challenge me openly, but I can see it—the hunger in their eyes. The silent questions they don't dare voice out loud."
Drogo's golden gaze darkened slightly. "They're waiting for you to slip."
"Exactly," Anos said, his tone laced with frustration. "The moment they sense an opportunity, the moment I show even the slightest weakness, they will strike. But trust me, I will not give them that opportunity."
The Demon King inhaled deeply, steadying himself.
"That's why tomorrow's battle isn't just a fight, Drogo." Anos said, his crimson eyes burning with conviction as he finally looked up. "It's a statement."
Drogo let out a slow exhale, understanding dawning in his expression.
"You don't just want to win," he murmured. "You want to crush him and have the whole Demon Kind witness it."
Anos nodded, his fingers flexing into a fist. "I want to prove that I am the Demon King. That I am not someone to be challenged. Not by humans. Not by the Demon Counts. Not by anyone."
Silence stretched between them for a moment.
Then, slowly, a smirk crept back onto Drogo's face.
"Well, if that's the case, then there's no problem," he said, his voice laced with absolute confidence. "You have me. And I'll make sure they remember who we are. We will start the fight with a bang, showing our superiority with the very first move we make–"
The weight on Anos's chest lightened significantly at those words, as he let out a small but sharp chuckle.
"Still as arrogant as ever, aren't we?" he asked, as Drogo huffed, his tail flicking slightly.
"It's not arrogance if it's true." Drogo replied, as both friends broke into a wide grin.
Their friendship had stood the test of time for decades and it had grown to the point where either could confide completely in another.
For Drogo, the challenge that Anos faced tomorrow was not something Anos faced alone, as it was a problem that he very much looked at from a personal perspective.
For him, it was a fight that both of them had to win at any cost.
---------
/// A/N- The countdown begins, the next book will be released exactly one week from now! ///

chapters.title: Chapter 813 - 813: Entry
chapters.content:
(Next Day, The Battlefield)
The next morning, the sky was a brilliant shade of blue, with the sun hanging high at its peak.
The temperature was neither too hot, nor too cold, which made it a perfect day for the fight to be held.
The temporary arena, which had seemed so vast just a day before, now looked overwhelmed.
The stands were packed far beyond their intended capacity, with hundreds of thousands of spectators, crammed together, their collective voices blending into an overwhelming roar.
Many who couldn't find proper seats had fashioned makeshift viewing platforms—climbing trees, standing on rocky ledges, or even balancing precariously on wooden planks hastily set up above the crowd.
It was chaos. It was packed to the maximum. And throughout the collective consciousness, only one thought seemed prevalent– the battle was about to begin.
********
Standing in the highest section of the human seating area, ChaosBringer observed the sky, his sharp gaze locked onto the position of the sun.
It had reached its zenith.
Midday.
Which meant that it was finally the decided upon time for the battle to begin.
"It's time–" He said, a slow sigh escaping his lips, as he steeled his heart for what was to come next.
And just as he had anticipated, a few seconds later, the winds in the arena begin to shift, causing his coat to flutter unnaturally.
*Flap* *Flap*
A sudden, powerful gust swept across the battlefield, causing banners to ripple violently and sending loose debris skittering across the ground.
The humans in the stands turned their heads towards the sky—and saw him.
The Demon King riding atop the Black Dragon Drogo, as far beyond the demon seating area, in the distance, a monstrous black silhouette seemed to be approaching.
At first, the Demon King and his Black Dragon were mere silhouettes against the distant horizon, their approach slow and deliberate—almost like they were savoring the anticipation.
But within seconds, that illusion shattered.
In a single, powerful beat of Drogo's wings, the massive beast surged forward, closing the distance with terrifying speed.
As they neared the battlefield, Anos stood tall on the dragon's back, his gaze sweeping across the arena like a conqueror surveying his domain.
Then, just before reaching the center, Drogo twisted mid-air, circling the arena twice, his enormous wings stirring brutal winds that sent shockwaves rippling through the crowd, as dust and debris swirled violently in his wake, forcing spectators to shield their eyes as the sheer force of his flight rattled the wooden stands.
And then—
THUD.
Drogo landed.
The sheer impact sent deep tremors through the earth, shaking the very foundations of the arena itself.
The Demon King had arrived.
Silence gripped the battlefield for the briefest of moments, before
"ROOOOOOAAAAARRRRR—!"
Drogo's mighty Dragon's Roar tore through the air, a primal, deafening sound that sent shivers down the spines of even the most hardened warriors.
The very air trembled under its weight, as though the battlefield itself acknowledged the presence of an apex predator.
[System Notification:- You are in the presence of the Black Dragon 'Drogo', you have been affected by 'Dragon's Fear', all stats drop by 70%]
[System Notification:- You have been affected by 'Dragon's Fear', You have lost all mobility for 60 seconds ]
Thousands of human players suddenly saw their screens flash red, their stats dropping under the influence of the Black Dragon's presence.
On the spectator stands, many physically trembled, their faces paling, as even high-level warriors amongst the humans felt the instinctual urge to flee.
ChaosBringer, watching from above, clenched his jaw.
"So this is the power of the Black Dragon!" He muttered, as he felt his stomach roll in fear, however, there was no time to dwell on it.
Because as the dust settled, Anos dismounted—and with an effortless grace, he landed on the battlefield.
*DEMONIC SHOUTS*
As Anos dismounted, the demons went ballistic crazy with their chants, completely drowning the arena with unintelligible shouts, as Anos raised his fist in the air in response, acknowledging the love of his people.
"Holy Shit, I don't think 'TheBoss' can win this? Just look at the Demon King, he's such a massive looking dude that has the Black Dragon as his bitch, there's no-way anyone can beat that"
"I can't even read the level of the Demon King or the Black Dragon, it just shows up as a (???) for me! Just how strong are they?"
"Do you think 'TheBoss' will even show up? I mean I wouldn't after listening to that dragons roar"
The humans commented, as doubts began to emerge about Leo's odds at winning this fight.
However, just as the human side seemed to be losing morale, the sun above their heads was suddenly blotted out by a fast moving object, as a massive shadow covered the arena.
BOOM.
With a thunderous impact, a giant swamp-green blur landed directly opposite Anos, sending cracks through the battlefield.
The ground shook just as violently as when Drogo had landed—
But this time, the shock didn't come from a dragon.
It came from something bigger.
A badass frog, covered in full body Armor, and massive swords protruding out of his back.
Dumpy, now in his fully grown terrifying 85-foot behemoth form, landed like an unstoppable force.
Unlike Drogo, he let out no roar.
Instead—
"Ribbit—."
A low, cool sound escaped his throat.
Yet it was not his voice that instilled fear.
It was the sheer sight of him.
Beneath his enormous feet, the ground itself began to smolder, the rocks hissing and corroding into blackened sludge, poisoned by the lethal toxins in his skin.
For a full 2 meter radius around him, a toxic magma formed, converting solid ground into a toxic sludge, as while the sight of the Black Dragon looked intimidating, the sight of Dumpy standing tall looked no less impressive.
*Land*.
Soundlessly landing in front of Dumpy, Leo did not receive any cheers from the human crowd.
No—
Instead, he silenced the Demon Crowd, as his entry seemed to intimidate both sides equally.

chapters.title: Chapter 814 - 814: Taunts
chapters.content:
"Yo, Demon King, you're looking like you had no sleep yesterday night my brother, did you wet yourself thinking about fighting me?" Leo began, taunting the demon king, as he chuckled under his mask.
"Ha…hahaha, good one master, the Demon King does have bags under his eyes" Dumpy added, as Leo turned toward his pet and gave him a thumbs up.
The duo talked casually in the presence of the Demon King and Black Dragon, as if they were not affected by their presence at all, while the rest of the human crowd felt stunned to hear Leo's remarks.
"Is he mad? Why is he talking to the Demon King in English? The Demon race doesn't even speak English language–"
"Did he really call the Demon King 'My Brother?', is 'TheBoss' from the hood or something?"
"Hahaha! Get in there Boss! Get under your opponent's skin!"
The human crowd, that had fallen silent upon his entry, began chuckling and roaring in approval after his opening comments, as slowly but surely the atmosphere behind Leo turned rowdy.
It started slow, as at first discussions only arose amongst spectators, however, soon it evolved into a full blown chant, as a synchronized scream of
"BOSS! BOSS! BOSS!"
Ran through the arena.
"The human is taunting you before the fight Drogo, do you wish for me to translate his words? Do you want to communicate?" Drogo asked Anos telepathically, as Anos nodded in reply.
"Might as well," He said in Demon Tongue, as Drogo expanded his translation magic, to cover both Leo and Anos.
"Greetings, Human Emperor, We meet again. I see you have taken my advice to heart and have begun your journey towards becoming a true king. However, I'm sad to see that you're not quite there yet" Anos said in Demon Tongue, with Leo being the only person in the arena who was able to understand it.
"Is that so? You really think I'm not quite there yet? Brother, look around?" Leo replied, his smirk widening, as he widened his arms and signalled for the crowd to cheer him on louder.
*Cheers*
Upon his signal, the human crowd exploded into cheers, as Anos chuckled loudly at his antics.
"Yes you're not quite there yet. The people behind you, they respect you, they fear you, but they don't revere you.
You are their Emperor, but you are not their God yet and although they obey, it's not blind obedience.
You can gaud them into cheering for you, but you command them to give their lives for you and they won't. But if I do the same to my underlings they won't take another breath.
As of now, you have a long way till you become a True leader, but unfortunately for you, your time to improve has run out.
By challenging me, you have bit off more than you can chew and that's a mistake that individuals like us can never afford to make.
I'm sure you have left behind a worthy legend, but today is the day it comes to an end–" Anos said, as his calm and logical words made Leo frown.
Leo was here to fight, to brawl, and not for lectures that sounded like they came from an elder brother.
"Oh spare me the lecture—
You know nothing about me, old man. I'm nothing like you.
'Fake It Till You Make It' only works till you make it, and after that you have to take risks.
It's funny you say that I can't afford to fight you, because that's rich coming from someone that doesn't even know what comes at the end of the act.
Unlike you, I have made it. I am the strongest human and there's no one left in these parts who can hold a candle to my strength.
You are the only opponent that can excite me on this continent and today I'm gonna conquer you as well.
Not because I'm stronger than you, or smarter than you, or more handsome than you, or younger than you.
I'm gonna beat you today, just because I'm more of a man than you.
I have the balls to push past my limits and challenge opponents to fights that I know I can't win.
Which is more than you will ever have" Leo said, as he replied to the demon king's logic with childish tantrums.
"What a manchild. If this is what you think, then you and I are indeed nothing alike.
This conversation was fun while it lasted, but I think we are done here, time for the fight to begin—" The Demon King said, as with a slight tap of his foot, he jumped high and effortlessly landed on top of Drogo's back.
"Justt Bring It—" Leo said, pulling out a dagger as he assumed his fighting stance.
Over their heads, a cloud momentarily passed over the sun, dimming the intensity of the sunlight slightly, before quickly passing on, as the full intensity of the light returned.
And just as it did, the fight began.
[Dragon's Breath]
Right- Off the bat, Drogo began the fight with a full powered dragon's breath, aimed at both Leo and Dumpy at once.
The attack was so enormous and so powerful, that the ground beneath its path melted and deformed as the attack propagated forward, while the temperature of the surroundings unbearably went up by a few degrees.
*CHEERS*
The entire Demon Faction erupted in a burst of mad cheers, looking at the attack move forward, only for the humans to respond in kind when Dumpy unsheathed his sword and leapt in front of Leo to block the move.
The giant frog, without so much as breaking a sweat, simply blocked the move through his raw power, as he maintained eye-contact with the black dragon throughout.
"Today I shall kill you with my own hands, you overgrown black lizard" Dumpy declared, as just like his master, he trash talked his opponent as well.
*Snort*
"You're not yet on my level, Child" The black dragon responded, as with a quick flick of its wings, it took to the skies, changing the orientation of the battle.

chapters.title: Chapter 815 - 815: First Hit
chapters.content:
Almost as soon as the battle began and the Black Dragon unleashed [Dragon's Breath] to throw the battlefield into chaos, the Demon King began preparing his grand attack—the [Void Breaker Slash].
A semi-divine technique, the Void Breaker Slash was one of Anos's most feared moves, a devastating cleave of pure dark energy that could cut through the very fabric of space itself.
It was an attack he could only unleash twice per battle.
But once was usually enough.
He had used this move before to cut down Master Swordsman Philips in Thumba City, turning a once-proud warrior into a legend of the past.
And today, he intended to use on Leo, hoping to turn him into a legend of the past as well.
Standing atop Drogo's back, high above the battlefield, Anos lifted his massive greatsword, [Doomcaller], the dark metal gleaming under the afternoon sun.
He exhaled deeply, as a low, ominous hum filled the arena as a swirling vortex of void energy began to manifest around his sword.
The air crackled, space itself warping unnaturally as the darkness around his blade condensed, growing heavier and more unstable.
The moment the humans saw the attack building, panic erupted among their ranks.
"Wait, wait, wait—what the hell is that?!"
"That's Void Breaker Slash! The move the Demon King used in Thumba City, i've seen fragmented clips of it before"
"That's his best move, can The Boss take it?!!"
The Demon side, however, smirked.
The Demon Counts seated in the highest seats of the viewing stands exchanged knowing glances, their lips curling into amused sneers.
"Hah. It's already over."
"Foolish humans. They really thought their 'Emperor' had a chance."
"Once His Majesty swings, that human and his slimy frog will be sliced in two."
"He won't even be able to see it coming. The might of the Demon King is unquestionable!"
Anos tightened his grip on his greatsword, feeling the weight of power coursing through his body.
Then—
He swung.
[VOID BREAKER SLASH]!
As a massive arc of void energy erupted from his blade, roaring forward like an apocalyptic crescent of destruction.
The attack was so powerful that the very sky above the arena seemed to darken, its sheer force tearing through the battlefield as it ripped apart the ground beneath it, leaving a deep trench of pure nothingness in its wake.
It was fast.
Too fast.
The attack surged toward Leo like an inescapable judgment.
The human crowd screamed.
The demons laughed.
But Leo—
Leo stood still.
He didn't move.
Didn't blink.
Didn't even breathe.
Instead, he calmly watched as the Void Breaker Slash came hurtling toward him, growing larger, more violent, more unstoppable.
And then— just before it struck—
His dagger flashed blue.
[FULL COUNTER]!
BOOOOOOM!
The instant the Void Breaker Slash collided with his dagger, a violent shockwave exploded outward, sending dust and debris flying in all directions.
Sparks flew.
The ground beneath Leo cracked under the force.
For a split second, it looked like he would be completely consumed by the attack—
But then—
With a sharp twist of his wrist, Leo redirected the entire force of the attack, sending it back toward its sender—
And that too with twice the power.
The massive crescent of void energy, now supercharged with Leo's counter, roared back toward Anos, the black energy distorting violently as it ripped through space.
The Demon Counts' smirks vanished.
Their eyes widened in pure disbelief.
"W-WHAT?!"
"HOW—?!"
"That's impossible!"
Anos's eyes narrowed sharply as he watched his own attack come barreling back toward him.
As for the first time—
His heartbeat quickened.
"Drogo…" He mouthed, as the Black Dragon squinted his eyes and cast an emergency protective spell around both of them.
[Defensive Veil]
A shell of light blue barrier covered the duo, shielding them from the incoming blow, however, the power of the slash was just too much for the barrier to hold-on for long.
Although the barrier successfully managed to mitigate some of the strength of the attack, in the end it shattered and the attack went on to draw first blood, as although Drogo shielded the Demon King completely, his own scales took a hit, with thick blood oozing down his body.
-17,000
A deep, guttural growl rumbled from Drogo's throat as the aftermath of the attack settled.
The mighty Black Dragon, revered across the demon lands, had just been wounded—a deep slash carved across his obsidian scales, thick, dark blood oozing down his side.
For the first time since the battle began, the Demon King narrowed his eyes.
Anos slowly turned his head, glancing at the injury on his companion's flank. His grip on his greatsword tightening, as the weight of the situation sank in.
And in that brief silence—
Plip.
A single drop of dragon blood splattered onto the battlefield below.
Plip. Plip.
Then another.
And another.
The Demon Counts seated in the stands, once full of smug confidence, now sat in frozen silence.
The realization crept in, slow and undeniable.
The Black Dragon Drogo, a creature of pure devastation, a being whose very presence instilled terror, had just bled—not from some divine calamity.
Not from an ancient prophecy.
But from a human.
For the first time, the demons watching understood—
That this battle was not going to be one-sided.
It was not going to be an easy display of superiority.
The human Emperor had come prepared.
And he was dangerous.
Murmurs began spreading throughout the demon seating area.
"Drogo… was hit?"
"The human countered the Void Breaker Slash?"
"No, that can't be right. That move is supposed to be impossible to return…! And yet—"
The confidence that once roared within the demon ranks wavered.
Meanwhile, on the human side—
A heartbeat of silence.
Then—
BOOM.
The entire human audience erupted.
The stands trembled under the force of thousands of cheers, players and NPCs alike losing their minds at what they had just witnessed.
"HE RETURNED IT! HE ACTUALLY RETURNED IT!"
"HE MADE THE DEMON KING'S STRONGEST SLASH LOOK WEAK—!"
"HE MADE THE DRAGON BLEED—HE ACTUALLY HURT THE BLACK DRAGON!"
"THE BOSS IS A MONSTER!"
ChaosBringer, watching from the highest platform, let out a slow breath.
"…Unbelievable," he muttered under his breath.
His hands gripped the railing tightly, his heart pounding in his chest. He knew Leo was strong. He knew it.
But this?
This was beyond anything he expected.
Back on the battlefield—
Leo casually rolled his shoulders, spinning his dagger between his fingers.
His posture hadn't changed.
Not one step back.
Not a single sign of exertion.
He stared at Anos, his masked face unreadable.
Then—
A smirk tugged at his lips.
"Scared yet, Demon King?" He asked, as his voice rang through the battlefield like a challenge.
Then—
He laughed.
A deep, low chuckle that carried through the battlefield.
He laughed like a maniac, taunting the Demon King and the dragon, as although he looked like a deranged fool, Leo knew exactly what he was up to.
This first counter was a make-or-break moment in his fight against the Demon King, as he needed to land a big blow to shatter his aura of invincibility.
The actual hit itself was not important, what was important was that the Demon King appear weak…. Appear mortal.
And that had been achieved with his hit.
And now that he appeared mortal.
Now that his followers began to wonder what was going on?
Leo began laughing at him to purposefully mock him, as he knew the Demon King had no other option but to go all-out now to save his reputation.
By landing the first blow, Leo controlled the pace of the battle now, which was absolutely crutial in his gameplan to win.

chapters.title: Chapter 816 - 816: The Black Sun
chapters.content:
As Anos looked around and saw pure fear in the eyes of his people for the first time ever, he realized that his carefully crafted image of years was crumbling.
For all their lives, the demons had imagined the Black Dragon and the Demon King as these invincible figures—symbols of power beyond measure.
And now, watching one of them bleed had suddenly shattered that illusion.
The once-roaring demon audience sat in stunned silence, their wide eyes flicking between the wound on Drogo's obsidian scales and the masked human standing defiantly below. Whispers rippled through the stands, uncertainty tainting their once-absolute confidence as Anos clenched his jaw.
This was not supposed to happen.
The plan had been simple: overwhelm the human with an undeniable show of power, crush him before his people, and reaffirm to the world that the Demon King's supremacy was absolute.
But instead—
Leo had done the unthinkable.
He had reversed Anos's strongest opening move and sent it back with twice the strength, giving it enough power to make even the mighty Black Dragon bleed.
Worst of all—he had laughed while doing it.
A deep scowl settled over Anos's face as he turned to glance at Drogo.
Plip.
Another drop of dragon's blood splattered against the battlefield below as Anos exhaled sharply through his nose.
For the first time in decades, a thought slithered its way into his mind—a thought he had never entertained before.
'Could we actually lose this fight?'
The thought lasted for a split second before Drogo's words pulled him back to reality.
"I'm okay, old friend. This small wound is nothing to me. My body's accelerated healing will close this wound before tomorrow morning. Just focus on the fight at hand for now."
Drogo's words snapped Anos out of his downward spiral, as ignoring the crowd and ignoring the million dark thoughts weighing heavily on his mind, Anos forced himself to focus.
He had to deal with Leo and win first.
Everything else could come after.
**********
(Meanwhile, Leo)
Leo keenly observed the change in the Demon King's facial expressions while laughing like a maniac.
Seeing Anos looking lost and shaken had been satisfying, but as the Demon King quickly regained his composure, Leo clicked his tongue in regret.
"The real fight's about to begin, Dumpy. Be prepared," Leo whispered, his voice calm but firm.
He knew by the look in the Demon King's eyes that he wasn't going to take the insults lying down anymore—that he was going to respond with a BANG!
And respond he did.
As the moment he regained his composure, Anos leaned slightly forward, whispering something into Drogo's ear.
"I see…" the Black Dragon said after hearing Anos's instructions, his golden eyes gleaming with understanding.
Then, without wasting another second, Drogo took off, flying vertically, as though he was aiming for space.
The Black Dragon's sudden decision to climb through the sky caught Leo off-guard.
For a split second, he considered commanding Dumpy to give chase.
But unlike the Black Dragon, who could fly indefinitely, Dumpy could not.
Leo made a calculated choice—he wouldn't chase.
Instead, he watched.
He observed as the Black Dragon and the Demon King climbed through the sky with terrifying speed, the dragon's enormous wings tearing through the air like great obsidian blades.
That was when everything started to change.
At first, it was subtle.
A strange heaviness began to settle over the battlefield, creeping in like an unseen force.
The air grew thicker, the pressure heavier, as though something immense was pressing down on every living thing.
Then—
"What's happening? Why can I suddenly not breathe properly?"
"Is it just me, or did our surroundings suddenly start turning dark?"
"My skin… it's tingling… but I don't know why?"
Unnatural phenomena gripped the arena the higher Drogo flew.
At first, nobody seemed to understand what was happening.
Then, as their gazes lifted, they saw it.
The massive black flames coiling around Drogo's body, writhing like living shadows, pulsing with waves of raw, overwhelming mana.
He was preparing something.
Something catastrophic.
And since it was an attack that took significant time to prepare, he had left the battlefield—rising higher and higher, separating himself from Leo and Dumpy below, ensuring that they could not interfere.
"Cowards! Running away from an active battle by flying—how disgraceful!" Dumpy shouted, his insult aimed more at the Demon Crowd than his opponents, trying to rile them up just like Leo had.
But this time—his words fell flat.
No one was listening.
Every pair of eyes was locked onto the sky.
The Black flames engulfing Drogo seemed to consume sunlight, as if it were their natural enemy, causing the sky around him to start to die.
The once-brilliant blue above the battlefield dimmed, not as if a cloud had passed, but as though the very light itself was being consumed.
A vast shadow stretched outward from where Drogo hovered, expanding unnaturally across the heavens, like an inkblot spreading through water.
It didn't block the sun.
It swallowed it whole.
The arena trembled.
"I can't… I can't move my legs properly…"
"My arms feel heavy—like something's pushing me down—"
"What… what the hell is that thing forming up there?!"
The human spectators panicked.
And even the demons, who had been stunned into silence by Leo's attack just moments ago, began to stir and speculate.
"I'm scared…."
"This attack feels a hundred times stronger than the one our King launched…"
"Is this the true power of the Black Dragon?"
They wondered, because now, there was no denying it.
Something cataclysmic was being born in the sky above.
BOOM.
At that moment, a pulse of pure mana erupted from Drogo's body, sending a shockwave downward that rattled the arena walls. The air crackled with electricity as the black flames around him thickened, coalescing into a singular, spinning mass.
The sphere grew.
It twisted, pulsed, and devoured the space around it—sucking in the very light that tried to touch it.
It was no longer just a gathering of flames.
It was a celestial force.
A sun made of pure destruction.
A Black Sun.
A technique whispered about in ancient legends.
A Divine Move, labeled among the top three strongest attacks in the world of Terra Nova Online.
A technique so feared, even demons themselves dreaded seeing it unleashed.
A technique that delivered threefold ruin—through its crushing gravity, its all-consuming heat, and its absolute impact.
"He's done for—the Human Emperor is done for!"
"The Black Sun is here! The move whispered in legends that can destroy entire cities!"
"Run! We must run! Or the sun shall consume us all—"
The Demon Counts spoke, panic evident in their voices, as they understood the significance of the attack brewing in the sky.
Unlike the common fools who only watched in awe, the Demon Nobles knew exactly what was coming, and they did not intend to stay back and see it descent.

chapters.title: Chapter 817 - 817: Madness
chapters.content:
Leo saw the Black Sun enlarging in the sky with genuine fear in his eyes.
He was not a gaming nerd and hence he had no idea about the sheer catastrophic power of the Black Sun, as per the game's historic lore.
However, he recognised the move from the list of the game's strongest moves that Captain Kid had given him, and hence he knew that it was a (Divine) ranked move at the least.
*Shiver*
Watching the Black Dragon enlarge it into a larger and larger mass with every passing second sent a shiver down his spine, as Leo understood at that moment deep down in his spine, that he could not hope to block or stop that move.
[Full Counter] was not going to work on a move of that size and power, nor did he have the strength to physically return it even if he tried.
'Run–' Screamed the survival instinct in his brain, urging him to escape while he still could, however, while his survival instincts asked him to run, his ego refused to behave like a coward.
"HA–"
"HAHA—"
"HUAHAHAHAHA—"
Leo laughed, pointing at the black sun, as this time he did not laugh mockingly, but laughed because he genuinely had a screw loose in his head.
"BRING IT, COME ON NOW, DON'T MAKE ME WAIT NO MORE–" He roared, as gripping both his daggers, he looked poised to counter that move, his stance expectant, even though he did not know how to.
Oddly enough, his voice reverberated loudly through the eerily silent arena, as both the human and demons were stunned to see him laugh at the face of such overwhelming power.
Apart from him, there was not a single person in the audience who was not afraid to die, however, like a true maniac Leo laughed in the face of death, spooking both the humans and demons alike.
"No way…. 'TheBoss' is actually asking the Black Dragon to bring it! Has he lost his mind?"
"Can he actually counter this power? If he can, I'll bow to him and accept him as my ancestor right here"
"The Boss definitely has a few screws loose in his head if he's asking for this attack to hit him head on. But I guess you don't become the number one player in the game without possessing outrageous balls and a few screws loose—" The humans said, as they gulped in anticipation.
And then, it happened.
Drogo finally unleashed the Black Sun.
The divine move hurtling down towards the ground as its sheer gravitational force crushed all the spectators beneath with an incredible pressure.
*CRACK*
*CRASH*
The make-shift stands made of wood, cracked and crumbled, as thousands of humans and demons alike fell to the ground from their viewing stands in a heap of mess.
*Sizzle*
*Sizzle*
The very air around the arena began to sizzle and steam as it looked like the attack began evaporating the moisture from the ground, the temperature quickly turning unbearable.
"Die—- we are all going to die!" A scream rang across the battlefield, as hundreds of thousands of demons and humans alike realized at that moment that the Black Sun wasn't just going to kill Leo, but all of them.
It seemed inevitable.
A fate already sealed.
However, at that moment, Dumpy finally jumped into the sky, the eyes of the giant frog confident and unyielding as he confronted the Black Sun well above the battlefield.
"Don't worry Lord Father, I've got this–" he said as he activated [Mana Absorb].
Using one of his inherent racial abilities, Mana Absorb, Dumpy crossed his blades and pushed against the descending sun, as he rapidly began to devour its energy.
"Ohhh yeah, this is some good shit—" He yelled, as his HP began depleting rapidly from the heat of the move.
-750
-750
-750.
With each passing second, the sheer heat and pressure of the move made Dumpy lose some HP, as the armor above his body began to bubble and melt.
However, as a trade-off for his pain, Dumpy began to absorb the black flames that made up the black sun, depleting it in size rapidly, as soon enough the move shrank, its heat and strength depleting.
"He's doing it! The frog is stopping the black sun!"
"GO! GO! GO! GREEN FROG, WE ARE ALL BEHIND YOU—"
"THE FROG IS MY NEW FAVORITE WARRIOR IN TERRA NOVA ONLINE, I WILL FOREVER WORSHIP HIM"
The humans roared in elation watching Dumpy's heroics, while the Demons watched with mouths agape, utterly stunned by the sight.
"Impossible…. This is a move that's supposed to destroy entire cities, how can a mere frog stop it?"
"Is the Human Emperor and his pet really this strong? This single move could have easily killed all of us Demon Counts together, but the Frog is opposing it–"
"The world is wide, The Human Emperor and his pet are not as weak as we thought"
The demons acknowledged, as no longer could they belittle Dumpy and Leo, after what they witnessed before their own eyes.
However, while the whole arena seemed to be impressed by Dumpy, Leo did not seem to be happy, as he screamed at the top of his lungs.
"DUMPYYYYYYY—-"
"USE MANA SUPPLEMENT, CHANNEL THAT STRENGTH THROUGH ME" Leo commanded, as although he did not say anything more, Dumpy's eyes widened in understanding.
Immediately, he began funneling the energy he absorbed from the Black Sun onwards to Leo, who dared to do something unbelievable through it.
Having seen the Black Dragon cast the move from start to end, Leo had received a once in a life-time notification from his class specific move just seconds ago.
A notification he did not intend to waste.
[System Notification:- You have mimicked the [Divine Move: Black Sun] you can now recreate it thrice within a week, as long as you have sufficient mana to cast it—] the notification said, as although Leo knew he did not have nearly enough mana to cast it on his own, with Dumpy's help…. He could.
—-------
