chapters.title: Chapter 823 - 823: One Of Them
chapters.content:
(The real world, VIP sector, The Arc Ship)
After logging out of the game, Leo wasted no time in thoroughly indulging in Amanda, and for hours, their bodies intertwined in an unrelenting dance of passion. The room was filled with the sound of labored breaths, muffled moans, and the rhythmic creaking of the bed beneath them.
She was insatiable, clinging to him like she never wanted to let go, her nails raking down his back, her breath hot against his ear as she gasped his name over and over again. And Leo? He took his time, savoring every inch of her, every gasp, every quiver, every cry of pleasure that spilled from her lips.
By the end, Amanda was sprawled beneath him, her limbs tangled with his, her skin glistening with sweat as she clung to him like a lifeline.
Huff… Huff…
"That was… unreal," Amanda panted, her voice barely above a whisper as she pressed a shaky hand to her forehead. "You were amazing, my champion."
Leo grinned, stretching his body like a satisfied predator, his fingers lazily tracing circles along the curve of her hip.
"You know," he mused, his tone teasing, "from here until we land, I could go like this every single day. After all, I haven't got much else to do."
Amanda's body immediately tensed, her legs clamping shut as if by instinct, her entire being radiating pure survival instinct at his words.
"No, no, no—absolutely not!" she shrieked, yanking the bedsheet up to her chest like a flimsy barrier between them.
Leo burst into laughter, pinching her nose with playful affection. "Hahaha… cute."
She swatted his hand away with a pout, her flushed face turning a deeper shade of red.
But as the heat of the moment slowly faded, reality began to creep back in.
Leo exhaled deeply, running a hand through his damp hair as an unsettling realization settled in his chest—his journey was over. From here until they landed, there was nothing left to accomplish, no more mountains to climb, no more battles to fight.
For someone like him, who thrived in the heat of conflict and ambition, the thought of idling away felt almost… depressing.
"Damn," he muttered, staring at the ceiling. "What the hell am I gonna do starting tomorrow?"
Amanda shifted beside him, propping herself up on one elbow as she studied him with a knowing expression.
"You know…" she began hesitantly, her fingers toying with the edge of the bedsheet, as if she were debating whether to say what was on her mind.
Leo turned his head slightly, catching the flicker of uncertainty in her eyes. "What?"
"You could…" she hesitated, then met his gaze head-on. "You could warn the others about what's coming. About what the future holds for them after we land. You could help them avoid a miserable fate."
Leo's expression flickered, a small scoff escaping his lips.
"You want me to be some kind of messiah now?" he asked, shaking his head with amusement.
Amanda's gaze didn't waver. "I'm not saying you need to be a savior, Leo. Just… a heads-up would be nice. They don't have to walk into this blindly."
Leo exhaled through his nose, sitting up slightly as he rested his arms on his knees.
"Haha, you know I want to," he admitted, rubbing the back of his neck. "But the moment I tell them the truth—the moment I tell them that their lives after landing on Terra Nova aren't gonna be all sunshine and rainbows—there'll be riots on a massive scale."
He turned to Amanda, his eyes sharp with cold calculation.
"People will start living like there's no tomorrow. Law and order on the ship will collapse. Right now, they're happy. They're enjoying their last few days in the game world without worrying about tier promotions or demotions or survival. Why would I take that away from them?"
Amanda's lips parted, but she didn't immediately respond. Instead, she sat there for a moment, just watching him, before slowly shaking her head in disappointment.
"You've changed," she murmured, her voice quiet but firm.
Leo frowned. "What?"
"You've changed, city boy. If this is what you think of the masses now… then you're not the same Leo I know from back on Earth."
She sat up fully, turning to face him, her eyes boring into his with a challenge.
"If you were still that boy from Earth—the one who was just Elena's cute younger child, just a repairman, just an ordinary guy struggling to get by— would you have wanted to know what the government was scheming behind the scenes?"
Leo inhaled sharply, his jaw tightening.
Amanda didn't stop.
"Would you have wanted to be warned about the dangers that were coming your way? Or would you have preferred to live in a happy bubble, blissfully unaware that you were doomed?"
Her words hit closer to home than Leo expected.
Because the truth was—he hated the way the government operated. He despised the way they kept secrets, how they made decisions for the 'greater good' without giving people a say in their own futures.
And yet—he was doing the exact same thing now.
He had assumed that the masses were too stupid to handle the truth.
He had taken it upon himself to decide what was best for them.
He had become one of them.
"…You know I can't say half of what I know, right? I mean people will have to take my word for it, I can't back it up with any proper proof," Leo muttered after a long silence.
"I did sign a non-disclosure with Captain Kid and I can't prove jackshit if someone calls me a liar—" Leo continued, finding an excuse to not do this, however, Amanda simply smiled, as she reached out to brush a strand of hair from his face.
"Just tell them what you told me," she said softly. "You're THE BOSS, you don't need proof to back your words, just your words alone are enough."

chapters.title: Chapter 824 - 824: Did What He Can
chapters.content:
(Terra Nova Online, The Forums)
As of today, less than five months remained until humanity reached planet Terra Nova, marking the end of their cosmic journey.
The countdown to a new world had begun, and for the hundreds of millions of players still immersed in Terra Nova Online, the transition was meant to be a dream come true—a fresh start in a land of endless opportunities, a utopia crafted for pioneers.
At least, that was what they had been sold.
Truth be told, Leo Skyshard had no interest in being a prophet or a public messenger. He had spent his entire life fighting for himself, making decisions based on what was best for him alone.
However, Amanda's words had struck a nerve, forcing him to confront a truth he hadn't realized— that he was no longer just a player.
He was an Emperor. A leader. The strongest warrior in Terra Nova Online.
And whether he liked it or not, people looked up to him.
So, against his usual instincts, Leo decided to give the people a warning.
Not as a savior.
Not as a saint.
But as someone who had seen behind the curtain and knew what was coming.
******
After logging into the game, the first thing Leo did was check the forums, where 4/5 posts were about his battle against the Demon King and the Black Dragon.
Predictable.
His fight had shaken the server, after all.
He scrolled through the top discussions, his eyes catching some of the most exaggerated, absurd, and downright hilarious takes from players still reeling from the battle:
— [User: TheRealChad]: "Bro, I swear, when TheBoss countered Void Breaker Slash, I saw my dead grandmother come back to life and whisper, 'he is HIM.' Like, this guy just played ping-pong with a semi-divine technique!"
— [User: DemonKingWeeps]: "DO Y'ALL REALIZE WHAT JUST HAPPENED??? The Black Dragon. The DEMON KING. TWO OF THE STRONGEST BEINGS IN THE GAME. And this madman spat in their faces and walked out with a dub like it was a casual Tuesday."
— [User: HolyFrogCult]: "DUMPY. MY LORD. MY SAVIOR. YOU HAVE OPENED MY EYES. FROM THIS DAY FORWARD, I SHALL PRAY TO THE GREEN FROG OF SALVATION. ALL HAIL LORD DUMPY!"
— [User: NPCFearsMe]: "Am I the only one who noticed that TheBoss literally laughed in the face of the Black Sun? Like, bruh. WHO DOES THAT???"
— [User: SweatyTryhard]: "Y'all don't understand. We witnessed a historic moment. People are gonna be talking about this fight for YEARS. TheBoss just redefined what it means to be overpowered in this game."
Leo smirked as he read the posts, his ego thoroughly satisfied.
"Looks like I'm not the only one who thinks Dumpy is the GOAT," Leo murmured, as he hoped that he could someday show Dumpy these chats in the real world, just to show him how popular he was.
He scrolled for a while, letting the praise and wild speculation of the server wash over him, until he was satisfied, which was when he clicked on the 'Create New Post' button for the first time ever.
The moment Leo's 'TheBoss is typing…' notification appeared, the entire forum froze.
He had never posted on the forums before from this account, and within seconds of players noticing it, the active user count on the forums skyrocketed, thousands of players refreshing the page in real-time, waiting for the Emperor's words.
— [User: ForumGoblin]: "H-HOLY SHIT, HE'S TYPING???"
— [User: ConspiracyMancer]: "EVERYONE SHUT THE HELL UP. THE GOD OF WAR IS ABOUT TO SPEAK."
— [User: WheresMyMana]: "If this is just him flexing about the fight, I'm still down, but I SWEAR—"
And then, Leo hit the send button.
—------
[ Title: The Future You're Not Ready For.
Posted by: TheBoss
(Disclaimer:- If you want to believe the words I'm about to post below, you can believe them, and if you don't want to and continue living in a bubble, I don't care for it either.
I'm making this post mostly for the members of the Uprising Guild who have supported me from day one, however, I'm posting it publicly so that those not within the uprising may also not remain uninformed.
However, if you have any problems with it, keep it to yourself, because I'm not going to entertain any replies beneath this post.
That being said, here is my grim warning for all )
For years, we've been told that Terra Nova is a paradise. A new world where we get to start fresh, free from the limitations of Earth. No debts. No poverty. No corruption. Just opportunity.
A new life, right?
Wrong.
Here's the truth they don't want you to know.
The moment we step off those ships, we're not going to be free.
We're going to be classified.
Organizations have already been preparing for this moment. The biggest players, the strongest fighters, the most skilled crafters—they'll be scouted, recruited, and absorbed into the most powerful factions within days. If you think you're just going to walk into the world and do whatever you want, you're delusional.
Those in higher sectors will have better-paying opportunities. Those in lower sectors will struggle to survive.
Yes, we'll all receive 'starter homes' and resources when we land. But those homes? They're in pre-built colonies, controlled by local governments and private corporations.
You will still have to work to sustain yourself. You will still have to fight to keep what's yours. And most of all—you will not be safe.
Terra Nova isn't just some game world we can log out of anymore. It's a new planet, with its own dangers, its own rules, and its own hidden threats.
The laws of Earth don't apply there and the 'human rights' that we are used to, don't really apply.
Our primary role in the new planet is that of migrant workers to move the economy and to replenish the war machine, and nothing else.
So prepare now. Train now. Think about what comes after this game, because if you're not ready—
You're most likely going to end up dead.
—--------
The moment Leo hit POST, the forums exploded.
The comment section flooded with reactions, ranging from pure panic to outright denial:
— [User: RealityCheck]: "HOLY SHIT. WE'RE SCREWED. WE ARE ACTUALLY SCREWED."
— [User: DenialGang]: "Nah, this is just fearmongering. The devs wouldn't let this happen. Right? RIGHT???"
— [User: CorporateShill]: "Sounds like a skill issue. Get good, peasants."
— [User: NoobHunter]: "Welp, guess I'm grinding every waking moment till we land. Ain't no way I'm getting stuck as a bottom feeder for the rest of my life."
— [User: TheGovernmentLied]: "So you're telling me I spent 4 years grinding my ass off, thinking I was gonna get a carefree retirement on Terra Nova, only to find out it's just Earth 2.0 but worse?!"
— [User: IAmAFool]: "Can someone else confirm this? Why do I feel like TheBoss is just doing this to get back at the righteous faction players? And to hassle them? I mean this can't be true right?"
The common netizens wondered, as Leo's post quickly got pinned to the top of the forums, with his threats being spread rapidly.
For a while, Leo watched the reactions of everyone under his post, but he soon got bored and closed the chat, thinking that he had done what he could and now the rest was up to them.

chapters.title: Chapter 825 - 825: Kid in trouble
chapters.content:
(Real World, Captain Kid's Office)
Captain Kid was not happy with Leo's post on the forums, as it stirred a pot within the common players that the Unity Government, who was paying for the transport of Earthlings, did not wish to be stirred.
Although Kid took the post down a mere 60 minutes after it went live, the damage had already been done.
Millions had already read the warning, and it was shared, reshared, and endlessly dissected across every forum, chat room, and player community in Terra Nova Online.
The initial responses varied wildly. Some dismissed Leo's warning as fear mongering, calling him a liar and an attention-seeker, but others took his words far more seriously.
And then there were those who did more than just take it seriously.
They demanded answers.
Within hours of the post going live, waves of players flooded the official game forums, system feedback channels, and even the Arc Ship's internal communication platforms.
"What are the Devs hiding from us?"
"Is it true that our future jobs are already decided based on our sector rank?"
"Why are we only hearing about this now? Shouldn't we have been informed?"
The pressure mounted rapidly, growing too large to ignore, and soon, Captain Kid found himself at the center of a brewing crisis.
His holo-screen was flooded with notification pings, flashing red alerts from his moderation team, relaying the same relentless reports.
The settlers were angry.
They were questioning the system, demanding clarity, asking for an official statement from the game developers to address the matter.
Kid cursed under his breath.
Issuing a clarification statement would only make things worse. If he denied Leo's words, people would see it as a cover-up and dig even deeper.
If he admitted the truth, it would spark even more chaos.
There was no winning move here.
And much to his growing dismay, it seemed that today's incident had already been reported to the Unity Government.
His communicator buzzed violently, and with a sinking feeling in his gut, Captain Kid swiped to accept the incoming call….
"KID YOU MORON—" The male voice on the other side cursed the second the connection was made, as Kid pushed the screen away from his ear.
"What the hell is going on over there?" The voice asked, as Kid did not need to see the screen to know who it was.
Administrator Ryker.
The Unity Government's direct overseer for this batch of the Arc Ship, and Kid's point of contact for this batch of travellers.
"Administrator, I can explain—" Kid began, however, before he could get another word out, the administrator went on a rant.
"You can explain? You can explain why millions of settlers already know information they were not supposed to hear for months after landing? You can explain how we now have a logistical nightmare on our hands because of one goddamn forum post?!" Ryker roared, as Kid winced, running a hand through his hair.
This was bad.
Very, very bad.
When the Arc Ship was launched, the Unity Government had planned out every step of the settlement process with careful precision.
The moment the settlers landed on Terra Nova, they were to be swiftly sorted—recruiters from the major organizations would approach the highest-ranked players first, absorbing them into lucrative positions of power, while those in lower sectors would be funneled into carefully crafted, low-level jobs.
On paper, they would be promised rapid promotions.
In reality, they would be locked into a system where power was monopolized by the elite, ensuring that the strongest controlled the flow of resources while the rest remained desperately chasing an illusion of progress.
The Unity Government hadn't planned for them to find out the truth until after they were already settled, by which time they would have been too deep into the system to resist.
But thanks to Leo Skyshard…
That plan was now in shambles.
And the Unity Government was furious.
"This debacle has cost us millions of mana points in projected losses," Ryker continued, his voice cold. "Your moderation team was supposed to control the narrative. Your security was supposed to suppress dissent. Instead, we are now seeing riots in the lower districts, and recruitment officers from multiple corporations here on Planet Terra Nova are scrambling to contain the fallout."
Kid gritted his teeth. "Sir, we—"
Ryker cut him off.
"I don't want excuses, Captain. I want a solution."
Kid exhaled slowly, trying to think. There was no good way out of this. Damage control was impossible now that the truth had been exposed. Even if they purged every last forum post, even if they sent out counter-messaging to discredit Leo, the seed of doubt had already been planted in the minds of millions.
Which meant that the only thing left to do…
Was punish the one responsible.
"We want Leo Skyshard." Ryker demanded, as Kid's breath stilled.
"Excuse me?"
"You heard me," Ryker's voice was cold and final.
"The Unity Government has decided that upon landing, Leo Skyshard is to be detained as a criminal for the disruption he has caused."
Kid felt his stomach twist into knots.
They wanted to hand Leo over.
They wanted to make an example out of him—likely charge him with economic sabotage, sedition, or some other bullshit excuse to justify imprisoning him and silencing him for good.
If Kid had been anyone else, he would have considered it.
After all, Leo was a thorn in his side too. The bastard was always making his job harder, constantly throwing wrenches into things.
And yet—
He couldn't do it.
Not just because Leo was TheBoss, not just because handing him over would cause riots amongst the Earthlings, but because Kid knew that if he did this, his own future with the Mu Clan would be dead on arrival.
Leo was still his last remaining leverage.
If he handed him over now, he would be nothing to the Mu Clan and his carefully laid plans of securing a cushy position post-settlement would vanish in an instant.
And that wasn't something Kid was willing to gamble away.
"I understand sir. It will be handled. We will ban Leo Skyshard from the game starting today, and we will also put him under house arrest.
He will be handed over to you in chains upon landing" Kid promised, as he lied through his teeth to save his skin.
"Do that. And do your best to fix this mess, or we will find a way to detain and arrest you as well–" Ryker threatened as he cut the call.

chapters.title: Chapter 826 - 826: Consequences
chapters.content:
(The VIP sector, Arc Ship, the real world)
The conversation that Leo had to be placed under house arrest and could not log-into Terra Nova Online anymore was an extremely uncomfortable one for Captain Kid, however, it was a conversation that he had to make nonetheless.
"You have to understand my position here too, Skyshard, they're asking me to hand you over as a criminal upon landing and there's nothing I can do about it.
If I don't put you under house arrest today and don't revoke your gaming access, they will know that I don't intend to hand you over later and will not let you escape.
By putting you under house arrest I'm doing you a favor and you will have to trust me for the rest" Kid explained, as Leo's frown deepened on his face.
"You hear this shit? Amanda? Acting like a saint has got me fucked. I told you warning the other players was a bad idea…." Leo jibed, as Amanda buried her head in her hands in shame.
"I'm sorry…." She said in a meek voice, as Leo chuckled at her cuteness.
"Don't be sorry, haha, it's not like I would do anything I don't want to do if I did not agree with it. I'm not a man who doesn't own up to his actions and blames others for it.
I'm just messing with you" Leo said, as Amanda instantly felt better hearing those words.
Leo had indeed messed up big time by antagonizing the Unity Government beyond the point of no return, however, it was an action already done and hence he could only take it as a lesson and move on.
"Captain, I understand what you're saying and it's not that bad being house arrested in this huge mansion, as long as I can train in my own yard.
Except that, I trust that you will somehow help me escape the fate of my impending prison sentence upon landing, because if you do not, I assure you that I'll find a way to leak all the shady dealings we have had on this ship and place you in the cell right next to me—" Leo threatened, as Kid broke a cold sweat.
If Leo really leaked what all shady dealings the two had on this ship, it wouldn't be the Unity Government hounding his ass, it would be The Universal Government.
And that was an enemy, Kid did not want to make.
"Yes, don't worry, I understand that my neck is now practically attached to yours, so trust me when I say this….. I will find a way to get you to safety upon landing.
But that will most likely mean that you will be separated from the rest of your family for a while.
We will have to collaborate with the Mu Clan, and there may be unexpected challenges," Kid explained, as Leo brushed him off.
"What will happen, will happen. Now if you don't mind, please let me enjoy my evening with my beautiful girlfriend, you're excused now" Leo said, as he accepted his fate easily and without kicking up a fuss.
Exhaling sharply, Kid stood up, as he extended his hand for Leo to shake.
*Clap*
The two shook hands, as Kid nodded in appreciation.
"Thanks for your understanding, and congratulations on your last fight against the Demon King. I did not think it was possible for a player to defeat the Black Dragon, but you did it.
While your time as 'TheBoss' might have come to an abrupt end, your legend will most likely never be forgotten" Kid said, as he finally took his leave.
********
Once alone, Leo tried to behave normally and cuddle with Amanda in a chirpy mood, however, Amanda was having none of it.
She kept muttering, "I'm sorry…" "I'm sorry" and even shed a couple of tears.
More than his gaming ban, Amanda seemed horrified about all the legal trouble that Leo had to face upon landing, as somehow she felt like this was all her fault.
"Why are you not mortified? The aliens literally want you cuffed and answerable for all your crimes! They're gonna hunt you like a criminal!
How can you remain so calm?" She asked, her voice breaking, as Leo simply chuckled to her words.
"Why am I so calm?" Leo asked, running his fingers through his hair.
"I am so calm, because what's the point of freaking out about the inevitable?
Yes, I'm afraid about what will happen to me upon landing, but what good will whining and crying like a bitch about it do?
What's done is done, and continuing to dwell on it is a waste of time.
I live in the present, and the way I see it, I might not get to see you for a while after landing, so let's ensure that these last 5 months that we have together are a period to remember" Leo said, as he forcefully pulled in Amanda for a kiss and began kissing her before she could argue back.
Truth be told, even Leo wasn't entirely sure how things would unfold once they reached Terra Nova, but worrying about it now was pointless.
The way he saw it, he had already set the events into motion—there was no going back. The only choice left was to ride the storm and make the best of what remained.
Amanda, however, wasn't as easily reassured. Her fingers clutched at his shirt, her forehead pressed against his chest as she whispered, "I just… I don't want anything to happen to you. If you get taken away, I won't be able to do anything to help."
Leo sighed, brushing his lips against the top of her head. "You're underestimating me, sweetheart. I've come too far to let some bureaucrats with a grudge be the end of me. If they think they can just lock me up like some fool, they're in for a rude awakening."
His words were confident, but Amanda could feel the tension in his body—the slight stiffness in his muscles, the controlled breath in his lungs. He was putting on a front for her sake, and though she appreciated it, she wished he wouldn't always act like he had to carry everything alone.
She pulled back slightly, meeting his eyes with a quiet intensity. "Promise me that no matter what happens, you'll find a way back to me."
Leo grinned, his cocky, lopsided smirk returning as he wiped away the stray tear from her cheek. "I promise." His voice was steady, his grip firm. "You think something as small as intergalactic law is gonna stop me? Come on, Amanda, I thought you knew me better than that."
She let out a watery chuckle despite herself. "You're impossible."
"And you love it." He winked, pulling her flush against him again.
And just like that, the somber conversation faded, replaced by warmth, by something they could hold onto, something that was real in the moment. Leo knew that the next five months would be a countdown, a slow march toward an uncertain fate, but for now, with Amanda in his arms, he refused to dwell on it.
The future could wait for all he cared.

chapters.title: Chapter 827 - 827: The Men's Talk.
chapters.content:
(A few days later, The VIP manor)
*THUMP* *THUMP*
Leo and Luke stood overlooking the new construction taking place in their mansion, as they surveyed the work of the Arc Ship Staff.
"You shouldn't have spent all your MP points on doing something so stupid brother, those MP might have proved to be useful for you after you land—" Leo muttered, as Luke only ruffled his hair lovingly in response.
"I can always make more MP, but I can't bring back lost time. With this new phone line extended to our mansion, you can call mom daily while on house arrest.
I'm sure it will make both of you feel better" Luke said, as Leo fell silent at his words.
After finding out about his house arrest, Luke had spent all his MP to drag a phone line to their mansion, so that Leo could talk to their mother these next few months to their heart's content.
"Brother, my future once we land on Terra Nova does not look so good.
I'm in a world of trouble and may get separated from you all.
I don't need to say this, but please take care of Amanda and mom while I'm away" Leo said in a sombre voice, as the mood around him turned gloomy.
"Of Course you don't have to say this. Amanda is like family for me too, so of course I'll look after her.
And mom too, I'm not gonna trust Jacob to have her back, so don't worry, I'll take care of the family when you're not around" Luke assured, as Leo nodded in satisfaction.
His brother was a reliable warrior and a reliable man, and Leo felt content leaving the security of the family up to him, especially now that he was a master level warrior himself.
"Right, congratulations on hitting the master realm. I always knew you could do it–" Leo said, changing the topic, as Luke laughed a mirthless laugh.
"I thought master was the pinnacle of what one could achieve. Atleast, that's what it felt like while we were on the Arc Ship, however, now I know that it's just the beginning.
Once we land, it's the bare minimum to be considered a real warrior, so I can't be too happy with this…. I must improve a lot going forward" Luke said, as he scoffed in disappointment.
If this was a year ago, he would be over the moon to have reached the 'Master' realm, however, now that he knew the exact power scale of the universe, he understood that 'Master' warriors were not even worth noting in the grand scheme of things.
"What's your plan, once we land? Are you really going to trust this Mu Clan for sponsoring you? Do you think they can pull you out of trouble?" Luke asked, as Leo let out a long sigh at his question.
"I don't know brother…. I just know I won't let Kid cuff me after we land, no matter what, and if push comes to shove, I'll use [Vanish] [Blade Switch] [Mirror World] and every other skill in my arsenal to evade the authorities and escape the planet as a vigilante.
According to my understanding, there are many planets in the universe that are bandit hubs, not regulated by any faction.
So if the Mu Clan can't pull me out, I'll just become an outlaw until I can figure a way back into society….." Leo said, as listening to his response it was Luke who let out a long sigh.
Leo's decision at the end to warn all players about their impending future was a controversial one, with great consequences to his personal life.
On one hand, he had given all Earthlings a headstart on what was about to come.
But on the other, he had made himself public enemy number one of the Unity Government.
As a brother, Luke could not appreciate what Leo did, however, as an Earthling he was proud of him.
"According to some ex-clan members that I talked to within the game, a lot of workers have stopped listening to their superiors in the lower sectors.
There are daily tensions at the work stations there and the superiors literally have to threaten the players with evaluation reports that will reflect on their profile after they land, to keep them in line and working.
You have stirred the pot big time, and made the life of many people on the ship a living hell–" Luke reported, as Leo shrugged his shoulders in nonchalance.
He did what he thought was right, and did not care about what the consequences of his actions were.
"I've thought about this a lot…. And while I don't think they will target and heckle you to find out where I am, because I'm telling none of you where I'm going.
However, if they do….
My suggestion is that you take everyone and move to any planet that's governed by the Universal Government.
The Universal Government is the number one power in the Universe, and the Unity Government can cry all they like, but their jurisdiction ends if you can skip planets.
I'm not sure what troubles you may face upon landing, but this could be a viable plan to get to safety–" Leo suggested, as Luke looked towards the sky, his face littered with frown lines.
"Yeah…. Not a bad plan" he said, his voice heavy, as he tried to hold back the tears forming in his eyes.
The two of them could pretend like everything was normal, but it was not.
In a few months, their life was about to turn upside down once they landed and there was a high chance that they got seperated for the first time in their entire lives, with it being unknown as to when they will meet again.
"Just be safe Leo. It doesn't matter 2 years, 5 years. Or hell even 20 years.
Just make sure to come back to us when you can" Luke said at the end, as Leo gave him a side hug.
"Of course, what will I even do without you?" He replied, as the brothers concluded their conversation.

chapters.title: Chapter 828 - 828: The Final Escape Plan
chapters.content:
(3 months later, The Arc Ship)
3 months passed in a blink of an eye for Leo, who spent most of his days leisurely training his existing skills, aside from spending quality time with Amanda and phone calls with his mother.
Life was pretty stable and mundane, however, beneath that facade of stability, Leo was anything but calm at his core.
"So what's the news from the Mu Clan Captain? What's the plan once we land?" Leo asked, as Captain Kid laid out the plan for him.
"I did make contact with the Mu Clan, and this is what they've informed me to do–" Kid began as he pointed at a schematic map of the Arc Ship.
"Once we land, we will be surrounded on all sides by Unity Government officials, who will begin the procedure of tagging and sorting all incoming migrants.
This process will take place through 3 points of exit. One through the East, one through the South, and one through the West" Kid pointed out, as he tapped the schematic map with a pencil-like tool.
"The North Exit, is for staff only, and it will also have the maximum security.
However, there is a loop-hole here" Kid said, as his voice brightened.
"According to Universal Law, the Universal Government officials get to escort the game data from the flight after landing.
Meaning that they get to walk into the ship with large containers and store all the PC hardware without questions—-"
He paused.
"These containers can't be searched by the Unity Government security, and they can't even touch them.
They're considered diplomatic property, and hence the plan is to smuggle you out on one of them.
Apparently, the Mu Clan has already bribed a government official who is going to be on duty that day for escorting the Game Data, and it will be him who will help you escape through the first layer of security—" Kid explained, as Leo let out a deep sigh.
The plan did sound solid so far, however, it relied completely on the competency of the universal government officer that the Mu Clan had bribed to take him out.
If he was competent enough, this plan would succeed without a hitch.
However, if he was not, then there could be serious trouble.
"After we get past the first security perimeter, you will most likely be on your own.
I will be detained by the Unity Government officials for not having handed you over, however, according to the orders I've received, there will be someone from the Mu Clan present outside the perimeter to escort you out of the planet and to a Mu Clan stronghold.
The name of this contact is 'Muiyan Faye', she is a woman that has short hair and olive skin.
You will need to trust her to get out of the planet" Kid explained, as Leo nodded in understanding.
"How safe do you think this plan is?" He asked, once Kid was done explaining, as Kid shrugged his shoulders in response.
"To be very honest, it seems safe on paper, however, these things never go as planned.
If everything goes well, you will most likely be a wanted fugitive with a small bounty on your head in the universe, however, the Mu Clan can easily get rid of it for you.
If nothing goes as planned you will be jailed, and then it will depend on how much the Mu Clan values you, for them to negotiate your release.
Either way, things are out of your hands and you can't do much about it" Kid said, as he placed a sympathetic hand over Leo's shoulders.
Unlike the gaming world where you could respawn if you died, the real world did not have such provisions.
Leo could not just fight his way out of the perimeter daggers blazing and hope for the best, because there was a real chance he could lose his life.
While he was still 'TheBoss' inside and outside the game, 'TheBoss' in the real world had to be more careful of the fights he picked, for now there was no [Death Evasion Token] to save him, in-case a plan went wrong.
*********
(Meanwhile ChaosBringer)
It did not take long for ChaosBringer to figure out that Leo had received a gaming ban, as his silence this time around was uncharacteristically absolute.
Since making that explosive post on the forums, Leo had not responded to a single message of his—despite ChaosBringer putting in a thousand different queries.
And although, for someone as inactive as 'TheBoss' who was known to disappear for long periods without responding, this wasn't uncharacteristic behaviour, ChaosBringer somehow knew deep down in his gut that something had gone horribly wrong for him this time around and that his lack of response this time wasn't natural.
Unfortunately, ChaosBringer had no way of reaching out to Leo in person.
He had no clue where the real 'Boss' was stationed aboard the Arc Ship, nor did he have the authority to request a meeting.
Yet, despite being unable to contact Leo directly, ChaosBringer refused to sit idly by.
If TheBoss couldn't move freely, then it was up to him to make sure that the uprising didn't crumble in his absence.
Hence, taking matters into his own hands, ChaosBringer began working from the shadows, doing the one thing he could, which was organizing the Uprising for life after landing.
He rallied the core members, securing their unity, and convinced them to stick together no matter what faction absorbed them after landing.
The key was survival.
If they splintered now, all the work TheBoss had put into building this force would be wasted.
And hence they had to stick together no matter what, with all players joining the same faction after landing and working in secret to help the boss.
In ChaosBringer's view, the core members of the uprising were the most important to retain and preserve the ideals of the guild.
Afterall, the core members were not just any players—they were the most loyal, the most dedicated individuals who loved 'TheBoss' to death.
They were the ones who owed him everything, the ones who had been saved, elevated, and guided by his leadership.
And though none of them had the power to change the course of events right now, they weren't the type of men to ever forget a debt of gratitude and would repay him with their lives if they ever had the chance.
Unfortunately for them, all they could do for now was to prepare.
But deep in their hearts, there was an unshaken belief—that one day, TheBoss would return. And when that day came, they would be ready, standing beside him once more, prepared to follow him into whatever battles lay ahead.

chapters.title: Chapter 829 - 829: Cash Grab
chapters.content:
(2 Days Before the Arc Ship Lands, Terra Nova Online)
A sudden chime echoed through the game world as two notifications flashed across every player's screen, signaling the final stretch of their journey in Terra Nova Online.
[System Notification: - Greetings players, it has been an honor for us to have hosted you for the past four years. However, like all good things, our journey together must also come to an end. The gaming servers will shut down after 24 hours, giving you one last day to enjoy the game to your heart's content.
As a parting gift, all real-life work assignments for the day have been suspended. You are free to immerse yourself in the game for the full 24 hours without any restrictions.]
[System Notification: - Greetings players, since this is the final day of the game, the operators have decided to open a special System Store that will allow you to purchase in-game items and bring them into the real world—provided you are willing to pay the price.
All purchased items will be delivered to you upon landing, so please check the store if you are interested.]
The first notification was straightforward, serving as an official reminder from the Arc Ship staff that the game servers would be permanently shut down in just 24 hours.
The second, however, caused an immediate frenzy.
For the first time since Terra Nova Online launched, players were being given the opportunity to bring their hard-earned in-game wealth and power into reality.
It was an offer too tempting to ignore, and within minutes, hundreds of thousands of players flooded the System Store, eager to see what was available.
The listings, however, sparked confusion, as all items were available through purchase only by spending MP.
A low-grade mana potion was listed at 10 MP, while a full mana potion had a price tag of 2,000 MP.
Skill scrolls and weapons were priced upwards of 50,000 MP, even for lower-tiered options.
There were no discounts. No alternative payment methods. And no purchases could be made using in-game gold or silver.
But despite the costs, the players had no reference point to judge whether these prices were fair or not, since they had no understanding of the market rates.
Was 10 MP for a basic mana potion expensive? Or was it a bargain? Was 50,000 MP for a skill scroll an absurd markup, or was it standard?
With no baseline to compare to, the majority of players paid the prices listed on the store happily, as they decided to land on Terra Nova with essentials such as basic health potions and stamina potions secured, which would give them a piece of mind.
However, with most players not having more than 200-500 MP in savings, purchasing a weapon or anything similar was purely a dream for most.
To solve this problem, a few players pooled their resources together, to buy a single weapon amidst the group, while others paid a protection fee to rankers, who they trusted to protect them incase things went wrong.
Regardless of their approach, one thing was certain—the System Store had turned the final day of Terra Nova Online into a whirlwind of uncertainty and desperate decision-making, as a majority of the server spent their MP like there was no tomorrow, not knowing that any remaining MP that they saved, would be transferred to a secure bank account in their name once the event ended.
This was a deliberate scheme, plotted by the Universal Government in tandem with the Unity Government, as while it would be the Unity Government who would purchase and fulfill all orders being made today, it would be the Universal Government who would make a big fat commission on-top.
With roughly 249 million players still left alive aboard the Arc Ship, and each player spending an average of 200-300 MP each.
It was a 625 billion MP turnover, with roughly 500 billion in pure profits, split evenly amongst both the Universal Government and the Unity Government.
With the universal minimum wage set at 1MP for 6 hours of labor, the amount spent by most players today was akin to 4 months of their salary for a foreseeable part of their future lives to come.
*********
(Leo's POV, real world)
Having never had the chance to play the game until the last day, Leo never got caught up in the scam of the system store and instead received a different piece of metal card from Captain Kid.
"So this just came- in this morning. You now have a VIP banking account with the Universal Warrior's Bank, with an account balance of an astronomical 927,000 MP.
You can find a branch for the Universal Warrior's Bank on almost any righteous faction planet, it's one of the biggest banks in the universe.
Or you can use this card to pay at any merchant outlet of your choice.
So, Keep it safe—" Kid said, as he handed Leo a black metal card that seemed to be made from an alloy that Leo did not quite recognise.
"Only 927,000? I remember having more money–" Leo protested upon receiving the card, as Kid shrugged his shoulders.
"There's a minimum deposit, A one time VIP account opening charge, A card issuance charge.
These are things that I don't determine, nor have any control over, so don't grill me over it" Kid replied, as Leo let out a long sigh.
MP was the currency of the universe and having 927,000 MP stored away was a big big bonus for him.
Since Kid had already educated him about the market rates of most popular items, Leo knew that with nearly a million MP, he could live a comfortable retired life even if he did nothing else, as most Captains who served in the Universal Government, could not save this sum up even after working hard for it their entire lives.
"Well, it's not so bad, if you survive to enjoy your wealth that is," Kid jibed at the end, as Leo gave him the stare as he left his mansion.

chapters.title: Chapter 830 - 830: The Last Dinner
chapters.content:
(One Day Before the Arc Ship Lands)
The countdown to a new life had officially begun.
With just one day remaining before the Arc Ship reached Terra Nova, the game servers had been permanently shut down, cutting off the last remnants of the digital world they had spent the past four years immersed in.
Now, all passengers were given clear instructions—pack up, finalize their affairs, and brace for landing.
Leo didn't have much packing to do. He had never been the sentimental type, nor did he enjoy hoarding items like others who clung desperately to pieces of their past.
However, there were a few select things that he couldn't bear to leave behind.
Turning to Amanda, he placed a small bundle in her hands, which included a worn sketchbook, a few sets of pencils and colored sticks that he had brought all the way from Earth, and a pair of training daggers from the Arc Ship.
"These are for you to carry," he said in a casual voice, as tears streaked down Amanda's face.
Amanda recognised the sketchbook, it was Leo's lifeline during their time in sector D, where he would often sketch scenery from back Earth and things like her mother's face to reminisce about a world left behind.
Over the years, he sketched less and less often, as he became more immersed in training and meditation, however, over the last 5 months he began sketching once again, this time to commemorate his time in Terra Nova Online.
His last drawing, was one where he stood over his in-game frog, with both being in full armor, which he signed at the bottom not as 'Leo Skyshard' but as 'TheBoss', his infamous in-game moniker.
Amanda knew just how much this book meant to him, and hence, she felt emotional when he handed it over to her instead of carrying it himself, knowing full well that he could not carry items out of the Arc Ship the way he was exiting.
"I'll keep them safe," she promised, her gaze meeting his, as Leo gave her a soft smile and a kiss on her head.
*********
With their time on the ship coming to an end, the final day had been reserved for family.
Alia and Luke had already made their way over to Leo's quarters, choosing to spend their last few hours together rather than being stuck in their own rooms.
It wasn't an occasion marked by extravagant goodbyes or drawn-out sentimentality—rather, it was a simple affair, where everyone tried to ignore the underlying tension.
Deep down, all of them knew that this was the last time they would be together like this.
By tomorrow, everything would change.
The comfortable security of the Arc Ship, the routines they had built, the people they had grown familiar with—all of it would be left behind as they stepped into the unknown, with all of them potentially facing major challenges the second they stepped out.
"Jeez, Amanda, it took you so long to learn how to cook the dishes that Leo likes. But by God did you get there by the end, This Broccoli Almond Soup is absolutely delicious.
I don't know if we will be able to get these ingredients once we land on Terra Nova, but if we don't, I will miss this dearly" Alia said, as Luke nodded in agreement.
"That's true…. This soup is delicious, but, I think it's exciting that we will be able to try new cuisines after we land on Terra Nova.
Imagine all the delicious foods in the universe that our Earthly palette has never tasted.
I mean, I don't know about you guys, but I'm hyped" Luke said, as Leo pointed towards his brother with a smile.
"At our next reunion, we should celebrate by having dinner just like this together, with the twist being that everyone must bring one of their favorite alien dishes.
I think that would be fun," Leo said, as everyone on the table nodded in agreement.
"That sounds like a good plan," Amanda added, her voice choking slightly as she spoke, as suddenly the light atmosphere turned slightly sombre.
All eyes turned towards Amanda, who tried to hold her tears together, and focus on drinking her food, however, her head hung in shame conveyed what her words did not.
Leo leaned over, hugging her tight, as Alia tried to lighten the mood once again.
"What do you mean, when we have dinner together again? I think we're going to have dinner together tomorrow itself, which means we might not have had enough time to try new dishes" Alia said, as Luke immediately picked up where she left off.
"That's true, it could also happen that way, but if it does, my vote is that we all bring one alien dish to the dinner table anyways…. You know, to have our first space dinner experience together….
So if it gives us all horrible stomach aches and diarrhea, at least we will be suffering together" Luke said, as everyone burst in laughter.
Leo smiled comfortably, looking around the dinner table, as although he did not know when he would enjoy the comfort of family like this again, what he did know was that this was surely not the last time that they were sitting and dining like this together.
The four of them were family, and no matter how far away the universe separated them. Leo had faith, that life would eventually pull them all back together.
—--------
/// A/N - That's it from my end folks. I hope you enjoyed the book Terra Nova Online, and I hope to see you all in the sequel, 'Timeless Assassin'.
As some of you who have started reading the book already must know, the sequel is set in a darker world where Leo is a more ruthless character, and while Terra Nova Online was a lighthearted book, the sequel will be a proper blood pumping action novel.
I was supposed to launch a promotional chapter teasing the next book after this chapter today.
But webnovel has delayed my ending event by a day due to mismanagement, so the teaser will come out tomorrow, after which this book will be set to completed. ///

chapters.title: Chapter 831 - 831: Teaser For Timeless Assassin.
chapters.content:
(7 Days Later, Leo's POV – Unknown Planet)
*Drip*
*Drip*
Thick drops of blood splattered onto the cold, sterile floor, leaving a crimson trail in Leo's wake.
A deep gash tore through his side, the wound pulsing with sharp, searing pain as he staggered forward, pressing a shaky hand against it in a desperate attempt to slow the bleeding.
His fingers were slick with his own blood, his grip weak, but he had no time to stop.
The facility around him was eerily silent, save for the distant hum of flickering overhead lights and the faint echo of his own ragged breaths.
White, sterile walls lined the dimly lit corridor, the scent of antiseptic thick in the air.
He had trusted the wrong people.
He had placed his faith in the wrong hands.
And now, he was paying the price.
His vision wavered, the edges of his world darkening as the loss of blood took its toll. Every breath was labored, each step heavier than the last, yet he pushed forward, sheer willpower being the only thing that kept him from collapsing.
'Stay awake.'
'Keep moving.'
'Survive.'
He kept muttering to himself, as he continued to trodd forward.
He was supposed to be smarter than this.
He was supposed to see the betrayal coming before it struck.
But this time, he had been outplayed.
After playing Terra Nova Online for such a long time, he should have known better than to buy into the narrative that the Righteous Faction was good and that the Evil Faction was bad.
However, he could only blame his own dumb decisions for the predicament that he was in now.
'I should have trusted Muiyan Faye. That woman was crazy, but at least she did not mean me harm–' Leo realized now, as he grit his teeth and pushed on, trying desperately to make his way out of this facility without losing consciousness.
However, at this critical moment his body started to fail him.
The paralytic poison laced on the dagger that had cut him started to take full effect on his body, making his legs go numb as he stumbled and fell to the ground.
*Thud*
*Crash*
As he fell down, he flipped a chair by his side in the hall as well, breaking it in the process.
'Well fuck, someone is sure to hear this noise—' Leo thought, as he felt the grip of the grim reaper tighten around his neck.
Things did not look so good for him right now, his chances of survival without external help were more or less 0.
Even if no-one else found him and kill him where he laid, he would eventually bleed out on this very cold floor.
Instinctively, he knew, that if he lost consciousness once, he was never going to wake up again, and hence Leo fought to stay awake.
Fought to stay alive.
As he dragged his paralyzed body across the cold floor, one arm at a time, as he left a bloody trail in his wake.
"There he is—" a voice suddenly said behind him, as Leo vaguely saw two figures clad in black coming his way.
"I'm done for…. This might be the end of me" Leo muttered to himself, as although he knew he was going to die, he still reached around his waist and clutched a dagger, as he planned to die fighting, even if he could not stand.
Oddly, there was no fear of death inside him.
Regret for not living longer and achieving more? Yes.
But no fear.
And he showed it when he looked defiantly into the eyes of his captors, who gazed down upon him with pity evident in their eyes.
"Look at his pathetic ass trying to plunge a dagger in us.
We are Grandmaster level warriors, kid, you can't harm us even if you tried" One of them said, as just at that moment, suddenly, Leo saw two bright bursts of light, followed by two exploding heads of his captors.
*BOOM*
*BOOM*
*SPLAT*
There was no fighting, no time to even react, as the two Grandmaster level fighters standing before Leo, died like insignificant dogs.
"Who?" Leo mused, as walking into his field of vision, he saw Muiyan Faye, the individual responsible to escort him out of planet Terra Nova, and the individual he mistook as his enemy after their first meeting.
"Look quite rough there…. Skyshard" Faye said, as Leo chuckled heartily in her presence.
"Save me–" he muttered, before passing out, as Muiyan Faye immediately rushed to heal and detoxify him, despite the toll it took on her own body.
"Amazing…"
"To have been cut by a dagger coated in Basilisk's poison and still come out this far? He must really have a strong will to survive and a freakish bloodline to match it" Muiyan Faye assessed, as she broke into beads of cold sweat.
As an agent of the evil cult, it was her duty to protect and nurture all individuals who could potentially possess the bloodline of the 'Timeless Assassin', and while it was not confirmed that he had such a bloodline, Muiyan Faye had a feeling that he did, which was why she went above and beyond to rescue him today from this Righteous Alliance facility.
"I hope for your own sake Skyshard that you do possess the bloodline of the ancient god.
For if you do not, you will become an enemy of the Righteous Alliance and a useless pawn for the Evil Cult.
And although we are not as wretched as the Righteous Alliance and don't dispose of the candidates that don't live up to our expectations, we don't nurture useless individuals either.
For your own sake. Prove your worth" She mused, as after applying some life saving aid, she slung his slump body over her shoulder and made her way out of the righteous faction medical facility.
Her destination?
The Evil Cult headquarters, Tithia.
